title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋八□□下復當
□□巡按廣東監察御史詹
===
□□□□□□陳一理李應
□□□□□同考試官提調
□□□□□□臣右布政
使鄒善監試則按察使史朝
寀副使孫光祖旣入院百執
事受法約惟謹乃合提學副
使林如楚所選士二千有奇
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋八□□下復當□□。巡按廣東監察御史詹□□□□□□陳一理、李應□□□□□同考試官；提調□□□□□□臣、右布政使鄒善；監試則按察使史朝寀、副使孫光祖。旣入院，百執事受法約惟謹，乃合提學副使林如楚所選士二千有奇，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), the realm [□□] was once again due for the [Provincial Examination □□]. The Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor Zhan [Zhentai 詹貞泰] [□□□□□□], [along with] Chen Yili 陳一理, Li Ying[…] 李應□, [□□□□] as Associate Examiners; the Proctors were [□□□□□□] and Right Administration Commissioner Zou Shan 鄒善; and the Surveillance Officials for the examination were Surveillance Commissioner Shi Chaocai 史朝寀 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Sun Guangzu 孫光祖. Once they had entered the examination compound, all the functionaries received the regulations and compacts with utmost care. Thereupon, they gathered the more than two thousand scholars selected by Education-Intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lin Ruchu 林如楚, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
三試拔其尤者七十有五人
竝其文籍
奏之貞泰不佞以職事宜宣言
首簡貞泰竊惟百匯莫弘於
□□□□□不知其幾
□□□□虛逼天津蓋天
□□□□□之雄注故
===
嶺海南冥之一都會也自任
囂開疆陸賈通使始入帝籍
而人文未宣彼其潗澕瀲灧
往往變雲物興寶藏珠璣犀
象瑇瑁丹砂之利甲於天下
唐宋以來儒術寢著則張九
齡余靖崔與之諸人相繼羽
punctuated: 三試拔其尤者七十有五人，竝其文籍奏之。貞泰不佞，以職事宜宣言首簡。貞泰竊惟百匯莫弘於□□，□□□不知其幾□□□□，虛逼天津，蓋天□□□□□之雄注，故嶺海、南冥之一都會也。自任囂開疆、陸賈通使，始入帝籍，而人文未宣。彼其潗澕瀲灧，往往變雲物、興寶藏，珠璣、犀象、瑇瑁、丹砂之利，甲於天下。唐、宋以來，儒術寢著，則張九齡、余靖、崔與之諸人，相繼羽
translation_en:
…Through three sessions of examinations, we selected the most outstanding seventy-five men, and together with their examination essays and registers, presented them in a memorial to the throne. Unworthy as I, Zhen Tai 貞泰, am, by virtue of my official duties it is fitting that I compose the prefatory remarks for the opening pages of the record.

I, Zhen Tai, venture to reflect that among all the great confluences of waters, none is vaster than [the southern sea?], [spanning] an unknown number of [thousand li?], its empty expanse pressing close upon the Celestial Ford; indeed, it is a mighty outpouring of nature's [vital forces?], and thus a great metropolis of the Linghai 嶺海 (Mountain-and-Sea) region and the Southern Ocean. Ever since Ren Xiao 任囂 opened up the frontier and Lu Jia 陸賈 served as envoy, the region first entered the imperial registers, yet its literary culture was not yet manifest. Its surging, billowing waters and shimmering expanses often transformed into auspicious clouds and vapors or gave rise to precious treasures, so that its wealth in pearls, rhinoceros horn, ivory, tortoiseshell, and cinnabar ranked first in the empire. From the Tang and Song dynasties onward, Confucian learning gradually grew prominent, and men such as Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, Yu Jing 余靖, and Cui Yuzhi 崔與之 successively [rose up to serve as wings]…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
翼後先起矣
明興
列聖紹熙代光揆以文教賓於制
科海隅蒼生靡然興文學冠
帶衣履與齊魯埒於是文章
如丘濬理學如陳獻章皆蔚
然為一時翹楚而其他名公
===
鉅卿炳烺相望未可一二數
向所云溟澥之精始鍾萃發
洩於交庾之間為俊藪而珠
璣犀象瑇瑁丹砂之利亦稍
間歇迺知天之至寶固有所
在不有以宣之不達今
皇上
punctuated:
翼，後先起矣。
明興，列聖紹熙代光，揆以文教，賓於制科，海隅蒼生靡然興文學，冠帶衣履與齊、魯埒。於是文章如丘濬、理學如陳獻章，皆蔚然為一時翹楚；而其他名公鉅卿，炳烺相望，未可一二數。向所云溟澥之精，始鍾萃發洩於交、庾之間，為俊藪，而珠璣、犀、象、瑇瑁、丹砂之利，亦稍間歇。迺知天之至寶固有所，在不有以宣之，不達。今皇上
translation_en:
… as wings to the court, rising one after another.
With the rise of the Ming, the successive sacred emperors carried forward the luminous glory from generation to generation. Governing through cultural education and welcoming talents as guests in the statutory civil examinations, they caused the common people of this coastal corner to turn overwhelmingly toward literary learning, until in caps, sashes, robes, and shoes the region rivaled Qi and Lu. Thus, in literary composition there were figures like Qiu Jun 丘濬, and in the Learning of Principle (Neo-Confucianism) figures like Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章, both flourishing as the preeminent talents of their age; while other renowned statesmen and great ministers shone in succession within sight of one another, too numerous to count one by one. What was earlier called the essence of the vast seas finally gathered and burst forth between Jiaozhi and Mount Dayu to become a marshland of outstanding talents, whereas the profits from pearls, rhinoceros horn, ivory, tortoiseshell, and cinnabar somewhat subsided. From this one knows that Heaven's supreme treasure indeed has its true abode, yet without something to bring it forth, it cannot reach fulfillment. Now His Majesty the Emperor…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
英睿神聖
握符凝
命覃聲敎之暨無問海内外靡不
矯翮思奮蓋千載一時也貞
泰始以聘往觀山河表裏臨
鴻濛測瀰泓遠睨於扶桑之
標浩瀚兼天一瞬無際西矚
===
於蒼梧鬱林崛崎崒嵂應接
不暇廼喟然而歎文不在玆
乎諸賢之聯翩翔輝有然矣
比從事獲與諸生之業言人
人殊然類能採英拮華腴贍
道德卽不能者亦不失繩墨
庶幾哉有當足以備他日煌
punctuated: 英睿神聖，握符凝命，覃聲敎之暨，無問海内外，靡不矯翮思奮，蓋千載一時也。貞泰始以聘往，觀山河表裏，臨鴻濛，測瀰泓，遠睨於扶桑之標，浩瀚兼天，一瞬無際；西矚於蒼梧、鬱林，崛崎崒嵂，應接不暇。廼喟然而歎：「文不在玆乎？諸賢之聯翩翔輝有然矣！」比從事，獲與諸生之業，言人人殊，然類能採英拮華，腴贍道德，卽不能者亦不失繩墨。庶幾哉有當，足以備他日煌
translation_en:
…is brilliantly wise and divinely sage, holding the imperial tally and consolidating the Mandate of Heaven. Where his far-reaching prestige and moral instruction extend, whether within the seas or beyond, there is no one who does not spread his wings and aspire to rouse himself to action—this is truly an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years.

When I, Zhentai, first traveled here upon invitation, I observed the inner and outer landscapes of mountains and rivers. Looking out over the primordial expanse and fathoming the boundless depths, I gazed afar toward the landmark of Fusang, where the vast waters merge with the sky, limitless at a glance; looking westward toward Cangwu and Yulin, the rugged, towering peaks were more than the eye could take in. Thereupon I sighed in admiration and said: "Is not culture lodged here? It is for this reason that so many worthies have soared in succession with such brilliance!"

When I took up my duties and was able to examine the essays of the candidates, their words differed from person to person, yet generally they were able to gather the finest blossoms of rhetoric and enrich their writings with morality and virtue; even those who fell short of this did not depart from the proper standards. Perhaps they have hit the mark, sufficing to prepare for a future day…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
煌乎盛矣此寧獨氣數然其
諸有作於風者耶叔孫穆子
曰太上立德其次立言迺今
言則人能矣顧所取與所用
異也辭章功實其大指殊科
今必以立談之間槩平生之
業旣已難矣乃復求十一於
===
千百則難之難者也彼其貌
言不適聲實縣絕諸士謂何
國家需賢如責質程功棄偽增
實吾即不敢設不然之事以
待異日脫有萬一將何所傅
其罪吾於是益竦然滋懼巳
語曰文理未明不可與并兼
punctuated: 煌乎盛矣！此寧獨氣數然？其諸有作於風者耶？叔孫穆子曰：「太上立德，其次立言。」迺今言則人能矣，顧所取與所用異也，辭章功實，其大指殊科。今必以立談之間，槩平生之業，旣已難矣；乃復求十一於千百，則難之難者也。彼其貌言不適、聲實縣絕，諸士謂何？國家需賢，如責質程功、棄偽增實，吾即不敢設不然之事以待異日；脫有萬一，將何所傅其罪？吾於是益竦然滋懼巳。語曰：「文理未明，不可與并兼；
translation_en: …gloriously flourishing indeed! Could this merely be a matter of cosmic destiny? Or is it rather inspired by the moral customs [of the age]? Shusun Muzi 叔孫穆子 said: "The highest achievement is to establish virtue; the next is to establish words." Now, when it comes to words, everyone is capable of producing them. Yet what is used for selection differs from what is needed in practical employment; literary composition and substantive achievement belong in their main import to different categories. To insist on judging a lifetime's undertaking in the span of a brief conversation is difficult enough; and to seek one or two out of hundreds and thousands is the most difficult of difficulties. Should their outward words fail to match [their inner character], and their reputation be utterly divorced from reality, what would the scholars themselves say to that? The state requires worthy men to demand substance, evaluate accomplishments, discard falsehood, and advance reality. Even though I dare not presume in advance that things will turn out otherwise in the future, if by some remote chance one in ten thousand should fail to measure up, where would the blame be laid? Because of this, I grow all the more awestruck and fearful. As the saying goes: "Before the pattern and principle are clear, one cannot encompass all things together; …"

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毛羽未成不可以高蜚今士
方負垂天之具躡風雲之會
將摵膠葛翼歊烝旁撃宇宙
而游乎太清此其表樹卽曲
江新會諸君子何多讓焉諸
士勉之毋自負
明時而令秀異獨稱山海巳也是
===
舉也總督兩廣軍務兵部左
侍郎凌雲翼敷德宣威奠綏
南服提督南贛軍務都察院
右副都御史江一麟崇文振
武底定粤疆若大理寺右寺
正田登年適至平刑樂觀盛
舉至于贊襄試事則左叅政
punctuated:
毛羽未成，不可以高蜚。」今士方負垂天之具，躡風雲之會，將摵膠葛、翼歊烝，旁撃宇宙而游乎太清。此其表樹，卽曲江、新會諸君子，何多讓焉？諸士勉之，毋自負明時，而令秀異獨稱山海巳也！
是舉也，總督兩廣軍務兵部左侍郎凌雲翼敷德宣威，奠綏南服；提督南贛軍務都察院右副都御史江一麟崇文振武，底定粤疆；若大理寺右寺正田登年適至平刑，樂觀盛舉。至于贊襄試事，則左叅政
translation_en:
… "when plumage is not yet fully grown, one cannot fly high." Today, you scholars possess the wings that hang like clouds across the sky and tread upon a timely meeting of wind and clouds; you are about to sweep through the vast heavens and ride the rising vapors, striking out across the universe to roam in the Great Purity. In the achievements you establish, why should you yield much even to the worthy gentlemen of Qujiang 曲江 [Zhang Jiuling 張九齡] and Xinhui 新會 [Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章]? Exert yourselves, scholars! Do not fail this enlightened age and leave the mountains and seas alone to be praised for their outstanding marvels!

In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and Left Vice Minister of War Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼 spread virtue and manifested majesty, pacifying the southern realm; Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs of Nan-Gan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Jiang Yilin 江一麟 exalted civil culture and invigorated martial prowess, bringing stability to the borders of Guangdong; and Right Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Dengnian 田登年 happened to arrive to administer justice equitably and rejoiced in witnessing this grand event. As for assisting in the affairs of the examination, Left Administration Vice Commissioner …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周浩右參政劉志伊金淛左
參議何子明右參議石磐鄭
恭副使趙可懷劉經緯施觀
民許嶽僉事徐汝陽咸防範
維周都督同知總兵張元勳
副總兵晏繼芳參將侯繼高
陳璘胡震吳良知遊擊將軍
===
暴以平陳典楊瑄署都指揮
僉事季金劉天慶咸捍禦維
勤左參議夏道南僉事姜忻
署都指揮僉事于文煥以入
賀行皆先事與勞者也於例得
書因竝書之
江西吉安府龍泉縣儒學敎
punctuated:
周浩、右參政劉志伊、金淛，左參議何子明，右參議石磐、鄭恭，副使趙可懷、劉經緯、施觀民、許嶽，僉事徐汝陽，咸防範維周。都督同知總兵張元勳，副總兵晏繼芳，參將侯繼高、陳璘、胡震、吳良知，遊擊將軍暴以平、陳典、楊瑄，署都指揮僉事季金、劉天慶，咸捍禦維勤。左參議夏道南，僉事姜忻，署都指揮僉事于文煥，以入賀行，皆先事與勞者也，於例得書，因竝書之。
江西吉安府龍泉縣儒學敎
translation_en:
… Zhou Hao 周浩, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Liu Zhiyi 劉志伊 and Jin Zhe 金淛, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner He Ziming 何子明, Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Shi Pan 石磐 and Zheng Gong 鄭恭, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhao Kehuai 趙可懷, Liu Jingwei 劉經緯, Shi Guanmin 施觀民, and Xu Yue 許嶽, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Ruyang 徐汝陽, who were all thorough in maintaining security and precautions; Vice Commissioner-in-Chief and Regional Commander Zhang Yuanxun 張元勳, Regional Vice Commander Yan Jifang 晏繼芳, Assistant Regional Commanders Hou Jigao 侯繼高, Chen Lin 陳璘, Hu Zhen 胡震, and Wu Liangzhi 吳良知, Mobile Corps Commanders Bao Yiping 暴以平, Chen Dian 陳典, and Yang Xuan 楊瑄, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Ji Jin 季金 and Liu Tianqing 劉天慶, who were all diligent in standing guard and providing defense. Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Xia Daonan 夏道南, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Xin 姜忻, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Yu Wenhuan 于文煥, who departed to present congratulations at court, all shared in the labor prior to the event; by precedent they are entitled to be recorded, and so I have recorded them together here.

Instructor of the Confucian School of Longquan County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text: 諭朱貞泰謹序
punctuated: 諭朱貞泰謹序。
translation_en: …Instructor Zhu Zhentai 朱貞泰 respectfully writes this preface.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
萬曆四年廣東鄕試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史詹貞吉〔惟一四川巴縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使施堯臣〔欽甫直隸青陽縣人庚戌進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使鄒善〔繼甫江西安福縣人丙辰進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使史朝宜〔直之福建晉江縣人癸丑進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司副使孫光祖〔子紹浙江慈谿縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官
江西吉安府龍泉縣儒學教諭朱貞泰〔一甫直隸華亭縣人戊午貢士〕
浙江台州府僊居縣儒學教諭楊重俊〔克宅江西進賢縣人丁卯貢士〕
同考試官
浙江紹興府蕭山縣儒學教諭黄時濟〔文道江西豐城縣人甲子貢士〕
河南衛輝府汲縣儒學教諭蔣思誠〔明卿廣西桂林右衛籍全州人甲子貢士〕
湖廣長沙府長沙縣儒學教諭陳一理〔貫之江西高安縣人戊午貢士〕
湖廣長沙府瀏陽縣儒學教諭李應暉〔汝晦福建甌寧縣人甲子貢士〕
河南汝寧府新蔡縣儒學教諭羅應台〔德臣貴州永寧衛籍直隸泰州人丁卯貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆四年廣東鄕試

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史詹貞吉〔惟一，四川巴縣人，戊辰進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使施堯臣〔欽甫，直隸青陽縣人，庚戌進士〕；
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使鄒善〔繼甫，江西安福縣人，丙辰進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使史朝宜〔直之，福建晉江縣人，癸丑進士〕；
廣東等處提刑按察司副使孫光祖〔子紹，浙江慈谿縣人，己未進士〕。

考試官：
江西吉安府龍泉縣儒學教諭朱貞泰〔一甫，直隸華亭縣人，戊午貢士〕；
浙江台州府僊居縣儒學教諭楊重俊〔克宅，江西進賢縣人，丁卯貢士〕。

同考試官：
浙江紹興府蕭山縣儒學教諭黄時濟〔文道，江西豐城縣人，甲子貢士〕；
河南衛輝府汲縣儒學教諭蔣思誠〔明卿，廣西桂林右衛籍，全州人，甲子貢士〕；
湖廣長沙府長沙縣儒學教諭陳一理〔貫之，江西高安縣人，戊午貢士〕；
湖廣長沙府瀏陽縣儒學教諭李應暉〔汝晦，福建甌寧縣人，甲子貢士〕；
河南汝寧府新蔡縣儒學教諭羅應台〔德臣，貴州永寧衛籍，直隸泰州人，丁卯貢士〕。
translation_en:

大壯利貞大者正也正大而天地之情可
見矣
縣象著明莫大乎日月
是以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義
書
敷納以言明庶以功
念終始典于學厥德脩罔覺
不役耳目百度惟貞
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
「賜也達，於從政乎何有？」
「義者，宜也，尊賢爲大。」
孟子曰：「君子所以異於人者，以其存心也。君子以仁存心，以禮存心。」

易
「九五，觀我生，君子无咎。象曰：觀我生，觀民也。」
「大壯，利貞。大者，正也。正大而天地之情可見矣。」
「縣象著明，莫大乎日月。」
「是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。」

書
「敷納以言，明庶以功。」
「念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。」
「不役耳目，百度惟貞。」
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu)
"Ci is a man of discernment; what difficulty would he have in administering government?" [Analects 6.8]
"Righteousness means what is fitting; honoring the worthy is its greatest exercise." [Doctrine of the Mean 20]
"Mencius said: 'That whereby the superior man is distinguished from other men is what he preserves in his heart: the superior man preserves benevolence in his heart, and preserves propriety in his heart.'" [Mencius 4B.28]

Book of Changes (Yi)
"Nine in the fifth place: Contemplating my own life-course, the superior man is without blame. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating my own life-course' means contemplating the condition of the people." [Hexagram 20, Guan]
"Great Power (Dazhuang): It is advantageous to be firm and correct. What is great is upright. Through uprightness and greatness, the disposition of Heaven and Earth can be seen." [Commentary on the Decision, Hexagram 34, Dazhuang]
"Of the suspended images that shine brightly, none is greater than the sun and the moon." [Appended Remarks, Part 1, Ch. 11]
"Therefore they established the Way of Heaven, calling it the dark (yin) and the bright (yang); established the Way of Earth, calling it the yielding and the firm; and established the Way of Man, calling it benevolence and righteousness." [Discussion of the Trigrams, Ch. 2]

Book of Documents (Shu)
"They set forth and receive reports in words, and clearly test the multitude by their achievements." [Canon of Shun / Counsels of Gao Yao]
"Keep your thoughts from beginning to end constantly fixed on learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being conscious of it." [Charge to Yue, Part 3]
"Do not be the slave of your ears and eyes; then all your measures will be贞 [correct/upright]." [Hounds of Lü]

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民

有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
成王之孚下土之式永言孝思孝思維則
龍旂陽陽和鈴央央鞗革有鶬
春秋
春王正月師次于郎以俟陳人蔡人甲
午治兵〔俱莊公八年〕
===

八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄

春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮

===

Edicts, Mandates, and Memorials [select one topic]:

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
起解金銀足色
私借驛馬
門禁鎖鑰
脩理橋梁道路
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問郊祀以饗帝學校以崇儒二者皆帝王
爲政之首務也粵自禋祀燔柴辟雝思
服虞周之盛蔑以加矣而制作備于周
===
禮及大戴保傅諸篇其文質損益之儀
可得而詳與漢唐宋願治之主間亦慕
循其跡爲史美談然漢以黑帝而增北
時唐于南郊祭太微宋並五方上帝而
祀之果于饗帝之禮合與中元臨雍拜
老貞觀大召名儒慶曆增脩大學講殿
以備臨幸果于崇儒之心符與我
太祖至誠格天右文重道
寶位初定卽謹
punctuated:
起解金銀足色。
私借驛馬。
門禁鎖鑰。
脩理橋梁道路。

第叄場

策〔五道〕

問：郊祀以饗帝，學校以崇儒，二者皆帝王爲政之首務也。粵自禋祀燔柴，辟雝思服，虞、周之盛，蔑以加矣。而制作備于《周禮》及《大戴‧保傅》諸篇，其文質損益之儀，可得而詳與？漢、唐、宋願治之主，間亦慕循其跡，爲史美談。然漢以黑帝而增北時，唐于南郊祭太微，宋並五方上帝而祀之，果于饗帝之禮合與？中元臨雍拜老，貞觀大召名儒，慶曆增脩大學講殿以備臨幸，果于崇儒之心符與？我太祖至誠格天，右文重道，寶位初定，卽謹
translation_en:
Forwarding Gold and Silver of Full Purity.
Illicitly Borrowing Post Horses.
Locks and Keys for Gate Restrictions.
Repairing Bridges and Roads.

Third Session

Policy Questions [Five items]

Question: The suburban sacrifices to make offerings to the Supreme Ruler, and schools to venerate Confucian scholars—both of these are the foremost duties of governance for emperors and kings. Ever since the pure sacrifices and burning of firewood on the altar, and the submission of hearts at the Biyong royal college, nothing could surpass the flourishing ages of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou. Moreover, their institutions are fully recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) and in various chapters such as "The Tutor and the Guardian" (Baofu) in the Book of Rites by Dai the Elder (Da Dai Liji); can the ceremonial details of their refinement and simplicity, their additions and reductions, be recounted in full? Monarchs of the Han, Tang, and Song who aspired to good governance also at times admired and followed in their footsteps, making for fine tales in the histories. Yet when the Han added the Northern Sacred Place (Beishi) on account of the Black Emperor, when the Tang sacrificed to the Taiwei enclosure at the Southern Suburb, and when the Song sacrificed jointly to the Supreme Rulers of the Five Directions—did these truly accord with the rites of making offerings to the Supreme Ruler? When in the Zhongyuan era [of the Later Han] the emperor visited the Biyong and paid homage to the aged, when in the Zhenguan era [of the Tang] renowned Confucian scholars were summoned on a grand scale, and when in the Qingli era [of the Song] the lecture hall of the Imperial University was expanded and repaired in preparation for imperial visits—did these truly correspond to the spirit of venerating Confucian scholars? Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), with utmost sincerity reaching Heaven, esteemed culture and honored the Way; as soon as the Imperial Throne was first settled, he immediately attended with reverence to…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖之功大矣然古之言性者不過曰上
帝降衷于下民若有恒性卽孔子垂訓
亦止曰性相近焉蓋至孟子而後性善
之說始著矣夫謂之性善其旨與性近
之語得無相格與然則謂其有功於聖
門者果安在也自是而下其說寖詳有
曰性惡者有曰善惡混者有曰善惡各
有定無善無不善者雖人持所見要皆
左右孟氏之說而同歸於從善背惡乃
===
不得與孟氏同功顧辭而闢之何與宋
儒善言性者宜莫如程子定性一書明
天地聖人之常揭大公順應之的說者
以爲功不在孟子下乃亦有惡亦不可
不謂性之說豈天命之體彼亦有未窺
與抑有得於相近之說而云然與後儒
或取譬於日或借喻於水毋亦各因所
見而言之與夫知性而後不謬於學知
性之初而後不昧於性彼謂聖賢敎人
punctuated: 聖之功大矣。然古之言性者，不過曰：「上帝降衷于下民，若有恒性。」卽孔子垂訓，亦止曰：「性相近焉。」蓋至孟子，而後「性善」之說始著矣。夫謂之「性善」，其旨與「性近」之語，得無相格與？然則謂其有功於聖門者，果安在也？自是而下，其說寖詳。有曰「性惡」者，有曰「善惡混」者，有曰「善惡各有定」、「無善無不善」者。雖人持所見，要皆左右孟氏之說，而同歸於從善背惡，乃不得與孟氏同功，顧辭而闢之，何與？宋儒善言性者，宜莫如程子。《定性》一書，明天地聖人之常，揭大公順應之的，說者以爲功不在孟子下。乃亦有「惡亦不可不謂性」之說，豈天命之體，彼亦有未窺與？抑有得於「相近」之說而云然與？後儒或取譬於日，或借喻於水，毋亦各因所見而言之與？夫知性而後不謬於學，知性之初而後不昧於性。彼謂聖賢敎人
translation_en: …the sages is great indeed! Yet when the ancients spoke of human nature, they said no more than: "The Lord on High bestows a moral sense upon the people below; compliance with it reflects their constant nature." Even when Confucius handed down his teachings, he said only: "By nature, men are nearly alike." It was only with Mencius that the doctrine of the goodness of human nature first became prominent. Now, when he calls human nature good, does its purport not conflict with the saying that natures are "nearly alike"? If so, where then does his supposed contribution to the school of the sages truly lie? From that time onward, theories grew increasingly elaborate. There were those who said human nature is evil, those who said it is a mixture of good and evil, and those who said good and evil each have fixed grades, or that it is neither good nor not-good. Although each person held to his own view, in essence they all flanked Mencius's theory and converged on following the good and turning away from evil. Yet they could not share in Mencius's merit, and instead people spoke out to refute them—why is this? Among the Song-dynasty Confucians who excelled at discussing human nature, none could surpass Master Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥). His Letter on Calming the Nature (Dingxing shu 定性書) elucidated the constancy of Heaven, Earth, and the sages, and held up the standard of supreme impartiality and harmonious responsiveness; commentators consider his contribution to be no less than that of Mencius. Yet he also had the saying that "evil too cannot but be called nature." Could it be that he too had failed to glimpse the substance of the Mandate of Heaven? Or did he say so because he had grasped the meaning of the doctrine that natures are "nearly alike"? Later Confucians either drew analogies from the sun or borrowed metaphors from water; did they not also speak each according to his own understanding? Now, only after one knows human nature will one not err in learning, and only after one knows the origin of human nature will one not be blind to human nature. Those who say that when the sages and worthies taught men…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
倫理外禮教者事巫詛僨悍則弓刀兼
佩射利則淫巧競奇綠林聚嘯錦帆通
驕而尚義勵節之風不多見矣此其故
何與說者謂民風倡於士習士習興於
教化我
國家膠庠之教遠暨海隅未嘗無以風之也
而民風若此何與茲欲道德一而風俗
同將何以導之與此觀風者所欲聞其
詳諸士毋徒剿說為也
===
問善生財者因天資地民不加賦官無轉
輸而公私俱利之若屯田若鹽法蓋其
大較也粵稽古制漢趙充國屯塞下稱
富饒矣彼唐宋關中之屯金陵兩淮岳
州之屯皆屯也法亦有合與管仲相齊
鬻海為利致富强矣近議者或謂毋縱
末作而歸之官或謂毋奪民利而捐之
民其見殊也議果孰當與
國家創典則以垂永久分屯設堡通商辦課
punctuated:
倫理外禮教者事巫詛，僨悍則弓刀兼佩，射利則淫巧競奇，綠林聚嘯，錦帆通驕，而尚義勵節之風不多見矣。此其故何與？說者謂民風倡於士習，士習興於教化。我國家膠庠之教遠暨海隅，未嘗無以風之也，而民風若此，何與？茲欲道德一而風俗同，將何以導之與？此觀風者所欲聞其詳，諸士毋徒剿說為也。

問：善生財者，因天資地，民不加賦，官無轉輸，而公私俱利之，若屯田、若鹽法，蓋其大較也。粵稽古制，漢趙充國屯塞下，稱富饒矣；彼唐宋關中之屯，金陵、兩淮、岳州之屯，皆屯也，法亦有合與？管仲相齊，鬻海為利，致富强矣；近議者或謂毋縱末作而歸之官，或謂毋奪民利而捐之民，其見殊也，議果孰當與？國家創典則以垂永久，分屯設堡，通商辦課，
translation_en:
…[human] relations; those outside the bounds of ritual and moral instruction engage in shamanism and cursing; the refractory and fierce wear both bows and blades; those who chase after profit compete in excessive ingenuity and novelty; bandits gather and whistle in the greenwood; brocade sails traffic in arrogance [pirates and smugglers]; while customs of prizing righteousness and encouraging integrity are rarely seen. What is the reason for this? Commentators say that popular customs are led by the habits of the literati, and the habits of the literati are aroused by transformative education. Our dynasty's education in the state and local schools reaches far to the corners of the sea—it has never failed to have the means to influence them—yet popular customs are like this; why? Now, if we wish to unify morality and make customs uniform, how shall we guide them? Those who observe local customs wish to hear the details of this; you gentlemen must not merely repeat plagiarized clichés.

Question: Those skilled at generating wealth rely on the seasons of Heaven and take advantage of the resources of Earth; the people are not burdened with additional taxes, the officials have no need for transport and shipment, and both public and private interests profit from it. Such are state farms (tuntian) and the salt administration (yanfa) in their broad outlines. Examining ancient institutions: in the Han, Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 established state farms along the frontier, which were praised as rich and abundant. As for the state farms of Guanzhong in the Tang and Song, and those of Jinling, Lianghuai, and Yuezhou—all were state farms; did their methods also accord with his? When Guan Zhong 管仲 served as minister of Qi, he sold the bounty of the sea for profit and achieved wealth and strength. Among later commentators, some say we should not indulge secondary occupations [commerce] and instead return the monopoly to the officials, while others say we should not seize the people's profits and instead leave them to the people. Their views differ; which argument is truly right? Our dynasty established institutional statutes to hand down in perpetuity, dividing state farms and setting up forts, facilitating merchants and assessing salt quotas…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其爲屯鹽計豈不至周密哉奈之何法
久而弊滋也其在佗處姑勿論已如廣
東屯田自龍江分屯以來尺籍盡廢矣
比來綜核非不嚴也而武夫狡卒侵漁
逋負不可勝窮其尤敝者展轉典賣乾
沒於豪右而莫能究詰也玆欲釐正之
使梗者樂輸豪者革念安所決策與提
舉司鹽場課額舊頗稱溢今則額縮而
辦納日隳矣司事者議處非不詳也而
===
竈丁日困率多流移其尤蠹者貪夫逐
末亡命煽黨私販於海上至飄忽也玆
欲裁恤之使流移者甦興販者戢安所
取衷與夫調瑟者移柱捄弊者通變斯
二者當必有要領在也諸士挾策待用
必籌之熟矣其悉以對
問三代以降談兵者尚矣齊桓晉文威行
天下莫之能禁當時之稱兵何術而不
及食豈古者兵出於農餉皆自給與然
punctuated:
其爲屯鹽計，豈不至周密哉！奈之何法久而弊滋也？其在佗處姑勿論已，如廣東屯田，自龍江分屯以來，尺籍盡廢矣。比來綜核非不嚴也，而武夫狡卒，侵漁逋負，不可勝窮；其尤敝者，展轉典賣，乾沒於豪右，而莫能究詰也。玆欲釐正之，使梗者樂輸，豪者革念，安所決策與？提舉司鹽場課額，舊頗稱溢，今則額縮而辦納日隳矣。司事者議處非不詳也，而竈丁日困，率多流移；其尤蠹者，貪夫逐末，亡命煽黨，私販於海上，至飄忽也。玆欲裁恤之，使流移者甦，興販者戢，安所取衷與？夫調瑟者移柱，捄弊者通變，斯二者當必有要領在也。諸士挾策待用，必籌之熟矣，其悉以對。
問：三代以降，談兵者尚矣。齊桓、晉文威行天下，莫之能禁，當時之稱兵何術而不及食？豈古者兵出於農，餉皆自給與？然
translation_en:
…how could its provisions for military state farms and the salt administration not be utterly thorough and meticulous! Yet what can be done when laws endure for a long time and abuses proliferate? Leaving aside other places for now, take the military state farms of Guangdong: ever since the division of farms at Longjiang, the registers have fallen into complete disuse. In recent times, verification and auditing have not been lax, yet martial men and cunning soldiers encroach upon them and default on their dues without end; the worst abuse is that the land is repeatedly mortgaged and sold off, embezzled by powerful families without anyone being able to investigate or hold them to account. If we now wish to rectify this, making the obstinate gladly pay their dues and the powerful abandon their greedy designs, upon what strategy should we decide? As for the salt tax quotas of the Salt Distribution Supervisorate's salterns, formerly they were quite known for yielding surpluses, but now the quotas have shrunk and payments are daily falling into ruin. Those in charge of affairs do not fail to deliberate on measures in detail, yet the saltern households grow more hard-pressed by the day, and most of them flee and scatter; the most destructive abuse is that greedy men pursue commercial profit, and fugitives incite gangs to smuggle salt on the seas, moving as swiftly and elusively as the wind. If we now wish to regulate and relieve this situation, reviving the displaced and suppressing the smugglers, where should we find the right balance? Now, he who tunes a zither shifts the bridges, and he who remedies abuses adapts to change; in both of these matters there must surely be a key principle. You gentlemen hold strategies in readiness for official employment and must have planned for this thoroughly; set forth your replies in full.
Question: Since the Three Dynasties, those who discuss military affairs have been numerous indeed. Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin extended their might across the realm, and none could check them; by what art did the military operations of that era avoid even mentioning provisions? Was it that in antiquity soldiers were drawn from the peasantry, so that rations were all self-supplied? Yet…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
城濮之戰晉師在楚三日穀或者因敵
爲糧與吾觀向秦之兵初起高陽生勸
襲陳留以得積粟乃有從軍擊胡天子
至遣大官齎數十乘其重如此夫師行
糧食自古記之矣今粵之兵食可指掌
言也而日患不給其原安在與或謂在
兵或謂在民夫清海無波則寢兵之說
起剖膚實饑則兵民之說岐且治平不
忘戰養兵以衞民民出食甚艱則兵可
===
少與抑武憃精悍能枵腹格敵與粵兵
餉歲入四十餘萬惟正之逋負尚數十
萬司
國計者已不遺餘力然每至束手有司苦於
朘削介胄之士敀敀可無慮與有欲汰
冗兵蠲積逋與民更始者其毋牾梧否
諸士桑梓之邦搤掔而談計必有得於
衷願詳著之毋略毋隱
punctuated: 城濮之戰，晉師在楚三日穀，或者因敵爲糧與？吾觀向秦之兵初起，高陽生勸襲陳留以得積粟；乃有從軍擊胡，天子至遣大官齎數十乘，其重如此。夫師行糧食，自古記之矣。今粵之兵食，可指掌言也，而日患不給，其原安在與？或謂在兵，或謂在民。夫清海無波，則寢兵之說起；剖膚實饑，則兵民之說岐。且治平不忘戰，養兵以衞民。民出食甚艱，則兵可少與？抑武憃精悍，能枵腹格敵與？粵兵餉歲入四十餘萬，惟正之逋負尚數十萬。司國計者已不遺餘力，然每至束手。有司苦於朘削，介胄之士敀敀，可無慮與？有欲汰冗兵、蠲積逋，與民更始者，其毋牾梧否？諸士桑梓之邦，搤掔而談，計必有得於衷，願詳著之，毋略毋隱。
translation_en:
… In the Battle of Chengpu, the army of Jin subsisted for three days on the grain of Chu; was this perhaps a case of relying on the enemy for provisions? When I observe how, when the forces opposing Qin first rose up, the Master of Gaoyang (Li Yiji 酈食其) urged a surprise attack on Chenliu to seize its stockpiled grain, and how, when troops marched against the Hu nomads, the Son of Heaven went so far as to dispatch the Grand Provisioner with several dozen carriages of supplies—such was the importance attached to rations. Indeed, that "an army marches accompanied by grain and provisions" has been recorded since antiquity.

Today, the military provisions of Guangdong can be counted as easily as pointing to one's palm, yet every day we suffer from insufficiency. Where does the root cause lie? Some say it lies with the troops; others say it lies with the people. When the seas are calm and without waves, arguments for laying down arms arise; when flesh is carved away to satisfy hunger, the interests of soldiers and civilians diverge. Moreover, in times of peace and order one must not forget warfare, and troops are maintained in order to protect the people. When it is exceedingly difficult for the people to produce food, can the number of troops be reduced? Or can fierce and foolishly brave warriors fight off the enemy on empty stomachs?

The annual revenue for Guangdong's military rations is over four hundred thousand taels, yet arrears in regular taxes still amount to several hundred thousand. Those in charge of the state finances have already spared no effort, yet they repeatedly find their hands tied. Local officials suffer from having to fleece the populace, while armored soldiers clamor for food [? 敀敀 for 嗷嗷]—how can this not be a cause for concern? There are those who wish to cull superfluous troops and remit accumulated tax arrears so as to make a fresh start with the people; would such measures not run into contradiction and obstruction? Gentlemen, this is your native land, and as you clasp your wrists in earnest discussion, you must surely have reached sound conclusions in your hearts. Please set them forth in detail, omitting nothing and concealing nothing.
