title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
賜也達於從政乎何有
鄭偉
同考試官教諭黃批此題人多於達字講欠
分曉惟是篇發揮明切而體格亦不凡錄之
考試官教諭楊批調高詞渾一洗塵格可
以式矣
考試官教諭朱批雄健可觀
===
聖人於賢者許其識之優於治焉甚矣治先識
也賢者有其識矣聖人之許之也宜哉想其告
季康子之意豈不以夫人之不同者才也而可
致于用則一而已矣子欲知賜乎自我觀之其
達可使也穎悟得於天成而智慮昭融已具乎
疏觀之哲推測深於多學而識見明敏足裕乎
康濟之猷理有出於常情所難度者賜獨先明
諸心焉明則足以類萬物之情而施于有政自
化裁之各當事有出於意見所不及者賜獨旁
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

「賜也達，於從政乎何有？」
鄭偉

同考試官教諭黃批：此題人多於「達」字講欠分曉，惟是篇發揮明切，而體格亦不凡，錄之。
考試官教諭楊批：調高詞渾，一洗塵格，可以式矣。
考試官教諭朱批：雄健可觀。

聖人於賢者，許其識之優於治焉。甚矣，治先識也！賢者有其識矣，聖人之許之也宜哉。想其告季康子之意，豈不以夫人之不同者才也，而可致于用則一而已矣。子欲知賜乎？自我觀之，其達可使也。穎悟得於天成，而智慮昭融，已具乎疏觀之哲；推測深於多學，而識見明敏，足裕乎康濟之猷。理有出於常情所難度者，賜獨先明諸心焉；明則足以類萬物之情，而施于有政，自化裁之各當。事有出於意見所不及者，賜獨旁…
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

"Ci is perceptive and discerning; what difficulty would he have in administering government?" [Analects 6.8]
Zheng Wei 鄭偉

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Huang: On this topic, most candidates failed to explain the word "perceptive and discerning" (da 達) with sufficient clarity. Only this essay expounds upon it clearly and incisively, and its style is also extraordinary; I have selected it for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yang: Its tone is lofty and its diction vigorous; it washes away vulgar conventions and can serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: Forceful, robust, and worthy of note.

With regard to the worthy, the Sage commended his insight as being more than equal to the task of governance. How crucial it is that governance puts insight first! Since the worthy possessed such insight, how fitting it was that the Sage commended him! Considering the purport of his reply to Ji Kangzi 季康子, was it not that while men differ in their particular talents, in their capacity to be put to practical use they are one and the same? You wish to know about Ci 賜 [Zigong 子貢]? As I see him, his perceptive discernment makes him fit for employment. His quick comprehension is a gift of nature, and his thoughts are bright and penetrating, already endowed with the wisdom of broad observation; his powers of inference are deepened by extensive learning, and his discernment is clear and keen, fully sufficient for plans of bringing peace and relief to the people. When there are principles that lie beyond what ordinary minds can fathom, Ci alone first illuminates them in his own heart; being thus clear-sighted, he is able to classify the conditions of the myriad things, so that when applied to governance, his adaptations and regulations are naturally appropriate in every case. When there are affairs that arise beyond the reach of ordinary anticipation, Ci alone comprehensively…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
通其故焉通則足以悉萬變之賾而授之以政
自時措之咸宜入而議制則酌當否以效之君
而君之聰明不患於不逮雖萬化錯綜然即其
通達者運量之迎機而解綽綽乎有餘裕矣出
而施令則權輕重以致之民而民之情僞不苦
於難知雖庶務紛紜然即其練達者張弛之觸
類而通恢恢乎有餘地矣若賜者韞而藏之固
適用之器也知而使之則大夫之選也以之從
政亦何難之有吁此見聖門之多才而夫子之
===
知賜者亦審矣然他日宰信陽而告之曰勤之
愼之論治而又以進賢爲賢豈達未足以盡政
乎蓋達才也三者所以善其才者也夫子而得
邦家子貢從焉則綏和化成魯其東周矣奈世
之莫知也使子貢僅以辯名且曰夫子名聞列
國蓋子貢後先之噫淺之乎窺聖賢矣
義者宜也尊賢爲大
徐兆魁
同考試官敎諭蔣 批 講宜字爲大字有體認
punctuated:
通其故焉，通則足以悉萬變之賾，而授之以政，自時措之咸宜。入而議制，則酌當否以效之君，而君之聰明不患於不逮；雖萬化錯綜，然即其通達者運量之，迎機而解，綽綽乎有餘裕矣。出而施令，則權輕重以致之民，而民之情僞不苦於難知；雖庶務紛紜，然即其練達者張弛之，觸類而通，恢恢乎有餘地矣。若賜者，韞而藏之，固適用之器也；知而使之，則大夫之選也。以之從政，亦何難之有！吁！此見聖門之多才，而夫子之知賜者亦審矣。然他日宰信陽，而告之曰「勤之愼之」；論治，而又以進賢爲賢，豈達未足以盡政乎？蓋達，才也；三者，所以善其才者也。夫子而得邦家，子貢從焉，則綏和化成，魯其東周矣！奈世之莫知也，使子貢僅以辯名，且曰「夫子名聞列國，蓋子貢後先之」。噫！淺之乎窺聖賢矣。
義者宜也尊賢爲大
徐兆魁
同考試官敎諭蔣 批 講宜字爲大字有體認…
translation_en:
…comprehends their underlying causes; being thus comprehensive, he is able to fathom the subtleties of myriad changes, and when entrusted with governance, he naturally applies measures appropriately to the occasion. Entering court to deliberate on institutions, he weighs what is proper or improper to offer up to his lord, so that the lord's insight is never troubled by falling short; though the myriad transformations be intricately intertwined, if one manages them through his comprehensive understanding, problems are resolved at the first opportunity, with ample room to spare. Going out to issue commands, he weighs relative importance in delivering them to the people, so that the people's true and false conditions are not hard to discern; though routine affairs be tangled and numerous, if one tightens or relaxes them through his seasoned understanding, he grasps by analogy and penetrates all, with vast room to maneuver. A man like Ci, when kept hidden away like jade in a case, is indeed a vessel fit for practical use; when recognized and employed, he is the choice for a Grand Master. If he is used to engage in governance, what difficulty could there be! Alas! In this we see the abundance of talent within the Sage's gate, and how thoroughly the Master knew Ci. Yet on another day, when Ci became magistrate of Xinyang, the Master advised him, saying, "Be diligent, be cautious"; and in discussing governance, he further regarded advancing the worthy as true worthiness—could it be that "comprehension" alone is insufficient to exhaust the art of governance? For comprehension is talent; those three precepts are the means to perfect that talent. Had the Master gained a state or noble house, with Zigong following him, peace would have been secured and transformation accomplished—Lu would surely have become an Eastern Zhou! Alas that the world did not recognize them, leaving Zigong to be famed merely for his eloquence, with people even saying, "That the Master's name was heard throughout the feudatory states was because Zigong attended him before and behind." Ah! How shallowly do they peer into the Sage and the worthies!

"Righteousness means appropriateness; honoring the worthy is its greatest part."
Xu Zhaokui 徐兆魁
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: The exposition of the words "appropriateness" and "is the greatest part" shows personal realization…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君子之與人異者異以心之所存者焉夫仁禮
人之同心也惟君子存之此其所以異於人與
孟子欲人善事其心也故曰心之於人大矣一
存亡之間人品之所由判也善觀君子者辨諸
此而已彼君子雖與人竝生於天下而能爲天
下立極焉共處於一世而能爲後世垂範焉若
是其異於人者豈其有所立異哉亦惟同此心
也而所以事其心者獨善是以同是人也而所
以立此身者獨異矣存心維何曰以仁也以禮
===
也天地好生之德人得之爲仁人而不仁無以
宅此心矣君子一心之所渾涵者惟在於元善
之懿焉任之也重道之也遠日孜孜焉體而全
之以至於中心安仁斯已矣天下後世所以覆
育於君子者非以此仁也哉天地秩敘之良人
得之爲禮人而無禮無以制此心矣君子一心
之所凝聚者惟在於亨嘉之會焉主之也敬持
之也莊日兢兢焉會而通之以至於中心至正
斯已矣天下後世所以範圍於君子者非以此
punctuated: 君子之與人異者，異以心之所存者焉。夫仁禮，人之同心也；惟君子存之，此其所以異於人與！孟子欲人善事其心也，故曰：心之於人大矣，一存亡之間，人品之所由判也。善觀君子者，辨諸此而已。彼君子雖與人竝生於天下，而能爲天下立極焉；共處於一世，而能爲後世垂範焉。若是其異於人者，豈其有所立異哉？亦惟同此心也，而所以事其心者獨善；是以同是人也，而所以立此身者獨異矣。存心維何？曰：以仁也，以禮也。天地好生之德，人得之爲仁；人而不仁，無以宅此心矣。君子一心之所渾涵者，惟在於元善之懿焉。任之也重，道之也遠，日孜孜焉體而全之，以至於中心安仁斯已矣。天下後世所以覆育於君子者，非以此仁也哉！天地秩敘之良，人得之爲禮；人而無禮，無以制此心矣。君子一心之所凝聚者，惟在於亨嘉之會焉。主之也敬，持之也莊，日兢兢焉會而通之，以至於中心至正斯已矣。天下後世所以範圍於君子者，非以此
translation_en:
The way in which the superior man differs from other men lies in what he preserves in his mind. Now benevolence and propriety are the mind shared by all people; yet only the superior man preserves them—is this not why he differs from other men?

Mencius wished for people to serve their minds well, and thus he said: The mind is of great importance to a person; in the single distinction between preserving it and losing it lies the division of human character. Those who are adept at observing the superior man simply discern it in this. Although that superior man is born into the world alongside other men, he is able to establish the supreme standard for the world; although he lives together with them in the same age, he is able to hand down a model for later generations. In differing so greatly from other men, is he deliberately seeking to set himself apart? It is only that while sharing this same mind, the way he serves his mind is uniquely good; therefore, while being the same in humanity, the way he establishes his person is uniquely different.

What is it that he preserves in his mind? It is said: By means of benevolence, and by means of propriety. The virtue of Heaven and Earth in loving life is obtained by man as benevolence; if a man is not benevolent, he has no way to give residence to this mind. That which the single mind of the superior man encompasses and nurtures lies solely in the excellence of primordial goodness. His burden is heavy and his way is distant; day by day he diligently embodies and perfects it, stopping only when he rests peacefully in benevolence at the center of his heart. Is not the reason the world and later generations are sheltered and nourished by the superior man because of this benevolence?

The innate goodness of Heaven and Earth in orderly arrangement is obtained by man as propriety; if a man lacks propriety, he has no way to regulate this mind. That which the single mind of the superior man condenses and gathers lies solely in the convergence of flourishing excellence. He presides over it with reverence and maintains it with gravity; day by day he cautiously comprehends and carries it through, stopping only when he reaches the utmost rectitude at the center of his heart. Is not the reason the world and later generations are molded and bounded by the superior man because of this…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮也哉吁君子之所以異於人者以此然則欲
爲君子舍事心何以哉抑君子之存心非固以
求異於人也求無愧於心求不怍於人而已惟
求無愧於心故心學日純惟求不怍於人故人
道益全古好生溫恭之聖法天下傳後世者用
此道也雖然吾心有真舜也存之如□□舜而
已矣
易
九五觀我生君子无咎象曰觀我生觀民
===
也
徐兆魁
同考試官教諭蔣批格調整雅辭理醇粹發
明中正爲觀之道可謂詳盡錄之□□□□
考試官教諭楊批平實莊重且於自觀觀
民處交互得體
考試官教諭朱批典雅
二聖交發五爻之義而爲觀之道備矣夫觀道
以中正示人者也考諸身而徵諸民觀道其備
punctuated:
禮也哉！吁，君子之所以異於人者以此。然則欲爲君子，舍事心何以哉？抑君子之存心，非固以求異於人也，求無愧於心，求不怍於人而已。惟求無愧於心，故心學日純；惟求不怍於人，故人道益全。古好生溫恭之聖，法天下、傳後世者，用此道也。雖然，吾心有真舜也，存之如□□舜而已矣。

易

九五，觀我生，君子无咎。象曰：「觀我生，觀民也。」

徐兆魁

同考試官教諭蔣批：格調整雅，辭理醇粹，發明中正爲觀之道，可謂詳盡。錄之□□□□。
考試官教諭楊批：平實莊重，且於自觀、觀民處，交互得體。
考試官教諭朱批：典雅。

二聖交發五爻之義，而爲觀之道備矣。夫觀道，以中正示人者也，考諸身而徵諸民，觀道其備
translation_en:
…ritual propriety! Ah, it is by this that the gentleman differs from other men. This being so, if one wishes to be a gentleman, how could one do so if one sets aside the service of the mind? Yet the gentleman's preservation of his mind is not done stubbornly in order to seek to differ from other men; he seeks only to have no shame in his mind and no embarrassment before other men. Because he seeks only to have no shame in his mind, the learning of his mind becomes daily more pure; because he seeks only to have no embarrassment before other men, the human way becomes ever more complete. The ancient sage who loved life and was gentle and reverent—by whom he served as a model for the world and transmitted his example to posterity—employed this very Way. Even so, within our own minds there is a true Shun; to preserve it in the manner of […][?] is to be Shun, and nothing more.

Classic of Changes (Yi)

"Nine in the fifth place: Contemplating my own life, the gentleman is without blame. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating my own life means contemplating the people.'"

Xu Zhaokui 徐兆魁

Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: The structure and tone are neat and refined, and the diction and reasoning are pure and unadulterated. Its elucidation of centrality and correctness as the Way of Contemplation (Guan) may be called exhaustive. Selected to be recorded […][?].
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: Plain, substantial, and dignified; moreover, where it treats contemplating oneself and contemplating the people, the interplay is well-proportioned.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Classically elegant.

The two sages jointly elucidated the meaning of the fifth line, and thus the Way of serving as a model for contemplation is complete. Now, the Way of Contemplation is that by which one displays centrality and correctness to others. By examining it in one's own person and verifying it among the people, is not the Way of Contemplation complete…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣乎且民之視效在君君之明徵在民不可不
合而觀之也九五以陽居尊四陰仰之誠爲觀
之主矣周公有見於自觀之道也故發其占曰
觀我生君子无咎意以君子之道本諸身身有
未善則加諸民者可知矣是必獨觀萬化之原
而考道期歸於無失內省百爲之主而視履務
協於其旋觀我之中即君子之建中與斯履帝
位而不疚也觀我之正即君子之表正與斯萃
有位而乃光也所謂有孚顒若立大觀之極者
===
此矣然則爲觀者可徒求之民哉夫子有見於
觀民之義也故申其象曰觀我生觀民也意以
君子之道徵諸民民有弗善則出乎身者可知
矣是必察民俗之淳漓以驗吾政之得失稽民
風之厚薄以徵吾治之隆汙民心罔中惟爾之
中而觀民以考其中者不容後也民心罔正惟
爾之正而觀民以考其正者不可忽也所謂省
方設敎成下觀之化者此矣然則爲觀者可徒
信諸己哉吁惟觀己也則敷政於民者益善惟
punctuated: 矣乎？且民之視效在君，君之明徵在民，不可不合而觀之也。九五以陽居尊，四陰仰之，誠爲觀之主矣。周公有見於自觀之道也，故發其占曰：「觀我生，君子无咎。」意以君子之道本諸身，身有未善，則加諸民者可知矣。是必獨觀萬化之原，而考道期歸於無失；內省百爲之主，而視履務協於其旋。觀我之中，即君子之建中與？斯履帝位而不疚也；觀我之正，即君子之表正與？斯萃有位而乃光也。所謂「有孚顒若」，立大觀之極者，此矣。然則爲觀者，可徒求之民哉？夫子有見於觀民之義也，故申其象曰：「觀我生，觀民也。」意以君子之道徵諸民，民有弗善，則出乎身者可知矣。是必察民俗之淳漓，以驗吾政之得失；稽民風之厚薄，以徵吾治之隆汙。「民心罔中，惟爾之中」，而觀民以考其中者，不容後也；「民心罔正，惟爾之正」，而觀民以考其正者，不可忽也。所謂「省方設敎」，成下觀之化者，此矣。然則爲觀者，可徒信諸己哉？吁！惟觀己也，則敷政於民者益善；惟
translation_en:
…complete? Moreover, what the people look to and emulate lies in the ruler, while the clear verification of the ruler lies in the people; one cannot fail to combine and examine them together.

The Nine in the Fifth Place, as a yang line occupying the position of honor, is looked up to by the four yin lines below; truly it is the lord of the Guan [Contemplation] hexagram. The Duke of Zhou perceived the Way of self-examination, and thus set forth the prognostication, saying: "Contemplating my own life, the superior man is without blame." His meaning is that the Way of the superior man is rooted in his own person; if there is anything less than good in his person, then how it affects the people can be known. Therefore, he must privately examine the source of the myriad transformations, and in scrutinizing the Way, aim to return to faultlessness; he must inwardly reflect upon the master of the hundred actions, and in examining his conduct, strive to harmonize with its consummate cycle. To contemplate my own centrality—is this not the superior man's establishing of the central standard? Thus he occupies the imperial throne without regret. To contemplate my own rectitude—is this not the superior man's displaying of rectitude as a model? Thus he gathers the allegiance of those in high position and shines forth gloriously. What the hexagram statement calls "possessing sincerity and an august bearing," thereby establishing the ultimate standard for great contemplation, is precisely this. If this is so, how could one who serves as the model for contemplation merely seek it in the people?

The Master [Confucius] perceived the principle of contemplating the people, and thus elaborated on its Image, saying: "'Contemplating my own life' means contemplating the people." His meaning is that the Way of the superior man is verified in the people; if there is anything not good among the people, then what has issued from his own person can be known. Therefore, he must observe whether the people's customs are pure or decadent in order to test the successes and failures of his governance; he must investigate whether the people's mores are generous or mean in order to verify the flourishing or decline of his rule. "The minds of the people have no attainment of the mean, save as you attain the mean"—thus contemplating the people in order to examine one's own centrality cannot be put last. "The minds of the people have no attainment of rectitude, save as you attain rectitude"—thus contemplating the people in order to examine one's own rectitude cannot be neglected. What the Image commentary calls "inspecting the regions and establishing instruction," thereby accomplishing the transformation of those below who look up in contemplation, is precisely this. If this is so, how could one who serves as the model for contemplation merely trust in himself alone?

Ah! Only by contemplating oneself does the administration spread among the people become ever better; only by…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
觀民也則考德於已者益詳二聖交發其義觀
道無餘蘊矣考之唐虞君臣相與飭戒惟是幾
安而清問下民咨詢岳牧其心曷嘗一日忘耶
敬忽之際誠天命人心之所關也而禹猶曰寡
人之民各自以其心爲心噫何其詳且切耶吾
固曰堯舜之安民也大而禹之慮民也深
□□□以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
□□□立人之道曰仁與義
楊文俊
===
同考試官教諭陳批〔此題作者恠拘於格則歉於理惟是作兼得之可式〕
考試官教諭楊批〔說理精到處人不可及〕
考試官教諭朱批〔詞意俱足〕
觀三才之所以立而性命之理昭矣蓋性命一
理也具於三才者雖異其名孰非是理之貫哉
大傳言此以見易之大也意以易之爲書也功
用固無所不周精蘊亦無所不備是故聖人作
易固以順性命之理矣而性命之理果安在哉
punctuated:
觀民也，則考德於已者益詳。二聖交發其義，觀道無餘蘊矣。考之唐虞，君臣相與飭戒，惟是幾安，而清問下民，咨詢岳牧，其心曷嘗一日忘耶？敬忽之際，誠天命人心之所關也。而禹猶曰：「寡人之民，各自以其心爲心。」噫，何其詳且切耶！吾固曰：「堯、舜之安民也大，而禹之慮民也深。」

□□□以立天之道，曰陰與陽；立地之道，曰柔□□□；立人之道，曰仁與義。
楊文俊
同考試官教諭陳批：〔此題作者，恠拘於格則歉於理，惟是作兼得之，可式。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔說理精到處，人不可及。〕
考試官教諭朱批：〔詞意俱足。〕

觀三才之所以立，而性命之理昭矣。蓋性命一理也，具於三才者雖異其名，孰非是理之貫哉？《大傳》言此，以見《易》之大也。意以《易》之爲書也，功用固無所不周，精蘊亦無所不備。是故聖人作《易》，固以順性命之理矣；而性命之理，果安在哉？
translation_en:
… observing the people, one's examination of the virtue within oneself becomes all the more thorough. The two sages mutually brought forth this meaning, leaving no remaining subtleties in the Way of Observation (Guan). Examining the era of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], ruler and ministers mutually admonished and cautioned one another solely over the subtle springs of peace, yet in clearly inquiring of the lower people and consulting the Four Peaks and Twelve Pastors, how could their minds ever forget the people for a single day? The boundary between reverence and negligence is truly where the Mandate of Heaven and the hearts of the people are at stake. And Yu still said, "The people of my humble self each take their own mind as their mind." Ah, how thorough and earnest this is! I therefore say: "Yao and Shun's giving peace to the people was great, and Yu's concern for the people was deep."

"[In former times the sages made the Changes; they…]" [□□□] to establish the Way of Heaven, called Yin and Yang; to establish the Way of Earth, called the soft [and the firm] [□□□]; and to establish the Way of Man, called benevolence and righteousness.

Yang Wenjun

Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: [Writers on this topic strangely enough fall short in principle when constrained by formal structure; only this composition attains both and can serve as a model.]
Examiner and Instructor Yang's comment: [Where the explanation of principle is precise and thorough, others cannot match it.]
Examiner and Instructor Zhu's comment: [Both the diction and the meaning are fully sufficient.]

Observe that by which the Three Powers are established, and the principle of human nature and the decree of Heaven becomes manifest. For nature and the decree are a single principle; although what is endowed in the Three Powers differs in name, which of them is not penetrated by this principle? The Great Treatise (Dazhuan) speaks of this in order to show the greatness of the Changes (Yi). The meaning is that, as a book, the Changes has functions that are indeed all-encompassing and a subtle essence that is also completely provided. Therefore, when the sages made the Changes, it was indeed to accord with the principle of nature and the decree; yet where, after all, does the principle of nature and the decree reside? …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蓋天位乎上地位乎下人位乎中非徒有散殊
布列者以昭可見之迹亦必有幾微易簡者以
立無極之真故以言乎立天之道則曰陰與陽
其靜也專其動也直一陰一陽以兩而運而確
然者由之不毀矣言乎立地之道則曰柔與剛
其靜也翕其動也闢一剛一柔以兩而化而隤
然者由之不變矣言乎立人之道則曰仁與義
蓋人得天地之氣以成形亦得天地之理以成
性藹然而爲和厚毅然而爲嚴凝一仁一義以
===
兩而施而混然中處者與天地合德矣觀其對
待之體則陰陽異氣也剛柔異質也仁義異德
也三才各以兩而相配分之一定而不移也察
其流行之機則陰陽互根也剛柔交錯也仁義
並用也兩者各相濟以成能理之循環而無端
也性命之理備于三才者如此易皆有以順之
其妙爲何如哉抑性命一也特隨在而異名耳
蓋太極者本然之妙動靜者所乘之機其動也
則爲陽爲剛爲仁其靜也則爲陰爲柔爲義要
punctuated: 蓋天位乎上，地位乎下，人位乎中，非徒有散殊布列者以昭可見之迹，亦必有幾微易簡者以立無極之真。故以言乎立天之道，則曰陰與陽。其靜也專，其動也直，一陰一陽以兩而運，而確然者由之不毀矣。言乎立地之道，則曰柔與剛。其靜也翕，其動也闢，一剛一柔以兩而化，而隤然者由之不變矣。言乎立人之道，則曰仁與義。蓋人得天地之氣以成形，亦得天地之理以成性，藹然而爲和厚，毅然而爲嚴凝，一仁一義以兩而施，而混然中處者與天地合德矣。觀其對待之體，則陰陽異氣也，剛柔異質也，仁義異德也，三才各以兩而相配，分之一定而不移也。察其流行之機，則陰陽互根也，剛柔交錯也，仁義並用也，兩者各相濟以成能，理之循環而無端也。性命之理備于三才者如此，易皆有以順之，其妙爲何如哉！抑性命一也，特隨在而異名耳。蓋太極者，本然之妙；動靜者，所乘之機。其動也，則爲陽、爲剛、爲仁；其靜也，則爲陰、爲柔、爲義，要
translation_en: For Heaven is positioned above, Earth is positioned below, and Man is positioned in the middle; not only are there dispersed and differentiated forms arrayed to manifest visible traces, there must also be subtle, easy, and simple principles to establish the reality of the Non-Ultimate (wuji). Therefore, speaking of the Way that establishes Heaven, it is called yin and yang. In its stillness it is focused; in its movement it is straight. Alternately yin and yang, operating as a pair, that which is firm and sure thereby never perishes. Speaking of the Way that establishes Earth, it is called the soft and the hard. In its stillness it is closed; in its movement it is opened. Alternately hard and soft, transforming as a pair, that which is docile and yielding thereby never alters. Speaking of the Way that establishes Man, it is called benevolence and righteousness. For Man receives the vital force (qi) of Heaven and Earth to form his physical body, and also receives the principle (li) of Heaven and Earth to form his nature—amiably becoming gentle and generous, resolutely becoming stern and composed. Alternately benevolence and righteousness, enacted as a pair, he who dwells integrally in the center unites in virtue with Heaven and Earth. Observing their substance in opposition: yin and yang differ in vital force, the hard and the soft differ in material constitution, and benevolence and righteousness differ in virtue; the Three Powers (sancai) each pair up by twos, their divisions fixed and unshifting. Examining the mechanism of their flowing operation: yin and yang are rooted in each other, the hard and the soft interweave, and benevolence and righteousness are employed together; each pair complements the other to accomplish its function, the cycle of principle having no end. Such is the way the principle of human nature and destiny is complete in the Three Powers, and the Changes (Yi) is able to accord with it all—how marvelous it is! Moreover, human nature and destiny are one; they merely take different names according to where they reside. For the Supreme Ultimate (taiji) is the inherent marvel, and movement and stillness are the mechanisms upon which it rides. In its movement, it becomes yang, the hard, and benevolence; in its stillness, it becomes yin, the soft, and righteousness. In sum, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之根柢於太極者也故曰易有太極是生兩儀
學者能定之以仁義而主靜則太極在吾心而
三才之道一以貫之矣
書
念終始典于學厥德脩罔覺
馮名望
同考試官教諭黃批〔辭鬯意懇深得經旨〕
考試官教諭易批〔理明事備義盡而詞密主意之旨宜式多士〕
===
考試官教諭朱批〔典雅精融陳忠顯著〕
大臣告君之務學由純心而進于化焉夫德脩
罔覺化不可知矣然必由一念之純致之明君
可不以務學爲急乎宜傅說以是迪高宗也其
意以爲帝王之治本于道帝王之學純于心是
故自學斆人學之始終備矣王可一念之或怠
耶殆必會體用以兼脩而遜志純于罔間合内
外以並進而時敏勵于有常恭默思道始固此
punctuated:
之，根柢於太極者也。故曰：「《易》有太極，是生兩儀。」學者能定之以仁義而主靜，則太極在吾心，而三才之道一以貫之矣。

《書》
念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。
馮名望
同考試官教諭黃批：〔辭鬯意懇，深得經旨。〕
考試官教諭易批：〔理明事備，義盡而詞密，主意之旨，宜式多士。〕
考試官教諭朱批：〔典雅精融，陳忠顯著。〕

大臣告君之務學，由純心而進于化焉。夫德脩罔覺，化不可知矣；然必由一念之純致之，明君可不以務學爲急乎？宜傅說以是迪高宗也。其意以爲：帝王之治本于道，帝王之學純于心。是故自學、斆人，學之始終備矣，王可一念之或怠耶？殆必會體用以兼脩，而遜志純于罔間；合内外以並進，而時敏勵于有常。恭默思道，始固此
translation_en:
… in sum, they are all rooted in the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji). Therefore it is said: "In the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate, which generates the Two Modes." If the student can settle himself with humanity and righteousness while making tranquility fundamental, then the Supreme Ultimate will reside within his own mind, and a single thread will bind together the Way of the Three Powers.

Book of Documents (Shu)
"Keep your thoughts from beginning to end constantly on learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being conscious of it."
Feng Mingwang 馮名望
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang: 〔The expression is fluent and the meaning sincere, deeply grasping the purport of the Classic.〕
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yi: 〔The principles are clear and the facts complete; the meaning is thorough and the phrasing tight. On the main theme of the passage, it is fit to serve as a model for the many scholars.〕
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu: 〔Classic in grace and finely integrated, setting forth loyalty with manifest brilliance.〕

When the great minister counsels his sovereign on devoting himself to learning, he shows how one proceeds from a pure mind to transformation. Now, when virtue is cultivated without one's being conscious of it, the transformation goes beyond awareness; yet it must be brought about through the purity of a single thought—how then could an enlightened ruler not regard devotion to learning as an urgent priority? Rightly did Fu Yue 傅說 use this to guide Emperor Gaozong 高宗! His meaning was as follows: The governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and the learning of emperors and kings finds its purity in the mind. Therefore, in learning for oneself and in teaching others, the beginning and end of learning are complete—how could the King allow even a single thought to grow lax? He must surely unite substance and function so as to cultivate both together, keeping a humble will pure without interruption; and combine the internal and the external so as to advance in both side by side, spurring himself to timely diligence with constancy. When in reverent silence he pondered the Way, at the beginning it was assuredly this…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
念也推之以至于承式百官其惺惺而不昧者
猶夫初也寤寐思治始固此心也推之以至于
作則萬邦其孳孳而不忘者未嘗替也由是操
存愈專則進脩愈妙而幾非在我念慮益精則
充養益融而化不可爲始之脩而來也猶可知
也兹則體用爲之無方而來者愈來不知其所
以來焉承式之具其冥會於此矣尚何罔顯之
慮于已哉始之來而積也猶有意也兹則內外
爲之合德而積者日積不知其所以積焉作則
===
之原其默運于是矣又何多聞之求諸人哉至
是則學古之功爲益密有獲之效爲已盡矣使
不自純其念而徒望諸人亦安能以有得耶抑
是道也即堯舜之允執成湯之日新而帝王授
受心法也高宗可謂知學矣而傅說猶惓惓及
此蓋以聖帝明王心學之純望之者不可以覩
明良相遇之盛乎然以中興之主而厥後猶有
祖巳之訓焉則人主之心安可以終始易慮哉
punctuated: 念也，推之以至于承式百官，其惺惺而不昧者，猶夫初也；寤寐思治，始固此心也，推之以至于作則萬邦，其孳孳而不忘者，未嘗替也。由是操存愈專，則進脩愈妙，而幾非在我；念慮益精，則充養益融，而化不可爲。始之脩而來也，猶可知也，兹則體用爲之無方，而來者愈來，不知其所以來焉，承式之具，其冥會於此矣，尚何罔顯之慮于已哉？始之來而積也，猶有意也，兹則內外爲之合德，而積者日積，不知其所以積焉，作則之原，其默運于是矣，又何多聞之求諸人哉？至是，則學古之功爲益密，有獲之效爲已盡矣。使不自純其念，而徒望諸人，亦安能以有得耶？抑是道也，即堯、舜之「允執」，成湯之「日新」，而帝王授受心法也。高宗可謂知學矣，而傅說猶惓惓及此，蓋以聖帝明王心學之純望之者，不可以覩明良相遇之盛乎？然以中興之主，而厥後猶有祖巳之訓焉，則人主之心，安可以終始易慮哉！
translation_en: …thought; and when he extends it to the point where the hundred officials receive their model from him, what remains alert and unclouded in him is still just as it was at the start. Reflecting on good governance waking and sleeping was indeed this mind at the start; and when he extends it to the point of serving as the standard for the myriad states, what remains diligent and unforgetful in him has never flagged. Thus, the more focused his preservation of mind, the more marvelous his advancement and cultivation, until the subtle springs of action are beyond mere conscious effort; the more refined his thoughts and reflections, the more harmonious his full nourishment of virtue, until transformation occurs beyond deliberate making. At the beginning, when cultivation brought results, it could still be consciously known; now, however, substance and function operate without fixed bounds, and what comes continues to come without his knowing how it comes. The wherewithal to serve as a model for the officials is tacitly united herein—what anxiety could there still be that his virtue might not be manifest in himself? At the beginning, when results came and accumulated, there was still deliberate intention; now, however, inner and outer unite in virtue, and what accumulates does so day by day without his knowing how it accumulates. The source of serving as a standard for the states operates silently herein—what need is there anymore to seek wide learning from others? At this point, the work of studying antiquity becomes ever more thorough, and the efficacy of attainment is completely realized. If he did not purify his own thoughts from beginning to end and merely looked to others, how could he ever attain anything? Moreover, this Way is none other than the "sincerely holding fast" of Yao and Shun, and the "daily renewal" of Cheng Tang—the method of the mind transmitted from one sovereign to another. Gaozong may well be said to have understood learning, yet Fu Yue still earnestly spoke to him of this; was it not because he hoped to see in him the pure learning of the mind of the sage emperors and enlightened kings, and may we not behold in this the flourishing of a meeting between an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister? Yet even for a ruler of dynastic revival, there was afterward still the admonition of Zu Ji; how then can a sovereign's mind ever alter its concern between beginning and end!

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
李樹聲
同考試官教諭羅批精醇古雅宛然董正治
官氣象經義之佳者
考試官教諭楊批聯□痛貫最為得體
考試官教諭朱批詞整理到
賢王總命大臣惟欲其率下以治民焉蓋設官
分職以為民也率內以倡外而治可致矣寧非
大臣之當務哉成王訓官至此以為朝廷立四
===
方之極綱紀為萬化之原冢宰而下六卿各有
攸司矣然豈徒自盡其職已哉蓋天生兆民使
司牧之內而卿士又外牧之表也顧其率而倡
之者非爾六卿責乎是必正色以率下於以懋
敦乎倡導之原端已以作先於以共起夫精明
之治佐理于一人之下而垂範于百寮之間將
使外而牧伯皆知朝廷意向所在而承流以宣
厥化者旁敷於不窮也輔理于朝著之內而儀
刑于寮屬之上將使外而州長皆知廟廊德意
punctuated:
六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。
李樹聲
同考試官教諭羅批：精醇古雅，宛然董正治官氣象，經義之佳者。
考試官教諭楊批：聯□痛貫，最為得體。
考試官教諭朱批：詞整理到。
賢王總命大臣，惟欲其率下以治民焉。蓋設官分職以為民也，率內以倡外而治可致矣，寧非大臣之當務哉？成王訓官至此，以為朝廷立四方之極，綱紀為萬化之原，冢宰而下，六卿各有攸司矣。然豈徒自盡其職已哉？蓋天生兆民，使司牧之，內而卿士，又外牧之表也。顧其率而倡之者，非爾六卿責乎？是必正色以率下，於以懋敦乎倡導之原；端已以作先，於以共起夫精明之治。佐理于一人之下，而垂範于百寮之間，將使外而牧伯皆知朝廷意向所在，而承流以宣厥化者，旁敷於不窮也；輔理于朝著之內，而儀刑于寮屬之上，將使外而州長皆知廟廊德意…
translation_en:
"The six Ministers have their divided duties. Let each lead his own subordinates to set an example for the pastors of the nine provinces, and thus richly perfect the myriad people."

Li Shusheng 李樹聲

Associate Examiner, Instructor Luo 羅 comments: Refined, pure, antique, and elegant; it vividly captures the spirit of supervising and rectifying the governing officials—a fine piece of Classics exposition.
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊 comments: Joined [?] and thoroughly coherent; most fitting in style.
Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: The diction is well-ordered and the reasoning reaches its mark.

When the worthy king gives a general charge to his great ministers, he desires only that they lead their subordinates in order to govern the people. For establishing offices and dividing duties is done for the sake of the people; by leading those inside the court to set an example for those outside in the provinces, good governance can be achieved. Is this not the urgent duty of great ministers?

When King Cheng 成王 reached this point in instructing his officials, he considered that the royal court establishes the standard for the four quarters, and that institutional order is the source of myriad transformations. From the Prime Minister down, the six Ministers each had their respective responsibilities. Yet how could they merely fulfill their own personal duties and nothing more? For Heaven gives birth to the myriad people and appoints officials to shepherd them, while inside the court the ministerial officers serve in turn as models for the provincial pastors outside. Now then, to lead and set an example for them—is this not the responsibility of you six Ministers?

Therefore, you must maintain a solemn countenance in leading those below, thereby earnestly cultivating the source of leadership and guidance; you must rectify yourselves to take the lead, thereby jointly rousing a clear and discerning governance. Assisting in administration beneath the One Man, and setting a standard among the hundred officials, you will cause the regional pastors and lords outside to all know where the court's intentions lie, so that those who receive the current and proclaim its transforming influence will spread it far and wide without end. Aiding governance within the court ranks, and serving as a model above your subordinate colleagues, you will cause the provincial governors outside to all know where the virtuous intentions of the temple and court…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所存而行令以致之民者四達而不悖也內與
外以勤恤而膏澤神于下究樂其樂焉利其利
焉熈熈乎阜厚之俗自畿甸以及侯服者廓如
矣所謂制治于未亂者非以是耶中與外以合
德而紀法因之丕著道德一焉風俗同焉皥皥
乎化成之休由都會以及四海者沛如矣所謂
保邦于未危者其在兹耶是雖阜成之職在諸
臣有同心而統率之權則六卿有專責矣果能
此道而國家建官之意其無負矣哉雖然此周
===
官之法度也推原其本又係于人君之一心蓋
君心一正則卿相皆正人而內之寮屬外之牧
伯各以彙進而兆民竝受其福唐虞之朝師師
濟濟卒致惟和咸寧之風者豈徒以其建官哉
故謂君心爲萬化之原信矣
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
鄭偉
同考試官教諭陳批〔周民愛君之情發揮明〕
punctuated:
所存，而行令以致之民者，四達而不悖也。內與外以勤恤，而膏澤神于下究，樂其樂焉，利其利焉，熈熈乎阜厚之俗，自畿甸以及侯服者，廓如矣。所謂制治于未亂者，非以是耶？中與外以合德，而紀法因之丕著，道德一焉，風俗同焉，皥皥乎化成之休，由都會以及四海者，沛如矣。所謂保邦于未危者，其在兹耶？是雖阜成之職，在諸臣有同心，而統率之權，則六卿有專責矣。果能此道，而國家建官之意，其無負矣哉！雖然，此周官之法度也，推原其本，又係于人君之一心。蓋君心一正，則卿相皆正人，而內之寮屬、外之牧伯，各以彙進，而兆民竝受其福。唐虞之朝，師師濟濟，卒致惟和咸寧之風者，豈徒以其建官哉？故謂君心爲萬化之原，信矣。

詩
「有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁，雨我公田，遂及我私。」
鄭偉
同考試官教諭陳批：〔周民愛君之情，發揮明〕
translation_en:
…resides, and their execution of orders to deliver this to the people will reach everywhere without hindrance. When inner and outer officials join in diligent compassion, the nourishing grace will miraculously penetrate down to the lowest levels; the people will rejoice in what brings them joy and profit from what brings them profit, and a harmonious, prosperous, and generous ethos will expand broadly from the royal domain out to the feudatory zones. Is this not what is meant by "securing order before disorder arises"? When the court and the provinces unite in virtue, laws and discipline are thereby grandly manifested; morality is unified and customs are made uniform, and the placid, contented blessings of transformative completion flow abundantly from the capital out to the Four Seas. Does not what is meant by "preserving the state before peril arises" lie right here? Thus, although all the officials share a single heart in the duty of bringing about abundance and completion, the Six Ministers bear the special responsibility for the authority to lead and direct them. If they can truly carry out this Way, the state's intention in establishing offices will surely not be betrayed! Even so, this is the institutional system of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan); if we trace it back to its root, it further depends upon the single mind of the ruler. For once the ruler's mind is rectified, the ministers and chancellors will all be upright men; the subordinate officials within and the regional pastors and leaders without will each advance according to their kind, and the millions of people will together receive their blessings. In the courts of Tang and Yu, officials emulated one another in dignified array, ultimately bringing about an ethos of harmony and universal peace—was that merely because of their establishment of offices? Therefore, to say that the ruler's mind is the source of myriad transformations is truly credible.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"The clouds form in dense masses, and the rain falls gently and plentifully; may it rain first on our public fields, and then reach our private ones."
By Zheng Wei 鄭偉
Associate Examiner Instructor Chen comments: [The affection of the people of Zhou for their ruler is expounded clearly…]

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
透且詞復委婉是善說詩者
考試官敎諭楊批冲雅不羣
考試官敎諭朱批悠暢
周人致望於天澤而冀蒙君之餘休焉夫天澤
無分於公私也周人以是而致望於天其歸德
於君者至矣大田答君之詞若曰養民者君之
德生物者天之功苗生盛矣苗害除矣能無望
於天澤耶彼雲所以興雨非盛不足以致之安
得雲之作也萋萋其盛有以兆多雨之徵矣乎
===
雨所以潤物非徐不足以入土安得雨之興也
祁祁其徐有以極深入之漸矣乎雨也而雲以
先之雲也而雨以繼之是誠生物之一機而天
地之大德也然豈吾人之所敢必哉亦曰天之
所眷在德而君之格天有素有公田焉乃公家
之所需者天必鑒君德而雨之矣則凡我私田
皆其所同井者有不因君澤而及之乎由中達
外均被乎霑足之休是天雖無意於民不能無
意於君而降康於君亦以斂福於民矣足此通
punctuated:
透，且詞復委婉，是善說《詩》者。
考試官敎諭楊批：冲雅不羣。
考試官敎諭朱批：悠暢。

周人致望於天澤，而冀蒙君之餘休焉。夫天澤無分於公私也，周人以是而致望於天，其歸德於君者至矣。《大田》答君之詞若曰：養民者，君之德；生物者，天之功。苗生盛矣，苗害除矣，能無望於天澤耶？彼雲所以興雨，非盛不足以致之，安得雲之作也，萋萋其盛，有以兆多雨之徵矣乎？雨所以潤物，非徐不足以入土，安得雨之興也，祁祁其徐，有以極深入之漸矣乎？雨也而雲以先之，雲也而雨以繼之，是誠生物之一機，而天地之大德也。然豈吾人之所敢必哉？亦曰天之所眷在德，而君之格天有素。有公田焉，乃公家之所需者，天必鑒君德而雨之矣。則凡我私田，皆其所同井者，有不因君澤而及之乎？由中達外，均被乎霑足之休，是天雖無意於民，不能無意於君，而降康於君，亦以斂福於民矣；足此通
translation_en:
…and thorough, while its phrasing is moreover nuanced and tactful—this is someone skilled at expounding the Book of Odes (Shi).
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: Serene, refined, and extraordinary.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Unhurried and fluent.

The people of Zhou placed their hopes in the moisture of Heaven, wishing to receive the overflow of their sovereign's blessings. Now, the moisture of Heaven makes no distinction between public and private; yet the people of Zhou expressed their hopes to Heaven in these terms, which shows the utmost attribution of virtue to their sovereign. In the ode "Large Fields" (Datian), the words answering the sovereign seem to say: Nourishing the people is the virtue of the sovereign; generating things is the achievement of Heaven. Now that the sprouts are growing luxuriantly and the pests have been eliminated, how could we not hope for the moisture of Heaven? Since clouds are what bring forth rain, if they are not dense they cannot induce it—how might we have the rising clouds be so densely massed (qiqi) as to presage an abundance of rain? Since rain is what moistens things, if it is not gentle it cannot soak into the soil—how might we have the falling rain be so gently unhurried (qiqi) as to reach the utmost gradualness of deep penetration? There is rain, preceded by clouds; there are clouds, followed by rain—this is truly the vital mechanism of generating things and the great virtue of Heaven and Earth. Yet how could this be something we dare take for granted? We would simply say that what Heaven favors is virtue, and our sovereign has long since moved Heaven. There are the public fields, which supply the needs of the ruling house; Heaven will surely behold the sovereign's virtue and rain upon them. Then as for all our private fields, which share the same well-field system—how could the rain not extend to them by virtue of the sovereign's grace? Reaching from the center to the outer plots, all alike receive the blessing of a drenching sufficiency. This means that even if Heaven has no special regard for the people, it cannot lack regard for the sovereign; and in sending down prosperity upon the sovereign, it also gathers blessings for the people. Satisfying this and extending to…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
彼同獲乎優渥之慶是民雖無賴於天不能無
賴於君而公田旣足百姓與之俱足矣吁以其
所望於天者望君周人之所賴於君者何切以
其所德於天者德君周人之所感於君者亦何
至耶雖然農夫何以有是言哉蓋有周盛時務
農重穀聖天子倡之賢公卿和之爲之民者鼓
舞而歌詠之一時氣象宛然康衢擊壤遺意也
而猶惓惓於先後間如此吾固知盛世之民處
畝畝而不忘君也已
===
成王之孚下土之式永言孝思孝思維則
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭羅批作此題者於孚式二字
講多未融獨此篇能悉其旨而精暢古雅是邃養
之士
考試官敎諭楊批意周詞俊
考試官敎諭朱批清健
聖孝之法天下惟其純而已矣蓋孝道通於人
心者也武王以純孝感天下而民之則之也有
punctuated:
彼，同獲乎優渥之慶。是民雖無賴於天，不能無賴於君，而公田旣足，百姓與之俱足矣。吁！以其所望於天者望君，周人之所賴於君者何切！以其所德於天者德君，周人之所感於君者亦何至耶！雖然，農夫何以有是言哉？蓋有周盛時，務農重穀，聖天子倡之，賢公卿和之，爲之民者鼓舞而歌詠之，一時氣象，宛然康衢擊壤遺意也，而猶惓惓於先後間如此，吾固知盛世之民，處畝畝而不忘君也已。
「成王之孚，下土之式。永言孝思，孝思維則。」
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭羅批：作此題者，於「孚」「式」二字講多未融，獨此篇能悉其旨，而精暢古雅，是邃養之士。
考試官敎諭楊批：意周詞俊。
考試官敎諭朱批：清健。
聖孝之法天下，惟其純而已矣。蓋孝道，通於人心者也。武王以純孝感天下，而民之則之也，有
translation_en:
… that, sharing together in the blessing of abundant moisture. Thus, even if the people do not rely directly upon Heaven, they cannot but rely upon their ruler; and once the public fields are sufficiently provided for, the common people have sufficiency along with them. Ah! Looking to their ruler with the hopes they place in Heaven—how earnest was the people of Zhou's reliance upon their ruler! Crediting their ruler with the grace they owe to Heaven—how profound was the people of Zhou's gratitude toward their ruler! Even so, why did the farmers speak these words? It was because in the flourishing age of the Zhou, agriculture was promoted and grain was valued; the sage Son of Heaven led the way, the worthy dukes and ministers harmonized with him, and those who were their people were inspired to dance and sing of it. The spirit of that age truly recalled the ancient sentiment of singing in the thoroughfares and striking the clods in contentment. Yet even so, they remained so earnestly mindful of the order of precedence between public and private; from this I truly know that the people of a flourishing age, though dwelling among theirThe fields and acres, never forget their ruler.

"He achieved the confidence of a king, and became the model of the lower world. Forever he cherished filial thoughts, and his filial thoughts were the pattern."

Ju Pingchen 車聘臣

Associate Examiner and Instructor Luo 羅 comments: Those who wrote on this theme mostly failed to thoroughly integrate their explanations of the two words "confidence" (fu 孚) and "model" (shi 式). This essay alone was able to exhaust their meaning, while being refined, fluent, ancient, and elegant—he is a scholar of deep cultivation.

Examiner and Instructor Yang 楊 comments: The ideas are comprehensive and the phrasing is outstanding.

Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: Clear and vigorous.

That the sage's filial piety serves as a model for the world lies solely in its purity. For the way of filial piety is something that resonates through all human hearts. King Wu 武王 moved the world with his pure filial piety, and that the people took him as their pattern had…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以哉此美武王之詩也若曰傳之異世而相通
者道推之天下而皆準者心人惟孝心之未純
斯無以孚天下而使之則耳惟我武王人紀肇
脩天下不言而信丕式見德道化不肅而成世
德之求匪直彰信之廣而已是則是傚以近天
子之光而黎民之敏德翕如焉配命之永匪特
默成之孚而已是訓是彜以會惟皇之極而四
海之德教沛如焉此武王之為天下則也而何
以得此哉蓋由其持執競之思而三后之丕緒
===
篤厚之而不忘崇大化之本而哲王之心法祗
承之而罔間以永世德也以此始亦以此終亹
亹乎神明之通也而一孝之感觸天下之為父
子者定矣以永配命也暫如是久亦如是翼翼
乎孝心之純也而一德之孚格天下之為愛敬
者同矣下土之孚而則也豈偶然哉吁武王之
感人心如此觀其所感而配京之實可徵矣武
王其達孝矣乎雖然文王以服事殷夫子稱為
至德而謂武未盡善豈其求德永命尚有間然
punctuated: 以哉！此美武王之詩也。若曰：傳之異世而相通者，道；推之天下而皆準者，心。人惟孝心之未純，斯無以孚天下而使之則耳。惟我武王，人紀肇脩，天下不言而信；丕式見德，道化不肅而成。世德之求，匪直彰信之廣而已，是則是傚，以近天子之光，而黎民之敏德翕如焉；配命之永，匪特默成之孚而已，是訓是彜，以會惟皇之極，而四海之德教沛如焉。此武王之為天下則也。而何以得此哉？蓋由其持執競之思，而三后之丕緒篤厚之而不忘；崇大化之本，而哲王之心法祗承之而罔間。以永世德也，以此始，亦以此終，亹亹乎神明之通也，而一孝之感觸，天下之為父子者定矣；以永配命也，暫如是，久亦如是，翼翼乎孝心之純也，而一德之孚格，天下之為愛敬者同矣。下土之孚而則也，豈偶然哉！吁！武王之感人心如此，觀其所感，而配京之實可徵矣。武王其達孝矣乎！雖然，文王以服事殷，夫子稱為至德，而謂武未盡善，豈其求德永命，尚有間然
translation_en: … reason indeed! This is an ode praising King Wu. It is as if to say: What is transmitted across different eras and yet remains mutually connected is the Way; what is extended throughout the world and universally holds true is the mind. Only when a person's filial mind is not yet pure does he lack the means to inspire trust in the world and cause it to take him as a model. Only our King Wu initiated the cultivation of human bonds, so that the world trusted him without his speaking; he grandly modeled and manifested his virtue, so that his moral transformation was accomplished without severity. In his seeking the hereditary virtue, it was not merely a matter of broadly displaying trustworthiness; people took him as their model and imitated him in order to draw near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven, and the common people's diligence in virtue was harmonious. In his perpetually matching the Mandate, it was not merely a matter of the trust achieved through silent accomplishment; people took him as their instruction and constant norm in order to converge upon the supreme standard of the August One, and moral teaching within the four seas flowed abundantly. This is how King Wu served as the model for the world. And how did he attain this? It was because he maintained a resolute and vigorous mindfulness, enriching and never forgetting the great heritage of the Three Sovereigns; and he revered the foundation of great transformation,敬fully inheriting without interruption the method of the mind of the wise kings. In perpetually continuing the hereditary virtue, he began with this and also ended with this—how tireless was his communion with the spiritual intelligence! And moved by this single filial piety, all who were fathers and sons in the world were settled in their roles. In perpetually matching the Mandate, he was like this for a short time and also like this for a long time—how reverent was the purity of his filial mind! And reached by the trust of this single virtue, all who practiced love and respect in the world were united. Was it by mere chance that the lower earth trusted him and took him as a model? Alas! Such was the way King Wu moved the minds of men. Observing what he moved, the reality of his being a counterpart in the capital can be verified. Was not King Wu a man of far-reaching filial piety! Even so, because King Wen served the Yin dynasty, the Master praised him as having the utmost virtue, whereas he said of Wu that he was not yet盡善 (completely good). Could it be that in his seeking virtue and perpetually matching the Mandate, there was still some flaw…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
耶不知時未至則遵養時晦時用介則應天順
人武王亦何心哉心乎奉天而已然而非武王
意也尚論武王之世者當原其心
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳莊公十有五年
李至
同考試官教諭黃批春秋望霸之意此作獨
能發揮明悉而詞更謹嚴可錄為式
考試官教諭楊批詞氣剴切非徒作者
===
考試官教諭朱批明確
春秋紀兵而主大國所以望伯業之成也夫伯
業成則行乎諸侯矣此伐郳之役齊猶後宋聖
人屬望之意深哉且郳曷為而伐也為宋討也
夫伯者專征而先諸侯例也齊何為序宋下耶
曰伯業未成而望之也蓋以成大業者在乎得
天下之權而孚大衆者在乎得天下之心桓也
北杏創會非不足以昭賜履也而安攘未臻何
以號召乎列辟伐宋節兵非不足以紹𡨥征也
punctuated:
耶？不知時未至，則遵養時晦；時用介，則應天順人。武王亦何心哉？心乎奉天而已，然而非武王意也。尚論武王之世者，當原其心。

春秋

秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳莊公十有五年

李至

同考試官教諭黃批：春秋望霸之意，此作獨能發揮明悉，而詞更謹嚴，可錄為式。
考試官教諭楊批：詞氣剴切，非徒作者。
考試官教諭朱批：明確。

《春秋》紀兵而主大國，所以望伯業之成也。夫伯業成，則行乎諸侯矣。此伐郳之役，齊猶後宋，聖人屬望之意深哉！且郳曷為而伐也？為宋討也。夫伯者專征而先諸侯，例也，齊何為序宋下耶？曰：伯業未成而望之也。蓋以成大業者，在乎得天下之權；而孚大衆者，在乎得天下之心。桓也北杏創會，非不足以昭賜履也；而安攘未臻，何以號召乎列辟？伐宋節兵，非不足以紹𡨥征也；
translation_en:
… Could one not know that when the time has not yet arrived, one abides in obscurity and nourishes one's strength; and when the time brings great fortune, one responds to Heaven and accords with human hearts? What ulterior motive did King Wu have? His heart was set solely on obeying Heaven, and yet this was not King Wu's original wish. Those who evaluate the era of King Wu should examine the true intentions of his heart.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In autumn, people of Song, people of Qi, and people of Zhu invaded Ni." (15th year of Duke Zhuang)

By Li Zhi 李至

Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang comments: This composition alone is able to expound clearly and thoroughly the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in hoping for a hegemon, and its diction is even more rigorous and precise; it may be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: The diction and tone are incisive and to the point; he is no mere ordinary writer.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Clear and exact.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals records military expeditions and places a great state in the lead, it is to express the hope for the accomplishment of the hegemonic enterprise. Now, once the hegemonic enterprise is accomplished, one's authority prevails among the feudal lords. Yet in this campaign to invade Ni, Qi was still listed after Song—how profound was the Sage's expectation! Moreover, why was Ni invaded? It was a punitive expedition undertaken on behalf of Song. For a hegemon to assume sole authority over punitive expeditions and take precedence over the feudal lords is the established rule; why, then, was Qi ranked below Song? The answer is: the hegemonic enterprise was not yet accomplished, and the Sage was looking forward to its completion. For achieving a great enterprise lies in gaining the authority of the realm, and winning the trust of the multitude lies in gaining the hearts of the realm. Duke Huan's initiating the covenant at Beixing was not insufficient to manifest the territorial mandate bestowed upon his house; yet while peace within and defense against outsiders had not yet been achieved, wherewith could he rally the various rulers? His restraining the troops in the invasion of Song was not insufficient to carry on the privilege of exclusive punitive expeditions; …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之伊誰繇哉
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕
杜華秋
同考試官敎諭黃批構思精密命詞蒼古發
明桓仲念深處宛然
考試官敎諭楊批辭嚴意足深于經者
考試官敎諭朱批整雅
===
觀伯主之威信而制外之念深矣于以見威信
迭著齊伯之所以謀楚者何至也始事之勤不
有足尚者哉且楚肆暴橫以凌鄭而復挾江黃
以爲巳援其目中巳無齊矣惟時桓與仲之經
營巳非一日其能以忘情乎於是爲檉與陽穀
之會焉夫檉之會兵革不試曷言乎威之振蓋
威天下者在握天下之勢方楚氛之孔熾也使
無威以振之則北方之國未必協從齊也念攘
楚之要樞在鄭也乃就犖地以結盟而彌縫匡
punctuated:
之伊誰繇哉？

「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉」〔僖公元年〕；「秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀」〔僖公三年〕。
杜華秋
同考試官敎諭黃批：構思精密，命詞蒼古，發明桓、仲念深處宛然。
考試官敎諭楊批：辭嚴意足，深于經者。
考試官敎諭朱批：整雅。
觀伯主之威信，而制外之念深矣。于以見威信迭著，齊伯之所以謀楚者，何至也！始事之勤，不有足尚者哉？且楚肆暴橫以凌鄭，而復挾江、黃以爲巳援，其目中巳無齊矣。惟時桓與仲之經營巳非一日，其能以忘情乎？於是爲檉與陽穀之會焉。夫檉之會，兵革不試，曷言乎威之振？蓋威天下者在握天下之勢。方楚氛之孔熾也，使無威以振之，則北方之國未必協從。齊也，念攘楚之要樞在鄭也，乃就犖地以結盟，而彌縫匡
translation_en:
… upon whom else did this depend?

"In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of宋 (Song), the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a man of Zhu at Cheng" [first year of Duke Xi]; "In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a man of Jiang, and a man of Huang met at Yanggu" [third year of Duke Xi].
Du Huaqiu
Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang comments: The conception is precise and thorough, and the phrasing is vigorous and antique. It brings to life with vivid clarity the deep-seated concerns of Duke Huan and Guan Zhong.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: The diction is rigorous and the meaning fully realized; the work of one deeply versed in the Classic.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Well-ordered and refined.
When we observe the hegemon's awe-inspiring prestige and good faith, we see how deep was his resolve to hold external foes in check. Through this, we witness prestige and good faith manifested in turn—how thorough indeed were the designs of the Hegemon of Qi against Chu! Is not his diligence at the inception of the enterprise worthy of esteem? Moreover, Chu was unleashing its violent arrogance to bully Zheng, while also coercing Jiang and Huang to serve as its own allies; in its eyes, Qi no longer existed. At that time, Duke Huan and Guan Zhong had already been planning and laboring for more than a single day—how could they remain indifferent? Thus they convened the meetings at Cheng and Yanggu. Now, at the meeting of Cheng, weapons and armor were not put to use; why then speak of the projection of awe-inspiring prestige? Because overawing the world lies in grasping the strategic momentum of the world. Just when the threatening aura of Chu was blazing fiercely, had there been no prestige to rouse them, the states of the north would not necessarily have united in following Qi. Mindful that the vital pivot for repelling Chu lay in Zheng, Qi proceeded to the territory of Luo [Cheng] to forge a covenant, patching up divisions and offering succor…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
救與列國共圖之夫以素所未集之兵一旦致
之麾下蓋不越乎樽俎之間而先聲所及中國
之威著矣異日次陘庭以納款楚竟不敢遺鄭
人一矢謂非振威之所致耶陽穀之會神明不
要曷言乎信之敦蓋信天下者在一天下之心
方夷屬之新附也使無信以申之則東方之國
未必堅從齊也念斷楚之右臂在江黃也乃繼
貫澤以講好而奇正分合俾二國共守之夫以
素所未同之國一旦聽吾約束蓋不藉于壇坫
===
之歃而意氣所感中國之信孚矣異日偕二國
以伐陳楚竟不敢越中原一步謂非敦信之所
致耶吁此一桓仲也能愼於楚未帖之先而不
能不肆於陳旣執之後君子有以識齊君臣之
量與器矣雖然獨濤塗之役巳哉楚師三至鄭
郊而救不力惡乎勤且齊藉力於江黃者不少
而使楚竟滅之遠齊近楚之諫徒廑仲父之思
矣然是時楚用子文以紓國難抑亦仲父耦也
謂無競維人信哉
punctuated: 救，與列國共圖之。夫以素所未集之兵，一旦致之麾下，蓋不越乎樽俎之間，而先聲所及，中國之威著矣。異日次陘庭以納款，楚竟不敢遺鄭人一矢，謂非振威之所致耶？陽穀之會，神明不要，曷言乎信之敦？蓋信天下者，在一天下之心。方夷屬之新附也，使無信以申之，則東方之國未必堅從。齊也念斷楚之右臂在江、黃也，乃繼貫澤以講好，而奇正分合，俾二國共守之。夫以素所未同之國，一旦聽吾約束，蓋不藉于壇坫之歃，而意氣所感，中國之信孚矣。異日偕二國以伐陳，楚竟不敢越中原一步，謂非敦信之所致耶？吁！此一桓、仲也，能愼於楚未帖之先，而不能不肆於陳旣執之後，君子有以識齊君臣之量與器矣。雖然，獨濤塗之役巳哉？楚師三至鄭郊，而救不力，惡乎勤？且齊藉力於江、黃者不少，而使楚竟滅之，「遠齊近楚」之諫，徒廑仲父之思矣。然是時楚用子文以紓國難，抑亦仲父耦也。謂「無競維人」，信哉！
translation_en: …rescue, planning it together with the various states. By bringing troops that had never previously been assembled under his command all at once, without even going beyond the banquet tables, his advance reputation spread and the prestige of the Central States was made manifest. On a later day, when he encamped at Xingting to receive terms of submission, Chu ultimately did not dare to shoot a single arrow at the people of Zheng—can this be said not to be the result of rousing his prestige? At the meeting of Yanggu, no oaths were exacted before the gods; why then speak of the strengthening of trust? For winning the trust of the world lies in unifying the hearts of the world. Just when the borderland dependencies had newly submitted, had there been no good faith to reassure them, the eastern states would not necessarily have firmly followed. Qi, mindful that cutting off Chu's right arm lay with Jiang and Huang, followed up the meeting at Guanze by cultivating friendly relations, arranging unorthodox and orthodox deployments, division and combination, so that the two states would jointly uphold them. By getting states that had never before been allied to obey our discipline all at once, without relying on the smearing of blood at the covenant altar, their spirits were moved and the good faith of the Central States inspired confidence. On a later day, when he joined the two states to attack Chen, Chu ultimately did not dare to cross a single step into the Central Plains—can this be said not to be the result of strengthening trust? Alas! These were the very same Duke Huan and Guan Zhong: they were able to be cautious before Chu was subdued, yet could not help becoming arrogant after Chen (Yuan Taotu) was seized. From this the gentleman can discern the capacity and vessel of the ruler and minister of Qi. Even so, was this true only of the campaign involving Yuan Taotu? The army of Chu thrice reached the outskirts of Zheng, and Qi's relief efforts were half-hearted—where was the diligence? Moveover, Qi relied on the strength of Jiang and Huang to no small degree, yet allowed Chu to wipe them out in the end; the remonstrance about "being far from Qi and near to Chu" merely left Uncle Zhong (Guan Zhong) with anxious thoughts in vain. Yet at that time Chu employed Ziwen to relieve the state's difficulties, and he too was a match for Uncle Zhong. Truly it is said: "What is most powerful is being a true man!"

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
樂者
考試官敎諭朱批明淨得旨
論造化生成之德幾於禮樂也蓋仁義者造化
生成之德也而與禮樂相近焉效法其有本乎
樂記之意謂夫人知禮樂肇端於天地矣而未
知其理之一也何言乎物不自生也作之以春
鼓出機於東震長之以夏壯化工於南離此天
地絪縕之德普萬物而無私者吾於合同而知
資生之仁也物不自成也秋而斂焉肅之以兌
===
金冬而藏焉止之以坎水此性命各正之理别
羣物而不過者吾於散殊而知曲成之義也然
是仁也氣行同和者也樂之有聲非氣之爲而
以和爲主乎取聲氣之順成者與元氣之順布
者而比之相去特幾希爾雖謂無聲爲有聲之
象可也樂之興于合同之初也以此是義也質
具異序者也禮之有體非質之爲而以序爲主
乎取制度之森嚴者與法象之森列者而比之
相去亦無幾爾雖謂無體爲有體之寓可也禮
punctuated:
「樂者」
考試官敎諭朱批：明淨，得旨。
論造化生成之德，幾於禮樂也。蓋仁義者，造化生成之德也，而與禮樂相近焉，效法其有本乎？《樂記》之意，謂夫人知禮樂肇端於天地矣，而未知其理之一也。何言乎？物不自生也，作之以春，鼓出機於東震；長之以夏，壯化工於南離。此天地絪縕之德，普萬物而無私者，吾於合同而知資生之仁也。物不自成也，秋而斂焉，肅之以兌金；冬而藏焉，止之以坎水。此性命各正之理，别羣物而不過者，吾於散殊而知曲成之義也。然是仁也，氣行同和者也。樂之有聲，非氣之爲而以和爲主乎？取聲氣之順成者，與元氣之順布者而比之，相去特幾希爾，雖謂無聲爲有聲之象可也，樂之興于合同之初也以此。是義也，質具異序者也。禮之有體，非質之爲而以序爲主乎？取制度之森嚴者，與法象之森列者而比之，相去亦無幾爾，雖謂無體爲有體之寓可也，禮
translation_en:
“[Therefore,] music…” [Record of Music, “Yuezhe…”]

Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Clear and pure; grasps the main purport.

In discussing the virtue of the creative and transformative forces in generating and bringing things to completion, it remarks that this comes close to rites and music. For benevolence and righteousness are the virtues of the creative and transformative forces in generating and completing things, and they are closely akin to rites and music—does not modeling oneself upon them have a fundamental basis? The meaning of the Record of Music (Yueji) is that while people know that rites and music originate in Heaven and Earth, they do not yet know that their principle is one. What does this mean? Things do not generate themselves: they are aroused by spring, stirring the mechanism of emergence in the eastern trigram Zhen; they are nourished by summer, invigorating the transformative work in the southern trigram Li. This is the virtue of the generative fusion of Heaven and Earth, extending universally to the myriad things without partiality; in their harmonious union, I recognize the benevolence that gives rise to life. Things do not bring themselves to completion: in autumn they are gathered in, made solemn by the metal of the trigram Dui; in winter they are stored away, brought to rest by the water of the trigram Kan. This is the principle whereby nature and destiny are each rectified, distinguishing the multitude of things without excess; in their differentiation and particularity, I recognize the righteousness that brings things to intricate completion. Yet this benevolence is that in which vital energy moves in shared harmony. That music has sound—is it not the working of vital energy, taking harmony as its keynote? If one takes the smooth completion of musical sounds and vital breath and compares it with the smooth diffusion of primordial energy, the distance between them is slight indeed. Even to say that the soundless is the image of that which has sound is permissible; it is for this reason that music arises at the beginning of harmonious union. This righteousness is that in which substantial form possesses distinct order. That rites have embodiment—is it not the working of substantial form, taking order as its keynote? If one takes the strictness of institutional regulations and compares it with the serried array of natural models and phenomena, the distance between them is likewise negligible. Even to say that the formless is the abode of that which has form is permissible; that rites…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之行於散殊之際也以此噫是探本之論也雖
然禮樂豈判然二物哉春夏秋冬一氣也生長
斂藏一機也知仁樂義禮所以爲近又知其所
以爲一則功用之妙不在聖人在吾心矣三代
而下古禮雖廢其數可陳若大樂則寥寥絕響
矣豈一元生物之仁流行於天地者有時而息
歟無亦求中聲者過也非知道者孰能識之
第貳場
論
===
人主以天下爲度
徐兆魁
同考試官教諭陳批以天爲喻切中題旨而
束結處尤見卓識取之
考試官教諭楊批體裁嚴整議論正大
考試官教諭朱批宏博中有奇特
人主之制治也以法而其行法也以天夫然後
可以通天下之志而善天下之治法者人主之
所制也法制于人主固宜可以自行其意而不
punctuated:
之行於散殊之際也，以此。噫！是探本之論也。雖然，禮樂豈判然二物哉？春、夏、秋、冬，一氣也；生、長、斂、藏，一機也。知仁樂、義禮所以爲近，又知其所以爲一，則功用之妙，不在聖人，在吾心矣。三代而下，古禮雖廢，其數可陳；若大樂，則寥寥絕響矣。豈一元生物之仁，流行於天地者，有時而息歟？無亦求中聲者過也。非知道者，孰能識之！

第貳場
論

人主以天下爲度
徐兆魁
同考試官教諭陳批：以天爲喻，切中題旨，而束結處尤見卓識，取之。
考試官教諭楊批：體裁嚴整，議論正大。
考試官教諭朱批：宏博中有奇特。

人主之制治也以法，而其行法也以天，夫然後可以通天下之志，而善天下之治。法者，人主之所制也。法制于人主，固宜可以自行其意，而不
translation_en:
… [That ritual] operates amidst diversity and differentiation is for this reason.

Ah! This is a discourse that probes the fundamental root. Even so, how could ritual and music be two completely separate things? Spring, summer, autumn, and winter are a single vital force (qi); germination, growth, gathering, and storing are a single mechanism. If one understands why benevolence and music, and righteousness and ritual, are close to one another, and also understands why they are one, then the subtlety of their efficacy does not lie in the sages, but in our own minds. From the Three Dynasties downward, although the ancient rituals fell into disuse, their institutional forms could still be set forth; as for great music, however, its echoes have died away into silence. Could it be that the benevolence of the primordial unity that gives life to all things, flowing between heaven and earth, at times ceases? Or is it rather the fault of those who seek the harmonious mean in sound alone? Who but one who understands the Way could recognize this!

"The Ruler Takes All Under Heaven as His Measure"
Xu Zhaokui 徐兆魁

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爵削地六師之移衣冠之畫嘉石之坐刑也所
以癉惡而懲罪也書曰天命有德五服五章哉
天討有罪五刑五用哉易曰火在天上大有君
子以遏惡揚善順天休命曰德曰服曰善曰揚
言賞也曰罪曰刑曰惡曰遏言刑也然而必曰
天命曰天討曰天之休命者明其皆出於天也
天之道福善而禍淫其於人也制以意不制以
形人或疑而翫焉於是舉禍福之柄而授之君
使司平之是賞罰者人主之所以代天以行其
===
理而非其所得恣已以便其私者也人主之尊
猶之天也有言遜於乃心則泰然喜逆於乃心
則艴然怒其情得肆也喜之發也甘雨煕陽怒
之發也疾霆隕霜其勢得行也憸夫壬人之欲
作威而作福也必有所窺而後動上徵好則諛
人者進上徵惡則譖人者進其機易投也以得
肆之情濟之以得行之勢而乘之以易投之機
然則人主之法何自而當天下之治亦何自而
善乎此其所以必天下爲度也物之有分寸尺
punctuated: 爵削地，六師之移，衣冠之畫，嘉石之坐，刑也，所以癉惡而懲罪也。《書》曰：「天命有德，五服五章哉！天討有罪，五刑五用哉！」《易》曰：「火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。」曰德、曰服、曰善、曰揚，言賞也；曰罪、曰刑、曰惡、曰遏，言刑也。然而必曰天命、曰天討、曰天之休命者，明其皆出於天也。天之道，福善而禍淫。其於人也，制以意，不制以形，人或疑而翫焉。於是舉禍福之柄而授之君，使司平之。是賞罰者，人主之所以代天以行其理，而非其所得恣已以便其私者也。人主之尊，猶之天也。有言遜於乃心，則泰然喜；逆於乃心，則艴然怒，其情得肆也。喜之發也，甘雨煕陽；怒之發也，疾霆隕霜，其勢得行也。憸夫壬人之欲作威而作福也，必有所窺而後動。上徵好，則諛人者進；上徵惡，則譖人者進，其機易投也。以得肆之情，濟之以得行之勢，而乘之以易投之機，然則人主之法何自而當，天下之治亦何自而善乎？此其所以必天下爲度也。物之有分、寸、尺、
translation_en: …ranks and the reduction of fiefs, the mobilization of the six armies, the symbolic portrayal on robes and caps, and sitting upon the admonition stone—these are punishments, the means by which evil is distressed and crime is chastised. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Heaven charges the virtuous; what are the five vestments and five insignia! Heaven punishes the guilty; what are the five punishments and five applications!" The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Fire above heaven: Great Possession (Dayou). The superior man thus represses evil and promotes good, obeying the benign mandate of Heaven." To speak of "virtue," "vestments," "good," and "promotion" is to speak of rewards; to speak of "guilt," "punishment," "evil," and "repression" is to speak of punishments. Yet why must it say "Heaven charges," "Heaven punishes," and "the benign mandate of Heaven"? To make clear that all of these issue from Heaven. The Way of Heaven is to bless the good and bring calamity upon the dissolute. In dealing with humankind, it governs through intent and not through physical form, so people sometimes doubt it and treat it lightly. Thereupon, Heaven takes the handles of calamity and blessing and entrusts them to the sovereign, causing him to administer them with fairness. Thus rewards and punishments are the means by which the ruler of men acts on behalf of Heaven to carry out its principles, and not something in which he may indulge himself to serve his private ends. The exalted position of the ruler of men is just like that of Heaven. When words are agreeable to his mind, he is serenely pleased; when they run counter to his mind, he flares up in anger—his emotions can be given free rein. When his pleasure manifests, it is like sweet rain and warm sunshine; when his anger manifests, it is like sudden thunderbolts and falling frost—his authority can be put into effect. Whenglib and deceitful men wish to arrogate to themselves the making of terror and the making of fortune, they necessarily spy out an opening before acting. When the sovereign shows a sign of fondness, flatterers advance; when the sovereign shows a sign of dislike, slanderers advance—such opportunities are easily exploited. Given emotions that can be given free rein, aided by authority that can be put into effect, and seized upon through opportunities that are easily exploited, how then can the laws of the ruler of men be fitting, and how can the governance of the empire be good? This is why he must take the empire as his standard of measure. That things have tenths of an inch, inches, feet,…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
丈引者度也而天下之度物者準於是矣織帛
於宮既成而鬻之市廣者不可狹而狹者不可
廣長者不可短而短者不可長其度定也是故
家有家度國有國度天下有天下之度卿大夫
以一家爲度故親愛賤惡不可忽於家諸侯以
國爲度故一噸一笑不可輕於國至若人主所
以爲之度者非特一國一家也天下之人孰非
人主之人哉御得其道戎夷蠻貊有莫敢不來
享不來王者吾安得而勿獎之也而何以私勞
===
爲也御失其道匹夫匹婦有敢怒而不敢言者
吾安得而盡讎之也而何以私怨爲也私意行
則公道蔽而人主之度失矣況其始之者濫觴
而繼之者滔天而不可止也於是有虐煢獨而
畏高明者焉有賞僭而及惡人刑濫而及善人
者焉有賞數而人不見德罰敝而人不知懼者
焉有輿臺紲組厮養續貂而帑藏爲竭者焉有
赭衣半道斷獄數萬而民無所措手足者焉其
甚也干陰陽之龢殄羣生之命此無他由其不
punctuated: 丈、引者，度也，而天下之度物者準於是矣。織帛於宮，既成而鬻之市，廣者不可狹而狹者不可廣，長者不可短而短者不可長，其度定也。是故家有家度，國有國度，天下有天下之度。卿大夫以一家爲度，故親愛賤惡不可忽於家；諸侯以國爲度，故一噸一笑不可輕於國。至若人主所以爲之度者，非特一國一家也。天下之人，孰非人主之人哉？御得其道，戎夷蠻貊有莫敢不來享、不來王者，吾安得而勿獎之也？而何以私勞爲也！御失其道，匹夫匹婦有敢怒而不敢言者，吾安得而盡讎之也？而何以私怨爲也！私意行則公道蔽，而人主之度失矣，況其始之者濫觴，而繼之者滔天而不可止也。於是有虐煢獨而畏高明者焉，有賞僭而及惡人、刑濫而及善人者焉，有賞數而人不見德、罰敝而人不知懼者焉，有輿臺紲組、厮養續貂而帑藏爲竭者焉，有赭衣半道、斷獄數萬而民無所措手足者焉。其甚也，干陰陽之龢，殄羣生之命。此無他，由其不
translation_en: … ten-foot (zhang) and hundred-foot (yin) units—that is a standard of measure, and those throughout the realm who measure things take their standard from this. When silk is woven in the home and, once finished, sold in the marketplace, what is wide cannot be made narrow and what is narrow cannot be made wide; what is long cannot be made short and what is short cannot be made long, because its measure is fixed. Therefore, a household has the measure of a household, a state has the measure of a state, and the realm has the measure of the realm. Grandees and great officers take a single household as their measure, and thus in their affections and aversions they cannot be careless within their household. The feudal lords take a state as their measure, and thus a single frown or a single smile cannot be treated lightly within their state. As for that which the ruler of men takes as his measure, it is not merely a single state or a single household. Among all the people of the realm, who is not the ruler's own person? When he governs them according to the proper Way, even the Rong, Yi, Man, and Mo tribes dare not fail to come with tribute and acknowledge his suzerainty—how could I not reward them, and what place is there for private favor? When he loses the proper Way in governing them, even ordinary men and women dare to be angry though they dare not speak—how could I treat them all as enemies, and what place is there for private resentment? When private motives prevail, public justice is obscured, and the measure of the ruler of men is lost—all the more so when what begins as a trickle strong enough only to float a goblet ends by flooding the heavens and cannot be stopped! Thereupon, there are cases of oppressing the solitary and helpless while fearing the high and mighty; there are cases of rewards being so excessive as to reach wicked men, and punishments so indiscriminate as to reach good men; there are cases of rewards being so frequent that people do not perceive them as grace, and penalties so worn out that people do not know fear; there are cases of menial servants wearing official cords and grooms adding sable tails to their caps until the state treasuries are exhausted; there are cases of convicts in reddish-brown garments filling half the roads and tens of thousands of criminal cases being decided until the people have nowhere to place their hands and feet. At its worst, this disrupts the harmony of yin and yang and destroys the lives of the multitude of living beings. This is for no other reason than that he does not …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知以天下爲度故也以天下爲度者以天下之
心爲心也以天下之心爲心者以天之心爲心
也以天之心爲心者公而不私也喜怒一人之
喜怒也非天下人之喜怒也私也好惡天下人
之好惡也非一人之好惡也公也吾弗欲窮吾
得肆之情而天下之同情可弗順乎吾弗欲挾
吾得行之勢而天下之大勢可弗合乎吾弗欲
啓吾易投之機而天下之大機可弗執乎善吾
彰焉功吾勸焉所以彰之勸之者無心也以天
===
下之好好之也非謂其私勞我故喜也即有舊
怨吾賞之矣惡吾癉焉罪吾懲焉所以癉之懲
之者無心也以天下之惡惡之也非謂其私怨
我故怒也即有微勞吾罰之矣温原陽樊之田
可賜而地不可隧也邑可多予而纓不可請也
執羈靮而從者不可私班邑也驚屬車之塵剟
寢廟之環者可誅而廷尉之法不可加也人主
之賞罰非固如此之徇乎天下之人也道本至
公惡得而參之以私治本至順惡得而與之以
punctuated: 知以天下爲度故也。以天下爲度者，以天下之心爲心也；以天下之心爲心者，以天之心爲心也；以天之心爲心者，公而不私也。喜怒，一人之喜怒也，非天下人之喜怒也，私也；好惡，天下人之好惡也，非一人之好惡也，公也。吾弗欲窮吾得肆之情，而天下之同情可弗順乎？吾弗欲挾吾得行之勢，而天下之大勢可弗合乎？吾弗欲啓吾易投之機，而天下之大機可弗執乎？善吾彰焉，功吾勸焉，所以彰之、勸之者，無心也，以天下之好好之也，非謂其私勞我故喜也，即有舊怨，吾賞之矣。惡吾癉焉，罪吾懲焉，所以癉之、懲之者，無心也，以天下之惡惡之也，非謂其私怨我故怒也，即有微勞，吾罰之矣。温、原、陽樊之田可賜，而地不可隧也；邑可多予，而纓不可請也；執羈靮而從者，不可私班邑也；驚屬車之塵、剟寢廟之環者可誅，而廷尉之法不可加也。人主之賞罰，非固如此之徇乎天下之人也，道本至公，惡得而參之以私？治本至順，惡得而與之以
translation_en: …failing to know how to take the realm as one's measure. To take the realm as one's measure is to take the mind of the realm as one's mind; to take the mind of the realm as one's mind is to take the mind of Heaven as one's mind; and to take the mind of Heaven as one's mind is to be impartial and not selfish. Joy and anger are the joy and anger of a single person, not the joy and anger of the people of the realm—they are selfish. Likes and dislikes are the likes and dislikes of the people of the realm, not the likes and dislikes of a single person—they are impartial. Even if I do not wish to indulge to the utmost the passions I am in a position to gratify, how could I fail to follow the shared sentiments of the realm? Even if I do not wish to presume upon the power I am in a position to wield, how could I fail to accord with the great trends of the realm? Even if I do not wish to open up opportunities through which I might easily be played upon, how could I fail to grasp the great pivotal moments of the realm? What is good, I make manifest; what is meritorious, I encourage. That whereby I manifest and encourage them is without personal bias: I love them with the love of the realm. It is not that I rejoice because they have rendered me some private service; even if there is an old grievance against them, I reward them. What is evil, I reprove; what is culpable, I punish. That whereby I reprove and punish them is without personal bias: I hate them with the hatred of the realm. It is not that I am angry because of some private grievance against me; even if they have rendered some slight service, I penalize them. The fields of Wen, Yuan, and Yangfan might be bestowed, yet a tunneled passage to the grave could not be granted; towns might be given in abundance, yet the cap-tassels of rank could not be requested; those who held the bridle and followed in exile could not be privately parcelled out fiefs; and though one who startled the horses in the dust of the imperial cortege or stole the jade ring from the ancestral temple screen deserved execution, the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement could not be made to impose a penalty beyond the law. In his rewards and punishments, the ruler does not merely bend to the people of the realm like this—rather, because the Way is fundamentally supremely impartial, how could one adulterate it with selfishness? Because governance is fundamentally supremely compliant with principle, how could one intrude upon it with…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
已吾不能使天下不賞而勸不怒而畏而恃吾
所以使之勸使之畏者皆得其平有以大當天
下之心焉爾此其方寸之內豁然混闢洞然昭
曠天地不足爲囊括日月不足爲照臨豈與夫
用智自私較恩怨於一介之微者同日語哉故
當其時殺之者不怨利之者不庸舉四海之內
含生之倫受氣之屬無不遵路遵道畏威懷德
共惟皇極之歸治與協風翔德與顥氣游九苞
儀庭庶草蕃廡人主凝旒端冕垂拱而舉萬年
===
之觴而天下晏然無事矣吾故曰人主之行法
以天有以通天下之志而善天下之治者此也
反是私意隔閡以之爲一家一國且不可況天
下乎蓋嘗稽古而知堯舜至公之心矣窮奇饕
餮之徒之不肖也禹益夷垂諸人之賢也堯豈
有不知哉而必以付之舜舜亦豈不能亟命而
遄罰之哉而必俟之欽哉惟恤之後詢岳咨牧
之餘其罰之也如畏其命之也如疑凜凜然唯
恐吾之好惡參之以先入之見而失其平也是
punctuated:
已？吾不能使天下不賞而勸、不怒而畏，而恃吾所以使之勸、使之畏者，皆得其平，有以大當天下之心焉爾。此其方寸之內，豁然混闢，洞然昭曠，天地不足爲囊括，日月不足爲照臨，豈與夫用智自私、較恩怨於一介之微者同日語哉！故當其時，殺之者不怨，利之者不庸，舉四海之內，含生之倫、受氣之屬，無不遵路遵道，畏威懷德，共惟皇極之歸。治與協風翔，德與顥氣游，九苞儀庭，庶草蕃廡，人主凝旒端冕，垂拱而舉萬年之觴，而天下晏然無事矣。吾故曰：人主之行法以天，有以通天下之志，而善天下之治者，此也。

反是，私意隔閡，以之爲一家、一國且不可，況天下乎？蓋嘗稽古而知堯、舜至公之心矣。窮奇、饕餮之徒之不肖也，禹、益、夷、垂諸人之賢也，堯豈有不知哉？而必以付之舜。舜亦豈不能亟命而遄罰之哉？而必俟之「欽哉惟恤」之後、詢岳咨牧之餘。其罰之也如畏，其命之也如疑，凜凜然唯恐吾之好惡參之以先入之見，而失其平也。是
translation_en:
… [interfere with it with one's own] self? I cannot make the world be encouraged without rewards or stand in awe without anger, yet I rely on the fact that the means by which I make them encouraged and make them stand in awe all attain fairness, and thus greatly satisfy the minds of the world. Within the square inch of such a ruler's heart, all is vast and open, clear and luminous; heaven and earth are scarcely sufficient to encompass it, and the sun and moon are scarcely sufficient to outshine it. How could this be spoken of on the same day as those who use cleverness for selfish ends and weigh favors and grudges over the slightest trifle! Therefore, in such an era, those who are put to death do not feel resentment, and those who are benefited do not take it as a personal favor. Throughout the four seas, all living beings and creatures endowed with vital breath without exception follow the road and follow the Way, standing in awe of majesty and cherishing virtue, all turning together toward the Supreme Ultimate of royal perfection. Governance soars with the harmonious winds, virtue roams with the luminous ether, the nine-colored phoenixes display their poise in the courtyard, and the multitudinous plants flourish in abundance. The ruler, with steady pendant-beads and upright ceremonial cap, lets his robes hang down with folded hands and raises the goblet of ten thousand years, while the empire is tranquil and free of trouble. Thus I say: when a ruler enforces the law in accordance with Heaven, he has the means to unite the wills of the world and perfect the governance of the world—this is what is meant.

Conversely, if selfish intentions create barriers, one cannot even govern a single family or a single state by such means, how much less the entire world? Indeed, I have examined antiquity and come to know the supremely impartial minds of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜. That the likes of Qiongqi 窮奇 and Taotie 饕餮 were unworthy, and that men such as Yu 禹, Yi 益, Yi 夷 [Boyi 伯夷], and Chui 垂 were worthy—how could Yao not have known this? Yet he insisted on entrusting the matter to Shun. And how could Shun have been unable to promptly appoint the worthy and swiftly punish the wicked? Yet he insisted on waiting until after the injunction "Be reverent! Be compassionate in punishments!" and after consulting the Four Peaks and taking counsel with the Twelve Pastors. When he punished them, it was as though he were fearful; when he appointed them, it was as though he were hesitant—trembling with caution, lest his own likes and dislikes be mixed with preconceived notions and thereby lose their fairness. This is…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
堯舜之心也能以天下爲度者堯舜也而宋之
儒者猶有言曰堯不從皐陶之殺人而聽四岳
之用鯀也以爲是聖人之好賞而惡刑也亦不
獨宋人言之也陽居大夏以生育長養爲事陰
居大冬而積於空虛不用之處是天之貴德而
不貴刑也漢董生亦甞言之矣豈治天下者固
不可使私蔽公而尤不可使刑勝德耶之二言
者是或一道也人主所以奉天而弘其度於天
下者此也不然信賞必罰申韓之刻核無以異
===
於聖人矣敢以是而足胡氏未發之意謹論
表

表〔元祐四年〕
鄭偉

是作體嚴詞整頌而能規可以觀忠藎之素陳矣
錄之
考試官敎諭楊批事核語麗忠悃藹然
punctuated:
堯、舜之心也，能以天下爲度者，堯、舜也。而宋之儒者猶有言曰：「堯不從皐陶之殺人，而聽四岳之用鯀也。」以爲是聖人之好賞而惡刑也。亦不獨宋人言之也：「陽居大夏，以生育長養爲事；陰居大冬，而積於空虛不用之處。」是天之貴德而不貴刑也，漢董生亦甞言之矣。豈治天下者，固不可使私蔽公，而尤不可使刑勝德耶？之二言者，是或一道也。人主所以奉天而弘其度於天下者，此也。不然，信賞必罰，申、韓之刻核，無以異於聖人矣。敢以是而足胡氏未發之意。謹論。

表

擬宋以范祖禹爲右諫議大夫兼侍講謝表〔元祐四年〕
鄭偉
同考試官敎諭黃批：場中作者，不靡則俗。獨是作體嚴詞整，頌而能規，可以觀忠藎之素陳矣。錄之。
考試官敎諭楊批：事核語麗，忠悃藹然。
translation_en:
… the mind of Yao and Shun; those able to take the entire world as their measure were Yao and Shun. Yet a Confucian scholar of the Song dynasty still remarked: "Yao did not follow Gao Yao in putting men to death, but instead heeded the Four Peaks in employing Gun." He considered this to show how the sages loved rewarding and abhorred punishing. Nor was it only a man of the Song who said this: "Yang resides in high summer and makes giving birth, nurturing, and fostering growth its business; yin resides in deep winter and accumulates in empty, unused places." That Heaven values virtue and does not value punishment—Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] of the Han dynasty also once spoke of this. Could it be that in governing the world, while one certainly must not let private bias obscure public impartiality, one must especially not let punishment prevail over virtue? These two sayings each represent a valid principle. It is by this that a ruler of men serves Heaven and broadens his magnanimity across the world. Otherwise, in making rewards certain and punishments inevitable, the harshness of Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非 would be no different from the way of the sages. I venture to use this to supplement the meaning left unexpressed by Mr. Hu [Hu Yin 胡寅]. I respectfully submit this discourse.

Memorial

Imitation of a Memorial of Thanks by Fan Zuyu 范祖禹 of the Song Dynasty upon His Appointment as Policy Critic-Adviser of the Right Concurrently Serving as Expositor-in-Waiting [4th year of the Yuanyou reign (1089)]
Zheng Wei 鄭偉
Associate Examiner Instructor Huang 黃 comments: Writers in the examination compound are either overly florid or vulgar. This piece alone is strict in form and orderly in diction, offering praise while remaining capable of admonition; from it one can observe the forthright presentation of loyal devotion. Record it.
Examiner Instructor Yang 楊 comments: The historical allusions are accurate and the phrasing is elegant, brimming with loyal sincerity.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫兼諫諍唐以學士職論思止輦受言誼
辟每勤於聽納橫經問道叔世尤切于箴
摩蓋學必講然後明而過以聞廼能改如
陽城有道猶或貽諍臣之譏必陸贄愛君
始不負平生之學洪惟
昭代尤愼任人謂諫院
經筵均屬根本之地故講官言責並稱侍從
之臣班列
北扉直隨
===
東閣事關
廊廟玉簡起而嚴霜飛語傍
絲綸
金鑾開而
春陽藹程功積事雖無尺寸可書端本澄源則
與尋常有間是宜人傑乃稱
國華玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
睿德日新
punctuated: 夫兼諫諍，唐以學士職論思。止輦受言，誼辟每勤於聽納；橫經問道，叔世尤切于箴摩。蓋學必講然後明，而過以聞廼能改。如陽城有道，猶或貽諍臣之譏；必陸贄愛君，始不負平生之學。洪惟昭代，尤愼任人。謂諫院、經筵，均屬根本之地；故講官、言責，並稱侍從之臣。班列北扉，直隨東閣。事關廊廟，玉簡起而嚴霜飛；語傍絲綸，金鑾開而春陽藹。程功積事，雖無尺寸可書；端本澄源，則與尋常有間。是宜人傑，乃稱國華。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，睿德日新，
translation_en:
… [Grand Masters] concurrently served in remonstrance and admonition, and the Tang dynasty charged its Academicians with deliberating and reflecting on state affairs. Halting the imperial carriage to receive counsel, righteous sovereigns were ever diligent in listening and accepting advice; holding forth the classics to inquire into the Way, even in later ages it was all the more urgent to offer admonition and moral polishing. For learning becomes clear only after it is expounded, and faults can be corrected only once they are heard. Even a man of the Way like Yang Cheng 陽城 still incurred criticism as a remonstrating official [for remaining silent]; only with a love for one's sovereign like that of Lu Zhi 陸贄 does one finally not betray the learning of a lifetime.

I humbly reflect that our Illustrious Dynasty is especially cautious in appointing men. Holding that the Bureau of Policy Criticism and the Classics Colloquium alike belong to the foundational places of governance, both Classics Colloquium Expositors and officials with speaking responsibilities are jointly termed Ministers in Attendance. Ranked within the Northern Postern, their duty follows into the Eastern Pavilion. When matters concern the imperial court, the jade tablet is raised and stern frost flies; when words draw near the silken imperial utterances, the Golden Bell Hall opens and spring sunlight is mild and genial. In measuring achievements and accumulating administrative deeds, although they may have not an inch or foot of merit to record, in rectifying the root and clarifying the source, their role differs vastly from the ordinary. For this, it is fitting to have anoutstanding talent who may truly be called a glory of the state.

This is indeed because I humbly encounter [Your Majesty, …], whose sagely virtue is daily renewed, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
英資天啓屬
旋乾轉坤之運正
親賢論道之時
動準成規舉經明行脩之士
志稽彞典
詔直言極諫之官法始罷新人惟求舊巋然大
老首歸圖任之初蕞爾小才亦濫
甄收之及俾從柱後獨立
禁中玉筍仍綴乎初銜寶珥載承乎
===
新渥臣草茅微賤章句荒疎弓必爲箕蚤服家
庭之訓田不納履乂謝姻黨之容固陋之
身以榮爲懼要華之選欲報彌難念當
訪落之元亦有勸學之疏雖拳拳而□□知
錄錄以何庸豈謂兼官猥加一介
渙汗莫收于
成命傴僂徒切於下情敢不益竭駑資仰承
鴻造立身惟名節自許進講非王道不陳苟有
裨于吾
punctuated: 英資天啓。屬旋乾轉坤之運，正親賢論道之時；動準成規，舉經明行脩之士；志稽彞典，詔直言極諫之官。法始罷新，人惟求舊。巋然大老，首歸圖任之初；蕞爾小才，亦濫甄收之及。俾從柱後，獨立禁中；玉筍仍綴乎初銜，寶珥載承乎新渥。臣草茅微賤，章句荒疎。弓必爲箕，蚤服家庭之訓；田不納履，乂謝姻黨之容。固陋之身，以榮爲懼；要華之選，欲報彌難。念當訪落之元，亦有勸學之疏；雖拳拳而□□，知錄錄以何庸。豈謂兼官，猥加一介！渙汗莫收于成命，傴僂徒切於下情。敢不益竭駑資，仰承鴻造！立身惟名節自許，進講非王道不陳；苟有裨于吾…
translation_en:
…and your heroic endowments are inspired by Heaven. At this juncture of revolving Heaven and turning Earth, it is precisely the time to draw close to the worthy and discourse upon the Way. In your actions you take established regulations as your standard, promoting scholars who understand the Classics and cultivate their conduct; in your aspirations you examine the constant canons, summoning officials who speak forthrightly and remonstrate to the utmost. Having just abolished the New Laws, in seeking men you look only to the old. The venerable elders, standing like solitary peaks, are the first to return at the outset of your plans for governance; yet even a petty talent such as myself has unworthily been reached by your selective recruitment. You cause me to attend behind the pillars and stand alone within the Forbidden Palace; in the jade-shoot ranks I remain attached to my former title, while with the jeweled ear-ornament of office I once again receive your new favor.

Your servant is of humble, rustic origins, and my mastery of textual exegesis is crude and sketchy. Knowing that a bow-maker's son must learn to weave willow baskets, I early submitted to my family's instructions; minding the adage not to adjust one's shoes in a melon field, I have long declined the indulgent accommodation of relatives and partisans. With a person so stubborn and rustic, I regard honor with trepidation; chosen for a post of such importance and splendor, I find it all the more difficult to repay your grace. I recall that at the very beginning of your succession and consultation with ministers, I too submitted a memorial encouraging imperial study; though earnest and […], I knew how mediocre and of what little use I was. How could I have expected that concurrent offices would be undeservedly bestowed upon a mere individual! Yet the royal command, once issued like sweat, cannot be rescinded as an established mandate, and in my stooped reverence I am only filled with earnest humility. How dare I not further exhaust my dull capacities in looking up to receive your vast creation! In establishing myself, I pledge only to uphold reputation and integrity; in advancing to lecture, I shall set forth nothing that is not the Kingly Way. If only it may be of some benefit to my…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君自甘焚草誓欲酬於國士竊慕獻芹伏願
惟木從繩
若金作礪
遜志典學由六經而會帝王之精
純心任賢達四聰以廣忠直之益
驗天命民情去留之際常如日之方中
察君子小人消長之機惟在心之不息
善繼善述調
玉燭於五辰
===
不愆不忘撫
瑤圖於千禩臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
punctuated:
君，自甘焚草；誓欲酬於國士，竊慕獻芹。伏願惟木從繩，若金作礪。遜志典學，由六經而會帝王之精；純心任賢，達四聰以廣忠直之益。驗天命民情去留之際，常如日之方中；察君子小人消長之機，惟在心之不息。善繼善述，調玉燭於五辰；不愆不忘，撫瑤圖於千禩。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁塲
策
translation_en:
… my ruler, I would gladly burn my drafts; swearing to repay the favor of being treated as a scholar of the state, I privately aspire to the humble offering of wild celery. I humbly pray that Your Majesty will be like wood that follows the marking-line, and like metal put to the whetstone; that with a humble will you will be constantly engaged in learning, grasping the essence of the emperors and kings through the Six Classics; that with a pure heart you will employ the worthy, opening your ears in all four directions to broaden the benefit of loyal and upright counsel; that in examining the juncture at which the Mandate of Heaven and the sentiments of the people remain or depart, you will ever be like the sun at its zenith; and that in discerning the mechanism by which superior men and petty men wax and wane, you will rely solely on unceasing vigilance of mind. Skilfully continuing the wills and carrying forward the undertakings of your predecessors, may you harmonize the Jade Torch of the seasons across the five cyclical periods; neither erring nor forgetting, may you preside over the Precious Chart of the empire for a thousand generations. Your servant is overcome to the utmost with awe and earnest trepidation as he gazes toward Heaven and looks up to Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第一問
馮名望
同考試官教諭蔣批饗
帝崇儒典禮最重此作考古覈今敷對詳盡末歸之身心尤有關鍵真
足以楊厲
昭代制作之隆宜錄以式
考試官教諭楊批揄楊
盛典無出此篇矣取之
考試官教諭朱批規
===
頌得體
人君其天命之主乎必心合乎天而後可
以事天人君其道統之宗乎必身體乎道
而後可以崇道蓋道原於天故事天者人
君之職天不可見求諸心以若之則天心
可監而滋至之休迓矣治本乎道故崇道
者人君之務道具於聖求諸身以體之則
聖學可明而日新之德成矣二者帝王所
以立人極而致盛治之大端也由今而遡
punctuated:
第一問
馮名望
同考試官教諭蔣批：饗帝崇儒，典禮最重。此作考古覈今，敷對詳盡，末歸之身心，尤有關鍵。真足以楊厲昭代制作之隆，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭楊批：揄楊盛典，無出此篇矣，取之。
考試官教諭朱批：規頌得體。
