人君其天命之主乎！必心合乎天，而後可以事天。人君其道統之宗乎！必身體乎道，而後可以崇道。蓋道原於天，故事天者人君之職。天不可見，求諸心以若之，則天心可監，而滋至之休迓矣。治本乎道，故崇道者人君之務。道具於聖，求諸身以體之，則聖學可明，而日新之德成矣。二者，帝王所以立人極而致盛治之大端也。由今而遡…
translation_en:
First Question
Feng Mingwang 馮名望

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Jiang 蔣: Sacrificing to the Supreme Lord and honoring the Confucians are the most weighty of state rituals. This composition examines antiquity and verifies the present, setting forth its answer in exhaustive detail, and at the end brings the matter back to the ruler's own person and mind—which is especially crucial. It is truly sufficient to extol the magnificence of the ritual institutions established by our illustrious dynasty, and ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊: In extolling the grand state rituals, nothing surpasses this piece. Selected.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱: Both admonition and praise hit the proper measure.

Is not the ruler of men the master of the Mandate of Heaven? Only when his mind is in harmony with Heaven can he serve Heaven. Is not the ruler of men the patriarch of the Transmission of the Way (daotong)? Only when he embodies the Way in his own person can he honor the Way. For the Way originates in Heaven; therefore, serving Heaven is the duty of the ruler of men. Heaven cannot be seen, yet if one seeks it within one's own mind and conforms to it, the mind of Heaven can be perceived, and ever-increasing blessings will be welcomed. Governance is rooted in the Way; therefore, honoring the Way is the task of the ruler of men. The Way is complete in the sages, and if one seeks it within one's own person and embodies it, the learning of the sages can be illuminated, and daily-renewed virtue will be achieved. These two are the great essentials whereby emperors and kings establish the ultimate standard for humankind and bring about flourishing governance. Tracing back from the present…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之唐虞其理可知也自漢而下昭事之禮
旣瀆亂而不經表章之功又彌文之徒飾
曠儀令典若有所待此有志之士所以願
舉
明主於三代之隆者也請遂言之郊祀何昉乎
記曰因名山升中于天因吉土饗帝于郊
蓋人主受命于天猶人受命于祖人子不
可一日不見父母故君不可一歲不祭天
郊之祭也大報本反始也故以其祖配焉
===
四代之郊見於祭法禋祀燔柴舜實先之
其重可知矣其制則掃地而祭器用陶匏
牲用犢之尚其質王被衮戴冕龍章而設
日月之象其文八變而黃鍾大呂以終之
盡其變然所以如此者豈徒飾於外哉必
有爲之本矣秦漢以來代有其制而其鑿
者漢以黑帝而增北畤唐罷感生而復祭
太微宋又兼五方帝而祀之皆謬妄不經
之甚攷而論之漢文天資謙讓祠官致敬
punctuated: 之唐、虞，其理可知也。自漢而下，昭事之禮旣瀆亂而不經，表章之功又彌文之徒飾，曠儀令典若有所待，此有志之士所以願舉明主於三代之隆者也。請遂言之：郊祀何昉乎？《記》曰：「因名山升中于天，因吉土饗帝于郊。」蓋人主受命于天，猶人受命于祖；人子不可一日不見父母，故君不可一歲不祭天。郊之祭也，大報本反始也，故以其祖配焉。四代之郊見於《祭法》，禋祀燔柴，舜實先之，其重可知矣。其制則掃地而祭，器用陶匏，牲用犢之尚其質；王被衮戴冕，龍章而設日月之象其文；八變而黃鍾、大呂以終之，盡其變。然所以如此者，豈徒飾於外哉？必有爲之本矣。秦、漢以來，代有其制。而其鑿者，漢以黑帝而增北畤，唐罷感生而復祭太微，宋又兼五方帝而祀之，皆謬妄不經之甚。攷而論之，漢文天資謙讓，祠官致敬，
translation_en:
… back to Tang and Yu, the principle of this can be known. From the Han dynasty onward, the rites of reverently serving [Heaven] became profane, disorderly, and uncanonical, while the work of exalting and honoring [the Way] became a mere outward ornament of elaborate forms. It was as if the long-neglected ceremonies and fine canons were awaiting something—and this is why men of high aspiration wish to raise our enlightened ruler to the flourishing heights of the Three Dynasties. Allow me to speak of this in detail.

When did the suburban sacrifice begin? The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "Making use of famous mountains, one announces the attainment of great peace to Heaven; making use of auspicious ground, one presents offerings to the Lord on High in the suburbs." Indeed, a ruler receives his mandate from Heaven just as a man receives his life from his ancestors; a filial son cannot go a single day without seeing his parents, and therefore a ruler cannot go a single year without sacrificing to Heaven. The sacrifice in the suburbs is the great requital of the root and return to the beginning, and therefore one associates one's ancestor with Heaven in the offering. The suburban sacrifices of the Four Dynasties appear in the "Law of Sacrifices" (Jifa), while the pure sacrifice and the burning of firewood on the altar were in fact initiated by Shun; from this, its weight and importance can be known. As for its system: they swept the bare ground to perform the sacrifice, used vessels of earthenware and gourds, and used a calf as the sacrificial victim, thereby prizing simplicity; the king wore the dragon robe and ceremonial cap, emblazoned with dragons and displaying the emblems of the sun and moon, thereby manifesting refinement; and the music went through eight changes, concluding with the Huangzhong and Dalü pitch-pipes, thereby exhausting all musical variations. Yet why was it done in this manner? Was it merely for outward adornment? There must certainly have been something that served as its fundamental root.

From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, every age had its own system. Yet among the contrived distortions, the Han added the Northern Altar on account of the Black Emperor, the Tang abolished the sacrifice to the Generative Emperor only to resume sacrificing to the Taiwei constellation, and the Song furthermore combined the Emperors of the Five Directions and sacrificed to them together—all of which were extreme cases of absurdity and uncanonical practice. If we examine and discuss them, Emperor Wen of Han was by nature modest and yielding, and when his sacrificial officials offered reverence …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毋有所祈猶有敬天之遺意嗣後而角獸
赤雞竝侈歌頌祗增矯誣一年四祭疑於
瀆三歲一郊疑於慢而溢恩濫賞有司困
不能供則其失可勝道哉蓋上無奉先思
孝之君下無據經守禮之臣欲其格天而
克享也胡可得哉視學何昉乎記曰三王
四代惟其師人君受天命而爲之主以師
表萬民也民之向背從違君實司之祀三
老五更於太學冕而總干所以敎諸侯之
===
弟也四代之學至周大備鎬京辟雍無思
不服而化民成俗矣其制於大昕鼓徵以
警眾也皮弁祭菜示敬道也簡不率敎者
屏之寄棘以示懲也所以如此者亦豈徒
具其儀哉必有爲之要矣漢唐而下代舉
其儀而其尤著者漢明帝臨雍拜老唐太
宗大召名儒宋仁宗增脩學舍數御臨幸
皆於鋪張顯設之具詳焉要而言之僻陋
之邦擾攘之際其視學校若敝屣斷梗而
punctuated:
毋有所祈，猶有敬天之遺意。嗣後而角獸、赤雞，竝侈歌頌，祗增矯誣。一年四祭，疑於瀆；三歲一郊，疑於慢。而溢恩濫賞，有司困不能供，則其失可勝道哉？蓋上無奉先思孝之君，下無據經守禮之臣，欲其格天而克享也，胡可得哉？
視學何昉乎？《記》曰：「三王四代惟其師。」人君受天命而爲之主，以師表萬民也。民之向背從違，君實司之。祀三老五更於太學，冕而總干，所以敎諸侯之弟也。四代之學，至周大備，鎬京辟雍，無思不服，而化民成俗矣。其制：於大昕鼓徵，以警眾也；皮弁祭菜，示敬道也；簡不率敎者，屏之寄棘，以示懲也。所以如此者，亦豈徒具其儀哉？必有爲之要矣。漢、唐而下，代舉其儀，而其尤著者：漢明帝臨雍拜老，唐太宗大召名儒，宋仁宗增脩學舍，數御臨幸，皆於鋪張顯設之具詳焉。要而言之，僻陋之邦、擾攘之際，其視學校若敝屣斷梗，而
translation_en:
…without praying for personal blessings, which still preserved the vestigial intent of revering Heaven. Thereafter, things like horned beasts and red pheasants were extravagantly celebrated in songs and eulogies, which only increased fabrication and deceit. Performing four sacrifices in a single year bordered on profanity; performing the suburban sacrifice once every three years bordered on negligence. Moreover, with excessive favors and lavish rewards that left the authorities hard-pressed and unable to supply them, how could all their failings possibly be recounted? Indeed, when above there is no ruler who honors his ancestors and meditates on filial piety, and below there are no ministers who rely on the Classics and uphold the rites, how could one possibly expect them to reach Heaven and have their offerings accepted?

When did the imperial inspection of the school originate? The Record states: "The Three Kings and Four Dynasties took only the worthy as their teachers." The ruler of men receives the Mandate of Heaven and becomes its lord in order to serve as a teacher and model for the myriad people. Whether the people turn toward or away from him, obey or defy him, is truly in the ruler's charge. Sacrificing to the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men in the Directorate of Education, wearing the ceremonial cap and holding a shield, was the means to teach fraternal respect to the feudal lords. The schools of the Four Dynasties reached full completeness in the Zhou: with the Biyong hall at the capital of Hao, there was none who thought of not submitting, and thus it transformed the people and perfected customs. As for its institutions: at dawn a drum was beaten to summon the students, in order to rouse the multitude; wearing the deerskin cap, offerings of water plants were made to show respect for the Way; and those who did not follow the teachings were singled out and banished to the remote frontiers (Ji and Ji) to demonstrate punishment. Why was it done in such a manner—could it merely have been to furnish the outward ceremonies? There must have been something essential underlying it. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, each age performed these ceremonies, and the most prominent examples were: Emperor Ming of Han visiting the Biyong to pay homage to the aged; Emperor Taizong of Tang summoning renowned Confucians on a grand scale; and Emperor Renzong of Song expanding and repairing the school buildings and repeatedly gracing them with his imperial presence. All of them were meticulous in the trappings of grand display and prominent arrangement. To sum it up, in rustic and benighted states or during times of turmoil, they regarded schools like worn-out sandals or broken twigs; yet…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於天理民彝自反有不能巳者及治定功
成乃欲藉此以為粉飾太平之具則其意
巳失矣況圜橋觀聽內德巳慚沙門作俑
名教首禍其如學何蓋上所先者多欲而
施仁義之君下所司者積□□□車馬之
臣欲其興道致治也又安可得哉𥙿降風
漓愈趨愈下不有
卓然英睿者出孰能舉而正之我
聖祖卽位卽舉
===
郊壇之祭觀其
語起居注熊鼎曰此事雖不盡合古制然一
念事天之誠不敢忘一哉
皇心所以為
敬天之本者豫矣又于
紀元之始卽脩辟雍太學之規
遣使詣曲阜致祭而曰仲尼之道與天地並
今為天下主期明教化以行先王之道至哉
皇言所以繼往聖之統者全矣請得而揚之蓋
punctuated: 於天理民彝，自反有不能巳者。及治定功成，乃欲藉此以為粉飾太平之具，則其意巳失矣。況圜橋觀聽，內德巳慚；沙門作俑，名教首禍，其如學何？蓋上所先者，多欲而施仁義之君；下所司者，積□□□車馬之臣。欲其興道致治也，又安可得哉？𥙿降風漓，愈趨愈下，不有卓然英睿者出，孰能舉而正之？我聖祖卽位，卽舉郊壇之祭。觀其語起居注熊鼎曰：「此事雖不盡合古制，然一念事天之誠，不敢忘。」一哉皇心！所以為敬天之本者豫矣。又于紀元之始，卽脩辟雍太學之規，遣使詣曲阜致祭，而曰：「仲尼之道，與天地並。今為天下主，期明教化，以行先王之道。」至哉皇言！所以繼往聖之統者全矣。請得而揚之。蓋
translation_en:
… yet when they reflected upon heavenly principle and the constant norms of the people, there was something they could not stop themselves from doing. When order was established and their achievements were complete, however, they then wished to rely on this as an instrument to gloss over a time of peace, and thus the true meaning was already lost. How much more so when, surrounded by spectators at the circular moat of the Imperial Academy, their inner virtue was already cause for shame; and when welcoming Buddhist monks set a ruinous precedent that brought the foremost disaster upon Confucian moral teaching—what could they do for learning? For those at the top who took the lead were rulers full of desires who merely made a display of benevolence and righteousness, while those below who held office were ministers who accumulated [… three illegible characters: 積□□□, likely "years to boast of their" (積年以誇)] carriages and horses. Even if one wished for them to promote the Way and bring about good governance, how could that possibly be attained? As the ages declined and customs degenerated, things sank ever lower. Were it not for the emergence of a supremely brilliant and sagacious ruler, who could raise them up and set them right?

When our Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu] ascended the throne, he immediately instituted the sacrifices at the Suburban Altar. Consider what he said to Imperial Diarist Xiong Ding 熊鼎: "Although this matter does not entirely conform to ancient institutions, my single-minded sincerity in serving Heaven is something I dare not forget." How unified was the august mind! That by which he established the foundation for revering Heaven was already prepared in advance. Furthermore, at the very beginning of his reign era, he immediately restored the regulations of the Imperial Hall (Biyong) and the Directorate of Education (Taixue), and dispatched an envoy to Qufu 曲阜 to offer sacrifices, saying: "The Way of Zhongni [Confucius] stands on a par with Heaven and Earth. Now that I am the ruler of All Under Heaven, I aim to clarify moral transformation so as to practice the Way of the former kings." How supreme were the august words! That by which he continued the succession of the past sages was complete. Allow me to extol this. For…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖卽位之初正
順天應人之會
省躬之旨深達于天人之際而革前代山川
之號正
宗廟祭祀之規却祥瑞而重農桑因脩省而
諭羣臣無一事不當於天心則不必求之齋
明盛服之時而心已無往非敬矣
聖祖紀元之始適用夏變夷之機
觀心之旨首得乎道統之傳而斥方術焚其
===
書
書大學衍義于壁大易有
講契絕學之微言洪範有
訓示皇極之要道無一事而不合於聖人則
不必於視學之時而念已無適非誠矣
精誠謨烈啓佑後人
列聖一心守而勿失二百年來海宇晏清禎瑞
畢至謂非
天心之所昭假乎六經昭垂道德同文謂非
punctuated: 聖祖卽位之初，正順天應人之會。省躬之旨，深達于天人之際；而革前代山川之號，正宗廟祭祀之規，却祥瑞而重農桑，因脩省而諭羣臣，無一事不當於天心，則不必求之齋明盛服之時，而心已無往非敬矣。聖祖紀元之始，適用夏變夷之機。觀心之旨，首得乎道統之傳；而斥方術焚其書，書《大學衍義》于壁，《大易》有講，契絕學之微言，《洪範》有訓，示皇極之要道，無一事而不合於聖人，則不必於視學之時，而念已無適非誠矣。精誠謨烈，啓佑後人，列聖一心，守而勿失。二百年來，海宇晏清，禎瑞畢至，謂非天心之所昭假乎？六經昭垂，道德同文，謂非
translation_en: … At the very beginning of the Sacred Ancestor’s accession to the throne, it was precisely the juncture of complying with Heaven and responding to the people. The purport of His self-examination penetrated deeply into the correlation between Heaven and humanity. Moreover, in abolishing the titles bestowed upon mountains and rivers by previous dynasties, rectifying the regulations for sacrifices in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, rejecting auspicious omens while emphasizing agriculture and sericulture, and instructing thesembled officials on account of self-cultivation and reflection—there was not a single matter that did not accord with the mind of Heaven. Thus, one need not seek it only at the moment of fasting, purification, and donning grand ritual attire, for His mind was already reverent in every respect. At the very beginning of the Sacred Ancestor’s inaugurating His reign era, it met the precise opportunity of transforming the barbarians through Chinese ways. The purport of His contemplating the mind first grasped the transmission of the orthodox succession of the Way. Moreover, in rejecting occult arts and burning their books, inscribing the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) upon the palace walls, holding lectures on the Great Changes (Dayi) that tallied with the subtle words of lost learning, and providing instructions on the Great Plan (Hongfan) that revealed the essential Way of the Supreme Ultimate—there was not a single matter that did not conform to the sages. Thus, it did not have to be only at the time of inspecting the Imperial University, for His thoughts were already sincere in every direction. With utmost sincerity, His grand plans and illustrious achievements enlightened and aided His descendants; the successive Sacred Emperors, with a single mind, have preserved them without fail. For two hundred years, the realm within the seas has been tranquil and clear, and auspicious omens have all arrived—can this be said not to be the manifestation of Heaven’s favor? The Six Classics shine forth for posterity, and morality and writing are unified—can this be said not to be…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖學之所講明乎夫五緯曜芒而萬古不晦以
其有樞也百川分派而萬古不息以其有
宗也
皇上
聖哲篤生
英年握紀
至誠之心純一不雜殆與周之成王異世同
符
諒闇旣釋卽
===
===
命宗伯秩禮司空治途肇祀
南郊嚴對越之禮
駕臨太學
躬釋奠之儀大小臣工薄海內外罔不顒顒
然快覩
聖人之興矣執事又欲外儀章而别有所陳毋
亦忠愛無已之心乎愚也涓滴而增渤澥
之波壘土而加泰山之岏竊甞求之我將
之詩成王之所以祭天也惟天其右之外
punctuated: 聖學之所講明乎？夫五緯曜芒而萬古不晦，以其有樞也；百川分派而萬古不息，以其有宗也。皇上聖哲篤生，英年握紀，至誠之心，純一不雜，殆與周之成王異世同符。諒闇旣釋，卽命宗伯秩禮，司空治途。肇祀南郊，嚴對越之禮；駕臨太學，躬釋奠之儀。大小臣工、薄海內外，罔不顒顒然快覩聖人之興矣。執事又欲外儀章而别有所陳，毋亦忠愛無已之心乎？愚也涓滴而增渤澥之波，壘土而加泰山之岏。竊甞求之《我將》之詩，成王之所以祭天也，惟「天其右之」外，
translation_en:
… what the sagely learning has expounded and illuminated? Now, the five planets shine brightly and do not grow dim through ten thousand ages because they have an axis; the hundred rivers branch into tributaries and do not cease flowing through ten thousand ages because they have an ocean as their ancestral source.

His Majesty, endowed by birth with sagely wisdom, took hold of the imperial sceptre in his youthful prime. His mind of utmost sincerity is pure, unified, and unadulterated, almost matching tally across different eras with King Cheng of Zhou. Once the period of imperial mourning was concluded, he immediately commanded the Minister of Rites to order the ceremonies and the Minister of Works to prepare the roads. He initiated the sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, solemnizing the rites of standing in the presence of Heaven; his imperial carriage visited the Directorate of Education, where he personally performed the ceremonies of the libation sacrifice to Confucius. Officials great and small, within and beyond the four seas, without exception looked up in reverent admiration, delighted to witness the rise of a sage.

Yet Your Excellency wishes to set forth something further beyond the ceremonial regulations—is this not out of an boundless heart of loyalty and affection? Foolish as I am, my effort is like adding a tiny drop to swell the waves of the Bohai Sea, or piling up a clod of earth to heighten the peak of Mount Tai. I have ventured to seek it in the ode "Wo jiang" [in the Book of Odes], which is how King Cheng sacrificed to Heaven. Beyond the words "May Heaven stand at the right hand [to accept the offering]," …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不敢加一詞焉其敬天何至也而必曰我
其夙夜畏天之威于時保之夫人君一身
視聽言動無非天者不特
郊壇承祭之時而不聞不覩天命巳降監焉必
寅恭朝夕而不敢懈也必顧畏民嵒而不
敢康也于匹夫匹婦而常若勝予焉于祁
寒暑雨而常若怨咨焉不求諸在天之天
而求在已之天則天可對而後其敬始純
訪落之詩成王之所以求學也將予就之
===
繼猶判渙其自省何至也而必曰日就月
將學有緝熙于光明夫人君一身內外動
靜無非學者不特
臨幸講說之際而
深宮內庭君德實成就焉必謹於人心道心
之幾而不敢忽也必察于君子小人之際
而不敢輕也一話一言必惟成德之彥若
好若惡考諸惟皇之極不求聖于聖而求
聖于心則聖可學而後其德始進敬旣盡
punctuated: 不敢加一詞焉，其敬天何至也！而必曰：「我其夙夜畏天之威，于時保之。」夫人君一身，視聽言動無非天者，不特郊壇承祭之時，而不聞不覩，天命巳降監焉。必寅恭朝夕而不敢懈也，必顧畏民嵒而不敢康也。于匹夫匹婦，而常若勝予焉；于祁寒暑雨，而常若怨咨焉。不求諸在天之天，而求在已之天，則天可對，而後其敬始純。《訪落》之詩，成王之所以求學也。「將予就之，繼猶判渙」其自省何至也！而必曰：「日就月將，學有緝熙于光明。」夫人君一身，內外動靜無非學者，不特臨幸講說之際，而深宮內庭，君德實成就焉。必謹於人心道心之幾而不敢忽也，必察于君子小人之際而不敢輕也。一話一言，必惟成德之彥；若好若惡，考諸惟皇之極。不求聖于聖，而求聖于心，則聖可學，而後其德始進。敬旣盡…
translation_en:
…he dared not add a single word—how supreme was his reverence for Heaven! Yet he invariably said: "May I, morning and night, stand in awe of the majesty of Heaven, and thus preserve its favor." Indeed, in the person of the ruler, every sight, sound, word, and action is nothing less than Heaven itself. It is not merely at the time of performing sacrifices at the suburban altar; even when nothing is heard or seen, the Mandate of Heaven already looks down in inspection. One must be reverent and respectful morning and evening, never daring to be remiss; one must look with awe upon the perilousness of the common people, never daring to take ease. Toward ordinary men and women, one should constantly feel as though they might prevail over oneself; in times of bitter cold and sultry rain, one should constantly feel as though they are murmuring in resentment. When one seeks Heaven not in the Heaven above, but in the Heaven within oneself, then one can stand before Heaven, and only then does one's reverence become pure.

The ode "Taking Counsel at the Beginning of Reign" (Fangluo) shows how King Cheng pursued learning. Beyond the lines "Hold fast to my purpose, yet lest it still be scattered and dispersed"—how supreme was his self-examination!—he invariably said: "With daily progress and monthly advance, I shall learn until Continuous Brightness illuminates me." Indeed, in the person of the ruler, whether inside or outside, in activity or in stillness, nothing is apart from learning. It is not merely on occasions of imperial visits and classical lectures; rather, within the deep palaces and inner courts, the ruler's virtue is truly brought to completion. One must be vigilant over the subtleincipience between the human mind and the Moral Mind, never daring to neglect it; one must examine the distinction between the noble man and the petty man, never daring to treat it lightly. In every spoken word and utterance, one must look solely to men of accomplished virtue; in every like and dislike, one must measure it against the Supreme Standard of the August Sovereign. When one seeks sagehood not in the sages themselves, but within one's own mind, then sagehood can be learned, and only then does one's virtue advance. Once reverence has been fulfilled…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣則以之
尊祖以之
敬宗以之
祈穀以之
報賽皆於此乎行之德旣進矣則以此用人
以此納諫以此行政以此養民皆於此乎
推之我
皇上聰明
天啓
===
仁孝聿至此正周旦所謂自貽哲命之初所其
無逸之日也自玆以往苟禁防稍弛則知
慮或分涵養未純則心志或逸所以乗時
而造就之者不有資於輔養乎啓沃有講
章而微辭奧義或未盡於心得史書有疏
解而嘉言格論或未罄於面陳所以隨事
而充廣之者不有賴於弼直乎今
經筵日
御無輟干寒暑章疏徹
punctuated: 矣，則以之尊祖，以之敬宗，以之祈穀，以之報賽，皆於此乎行之；德旣進矣，則以此用人，以此納諫，以此行政，以此養民，皆於此乎推之。我皇上聰明天啓，仁孝聿至，此正周旦所謂「自貽哲命」之初，「所其無逸」之日也。自玆以往，苟禁防稍弛，則知慮或分；涵養未純，則心志或逸。所以乗時而造就之者，不有資於輔養乎？啓沃有講章，而微辭奧義或未盡於心得；史書有疏解，而嘉言格論或未罄於面陳。所以隨事而充廣之者，不有賴於弼直乎？今經筵日御，無輟干寒暑；章疏徹
translation_en:
… has been exhausted, then through it honoring the ancestors, through it revering the lineage, through it praying for grain, and through it offering thanksgiving sacrifices—all are practiced from this. Once virtue has advanced, then through this employing men, through this accepting remonstrance, through this administering government, and through this nourishing the people—all are extended from this.

Our August Emperor, his intelligence and insight inspired by Heaven and his benevolence and filial piety having reached the utmost, is right now at what Zhou Dan 周旦 [the Duke of Zhou] called the beginning of "bequeathing to oneself a wise decree" and the days of "making luxury-free diligence one's dwelling place." From this point onward, if restraints and precautions are slightly relaxed, his wisdom and deliberation might be divided; if his moral cultivation is not yet pure, his mind and will might stray into ease. To seize the moment and bring his cultivation to completion—does this not depend upon tutorial nourishment? For enlightenment and guidance there are lecture texts, yet their subtle words and profound meanings might not be fully realized in personal comprehension; for historical records there are commentaries and explanations, yet their fine words and standard discourses might not be exhausted in face-to-face presentations. To expand and broaden his understanding in accordance with affairs—does this not rely upon corrective assistance? Now the Classics Mat is attended daily without interruption in winter's cold or summer's heat [reading 于 for 干], and memorials are thoroughly…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
覽不倦于昕夕眞德秀所謂惟學惟敬惟親
君子旣交盡而無歉卽此可以近法
列祖遠紹虞周而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣書曰
念終始典于學愚也敢以此規詩曰於乎
皇王繼序思不忘愚又敢以此
頌
第二問
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭蔣批聖賢言性隨時立訓其
===
旨本不異是作發揮明悉非剽說比錄之
考試官敎諭楊批醞藉宏深議論明正窺
性學之奧者敬服敬服
考試官敎諭朱批知性盡性學聖功夫也
此作得之
達乎理之原者可與論性矣明乎性之初
者可與語學矣所謂理之原者何無極之
眞天載之神純粹至善者也固性之從出
也所謂性之初者何不雜于質不囿于氣
punctuated:
覽不倦于昕夕。眞德秀所謂惟學、惟敬、惟親君子，旣交盡而無歉，卽此可以近法列祖，遠紹虞、周，而陋漢、唐、宋於不足言矣。《書》曰：「念終始典于學。」愚也敢以此規。《詩》曰：「於乎皇王，繼序思不忘。」愚又敢以此頌。

第二問
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭蔣批：聖賢言性，隨時立訓，其旨本不異。是作發揮明悉，非剽說比，錄之。
考試官敎諭楊批：醞藉宏深，議論明正，窺性學之奧者，敬服，敬服。
考試官敎諭朱批：知性盡性，學聖功夫也。此作得之。

達乎理之原者，可與論性矣；明乎性之初者，可與語學矣。所謂理之原者何？無極之眞，天載之神，純粹至善者也，固性之從出也。所謂性之初者何？不雜于質，不囿于氣，
translation_en:
… perusal, untiring from morning to evening. Since what Zhen Dexiu 眞德秀 called devoting oneself solely to learning, to reverence, and to drawing close to gentlemen has all been fulfilled without deficiency, by this very means His Majesty can take the succession of imperial ancestors as a near model, continue the line of Yu [Shun] and Zhou from afar, and look down upon Han, Tang, and Song as unworthy of mention. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Be mindful from beginning to end to be constantly devoted to learning." In my simplicity, I venture to offer this as admonition. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Oh, the august kings! Continuing the succession, we think of them without forgetting." In my simplicity, I further venture to offer this as praise.

Second Policy Question
Che Pingchen 車聘臣
Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Sages and worthies, in speaking of human nature, established their teachings according to the times, yet their purport was fundamentally no different. This essay expounds the matter with clarity and thoroughness; it is not comparable to plagiarized talk. Record it.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: Cultivated and profoundly deep, its arguments clear and upright—one who has peered into the mysteries of the study of human nature. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Knowing one's nature and fully realizing one's nature are the effort of learning to become a sage. This essay has grasped it.

Only with one who has penetrated the source of principle can one discuss human nature; only with one who understands the beginning of human nature can one speak of learning. What is meant by the source of principle? It is the reality of the Ultimateless, the spirit of Heaven's operations—pure and supremely good; indeed, it is that from which human nature issues. What is meant by the beginning of human nature? Unmixed with physical substance and unagitated by vital force, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有善而無惡者也乃理之本然也是故性
可以恒言可以善言而不可以清濁厚薄
論也清濁可以言氣厚薄可以言質而不
可以論性之初也嗚呼人性皆善也人性
之初皆相近也而岐而二之是豈知性者
哉君子明乎帝降之原察乎民秉之始則
諸說之紛紛可以折衷之而無惑矣且性
之說奚始乎自伏羲氏之一畫而陰陽之
理著自堯授舜以允執厥中之一言而精
===
一之旨闡雖未甞明言性而性之說已肇
矣及成湯之誥曰上帝降衷于下民若有
恒性衷者中也言乎其弗偏也恒者常也
言乎其弗易也弗偏弗易雖未甞明言善
而善之旨已昭矣嗣後一變爲春秋而詐
力興再變爲戰國而功利熾于是近者習
而遠矣乃不曰吾自背馳之而諉曰我性
則然善者流而惡矣乃不曰吾自戕賊之
而諉曰我性則然孔子憂性學之失真也
punctuated: 有善而無惡者也，乃理之本然也。是故性可以恒言，可以善言，而不可以清濁厚薄論也。清濁可以言氣，厚薄可以言質，而不可以論性之初也。嗚呼！人性皆善也，人性之初皆相近也，而岐而二之，是豈知性者哉！君子明乎帝降之原，察乎民秉之始，則諸說之紛紛，可以折衷之而無惑矣。且性之說奚始乎？自伏羲氏之一畫，而陰陽之理著；自堯授舜以「允執厥中」之一言，而精一之旨闡。雖未甞明言性，而性之說已肇矣。及成湯之誥曰：「上帝降衷于下民，若有恒性。」衷者，中也，言乎其弗偏也；恒者，常也，言乎其弗易也。弗偏弗易，雖未甞明言善，而善之旨已昭矣。嗣後一變爲春秋，而詐力興；再變爲戰國，而功利熾。于是近者習而遠矣，乃不曰「吾自背馳之」，而諉曰「我性則然」；善者流而惡矣，乃不曰「吾自戕賊之」，而諉曰「我性則然」。孔子憂性學之失真也，
translation_en:
…having goodness and no evil; it is the original state of principle. For this reason, human nature may be spoken of as constant, and may be spoken of as good, yet it cannot be discussed in terms of clarity or turbidity, thickness or thinness. Clarity and turbidity may describe vital force (qi 氣), and thickness and thinness may describe physical endowment (zhi 質), yet they cannot be used to discuss the beginning of human nature. Alas! Human nature is all good, and in its beginning human nature is all similar; to divide them into two—how could that be the mark of one who understands human nature? When the gentleman comprehends the origin of what the Supreme Lord bestows and examines the beginning of what the people hold fast to, then the multitude of conflicting doctrines can be weighed and reconciled without confusion.

Moreover, where did the doctrine of human nature begin? From the single stroke of Fuxi 伏羲, the principle of yin and yang became manifest; from Yao's 堯 charge to Shun 舜 in the single phrase "sincerely hold fast the Mean," the purport of refinement and singleness was elucidated. Although they never explicitly spoke of human nature, the doctrine of human nature had already been initiated. When it came to the Announcement of Tang the Successful (Cheng Tang 成湯), he said: "The Supreme Lord has conferred the moral mean upon the common people; if they follow their constant nature..." "Moral mean" (zhong 衷) means the center, speaking of its being unskewed; "constant" (heng 恒) means unchanging, speaking of its being immutable. Being unskewed and immutable, although he did not explicitly speak of goodness, the purport of goodness was already clear.

Thereafter, with a first transformation into the Spring and Autumn period, deceit and force arose; with a second transformation into the Warring States period, utility and profit blazed forth. Thereupon what was similar became distant through practice, yet people did not say, "I myself have turned away from it," instead shifting the blame by saying, "My nature is simply so." What was good degenerated into evil, yet people did not say, "I myself have violated and ruined it," instead shifting the blame by saying, "My nature is simply so." Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) worried that the learning of human nature was losing its truth,…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而有性相近之說焉近者對遠言之譬之
五方童子習於齊則爲齊語習於楚則爲
楚語甚至重九譯而不能相通然其初呱
呱之聲舉相似也朱子所謂以其初而言
之則皆不甚相遠者是也是性之爲體固
不離乎氣質而亦不囿於氣質之中矣孟
子憂聖道之失而欲閑之也而有性善之
說焉善者對惡言之譬諸眾水之流在江
淮則爲江淮在河漢則爲河漢甚至千支
===
萬派之不一然其就下之勢罔不一也朱
子所謂人之情本但可以爲善而不可以
爲惡者是也是聖賢之爲教言雖若有異
同而意則實無牴牾矣謂孟子之見不出
于孔氏不可也謂孟子非有功于聖門不
可也夫性一理也理一性也上古忘象而
得意故存之而不論聖人識精以達微故
論之而不辯君子貞教以軌物故辯之而
極詳孟子而下羣說競起告子立赤幟以
punctuated: 而有「性相近」之說焉。近者，對遠言之。譬之五方童子，習於齊則爲齊語，習於楚則爲楚語，甚至重九譯而不能相通，然其初呱呱之聲，舉相似也。朱子所謂「以其初而言之，則皆不甚相遠」者，是也。是性之爲體，固不離乎氣質，而亦不囿於氣質之中矣。孟子憂聖道之失而欲閑之也，而有「性善」之說焉。善者，對惡言之。譬諸眾水之流，在江淮則爲江淮，在河漢則爲河漢，甚至千支萬派之不一，然其就下之勢，罔不一也。朱子所謂「人之情本但可以爲善，而不可以爲惡」者，是也。是聖賢之爲教，言雖若有異同，而意則實無牴牾矣。謂孟子之見不出于孔氏，不可也；謂孟子非有功于聖門，不可也。夫性一理也，理一性也。上古忘象而得意，故存之而不論；聖人識精以達微，故論之而不辯；君子貞教以軌物，故辯之而極詳。孟子而下，羣說競起。告子立赤幟以
translation_en:
…and thus put forward the doctrine that "natures are close to one another." "Close" is spoken of in contrast to "distant." Take, for example, children from the five directions: if accustomed to Qi, they speak the language of Qi; if accustomed to Chu, they speak the language of Chu; and at the extreme, even through ninefold translation they cannot understand one another—yet at the very beginning, the sound of their infant cries is altogether similar. What Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] meant when he said, "Speaking of it in terms of its beginning, none are very far apart," is precisely this. Thus, the substance of human nature inherently is not separate from physical endowment (qizhi), yet neither is it confined within physical endowment.

Mencius, worried about the loss of the Sage's Way and wishing to defend it, put forward the doctrine that "human nature is good." "Good" is spoken of in contrast to "evil." Take, for example, the flowing of the multitude of waters: in the Yangzi and the Huai, they become the Yangzi and the Huai; in the Yellow River and the Han, they become the Yellow River and the Han; and at the extreme, they diverge into a thousand branches and ten thousand streams—yet in their tendency to flow downward, there is none that is not the same. What Master Zhu meant when he said, "Human feelings (qing) in their origin are only capable of doing good and are not capable of doing evil," is precisely this.

Thus, in the teachings established by the sages and worthies, although their words seem to have differences and similarities, their underlying meaning in truth has no contradiction. To say that Mencius's view did not derive from Confucius is impermissible; to say that Mencius made no meritorious contribution to the school of the Sage is likewise impermissible. Now, human nature is one with principle (li), and principle is one with human nature. In high antiquity, people forgot the outward emblems and grasped the inner meaning, so they preserved it without discussing it; the Sage [Confucius] possessed refined insight that penetrated the subtle, so he discussed it without debating it; the superior man [Mencius] rectified the teachings to provide a standard for all things, so he debated it in the utmost detail. From Mencius onward, a multitude of doctrines arose in competition. Gaozi raised his own red banner to…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
角勝天下杞柳湍水之喻起性惡與善惡
混之端矣荀子謂枸木必檃栝而後直鈍
金必礱厲而後利非杞柳之說乎楊子謂
有刀者礱諸有玉者錯諸不礱不錯焉攸
用非湍水之說乎此其意非不欲天下同
歸於善與孟氏之書相左右豈知直利卽
性檃厲非矯也刀玉本器礱錯非強也故
東西上下之折情才四端之說辭而闢之
不遺餘力豈好辯哉不得已也自今觀之
===
孟子之言善也窮其本始而究理之原循
其性之自然也諸子之言性也迷其本始
而徇氣之迹舍其性之本然也吁性豈易
言哉宋儒之善言性者莫如程伯子定性
一書其言普物無心者天地之常順事無
情者聖人之常廓然大公物來順應者君
子法天地希聖人之要斯言也真有以窺
孔孟之奧探性命之原矣說者疑其有惡
亦不可不謂性之說似與性善相近之旨
punctuated: 角勝天下，杞柳、湍水之喻，起性惡與善惡混之端矣。荀子謂「枸木必檃栝而後直，鈍金必礱厲而後利」，非杞柳之說乎？楊子謂「有刀者礱諸，有玉者錯諸，不礱不錯，焉攸用」，非湍水之說乎？此其意非不欲天下同歸於善，與孟氏之書相左右，豈知直、利卽性，檃、厲非矯也；刀、玉本器，礱、錯非強也。故東西上下之折，情、才、四端之說，辭而闢之，不遺餘力，豈好辯哉？不得已也。自今觀之，孟子之言善也，窮其本始而究理之原，循其性之自然也；諸子之言性也，迷其本始而徇氣之迹，舍其性之本然也。吁！性豈易言哉？宋儒之善言性者，莫如程伯子《定性》一書。其言「普物無心者，天地之常；順事無情者，聖人之常；廓然大公，物來順應者，君子法天地、希聖人之要」，斯言也，真有以窺孔、孟之奧，探性命之原矣。說者疑其有「惡亦不可不謂性」之說，似與性善、相近之旨…
translation_en: …compete for mastery in the world. His analogies of the杞柳 (corchorus willow) and 湍水 (whirling water) gave rise to the beginnings of the doctrines that human nature is evil and that good and evil are mixed in it. Xunzi 荀子 said, "Crooked wood must undergo steaming and bending before it becomes straight; blunt metal must be ground and whetted before it becomes sharp." Is this not the argument of the willow? Yangzi 楊子 [Yang Xiong 楊雄] said, "He who has a blade grinds it; he who has jade polishes it. Without grinding and polishing, of what use are they?" Is this not the argument of the whirling water? In their intentions, it was not that they did not wish the whole world to return together to goodness, thereby assisting the writings of Master Meng [Mencius]; yet how could they know that straightness and sharpness are themselves the nature, and that bending and whetting are not a forced distortion; that the blade and the jade are inherently vessels, and that grinding and polishing are not an external compulsion? Therefore, with the refutations regarding east and west, up and down, and the explanations of genuine feelings, natural endowment, and the Four Beginnings, Mencius denounced and refuted them, sparing no effort. Was it because he was fond of disputing? He had no alternative. Viewed from the present, when Mencius spoke of goodness, he plumbed its fundamental beginning and investigated the source of principle, following what is spontaneous in human nature; when the various other philosophers spoke of human nature, they lost sight of its fundamental beginning and pursued the traces of material force (qi), abandoning what is original in human nature. Alas! Is human nature easy to speak of? Among the Song Confucians who excelled at discussing human nature, none surpassed the letter on Settling the Nature (Dingxing shu) by Master Cheng the Elder [Cheng Hao 程顥]. It states: "To pervade all things without a deliberate mind is the constancy of Heaven and Earth; to respond to affairs without personal emotion is the constancy of the sage; to be vast and utterly impartial, responding smoothly to things as they come, is the essential way for the noble man to model himself on Heaven and Earth and aspire to be a sage." These words truly succeeded in peering into the profound depths of Confucius and Mencius and probing the source of human nature and the decree of Heaven. Yet commentators doubt his statement that "evil also cannot but be called nature," which seems to… with the purport that human nature is good and that natures are close to one another…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或戾豈知孔孟之言直探乎天命之體程
子之言示人以澄治之功夫性之體本善
也猶水之體本清也善失而流於惡甚至
於倍蓰無算者謂之非性固不可謂為性
之本然可乎清失而流於濁甚至於塵滓
莫辨者謂之非水固不可謂為水之本然
可乎謂越椒為滅宗者以豺聲也使能如
周處之速改焉何至於滅耶謂叔魚為賄
亡者以豕喙也使能如戴淵之急反焉何
===
至於亡耶知下愚之不出於天則惡之非
性也明矣知暴棄之皆由於巳則性之貴
乎善反而非有定也又明矣孟子發性善
之旨于仁義充塞之時所以距詖行正人
心者功固不在禹下程子闡性即理之旨
于理學幾晦之日所以繼往聖開來學者
功亦不在孟子下矣後儒取譬於日借喻
於水豈謾言哉觀日者有自蔀屋之下觀
者皆雲翳也有自山之中而觀者雲與日
punctuated: 或戾。豈知孔孟之言，直探乎天命之體；程子之言，示人以澄治之功。夫性之體本善也，猶水之體本清也。善失而流於惡，甚至於倍蓰無算者，謂之非性固不可，謂為性之本然可乎？清失而流於濁，甚至於塵滓莫辨者，謂之非水固不可，謂為水之本然可乎？謂越椒為滅宗者，以豺聲也，使能如周處之速改焉，何至於滅耶？謂叔魚為賄亡者，以豕喙也，使能如戴淵之急反焉，何至於亡耶？知下愚之不出於天，則惡之非性也明矣；知暴棄之皆由於巳，則性之貴乎善反而非有定也又明矣。孟子發「性善」之旨于仁義充塞之時，所以距詖行、正人心者，功固不在禹下；程子闡「性即理」之旨于理學幾晦之日，所以繼往聖、開來學者，功亦不在孟子下矣。後儒取譬於日，借喻於水，豈謾言哉？觀日者，有自蔀屋之下觀者，皆雲翳也；有自山之中而觀者，雲與日…
translation_en: …might conflict with them. How could they fail to understand that the words of Confucius and Mencius probe directly into the substance of Heaven's mandate, whereas Master Cheng's words show people the effort of clarifying and governing it? Now, the substance of human nature is originally good, just as the substance of water is originally clear. When goodness is lost and flows into evil, even to the point of differing twice, fivefold, or beyond calculation, one certainly cannot say that it is not nature, yet how could one call it the original state of nature? When clarity is lost and flows into turbidity, even to the point where dust and dregs cannot be distinguished from the water, one certainly cannot say that it is not water, yet how could one call it the original state of water? It was said that Yue Jiao 越椒 would destroy his clan because he had the voice of a jackal; yet had he been able to reform swiftly like Zhou Chu 周處, how would he have come to destruction? It was said that Shuyu 叔魚 would perish through bribery because he had the snout of a pig; yet had he been able to turn back urgently like Dai Yuan 戴淵, how would he have come to ruin? Once we know that the lowest stupidity does not issue from Heaven, it is clear that evil is not human nature; once we know that self-violence and self-abandonment all stem from oneself, it is again clear that what matters for human nature is skillfully returning to it, rather than its being immutably fixed. Mencius set forth the doctrine that "human nature is good" at a time when benevolence and righteousness were blocked up; in repelling one-sided deeds and rectifying people's minds, his merit was truly not inferior to that of Yu 禹. Master Cheng elucidated the doctrine that "human nature is principle" in days when the Learning of Principle was nearly obscured; in carrying on from past sages and opening the way for future scholars, his merit was likewise not inferior to that of Mencius. When later Confucians drew comparisons to the sun and borrowed metaphors from water, how could those have been idle words? Among those who gaze at the sun, there are those who view it from beneath a shaded hovel, where all is cloud and haze; there are those who view it from halfway up a mountain, where clouds and sun…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
半也惟登泰山之巔而觀之則雲霧在下
杲日當空矣觀水者有自下流觀者皆濁
流也有自江漢合流而觀者清與濁半也
惟窮岷山之原而觀之則山下出泉靜清
無殽矣荀子其蔀屋下流之見乎楊子其
山半與合流之見乎孟子則直登泰嶽之
巔窮岷山之原而有真見乎言雖不同各
因所見而已矣見雖不同各隨所造而已
矣執事又謂觀性當觀其初請即朱子之
===
言以溯孟氏而究言之可乎乍見孺子將
入於井一事之初也其真心之發曷甞參
以要譽惡聲之私哉平旦之好惡一日之
初也其良心之露曷甞參以旦晝之所爲
哉人少則慕父母一生之初也其一念之
真曷甞參以好色慕君之情哉此則如水
之未波而澄也如日之未翳而瑩也粹然
善而已學者能即此而充之一事之始終
皆乍見時也衆念不得而間之則事即理
punctuated: 半也；惟登泰山之巔而觀之，則雲霧在下，杲日當空矣。觀水者有自下流觀者，皆濁流也；有自江漢合流而觀者，清與濁半也；惟窮岷山之原而觀之，則山下出泉，靜清無殽矣。荀子其蔀屋、下流之見乎？楊子其山半與合流之見乎？孟子則直登泰嶽之巔、窮岷山之原而有真見乎？言雖不同，各因所見而已矣；見雖不同，各隨所造而已矣。執事又謂觀性當觀其初，請即朱子之言以溯孟氏而究言之，可乎？乍見孺子將入於井，一事之初也，其真心之發，曷甞參以要譽、惡聲之私哉？平旦之好惡，一日之初也，其良心之露，曷甞參以旦晝之所爲哉？人少則慕父母，一生之初也，其一念之真，曷甞參以好色、慕君之情哉？此則如水之未波而澄也，如日之未翳而瑩也，粹然善而已。學者能即此而充之：一事之始終，皆乍見時也，衆念不得而間之，則事即理
translation_en:
… half; only when one ascends to the summit of Mount Tai to observe it do the clouds and mists lie below while the bright sun hangs high in the sky. Among those who observe water, there are those who observe it from the lower reaches, where all is muddy current; there are those who observe it from the confluence of the Yangtze and Han rivers, where the clear and the muddy are half and half; only when one traces it all the way to its source in the Min Mountains to observe it does the spring issue forth from beneath the mountain, still, clear, and unmixed. Is not Xunzi's view that of the shaded hut and the lower reaches? Is not Yangzi's [Yang Xiong's] view that of halfway up the mountain and the confluence of the rivers? And did not Mencius directly ascend to the summit of Mount Tai and trace the source in the Min Mountains to attain true insight? Although their words differ, each simply follows from what he saw; although their views differ, each simply accords with the level he attained.

Your Excellency also states that in observing human nature one ought to observe its beginning. May I be permitted to draw upon Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi's] words to trace back to Mencius and discuss this exhaustively? Suddenly seeing a child about to fall into a well is the beginning of a single affair; in that stirring of the true mind, how could it ever be mingled with the selfish motives of seeking praise from the child's parents or dreading a bad reputation? The likes and dislikes of the calm of dawn are the beginning of a single day; in that manifestation of the innate good mind, how could it ever be mingled with the doings of the daytime? That a person when young yearns for his parents is the beginning of a whole life; in that genuineness of a single thought, how could it ever be mingled with the passions of desiring beauty or yearning for a ruler? This is like water that is clear before it has risen in waves, or like the sun that is lustrous before it has been obscured by clouds—purely good and nothing more. If the student can take his start from this and fully extend it: when from beginning to end a single affair is entirely as at the moment of that sudden sight, and a multitude of distracting thoughts cannot come between, then the affair is itself Principle …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣一日之好惡皆平旦時也旦晝不得而
梏之則可語日至矣一生之耄倪皆孩提
時也婚宦不得而移之則可語終身慕矣
學而至此是之謂知性知性則知止矣知
止則定矣定則無將迎無內外無自私用
智而大公之體立順應之用行矣體用一
顯微合而天地聖人之常不在君子而在
我矣斯固盡性之極功而學性者之標準
也彼謂敎人性非所先者烏足以達此哉
===
雖然天下之言性亦多矣然性不貴言貴
盡也必如曾子之愼獨而後謂之盡必如
周子之研幾而後謂之盡必如程子之定
性而後謂之盡性盡則天地之性自存氣
質之性自弗性矣悟孔子所謂性近雖有
舊習而吾可奪也識孟子所謂性善雖有
頹俗而吾可挽也斯非所謂揭日於重光
廻狂瀾而東之者乎繼程子而興者世豈
無其人耶愚也有志而未得其要惟執事
punctuated:
矣；一日之好惡，皆平旦時也，旦晝不得而梏之，則可語日至矣；一生之耄倪，皆孩提時也，婚宦不得而移之，則可語終身慕矣。學而至此，是之謂知性。知性則知止矣，知止則定矣。定則無將迎、無內外、無自私用智，而大公之體立，順應之用行矣。體用一，顯微合，而天地聖人之常，不在君子而在我矣。斯固盡性之極功，而學性者之標準也。彼謂敎人性非所先者，烏足以達此哉！
雖然，天下之言性亦多矣，然性不貴言，貴盡也。必如曾子之愼獨，而後謂之盡；必如周子之研幾，而後謂之盡；必如程子之定性，而後謂之盡。性盡，則天地之性自存，氣質之性自弗性矣。悟孔子所謂性近，雖有舊習而吾可奪也；識孟子所謂性善，雖有頹俗而吾可挽也。斯非所謂揭日於重光、廻狂瀾而東之者乎？繼程子而興者，世豈無其人耶？愚也有志而未得其要，惟執事
translation_en:
…; if all the likes and dislikes throughout a single day are as they are at dawn, and the actions of the daytime cannot fetter them, then one can speak of reaching it daily; if throughout a whole lifetime, in both old age and youth, one is as one was in infancy, and marriage and official career cannot alter it, then one can speak of yearning for one's parents all one's life. When learning reaches this point, this is called knowing human nature. Knowing human nature, one knows where to abide; knowing where to abide, one is settled. Being settled, there is neither anticipation nor lingering, neither inner nor outer, neither selfishness nor contrivance; the substance of supreme impartiality is established, and the function of spontaneous response is carried out. Substance and function become one, the manifest and the subtle are united, and the constancy of Heaven, Earth, and the sages resides not in the noble man alone, but within myself. This is indeed the ultimate achievement of fully realizing human nature, and the standard for those who study human nature. How could those who claim that human nature is not the first priority in teaching people ever attain this!

Even so, discussions of human nature in the world have been numerous indeed; yet with human nature, what is valued is not speaking of it, but fully realizing it. Only when one is like Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) in being watchful over oneself when alone can it be called fully realized; only when one is like Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) in investigating the subtle incipient tendencies can it be called fully realized; only when one is like Master Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥) in settling one's nature can it be called fully realized. When human nature is fully realized, the nature of Heaven and Earth is naturally preserved, and the psychophysical nature is naturally not claimed as one's true nature. Awakening to what Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) called human natures being close to one another, even if there are old habits, we can overcome them; recognizing what Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) called human nature being good, even if there are decadent customs, we can reverse them. Is this not what is meant by holding up the sun in renewed brilliance and turning back the raging waves to make them flow east? Among those who rise up to succeed the Masters Cheng, how could the world lack such a person? Ignorant as I am, I have the aspiration but have not yet grasped its essentials; I only pray that Your Excellency…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
揭性眞而進敎之幸甚
第三問
陳其美
同考試官敎諭羅批粵風俗談之比比而莫
爲正救子獨以士習歸之敎化寓轉移之機其根
極理要者錄之以式
考試官敎諭楊批民風士習統之在上不
在下是作得旨而文復爾雅取之
考試官敎諭朱批以政本立論有味乎其
===
言之也可以式矣
善天下之俗者不可不愼其機挽天下之
敝者不可不求其本機也者倡於一人而
倣於眾人興於一時而流於百世相率而
趨莫知所自不愼其機而欲俗之善也難
矣本也者運之於上而導之於下行之於
近而通之於遠不令而行不疾而速不求
其本而欲敝之挽也難矣士習者其民風
之機乎政敎者其士習之本乎知此始可
punctuated:
揭性眞而進敎之，幸甚。

第三問
陳其美
同考試官敎諭羅批：粵風俗談之比比，而莫爲正救。子獨以士習歸之，敎化寓轉移之機，其根極理要者。錄之以式。
考試官敎諭楊批：民風士習，統之在上，不在下。是作得旨，而文復爾雅，取之。
考試官敎諭朱批：以政本立論，有味乎其言之也，可以式矣。

善天下之俗者，不可不愼其機；挽天下之敝者，不可不求其本。機也者，倡於一人而倣於眾人，興於一時而流於百世，相率而趨，莫知所自。不愼其機，而欲俗之善也難矣。本也者，運之於上而導之於下，行之於近而通之於遠，不令而行，不疾而速。不求其本，而欲敝之挽也難矣。士習者，其民風之機乎！政敎者，其士習之本乎！知此，始可…
translation_en:
…reveal the truth of human nature and advance me in your instruction, I would be most fortunate.

Third Question
Chen Qimei 陳其美
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Luo 羅: People talk everywhere about the customs of Guangdong, yet none offer a proper remedy. You alone attribute them to the habits of the literati, wherein moral transformation holds the pivot of change—this gets to the very root of the principle and its essentials. Recorded to serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yang 楊: Popular customs and literati habits are governed from above, not from below. This essay grasps the main point, and its prose is moreover refined and elegant; I select it.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱: Establishing the argument upon the foundation of governance, how meaningful are its words! It may well serve as a model.

Those who would improve the customs of the world must be careful about their pivot; those who would reverse the ills of the world must seek out their root. As for the pivot, it is initiated by one person and imitated by the multitude, arising in a single moment and flowing down through a hundred generations, with people leading one another forward without knowing whence it came. If one is not careful about this pivot, desiring that customs become good will be difficult indeed. As for the root, it is set in motion from above and guides those below, practiced what is near and extending to what is far, proceeding without commands and advancing swiftly without haste. If one does not seek out this root, desiring that ills be reversed will be difficult indeed. Are not the habits of the literati the pivot of popular customs? Is not governance and instruction the root of the habits of the literati? Only when one understands this can one…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
語於東粵之風俗矣夫風俗何自而起乎
上行下效謂之風衆心安定謂之俗風之
所在如影之於形響之於聲嚴刑不為禁
重賞不為勸俗所喜好非有徴發期會而
遠近若一其所係於民者非小於此而無
所以化導之可乎故一其道德同其風俗
命太師陳詩以觀民風令輶軒循行天下
問俗凡所以維持誨導之者無所不至記
曰脩其敎不易其俗齊其政不易其宜管
===
子曰禮義廉恥是謂四維皆言化導之具
也夫風俗又何自而敝乎上無以敎則下
無以學情欲不節則流好尚不謹則辟風
俗不厚則偷民情愈趨愈下將至於大壞
極敗而不可反而其本初則不然於此而
無所以救正之可乎故齊其法制詳其命
令禮禁未然之前法施已然之後所以挽
回整頓之者無所不至易曰窮則變變則
通通則久董子曰已雕已琢還反其樸皆
punctuated: 語於東粵之風俗矣。夫風俗何自而起乎？上行下效謂之風，衆心安定謂之俗。風之所在，如影之於形、響之於聲，嚴刑不為禁，重賞不為勸；俗所喜好，非有徴發期會，而遠近若一。其所係於民者非小，於此而無所以化導之，可乎？故一其道德，同其風俗，命太師陳詩以觀民風，令輶軒循行天下問俗，凡所以維持誨導之者，無所不至。《記》曰：「脩其敎不易其俗，齊其政不易其宜。」《管子》曰：「禮、義、廉、恥，是謂四維。」皆言化導之具也。夫風俗又何自而敝乎？上無以敎，則下無以學；情欲不節則流，好尚不謹則辟，風俗不厚則偷。民情愈趨愈下，將至於大壞極敗而不可反，而其本初則不然。於此而無所以救正之，可乎？故齊其法制，詳其命令，禮禁未然之前，法施已然之後，所以挽回整頓之者，無所不至。《易》曰：「窮則變，變則通，通則久。」董子曰：「已雕已琢，還反其樸。」皆…
translation_en:
… speak of the customs of Eastern Yue [Guangdong]. Now, how do customs arise? What superiors practice and inferiors emulate is called a "prevailing trend" (feng); what settles in the minds of the multitude is called "custom" (su). Where a prevailing trend exists, it is like a shadow to a form or an echo to a sound: severe punishments cannot prohibit it, nor heavy rewards encourage it. What custom delights in requires no conscription or appointed gathering, yet near and far are as one. Its bearing upon the people is no small matter; in the face of this, how could one lack the means to transform and guide them? Therefore, rulers unified morality and harmonized customs, commanding the Grand Music Master (taishi) to present poems in order to observe the popular ethos, and ordering light-carriage emissaries (youxuan) to tour the realm and inquire after local customs—going to every length in the means of sustaining, instructing, and guiding them. The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "Cultivate their instruction without changing their customs; make uniform their governance without changing what is suited to them." The Master Guan (Guanzi) says: "Propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame—these are called the Four Bonds." Both speak of the instruments of transformation and guidance.

And how, in turn, do customs fall into decay? When superiors lack the means to instruct, inferiors lack the means to learn. When passions and desires are not moderated, they become dissolute; when preferences and fashions are not guarded, they become perverse; when customs are not generous, they become shiftless. As the dispositions of the people sink ever lower, they will reach a point of great ruin and extreme corruption from which there is no return—even though they were not so in their original beginning. In the face of this, how could one lack the means to rescue and rectify them? Therefore, rulers made uniform their laws and institutions and made detailed their ordinances and commands, using propriety to prohibit misconduct before it arises and applying the law after it has occurred—going to every length in the means of restoring and poner in order. The Book of Changes (Yijing) says: "When a state of affairs is exhausted, it changes; through change, it achieves continuity; through continuity, it endures." Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] said: "Once carved and polished, return to uncarved simplicity." All of these…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
言反正之機也故曰廉耻者士人之美節
敎化者朝廷之急務不知敎化而欲望士
習民風之善也難矣夫粤天下之澤國也
負山阻海火耕水耨其民樸重喭慤若難
遽以道德一之者然其貞元未散良心易
感而嘉言易入一有賢者倡之其從善更
輕而守志益堅也是故高固以才能相楚
威王始進鐸椒春秋引君當道因致五羊
銜榖之瑞南海之民風動而圖像以表厥
===
賢自是人文漸盛民俗漸淳志曰衣冠禮
樂無異中州又曰今之交廣古之鄒魯其
化民成俗之休可想見矣自兹以後代不
乏賢士勤于德民易其俗若羅威唐頌之
厚彝倫篤行誼則民化而敬老親親矣馮
元之通經術登膴仕則民化而博學好古
矣俗崇正道而陋緇黄非因梁觀國之以
禮敦俗乎俗守名義而樂恬退非由崔與
之之清風高節乎俗皆務學非因二陳以
punctuated: 言反正之機也。故曰：廉耻者，士人之美節；敎化者，朝廷之急務。不知敎化而欲望士習民風之善也，難矣。夫粤，天下之澤國也。負山阻海，火耕水耨，其民樸重喭慤，若難遽以道德一之者；然其貞元未散，良心易感而嘉言易入，一有賢者倡之，其從善更輕而守志益堅也。是故高固以才能相楚威王，始進《鐸椒春秋》，引君當道，因致五羊銜榖之瑞，南海之民風動而圖像以表厥賢。自是人文漸盛，民俗漸淳。《志》曰：「衣冠禮樂，無異中州。」又曰：「今之交、廣，古之鄒、魯。」其化民成俗之休，可想見矣。自兹以後，代不乏賢，士勤于德，民易其俗。若羅威、唐頌之厚彝倫、篤行誼，則民化而敬老親親矣；馮元之通經術、登膴仕，則民化而博學好古矣。俗崇正道而陋緇黄，非因梁觀國之以禮敦俗乎？俗守名義而樂恬退，非由崔與之之清風高節乎？俗皆務學，非因二陳以
translation_en: … speak of the pivotal moment for returning to what is right. Therefore it is said: a sense of honor and shame is the fine integrity of scholars; moral transformation through education is the urgent task of the court. Without understanding moral transformation through education, to hope for the goodness of literati habits and popular customs is difficult indeed. Now, Yue [Guangdong] is a watery region of the realm. Backed by mountains and bounded by the sea, practicing slash-and-burn farming and wet-rice weeding, its people are simple, stolid, blunt, and sincere, as though it would be difficult to unify them suddenly through morality and virtue. Yet their pure primordial vitality has not dissipated; their innate good conscience is easily moved and fine words easily enter them. Once there is a worthy man to take the lead, their following of goodness is all the readier and their adherence to high purpose all the firmer. For this reason, when Gao Gu 高固 served King Wei of Chu 楚威王 as minister by virtue of his talent and ability, he first presented Duo Jiao's Spring and Autumn Annals (Duo Jiao Chunqiu 鐸椒春秋) to guide his ruler onto the proper Way, thereby bringing about the auspicious omen of the five rams holding grain stalks in their mouths; the people of Nanhai 南海 were stirred as by the wind and painted his portrait to honor his worthiness. From this time on, cultural refinement gradually flourished and popular customs gradually became pure. The Gazetteer (Zhi 志) says: "In caps and robes, rites and music, it does not differ from the Central Plain." It also says: "Present-day Jiao 交 and Guang 廣 are the Zou 鄒 and Lu 魯 of antiquity." The beauty of its transforming the people and perfecting customs can well be imagined! From this time onward, no era lacked worthies; scholars were diligent in virtue, and the people changed their customs. Because of men like Luo Wei 羅威 and Tang Song 唐頌, who enriched normal human relationships and were earnest in righteous conduct, the people were transformed and respected elders and loved their kin. Because of Feng Yuan 馮元, who mastered classical learning and rose to prominent office, the people were transformed and became broadly learned and fond of antiquity. That customs revere the orthodox Way and disdain Buddhist monks and Daoist priests—is this not because Liang Guanguo 梁觀國 enriched customs through ritual? That customs uphold moral duty and delight in quiet retirement—is this not due to the pure influence and lofty integrity of Cui Yuzhi 崔與之? That popular customs all devote themselves to learning—is this not because the two Chens 陳 became…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
經學鳴二莫以文章顯乎上下相觀後先
相望流風餘韻郁郁彬彬固皆諸賢有以
倡之也謂民風不本於士習可乎夫粵以
質直慓悍之地賴諸賢興起斯文旣已化
爲禮義之俗又加以我
國家仁漸義摩之敎名世之賢相繼迭出弘
正以前士多羔羊素絲之風而民亦知重
義輕利以共享夫盜息民安之治古今稱
全盛焉乃今則若有異往昔者風敎漸澆
===
則士賤行檢矣俗化漸侈則人棄本業矣
嶺之東西海之南北所云沃野千里者有
未墾之土矣惠潮山海之交向所云新民
復業者有集榖啄粟之思矣流移逋播之
民昔之嗷嗷待哺者有化離無家之歎矣
男不耕耘女不蠶織而靡衣媮食者有競
淫尚侈之習矣貴游賈竪侈靡儇譎而信
義衰廢矣豪右大俠田連阡陌賦不盈銖
兩而齊民編戶相朘削以趨於盡矣禮讓
punctuated: 經學鳴、二莫以文章顯乎？上下相觀，後先相望，流風餘韻，郁郁彬彬，固皆諸賢有以倡之也。謂民風不本於士習，可乎？夫粵以質直慓悍之地，賴諸賢興起斯文，旣已化爲禮義之俗；又加以我國家仁漸義摩之敎，名世之賢，相繼迭出。弘、正以前，士多羔羊素絲之風，而民亦知重義輕利，以共享夫盜息民安之治，古今稱全盛焉。乃今則若有異往昔者：風敎漸澆，則士賤行檢矣；俗化漸侈，則人棄本業矣。嶺之東西、海之南北，所云沃野千里者，有未墾之土矣。惠、潮山海之交，向所云新民復業者，有集榖啄粟之思矣。流移逋播之民，昔之嗷嗷待哺者，有化離無家之歎矣。男不耕耘，女不蠶織，而靡衣媮食者，有競淫尚侈之習矣。貴游賈竪，侈靡儇譎，而信義衰廢矣。豪右大俠，田連阡陌，賦不盈銖兩，而齊民編戶，相朘削以趨於盡矣。禮讓
translation_en: … gaining renown through classical scholarship, and the two Mos (Er Mo 二莫) distinguishing themselves through literary writing? Superiors and inferiors observed one another, predecessors and successors looked to each other; their lingering customs and enduring refinement were rich and resplendent—all of this was truly because those worthies took the lead. Can one say that popular customs are not rooted in the habits of the literati? Now, although Guangdong was a land of bluntness and fierce temperaments, by relying on those worthies to rouse this culture, it had already been transformed into a land of ritual and righteousness. Added to this was the teaching of our Dynasty, which steeped the people in benevolence and polished them with righteousness, so that world-renowned worthies emerged one after another. Before the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras, scholars mostly possessed the integrity of the "lambskin and white silk" (gaoyang susi) [of the Classic of Poetry], while the common people also knew to value righteousness and slight profit, jointly enjoying a governance in which banditry ceased and the people were at peace—acclaimed as the height of flourishing across past and present. Yet today, things seem different from the past: as moral teachings have gradually grown thin, scholars have come to slight personal conduct; as popular customs have gradually grown extravagant, people have abandoned their fundamental occupations (farming). East and west of the passes, north and south of the sea, in what were called a thousand li of fertile plains, there are now uncultivated lands. Where the mountains and sea meet in Huizhou 惠州 and Chaozhou 潮州, those who were formerly called "new people returning to their livelihoods" now harbor thoughts of gathering in the paper-mulberry trees and pecking at our grain [like the wandering birds in the Classic of Poetry]. Displaced and fleeing people, who in the past cried out waiting to be fed, now sigh over separation and homelessness [? 化離 for 仳離]. Men do not plow or weed, women do not tend silkworms or weave, and those who dress extravagantly and live idly for the moment have formed habits of vying in licentiousness and prizing luxury. Noble idlers and merchant youths are extravagant, frivolous, and deceitful, while trustworthiness and righteousness have declined and fallen into disuse. Powerful magnates and great stalwarts own fields stretching across the paths, yet their tax payments do not fill a fraction of an ounce of silver, while the registered commoners are fleeced and exploited until they are driven to utter exhaustion. In a land of ritual and deference…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之地師徒相遠三家九市衣冠雜遝而文
教鮮敦綱維不立矣民風士習日趨於敝
蓋不止於執事所云獵聲華悖倫理事巫
詛者其綠林嘯聚錦帆通蹻何惑也此固
風之所靡可爲太息者其視向之衣冠禮
樂文章節義羔羊素絲盜息民安之俗不
啻逕庭矣能無待於教化乎所以握其機
要而反其本初者誠不可不汲汲矣夫今
日之事豈庠序學校之未設乎設矣而實
===
德未脩也豈六德三物之未講乎講矣而
實意未孚也豈衣冠文物之未盛乎盛矣
而實行未覩也豈法制禁令之未備乎備
矣而實政未舉也豈督促稽查之未嚴乎
嚴矣而實效未臻也孔子曰教化之流非
家至而人益之也以身先之而已賈生曰
移風易俗使天下回心而向道類非俗吏
之所能爲則夫示之以好惡陳之以禮義
謹之以好尚所以端士習而淑民風信有
punctuated: 之地，師徒相遠，三家九市，衣冠雜遝，而文教鮮敦，綱維不立矣。民風士習，日趨於敝，蓋不止於執事所云獵聲華、悖倫理、事巫詛者；其綠林嘯聚、錦帆通蹻，何惑也！此固風之所靡，可爲太息者，其視向之衣冠禮樂、文章節義、羔羊素絲、盜息民安之俗，不啻逕庭矣。能無待於教化乎？所以握其機要而反其本初者，誠不可不汲汲矣。夫今日之事，豈庠序學校之未設乎？設矣，而實德未脩也。豈六德三物之未講乎？講矣，而實意未孚也。豈衣冠文物之未盛乎？盛矣，而實行未覩也。豈法制禁令之未備乎？備矣，而實政未舉也。豈督促稽查之未嚴乎？嚴矣，而實效未臻也。孔子曰：「教化之流，非家至而人益之也，以身先之而已。」賈生曰：「移風易俗，使天下回心而向道，類非俗吏之所能爲。」則夫示之以好惡，陳之以禮義，謹之以好尚，所以端士習而淑民風，信有
translation_en:
… places [of propriety and deference], teachers and disciples grow distant from one another; in the villages and marketplaces, caps and robes mingle in disorderly crowds, while literary and moral teaching is rarely cultivated and the fundamental bonds of society are not established. Popular customs and the habits of scholars deteriorate day by day, going well beyond what Your Excellency referred to as hunting after showy reputation, violating human relationships, and practicing shamanism and cursing; what wonder is it, then, that bandits gather whistling in the greenwood and brocade-sailed pirates communicate with brigands like Robber Jiao? This is truly a case of customs being swept away, over which one can only heave a deep sigh. Compared with the former customs—of caps and robes, rites and music, literary refinement and moral integrity, the incorruptibility celebrated in "Lambskin" and "White Silk" [of the Classic of Poetry], when banditry ceased and the people were at peace—it could not be more worlds apart. Can this not await moral transformation through education? Thus, in grasping the pivotal mechanism and returning to the original foundation, one truly cannot fail to be urgently devoted.

Now, in the affairs of today, is it that local and prefectural schools have not been established? They have been established, yet genuine virtue is not cultivated. Is it that the Six Virtues and Three Things have not been expounded? They have been expounded, yet genuine intent has not inspired trust. Is it that caps, robes, and cultural institutions are not flourishing? They are flourishing, yet genuine conduct is not seen. Is it that legal statutes and prohibitions are not complete? They are complete, yet genuine governance is not carried out. Is it that supervision, urging, and inspection are not strict? They are strict, yet genuine results are not achieved. Confucius said: "The spread of moral teaching is not a matter of going to every household and benefiting every person; one simply leads them in person." Master Jia [Jia Yi 賈誼] said: "Transforming customs and changing habits, causing the whole world to turn its heart toward the Way—this is not the sort of thing that vulgar clerks are capable of doing." Therefore, showing them what to love and hate, setting forth rites and righteousness for them, and being circumspect in what one prizes and esteems—the means by which to rectify the habits of scholars and purify the customs of the people truly lies …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不在人而在我者是故風教澆則挽之以
樸俗化侈則程之以儉土蕪穢則勸之以
耒耜民反側則申之以法令逋播者業之
媮惰者作之詛盟者詰之并兼則均之以
賦役而摧其豪奢庠序則課之以章程而
黜其浮靡如此則民有所趨避而回行易
嚮孰敢不式士習有不端民風有不淑者
否也雖然主之不可以不斷而行之又不
可以不力其政令貴一其誅賞貴必無牽
===
於游詞無脂韋於權豪無姑息於諧媚之
夫如是而猶不從不得不深治之如所謂
屏之遠方終身不齒者則其勢自不能不
變而奚患其靡也語曰更化則善治今適
更化之時猶日以簿書期會爲大故而不
知所以易民視匡失俗豈理也哉嗟夫齊
其法制詳其命令期於必行固矣然衣食
足而後禮義興粤兵興數十年繼以水旱
重以征輸民無食矣奚暇治禮義哉則所
punctuated: 不在人而在我者。是故風教澆則挽之以樸，俗化侈則程之以儉，土蕪穢則勸之以耒耜，民反側則申之以法令；逋播者業之，媮惰者作之，詛盟者詰之；并兼則均之以賦役而摧其豪奢，庠序則課之以章程而黜其浮靡。如此，則民有所趨避而回行易嚮，孰敢不式？士習有不端、民風有不淑者否也？雖然，主之不可以不斷，而行之又不可以不力。其政令貴一，其誅賞貴必，無牽於游詞，無脂韋於權豪，無姑息於諧媚之夫。如是而猶不從，不得不深治之，如所謂「屏之遠方，終身不齒」者，則其勢自不能不變，而奚患其靡也？語曰：「更化則善治。」今適更化之時，猶日以簿書期會爲大故，而不知所以易民視、匡失俗，豈理也哉！嗟夫！齊其法制，詳其命令，期於必行，固矣。然衣食足而後禮義興。粤兵興數十年，繼以水旱，重以征輸，民無食矣，奚暇治禮義哉？則所
translation_en: … does not rest with others, but with ourselves. Therefore, when moral instruction grows thin, restore it with simplicity; when customs become extravagant, regulate them with frugality; when the land lies overgrown and untended, encourage the people with plow and share; when the people are restless and recalcitrant, make clear to them the laws and ordinances. Settle those who have fled and scattered into livelihoods; rouse those who are idle and negligent; interrogate those who form illicit oaths and covenants. Where there is land engrossment, equalize it through taxes and labor services and curb the powerful and extravagant; in the local schools, test them according to established regulations and dismiss the superficial and ornate. If this is done, the people will know what to pursue and what to avoid, turning their conduct around and changing their direction—who then would dare not conform? Would there still be any scholars whose habits are not upright, or any popular customs that are not pure? Even so, in presiding over this one cannot lack decisiveness, and in carrying it out one cannot lack vigor. Administrative orders must be unified, and punishments and rewards must be certain; do not be swayed by floating talk, do not be pliant and obsequious toward the powerful and overbearing, and do not be indulgent toward flattering and sycophantic men. If after all this they still do not obey, one has no choice but to punish them severely—such as what is called "banishing them to distant regions and excluding them from the community for life." Then by the very force of circumstances they cannot fail to change, so why worry about their decadence? The proverb says: "When teaching and transformation are renewed, good governance follows." Now is precisely the time for renewing transformation; yet if we still daily treat account books and scheduled meetings as the great affairs of state, without knowing how to change the people's outlook and rectify errant customs, how could that be reasonable! Alas! To make uniform the laws and institutions, to make detailed the orders and commands, and to insist upon their strict enforcement—this is of course essential. Yet only when food and clothing are sufficient do rites and righteousness flourish. In Guangdong, military campaigns have been waged for several decades, followed by floods and droughts, and compounded by heavy tax levies and transport duties. The people have nothing to eat—what leisure do they have to cultivate rites and righteousness? Thus, that by which…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以節其財力遂其生養使得優游於仁義
禮樂之中以待其善念自生而民志自定
者不可不首加之意也一其道德同其風
俗其機在上固矣然親民之職莫若守令
敎化之務如所謂興社學舉義倉行保甲
之法布激勸之典皆其所最急者非得賢
守令身任而力行之實德不能以流通善
政不可以遍及矣則愼選守令又爲脩敎
化之首務也此其機本所在尤不可忽敢
===
敬申言之
第四問
李玉
同考試官敎諭陳批
疏陳利害作者逸興定
然而所畫鹽正裁恤公私兼利具見經濟之略非
徒文之工也宜錄
考試官敎諭楊批指陳利弊切中機宜
考試官敎諭朱批條對明悉
天下有自然之利善興利者循其法以導
punctuated:
以節其財力，遂其生養，使得優游於仁義禮樂之中，以待其善念自生而民志自定者，不可不首加之意也。一其道德，同其風俗，其機在上固矣。然親民之職莫若守令，敎化之務，如所謂興社學、舉義倉、行保甲之法、布激勸之典，皆其所最急者。非得賢守令身任而力行之，實德不能以流通，善政不可以遍及矣。則愼選守令，又爲脩敎化之首務也。此其機本所在，尤不可忽，敢敬申言之。

第四問
李玉
同考試官敎諭陳批：疏陳利害，作者逸興定然，而所畫鹽政裁恤，公私兼利，具見經濟之略，非徒文之工也，宜錄。
考試官敎諭楊批：指陳利弊，切中機宜。
考試官敎諭朱批：條對明悉。

天下有自然之利，善興利者循其法以導
translation_en:
… wherewith to economize their financial and physical resources and fulfill their livelihood and nourishment, enabling them to dwell at ease amid benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, waiting until their good intentions arise of themselves and the people's minds become settled of themselves—this is something to which attention must first be given. To unify their morality and harmonize their customs—the pivot for this certainly lies with those above. Yet among offices close to the people, none compares to Prefects and Magistrates. In the task of moral transformation through education, matters such as establishing community schools, setting up charitable granaries, implementing thebaojia mutual-security system, and promulgating statutes for encouragement and exhortation are all most urgent. Unless one obtains worthy Prefects and Magistrates to take personal responsibility and carry them out vigorously, genuine virtue cannot circulate and good governance cannot reach everywhere. Thus, carefully selecting Prefects and Magistrates is in turn the foremost task in cultivating moral transformation. Where this pivot and foundation lie must especially not be neglected; I venture respectfully to state this further.

Question Four
Li Yu 
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen: He sets forth the advantages and disadvantages; the author's transcendent inspiration is assured [?], and what he plans regarding salt administration [reading 政 for 正]—curtailment and relief, benefiting both public and private interests—fully reveals a strategy for statecraft, not merely skill in writing. It ought to be recorded.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yang: He points out advantages and abuses, hitting the mark on what is opportune and appropriate.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: His point-by-point reply is clear and thorough.

In the world there are natural profits; those who are good at promoting profit follow the proper methods to guide …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之而後其利爲不窮天下無不敝之法善
行法者因其敝而通之而後其法爲可久
何則法以正經若持衡然一成而不易者
也變以趨時若轉圜然推行於不滯者也
用法者知其利之所由興又知其法之所
由廢酌古以準今補偏以救敝
國家之大計可從而理矣是故屯政也鹽法
也先王所以因天地自然之利而裕軍國
之需於不匱者也第法玩於因循之久而
===
害成於姑息之過乘其弊而亟反是在今
日誠不容緩者愚嘗考鏡古今綜覈利弊
而得其捄之之要矣屯田非古也自趙充
國祖鼂錯屯戍之議以制諸羌計羌虜故
田及公田民未墾者爲屯塞下内有亡費
之利外有守禦之備古今防邊之法莫是
過矣唐因之而屯關中魏因之而屯金陵
兩淮宋因之而屯荆襄岳州取而較之漢
止數郡之屯宋有括牛之擾唐法爲最善
punctuated: 之，而後其利爲不窮；天下無不敝之法，善行法者因其敝而通之，而後其法爲可久。何則？法以正經，若持衡然，一成而不易者也；變以趨時，若轉圜然，推行於不滯者也。用法者知其利之所由興，又知其法之所由廢，酌古以準今，補偏以救敝，國家之大計可從而理矣。是故屯政也、鹽法也，先王所以因天地自然之利，而裕軍國之需於不匱者也。第法玩於因循之久，而害成於姑息之過，乘其弊而亟反，是在今日誠不容緩者。愚嘗考鏡古今，綜覈利弊，而得其捄之之要矣。屯田非古也，自趙充國祖鼂錯屯戍之議以制諸羌，計羌虜故田及公田民未墾者，爲屯塞下，内有亡費之利，外有守禦之備，古今防邊之法莫是過矣。唐因之而屯關中，魏因之而屯金陵、兩淮，宋因之而屯荆、襄、岳州。取而較之，漢止數郡之屯，宋有括牛之擾，唐法爲最善…
translation_en: … guide them, and only then will those benefits be inexhaustible. Under heaven there are no laws that do not deteriorate; those skilled at implementing laws adapt them in light of their deterioration, and only then can those laws endure. Why is this so? Laws establish the fundamental norms—like holding a balance scale, once fixed they do not change; adaptation responds to the times—like turning a wheel, it moves forward without stagnation. When those who apply the laws understand how benefits arise and also understand how laws fall into disuse, deliberating on antiquity to set standards for the present and remedying imbalances to rescue what has deteriorated, the great policies of the state can thereby be put in order. Therefore, the administration of state farms (tunzheng) and the salt monopoly laws (yanfa) were the means by which the former kings drew upon the natural benefits of heaven and earth to supply the needs of the military and the state without depletion. Yet laws come to be treated lightly through long-standing routine, and harms take shape through excessive indulgence; seizing upon these abuses and urgently reversing them is truly something that brooks no delay today. I have examined the past and present as in a mirror, comprehensively verified the advantages and abuses, and grasped the essentials of how to remedy them. Military state farms (tuntian) did not exist in high antiquity. Ever since Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 modeled himself on Chao Cuo's 鼂錯 proposal for garrison farming in order to control the various Qiang 羌 tribes—calculating the former lands of the Qiang captives as well as public lands not yet reclaimed by the people, and establishing state farms along the frontier—internally there was the benefit of avoiding expenditure, and externally there was preparedness for defense. Among frontier defense methods past and present, none has surpassed this. The Tang followed it and established state farms in Guanzhong 關中; the Wei followed it and established state farms in Jinling 金陵 and the Lianghuai 兩淮 region; the Song followed it and established state farms in Jing 荆, Xiang 襄, and Yuezhou 岳州. Taking them together for comparison, the Han had state farms in only a few commanderies, and the Song suffered the disturbance of requisitioning oxen, whereas the Tang method was the best…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
提舉司專理之課額有定徴行鹽有分地
令輸粟實塞而照引支給蓋斟酌唐宋之
法而計慮爲益精矣奈之何日久而弊滋
也餘鹽行而常股滯正引阻而邊儲匱鹽
法幾大壞矣而廣東又其甚焉者東北二
提舉司鬻鹽之場二十八歲徴課一萬五
千九百有奇乃核丁則逋而亡者十三督
課則負而縮者十五兼之豪家悍卒揚帆
聯艦興販飄忽於鯨波者寔繁也是可不
===
亟爲之治乎夫樂因循而憚變更者曲士
之所守也任骯髒而重怨嫌者委儒之所
希也粵之屯鹽弊非一日執事謂瑟不調
當移其柱誠然也玆欲祛積習之弊以復
祖宗之盛是不必別求所謂法也惟申明
舊制去其所以害法者而已何者屯田之弊端
雖多而逋負於頑梗兼併於豪右此其大
較也釐正之要在憲臣執其綱於上而嚴
有司清理之寄夫列田爲屯尺寸皆官土
punctuated:
提舉司專理之，課額有定徴，行鹽有分地，令輸粟實塞，而照引支給，蓋斟酌唐、宋之法，而計慮爲益精矣。奈之何日久而弊滋也？餘鹽行而常股滯，正引阻而邊儲匱，鹽法幾大壞矣，而廣東又其甚焉者。東北二提舉司鬻鹽之場二十八，歲徴課一萬五千九百有奇。乃核丁，則逋而亡者十三；督課，則負而縮者十五。兼之豪家悍卒，揚帆聯艦，興販飄忽於鯨波者寔繁也。是可不亟爲之治乎？

夫樂因循而憚變更者，曲士之所守也；任骯髒而重怨嫌者，委儒之所希也。粵之屯、鹽弊非一日，執事謂「瑟不調當移其柱」，誠然也。玆欲祛積習之弊，以復祖宗之盛，是不必別求所謂法也，惟申明舊制，去其所以害法者而已。

何者？屯田之弊端雖多，而逋負於頑梗，兼併於豪右，此其大較也。釐正之要，在憲臣執其綱於上，而嚴有司清理之寄。夫列田爲屯，尺寸皆官土…
translation_en:
…Supervisorates exclusively managed it. The tax quotas had fixed assessments, and the distribution of salt had designated regions. Merchants were ordered to transport grain to supply the frontier garrisons and were issued salt in accordance with their salt vouchers. Indeed, this was adapted after deliberation from the methods of the Tang and Song dynasties, and the planning and consideration were even more refined. How is it that with the passage of time, abuses have proliferated? As surplus salt circulates, the regular reserve stock stagnates; as regular salt vouchers are obstructed, frontier provisions grow depleted. The salt administration has nearly been utterly ruined, and in Guangdong the situation is even worse. The two Supervisorates of the East and North have twenty-eight salterns for selling salt, with an annual tax quota assessed at over fifteen thousand nine hundred. Yet when the registered adult males are verified, three out of ten have defaulted and fled; when the tax quotas are supervised, five out of ten are in arrears and falling short. Added to this, powerful families and unruly soldiers hoist sails and link vessels, engaging in illicit trafficking and darting unpredictably across the whale-tossed waves in truly great numbers. How could one not urgently set this in order?

Now, taking pleasure in routine and dreading change is what parochial scholars cling to; indulging in unbending obstinacy [?] while dreading resentment and suspicion is what accommodating pedants aspire to. The abuses in the military agricultural colonies and the salt administration of Guangdong have not arisen in a single day. When you, sir, state that "when a zither is out of tune, one must shift its bridges," that is truly so. If we now wish to dispel the abuses of entrenched habits in order to restore the flourishing state of our imperial ancestors, there is no need to seek separately for some so-called new method; we need only reiterate and clarify the old regulations and remove that which harms the system, and nothing more.

Why is this? Although the abuses of the military agricultural colonies are numerous, defaulting and arrears by the obstinate and refractory, and annexation by powerful magnates—these are the main outlines of the problem. The essential point in rectifying and reforming them lies in the surveillance officials holding firm to the overarching principles from above, while strictly enforcing the responsibility of the local authorities to clear up and put the lands in order. Now, when fields are laid out as military agricultural colonies, every inch and foot is government land…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也按畝起徵升斗皆公儲也而倂兼逋負
邦有常刑必也稽戸籍之存亡舉丈量之
明法盜賣者必懲私佃者必禁卽界紊籍
去而閭閻故老豈無一二存者自首者宥
占據自其祖父者宥其亂籍私匿而弗悛
者繩之無少貸也而有田無稅者行沒官
之令計丁分給者嚴限田之條畫之經界
載諸版籍東作則秉耒以耕西成則荷戈
以練食不虧而兵亦足雖充國金城之屯
===
孔明渭濱之耕率是道也何憂乎屯政之
不復耶鹽法之弊孔雜出而課額折於流
移商賈阨於私販此其大都也整飭之要
在憲臣握其樞於上而重有司稽察之柄
夫分漏辦鹽凡以恤竈也戢販防姦凡以
通商也而公課私鹺國有成憲必也先覈
額辦之丁申布招商之令戸絕者速爲查
豁拖負者以漸追徵卽流離轉徙而遺埕
故漏必有私自封殖者願自賠納者聽願
punctuated:
也，按畝起徵，升斗皆公儲也。而倂兼逋負，邦有常刑。必也稽戸籍之存亡，舉丈量之明法。盜賣者必懲，私佃者必禁。卽界紊籍去，而閭閻故老豈無一二存者？自首者宥，占據自其祖父者宥，其亂籍私匿而弗悛者，繩之無少貸也。而有田無稅者，行沒官之令；計丁分給者，嚴限田之條。畫之經界，載諸版籍。東作則秉耒以耕，西成則荷戈以練。食不虧而兵亦足，雖充國金城之屯、孔明渭濱之耕，率是道也。何憂乎屯政之不復耶？
鹽法之弊孔雜出，而課額折於流移，商賈阨於私販，此其大都也。整飭之要，在憲臣握其樞於上，而重有司稽察之柄。夫分漏辦鹽，凡以恤竈也；戢販防姦，凡以通商也。而公課私鹺，國有成憲。必也先覈額辦之丁，申布招商之令。戸絕者速爲查豁，拖負者以漸追徵。卽流離轉徙，而遺埕故漏，必有私自封殖者。願自賠納者聽，願
translation_en:
… and when taxes are levied by the mu, every pint and peck is public grain. Yet for annexation of land and defaulting on taxes, the state has regular punishments. It is essential to investigate whether registered households still exist or have died out, and to enforce the clear regulations for land surveying. Those who illicitly sell military farmlands must be punished, and those who privately lease them must be prohibited. Even if boundaries are confused and registers lost, how could there not be one or two village elders still living? Those who confess voluntarily should be pardoned, and those whose occupation of the land dates back to their fathers and grandfathers should be pardoned; as for those who tamper with registers, privately conceal land, and refuse to repent, they should be prosecuted according to the law without the slightest leniency. For those who hold land without paying tax, enforce the order of confiscation by the state; for land distributed according to adult males, strictly apply the regulations limiting landholdings. Demarcate the boundaries and record them in the official registers. When spring farming begins, they grasp the plow to till; when autumn harvest is done, they shoulder the spear to drill. Food supplies will not run short and troops will also be sufficient. Even Zhao Chongguo's (趙充國) military agricultural colonies at Jincheng and Zhuge Kongming's (諸葛孔明) farming along the banks of the Wei River followed this very way. What worry would there be that the administration of military farmlands could not be restored?

As for the salt administration, abuses arise from many quarters, yet the loss of tax quotas due to the flight and migration of salt-producers and the distress of merchants caused by illicit trafficking—these are the main issues. The key to rectifying this lies in the Censorial Officials holding the pivot at the top, while giving greater weight to the authority of local officials to inspect and investigate. Allocating leaching-vats [?] to produce salt is entirely for the purpose of showing compassion to the salt-producing households; suppressing smugglers and guarding against villains is entirely for the purpose of facilitating the trade of merchants. Concerning public salt quotas and illicit salt, the state has established statutes. It is essential first to verify the adult males subject to the quota of salt production, and to reiterate and promulgate the orders for recruiting merchants. Households that have died out should promptly be investigated and exempted, while arrears owed should be recovered gradually. Even where salt-producers have scattered and migrated away, leaving behind abandoned salt-fields and old leaching-vats, there must be those who are privately enriching themselves from them. Those who are willing to make up and pay the taxes themselves should be permitted to do so; those who are willing…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
還本業者聽其私逸自便逃竈而爲民者
究之無少假也而內地私鬻者責之巡捕
海澨煽構者責之巡哨觸禁者盡法故縱
者連坐內可爲度支之助外可防嘯聚之
虞課漸完而商日益卽不必桑孔之平準
劉晏之常平財恒足也何憂乎鹽政之不
脩耶雖然此特就明問之所及者耳愚竊
有說焉傳曰有治人無治法書曰惟克果
斷乃罔後艱今粤中民力竭矣而山海之
===
寇猶然竊發卽欲去兵勢所不能其藉財
用非淺尠矣若徒執拘攣之見而狃於苟
安重疑畏之心而懈於責成則弊日益深
法日益廢脫有緩急斂民增賦不亦重其
困乎故愚以爲捄弊莫先任人而决斷之
機尤在加之意焉蓋清屯有專官捕鹽有
定職其責成非不詳且切矣顧一官而諸
司委焉一職而衆務紛焉一日作之十日
輟之辟十羊九牧道旁作舍縱才堪兼撫
punctuated:
還本業者聽，其私逸自便、逃竈而爲民者，究之無少假也。而內地私鬻者，責之巡捕；海澨煽構者，責之巡哨。觸禁者盡法，故縱者連坐。內可爲度支之助，外可防嘯聚之虞。課漸完而商日益，卽不必桑、孔之平準，劉晏之常平，財恒足也，何憂乎鹽政之不脩耶？

雖然，此特就明問之所及者耳，愚竊有說焉。《傳》曰：「有治人，無治法。」《書》曰：「惟克果斷，乃罔後艱。」今粤中民力竭矣，而山海之寇猶然竊發，卽欲去兵，勢所不能，其藉財用非淺尠矣。若徒執拘攣之見而狃於苟安，重疑畏之心而懈於責成，則弊日益深，法日益廢。脫有緩急，斂民增賦，不亦重其困乎？故愚以爲捄弊莫先任人，而决斷之機，尤在加之意焉。蓋清屯有專官，捕鹽有定職，其責成非不詳且切矣。顧一官而諸司委焉，一職而衆務紛焉，一日作之，十日輟之，辟十羊九牧，道旁作舍，縱才堪兼撫，
translation_en:
… to return to their original occupation, let them be permitted to do so; as for those who slip away for their own convenience, fleeing the salt-boiling households to become ordinary commoners, they should be investigated and prosecuted without the slightest leniency. For those who illicitly peddle salt in the interior, hold the police patrols responsible; for those who stir up trouble along the coastal fringes, hold the maritime patrols responsible. Those who violate the prohibitions should be punished to the full extent of the law, and those who intentionally let them go should be held jointly liable. Internally, this can serve as an aid to state expenditures; externally, it can guard against the danger of outlaws banding together. As the tax quotas are gradually fulfilled and merchants increasingly profit, even without the price-equalization (pingzhun) policies of Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin or the ever-normal (changping) system of Liu Yan, wealth will be constantly sufficient—what worry would there be that the salt administration is not in good order?

Even so, this merely addresses what was raised in your enlightened question; I humbly have a further point to make. The commentary says: "There are governing men, not governing laws." The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Only by being able to make resolute decisions will there be no subsequent difficulties." Today in Guangdong, the strength of the people is exhausted, yet bandits in the mountains and on the seas still covertly erupt. Even if we wished to dispense with troops, circumstances make it impossible, and our reliance on financial resources is far from slight. If we merely cling to narrow, rigid views and remain habituated to temporary ease, or harbor heavy doubts and fears and grow lax in demanding results, then abuses will deepen day by day and the laws will fall into greater disuse day by day. Should an emergency arise, extracting levies from the people and increasing taxes—would this not compound their distress? Therefore, I humbly believe that in remedying abuses nothing takes precedence over appointing the right men, and the pivot of decisive action lies especially in paying close attention to this. Now, there are dedicated officials for clearing up military farm (tuntian) land, and fixed posts for apprehending salt smugglers; the assignment of responsibilities is neither unspecific nor lacking in urgency. Yet a single official receives commissions from multiple agencies, and a single post is entangled in a multitude of affairs. They work at it for one day and suspend it for ten—like having nine herdsmen for ten sheep, or building a house by the roadside. Even if someone had the talent to manage multiple duties simultaneously, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
支吾且不暇安望其有成績耶惟在當事
者念
國計之重而思更化之難毅然以古法爲必
可復而不辭勞怨奮然以時弊爲必當革
而不阻權豪有司之職屯鹽者必以是考
課最而不得以他委妨其職掌武弁之管
屯哨者必以是專督責而必以季終等其
賞罰假之便宜竟以歲月俾軍有恒產竈
無舊逋則屯政肅而軍實充鹽法脩而邊
===
儲裕雖百世可行非獨今日已也先民有
言詢于芻蕘惟執事采擇焉
第五問
鄭育漸
同考試官教諭羅批兵食之畫士子類能條
之獨是篇鏡古籌今慮周計悉當於粵政有裨不
但文逼秦漢而已
考試官教諭楊批筆意高古條議精確錄
之
punctuated:
支吾且不暇，安望其有成績耶？惟在當事者念國計之重，而思更化之難，毅然以古法爲必可復，而不辭勞怨；奮然以時弊爲必當革，而不阻權豪。有司之職屯鹽者，必以是考課最，而不得以他委妨其職掌；武弁之管屯哨者，必以是專督責，而必以季終等其賞罰。假之便宜，竟以歲月，俾軍有恒產，竈無舊逋，則屯政肅而軍實充，鹽法脩而邊儲裕，雖百世可行，非獨今日已也。先民有言：「詢于芻蕘。」惟執事采擇焉。
第五問
鄭育漸
同考試官教諭羅批：〔兵食之畫，士子類能條之，獨是篇鏡古籌今，慮周計悉，當於粵政有裨，不但文逼秦漢而已。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔筆意高古，條議精確，錄之。〕
translation_en:
…they would not even have time to muddle through, so how could one hope for them to achieve tangible results? It rests solely with those in authority to bear in mind the gravity of the state finances and reflect upon the difficulty of reforming governance: resolutely regarding the ancient methods as certainly restorable without shrinking from toil or resentment, and boldly viewing current abuses as necessarily requiring eradication without being deterred by the powerful and influential. For civil officials whose duties concern the military farms and salt administration, their performance evaluations must be based on this, and other commissions must not be allowed to interfere with their responsibilities. For military officers in charge of farming colonies and patrols, their supervision and accountability must be focused exclusively on this, and their rewards and punishments must be graded at the end of every quarter. Grant them discretionary authority to act as circumstances require, and allow them sufficient years and months to see it through, so that the soldiers have permanent property and the salt-boiling households have no old arrears. Then the administration of military farms will be well-ordered and military supplies abundant; the salt laws will be properly maintained and frontier provisions plentiful. Such measures could be practiced for a hundred generations, not merely today. As the ancients had a saying, "Consult the grass- and firewood-gatherers." May Your Excellency select from these humble views.

Question Five
Zheng Yujian
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Luo comments: [Plans for military forces and food supplies are something candidates can generally itemize, but this essay alone mirrors antiquity to plan for the present, with comprehensive forethought and thorough calculation. It should be of real benefit to the governance of Guangdong, and is not merely prose that rivals that of the Qin and Han.]
Examiner and County Director of Studies Yang comments: [The brush-conception is lofty and antique, and the itemized proposals are precise and accurate. Record it.]

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭朱批博學宏猷非淺學可到
執事以東粤兵食爲問愚經生耳安足與
計天下事雖然則甞聞之矣昔齊桓以良
車三百乘敎卒萬人以爲兵首南伐至召
陵北伐山戎西伐大夏涉流沙束馬懸車
登太行至卑耳山橫行天下莫之能禁晉
文造五兩之士五乘銳卒千人先以接敵
侵曹伐衞抑楚會盟踐土尊天子於雍諸
侯莫能難夫齊晉盟主攘夷尊周豈待漕
===
