輓方輸轉道千里哉其名正其義順行令
中國所在傳食至其人徒之費多不滿萬
所謂城濮之戰晉師在楚三日穀者是矣
豈若後世謀詐用而從橫長短之說起於
是有輕點烏合假道借食兵興數十萬而
用始絀是以無名之師無用之食聖人畏
之故兵不在多寡在於選練將不在勇怯
在於知兵國之大計不可不審也夫敎笞
不可弛於家刑罰不可廢於國征伐不可
punctuated:
考試官敎諭朱批：博學宏猷，非淺學可到。

執事以東粤兵食爲問，愚經生耳，安足與計天下事？雖然，則甞聞之矣。昔齊桓以良車三百乘、敎卒萬人以爲兵首，南伐至召陵，北伐山戎，西伐大夏，涉流沙，束馬懸車，登太行，至卑耳山，橫行天下，莫之能禁。晉文造五兩之士五乘、銳卒千人，先以接敵，侵曹伐衞，抑楚，會盟踐土，尊天子於雍，諸侯莫能難。夫齊、晉盟主，攘夷尊周，豈待漕輓方輸、轉道千里哉？其名正，其義順，行令中國，所在傳食，至其人徒之費，多不滿萬，所謂城濮之戰，晉師在楚三日穀者是矣。豈若後世謀詐用而從橫長短之說起，於是有輕點烏合，假道借食，兵興數十萬而用始絀。是以無名之師、無用之食，聖人畏之。故兵不在多寡，在於選練；將不在勇怯，在於知兵。國之大計，不可不審也。夫敎笞不可弛於家，刑罰不可廢於國，征伐不可…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: "Broad learning and grand plans, not something shallow scholarship could attain."

Your Excellency asks about soldiers and provisions in Eastern Yue (Guangdong). I am merely a foolish student of the classics; how could I be worthy of discussing the affairs of the realm? Even so, I have heard something of the matter. In antiquity, Duke Huan of Qi used three hundred fine war chariots and ten thousand trained foot soldiers as his vanguard. In the south he campaigned as far as Shaoling; in the north he attacked the Mountain Rong; in the west he campaigned against Daxia and crossed the Flowing Sands; binding his horses and hoisting his chariots, he ascended the Taihang Mountains as far as Mount Bei'er. He ranged freely across the realm, and none could stop him. Duke Wen of Jin organized five chariots of warriors in five-man squads and a thousand elite troops to engage the enemy first. He invaded Cao, attacked Wei, curbed Chu, convened the covenant at Jiantu, and honored the Son of Heaven at Yong, while none of the feudal lords could challenge him. Now, when Qi and Jin acted as leaders of the covenant, repelling the barbarians and honoring the Zhou royal house, did they have to wait for grain transport by water and land to be hauled over a thousand li? Their cause was just and their principle was righteous; when they issued commands across the Central States, their troops were fed by relay wherever they went, and as for the expense in men and followers, at most it did not reach ten thousand. This is what is meant by the saying that at the Battle of Chengpu, the Jin army ate Chu's grain for three days. How could this be like later ages, when deceitful schemes were employed and the theories of vertical and horizontal alliances and of manipulation arose, so that men were lightly conscripted into unruly mobs, requesting right of passage and borrowing provisions, raising armies of several hundred thousand until resources finally ran short? Therefore, an army without a just cause and provisions consumed to no avail are things the sages feared. Thus, with troops, it is not a matter of their numbers, but of selecting and training them; with generals, it is not a matter of their bravery or cowardice, but of their understanding of warfare. The great plans of the state cannot but be carefully examined. Now, instruction and the rod cannot be relaxed in the family, punishments and penalties cannot be abolished in the state, and punitive expeditions cannot…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
偃於天下施之有順逆行之有次第而法
曰以逸待勞勝以虞待不虞勝又曰以飽
待饑勝夫千里饋糧士有饑色師不宿飽
難與應敵故兵不如者勿與挑戰粟不如
者勿與持乆此言食之爲重也長平之戰
秦以輕兵遮趙食而括斃河北之軍築甬
道輸之粟項羽渡河九戰絕之虜王離破
秦軍沛公竝兵而西高陽生仗策襲陳留
得積粟入關驃騎從軍天子至遣大官齎
===
數十乘重車餘梁肉如此其備也夫師行
糧食蓋自古記之今公私所汲汲而苦不
贍者其究安在或曰在兵而不在食愚則
曰在食而不在兵當事者待猶莫爲善後
之計而愚竊有惑也夫以粵之寥邈民疲
於作業農桑之事罕焉然以司府之兵食
計之歲入不下四十二萬惠潮之間曠土
千里惟正之負輸尚數十萬以其所入給
其所出而又取盈於常供游食之待哺者
punctuated: 偃於天下，施之有順逆，行之有次第。而法曰：「以逸待勞勝，以虞待不虞勝。」又曰：「以飽待饑勝。」夫千里饋糧，士有饑色；師不宿飽，難與應敵。故兵不如者，勿與挑戰；粟不如者，勿與持乆。此言食之爲重也。長平之戰，秦以輕兵遮趙食，而括斃；河北之軍，築甬道輸之粟，項羽渡河，九戰絕之，虜王離，破秦軍；沛公竝兵而西，高陽生仗策襲陳留，得積粟入關；驃騎從軍，天子至遣大官齎數十乘，重車餘梁肉。如此其備也！夫師行糧食，蓋自古記之。今公私所汲汲而苦不贍者，其究安在？或曰在兵而不在食，愚則曰在食而不在兵。當事者待猶莫爲善後之計，而愚竊有惑也。夫以粵之寥邈，民疲於作業，農桑之事罕焉。然以司府之兵食計之，歲入不下四十二萬；惠、潮之間，曠土千里，惟正之負輸尚數十萬。以其所入給其所出，而又取盈於常供，游食之待哺者…
translation_en: …be laid down in the empire; their application depends on whether circumstances are favorable or adverse, and their execution follows a proper sequence. Moreover, the military manuals say: "To await the exhausted in ease brings victory; to await the unprepared in preparedness brings victory." And they also say: "To await the hungry while well-fed brings victory." Indeed, when grain is transported a thousand li, the soldiers wear a hungry look; if an army does not have a full meal the night before, it is hard to engage the enemy with it. Therefore, if one's troops are inferior, do not provoke battle with the enemy; if one's grain is inferior, do not engage in a protracted standoff with them. This speaks to the paramount importance of provisions. In the Battle of Changping, Qin used light troops to cut off the provisions of Zhao, and Zhao Kuo perished. For the army north of the Yellow River, a walled corridor was built to transport grain to it; Xiang Yu crossed the river, severed the supply line in nine battles, captured Wang Li, and shattered the Qin army. When the Duke of Pei (Liu Bang) joined forces and marched west, the Scholar of Gaoyang (Li Yiji) leaned on his riding whip and advised a surprise attack on Chenliu, securing its stockpiled grain before entering the Pass. When the General of Fast Cavalry (Huo Qubing) went on campaign, the Son of Heaven went so far as to dispatch the Grand Provisioner with several dozen carriages of supplies, and the heavy wagons had a surplus of fine grain and meat. Such was the thoroughness of their preparations! That an army marches on its provisions has indeed been recorded since antiquity. Today, both public and private resources are anxiously strained and suffer from insufficiency—where does the root of the problem ultimately lie? Some say it lies in troops and not in provisions, but I, in my simplicity, say it lies in provisions and not in troops. Those in authority still wait and make no plans for rehabilitation and future security, at which I cannot help feeling perplexed. Consider the remoteness of Guangdong: the people are exhausted by their livelihoods, and the pursuits of agriculture and sericulture are scarce. Yet if we reckon the military provisions of the provincial agencies and prefectures, the annual revenue is no less than 420,000; and between Huizhou and Chaozhou, where uncultivated land stretches for a thousand li, the arrears in regular tax quotas still amount to several hundred thousand. If we use what is taken in to supply what is expended, and furthermore extract a surplus beyond the regular quotas, while the idle consumers waiting to be fed…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聱聱然誰何此其難可知矣稱兵之後死
事之民不得一筭之復議者見邊烽不驚
遂欲倣古寓兵於農之意嗟乎寢兵之說
勝則阻險不守矣兵民之說岐則士卒不
戰矣以其食之不給也而因以廢兵何異
因噎而廢食因溺而廢舟者乎故陸兵以
待萑葦之竊發水兵以待島嶼之出沒規
制華夷遏鎭要害缺一不可至其慎功實
之辨去浮淫之蠹防冒濫之原不可不察
===
也說者謂今之兵將非昔矣選練矣服習
矣其節約明矣步伐合地宜矣而執事猶
有不然者何耶夫明者視於無形聰者聽
於無聲誠先其未然則天下事無足爲者
今試舉一歲之所入而覈其所出其果一
一中食而無游靡者乎民之出食果足歲
計而無單竭抑損者乎官持尺籍料量果
鱗次輻輳無壅蹙於將事者乎田租河渡
鹽鐵榷會其果時入而不乾沒於胥吏逋
punctuated: 聱聱然誰何？此其難可知矣。稱兵之後，死事之民不得一筭之復；議者見邊烽不驚，遂欲倣古寓兵於農之意。嗟乎！寢兵之說勝，則阻險不守矣；兵民之說岐，則士卒不戰矣。以其食之不給也，而因以廢兵，何異因噎而廢食、因溺而廢舟者乎？故陸兵以待萑葦之竊發，水兵以待島嶼之出沒，規制華夷，遏鎭要害，缺一不可。至其慎功實之辨，去浮淫之蠹，防冒濫之原，不可不察也。說者謂今之兵將非昔矣，選練矣，服習矣，其節約明矣，步伐合地宜矣，而執事猶有不然者，何耶？夫明者視於無形，聰者聽於無聲；誠先其未然，則天下事無足爲者。今試舉一歲之所入而覈其所出，其果一一中食而無游靡者乎？民之出食果足歲計而無單竭抑損者乎？官持尺籍料量，果鱗次輻輳，無壅蹙於將事者乎？田租、河渡、鹽鐵、榷會，其果時入而不乾沒於胥吏、逋…
translation_en: … clamorously—who can question them? From this, the difficulty of the situation can be known. After military operations, the people who died in service do not receive the exemption of even a single poll-tax unit; yet when discussants see that the frontier beacons are not alarmed, they immediately wish to imitate the ancient intention of lodging soldiers among the farmers. Alas! When the doctrine of laying down arms prevails, strategic passes are left unguarded; when the doctrines regarding soldiers and civilians diverge, the troops do not fight. Because provisions are insufficient, to thereby abolish the troops—how is this any different from giving up eating for fear of choking, or abolishing boats because of drowning? Therefore, land forces are used to guard against the covert outbreaks of bandits in the marshes, and naval forces are used to guard against the sudden appearances of pirates among the islands. In regulating Chinese and non-Chinese and suppressing and garrisoning strategic points, neither can be dispensed with. As for carefully distinguishing true merit, eliminating the parasites of superfluous extravagance, and guarding against the sources of fraudulent abuse, these must not fail to be examined. Commentators say that today's troops and generals are no longer like those of the past: they are selected and trained, accustomed to service, their discipline and compacts are clear, and their maneuvers suit the terrain; yet Your Excellency still considers it not so—why is this? Now, the clear-sighted see what is formless, and the acute of hearing hear what is soundless; if one truly anticipates things before they materialize, then nothing in the world is too difficult to accomplish. Now, suppose we take the revenue of an entire year and verify its expenditures: does every single item truly go to feed the troops without any idle waste? Are the provisions produced by the people truly sufficient for the annual budget without exhaustion or curtailment? When officials hold the muster rolls and measure out grain, do supplies truly arrive in orderly succession like fish scales and converge like wheel spokes, without bottleneck or shortage when operations are underway? As for land taxes, river-ferry tolls, salt and iron monopolies, and commercial excises, are they truly brought in on time without being embezzled by clerks and subofficial functionaries or defaulted on…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
貸於豪富者乎彼其林林相聚星羅碁布
爲其先於無形而制其未動也枵腹而待
則良平失其智衞霍無所策彼之視我如
振落我之視彼如赴湯火是我制於敵而
不能制敵進退之權皆不在我其去來任
之矣然則所云兵將水陸者其聲實安在
乎古者兵民不分無事則耰鋤良民有事
則荷戈接敵故軍興不煩均節而九賦九
式無所謂兵旅之費今兵民二而緩急無
===
所恃羽書狎至所調發不逮千數邦內騷
動有司屏營旁皇日餼月餼行饟坐餉袖
手待絀主將齘齔所謂民外之兵不耕而
食者其不能贍勢也吾觀漢將以雲中守
却匈奴七百餘里虜不敢南下牧馬今得
爲漢故事乎守自守而將自將故將得調
其攻殺刺擊而不得適饑飽其有所掣肘
而不能專制者亦勢也又況兵力有不盡
然者此民所以囂囂苦不足也分屯列戍
punctuated: 貸於豪富者乎？彼其林林相聚，星羅碁布，爲其先於無形而制其未動也。枵腹而待，則良、平失其智，衞、霍無所策。彼之視我如振落，我之視彼如赴湯火，是我制於敵而不能制敵，進退之權皆不在我，其去來任之矣。然則所云兵將水陸者，其聲實安在乎？古者兵民不分，無事則耰鋤良民，有事則荷戈接敵，故軍興不煩均節，而九賦九式無所謂兵旅之費。今兵民二而緩急無所恃，羽書狎至，所調發不逮千數，邦內騷動，有司屏營旁皇，日餼月餼，行饟坐餉，袖手待絀，主將齘齔。所謂民外之兵，不耕而食者，其不能贍，勢也。吾觀漢將以雲中守却匈奴七百餘里，虜不敢南下牧馬，今得爲漢故事乎？守自守而將自將，故將得調其攻殺刺擊，而不得適饑飽，其有所掣肘而不能專制者，亦勢也。又況兵力有不盡然者，此民所以囂囂苦不足也。分屯列戍
translation_en: …or defaulted on by wealthy magnates? Those troops are gathered in dense multitudes and arrayed like stars in the sky or pieces on a go board, in order to forestall threats before they take shape and control the enemy before he moves. Yet if they must wait on empty stomachs, then even Zhang Liang 張良 and Chen Ping 陳平 would lose their wisdom, and Wei Qing 衛青 and Huo Qubing 霍去病 would have no strategy to offer. The enemy would regard us as easy as shaking down falling leaves, while we would regard facing them as walking into boiling water or fire. Thus we would be controlled by the enemy rather than able to control them; the initiative to advance or retreat would not rest with us at all, and they would come and go as they please. That being so, where is the correspondence between reputation and reality in what we have said about troops, generals, and land and naval forces? In antiquity, soldiers and civilians were not separated: in times of peace they were good subjects wielding hoes and rakes, and in times of crisis they shouldered halberds to engage the enemy. Therefore, raising an army did not require the trouble of equalizing and regulating supplies, and among the nine revenues and nine expenditure formulas there was no separate category for military expenses. Today, soldiers and civilians are split in two, and yet in an emergency there is nothing to rely upon. When feathered dispatches arrive in rapid succession and the troops mobilized do not even reach a thousand, the whole region is thrown into turmoil. The authorities pace about in anxious confusion over daily and monthly rations, campaign provisions and garrison pay, folding their hands as they await exhaustion of funds while the commanding generals gnash their teeth in frustration. That these so-called soldiers outside the civilian population, who eat without tilling, cannot be adequately supported is the inevitable trend of circumstances. I observe that in the Han dynasty, generals serving as Grand Administrators of Yunzhong 雲中 drove the Xiongnu 匈奴 back more than seven hundred li, so that the raiders dared not come south to pasture their horses. Can we follow that Han precedent today? Civil administrators govern on their own and military commanders command on their own; thus a general may direct the attacking, killing, thrusting, and striking, but cannot regulate his men's hunger and satiety. That he has his hands tied and cannot exercise sole authority is also the inevitable trend of circumstances. How much more so when the strength of the troops does not even live up to this—which is why the common people clamor in distress over insufficiency. Since the system of dividing agricultural colonies and arraying frontier garrisons…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之法旣不能如古而雜耕渭濱之事兵又
不肯屈首就信地以稍寬民力吾知司計
者有不能一夕高枕矣然則故額不可增
也量入而出計口而授其有司之事乎程
其武力嚴其節制省其技擊必其賞罰其
將帥事乎先後虛實雲物風候陰符武經
之類羣七校之士而聽命不使有一夫偷
靡焉則將知兵兵習戰攻則取守則固懷
敵附遠何招不至兵得以保境民得以脩
===
業兵民相用百世之利也管子曰國不虛
重兵不虛勝民不虛用令不虛行國重以
兵兵勝在民民用以令令行以財今嶺海
之民疲矣正賦之外所輸幾何縣官之督
促無已入不及十分之一而云終歲勤動
其厭兵者一切偷安目前曰無事見兵而
不見敵有事見敵而不見兵寧蠲四十萬
之輸使民自戰守彼雖善攻終不能歲得
四十萬我卽不善守終不至歲失四十萬
punctuated: 之法，旣不能如古，而雜耕渭濱之事，兵又不肯屈首就信地，以稍寬民力，吾知司計者有不能一夕高枕矣。然則故額不可增也，量入而出，計口而授，其有司之事乎？程其武力，嚴其節制，省其技擊，必其賞罰，其將帥事乎？先後、虛實、雲物、風候、《陰符》、《武經》之類，羣七校之士而聽命，不使有一夫偷靡焉。則將知兵，兵習戰，攻則取，守則固，懷敵附遠，何招不至？兵得以保境，民得以脩業，兵民相用，百世之利也。《管子》曰：「國不虛重，兵不虛勝，民不虛用，令不虛行。國重以兵，兵勝在民，民用以令，令行以財。」今嶺海之民疲矣！正賦之外，所輸幾何？縣官之督促無已，入不及十分之一，而云終歲勤動。其厭兵者，一切偷安目前，曰：「無事見兵而不見敵，有事見敵而不見兵。寧蠲四十萬之輸，使民自戰守；彼雖善攻，終不能歲得四十萬，我卽不善守，終不至歲失四十萬。」
translation_en: … the method of [distributing agricultural colonies and garrison posts] can no longer be practiced as in antiquity, and as for the practice of farming intermingled with locals along the banks of the Wei River, the soldiers are likewise unwilling to bow their heads and take to their assigned lands so as to slightly relieve the strength of the people. I know that those in charge of fiscal planning cannot rest easy on their pillows for even a single night! If that is the case, then the established quotas cannot be increased. Measuring expenditures against revenues and doling out rations by counting mouths—is that not the business of the civil authorities? Assessing their martial strength, enforcing strict discipline upon them, inspecting their combat skills, and making certain their rewards and punishments—is that not the business of the generals and commanders? In matters such as priority and sequence, emptiness and solidity, cloud omens and wind signs, and texts like the Secret Tally (Yinfu) and the Military Classics (Wujing), if one gathers the troops of the seven regiments to obey commands without allowing a single man to be idle or wasteful, then the generals will know their troops, and the troops will be practiced in warfare. When attacking, they will capture; when defending, they will hold fast. In winning over enemies and attracting those from afar, whom could they summon that would not come? When the soldiers are able to protect the borders and the people are able to attend to their livelihoods, soldiers and civilians mutually supporting one another is a benefit for a hundred generations. The Master Guan (Guanzi) says: "A state does not become weighty out of nothing; an army does not win victories out of nothing; the people are not employed out of nothing; orders are not carried out out of nothing. A state becomes weighty through its army; an army wins victories through its people; the people are employed through orders; and orders are carried out through wealth." Today, the people of the Linghai region [Guangdong] are exhausted! Beyond the regular tax quota, how much more are they made to contribute? The relentless dunning by government authorities never ceases; what is actually collected does not reach one part in ten, yet the people are kept toiling the whole year round. Those who are weary of the military altogether seek only temporary ease for the present moment, saying: "In times of peace, we see the soldiers but do not see the enemy; in times of trouble, we see the enemy but do not see the soldiers. It would be better to remit the contribution of four hundred thousand and let the people fight and defend for themselves; even if the enemy is skilled at attacking, in the end they could not gain four hundred thousand in a year, and even if we are not skilled at defending, in the end we would not go so far as to lose four hundred thousand in a year." …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
强在俛仰之間故兵不足則召募之耳食
不足則徵發之耳此不過在股掌之上非
阨塞秘伏而籌也至於兵不習戰以其將
予敵將不知兵以其國予敵嚴矣哉然則
桓文之兵可謂入其域而有節制者而猶
不足以敵湯武之仁義則所云技擊銳士
又在桓文下矣若今之士去秦魏又下矣
吾故曰兵不在多寡而在選練將不在勇
怯而在知兵書生何知鄰於狂瞽惟執事
===
裁擇
punctuated: 强在俛仰之間，故兵不足則召募之耳，食不足則徵發之耳，此不過在股掌之上，非阨塞秘伏而籌也。至於兵不習戰，以其將予敵；將不知兵，以其國予敵。嚴矣哉！然則桓、文之兵，可謂入其域而有節制者，而猶不足以敵湯、武之仁義，則所云技擊、銳士，又在桓、文下矣。若今之士，去秦、魏又下矣。吾故曰：兵不在多寡而在選練，將不在勇怯而在知兵。書生何知，鄰於狂瞽，惟執事裁擇。
translation_en:
… [weakness and] strength can shift in the blink of an eye. Therefore, if troops are insufficient, one simply recruits them; if provisions are insufficient, one simply requisitions them. These matters lie merely in the palm of one's hand, not requiring secret calculations over strategic passes and hidden ambushes. As for the saying that "if soldiers are not practiced in warfare, it is handing one's general over to the enemy; if the general does not understand military affairs, it is handing one's state over to the enemy"—how stern a warning this is!

Thus, the armies of Dukes Huan of Qi and Wen of Jin may be said to have entered the realm of disciplined control, yet even they were no match for the benevolence and righteousness of Kings Tang and Wu; those referred to as "skilled fighters" (jiji) and "elite troops" (ruishi) were lower still than the soldiers of Huan and Wen. As for the soldiers of today, they fall even further below those of Qin and Wei. Therefore I say: the effectiveness of troops lies not in their numbers, great or small, but in their selection and training; the worth of a general lies not in his bravery or cowardice, but in his understanding of military affairs. What does a mere scholar know? My words border on rashness and blindness; I pray only that Your Excellency will judge and select from them.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
此其尤章明較著者也然天生五材誰能
去兵國家雖平忘戰必危自古及今未有
易者是故嚴覈實而舟游之師虛實相半
矣則冒名之罰宜重也精武技而貴游之
子濫竽行列矣則浮冗之禁宜亟也謹斥
堠而信地之別依違觀望矣則失事之罪
宜正也戒姑息而脅從之黨哨聚要賞矣
則招撫之失宜究也兵以禦備而偏將裨
將人奴役使矣則點閱之法宜慎也而又
===
爲之慎召募覈功實撫民不以入士伍謁
客不以待行間試之以刺擊而陰簡其白
徒不必補可也均之以營伍而稍減其名
額數不必六可也專之以責任而統之以
裨將遙授名色之類不必多可也縱賊與
退縮同罰頂名與失事同罰起居不精動
靜不必士不選練卒不服習則將領同罰
如此則民之營衞也國之屏蔽也彼其食
之也奚尤焉雖然兵凶器戰危事以弱爲
punctuated: 此其尤章明較著者也。然天生五材，誰能去兵？國家雖平，忘戰必危，自古及今，未有易者。是故嚴覈實，而舟游之師虛實相半矣，則冒名之罰宜重也；精武技，而貴游之子濫竽行列矣，則浮冗之禁宜亟也；謹斥堠，而信地之別依違觀望矣，則失事之罪宜正也；戒姑息，而脅從之黨哨聚要賞矣，則招撫之失宜究也；兵以禦備，而偏將、裨將人奴役使矣，則點閱之法宜慎也。而又爲之慎召募、覈功實，撫民不以入士伍，謁客不以待行間；試之以刺擊，而陰簡其白徒，不必補可也；均之以營伍，而稍減其名額，數不必六可也；專之以責任，而統之以裨將，遙授名色之類不必多可也。縱賊與退縮同罰，頂名與失事同罰，起居不精，動靜不必，士不選練，卒不服習，則將領同罰。如此則民之營衞也，國之屏蔽也，彼其食之也奚尤焉？雖然，兵凶器，戰危事，以弱爲
translation_en:
…These are the most manifestly obvious examples. Yet Heaven produces the five materials—who can do away with weapons? Though the state be at peace, to forget warfare will surely bring peril; from antiquity to the present, this principle has never changed.

Therefore, we seek to strictly verify actual strength, yet among the naval patrolling forces, half the rosters are empty and half real—thus the punishment for fraudulent assumption of names ought to be made heavy. We seek to refine martial skills, yet the sons of roving notables pad the ranks without competence—thus the prohibition against superfluous and idle personnel ought to be made urgent. We seek to maintain vigilant lookouts, yet across the divisions of assigned garrison sectors they hesitate and watch from the sidelines—thus the crime of dereliction in military affairs ought to be rectified. We seek to guard against indulgent leniency, yet coerced followers gather at the whistle to demand rewards—thus the failures of pacification and appeasement ought to be investigated. Troops are meant for defense and preparedness, yet Assistant Commanders and Deputy Commanders treat them like personal servants for menial labor—thus the procedures for roll-call and inspection ought to be made rigorous.

Furthermore, we must exercise care in recruitment and verify the reality of merits: pacified commoners should not be inducted into the military ranks, and visiting hangers-on should not be entertained within the camps. Test the men in thrusting and striking while quietly culling out the untrained civilians—there is no need to fill up the vacant slots. Equalize them across the camp squads and slightly reduce their nominal quotas—the number of camps need not be fixed at six. Consolidate their responsibilities and place them under the command of Deputy Commanders—nominal appointments held from afar and similar titles need not be numerous. Let letting bandits escape carry the same punishment as retreating in cowardice; let substituting names on the roster carry the same punishment as operational failure; and if daily routines are not precise, movements not decisive, officers not selected and trained, and soldiers not obedient and practiced, let the commanding officers share the same punishment.

If this is done, the troops will act as the vital protective energy of the people and the protective screen of the state—what fault could there be in their consuming the state's rations? Even so, weapons are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is a perilous affair; to make weakness into…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之事賓興之舉乎爰及唐宋
文獻乃可徵然亦堇堇指數
皇明受
天景命南嚮而聽所漸摩覆露無
先于南者粤自是蔚為文明
之區夷考科目得人則莫若
弘正之際與嘉靖初元雖立
===
功立德所究人人殊總之弗
遜于古頃粤又稱兵士惴焉
未有寧宇賴
朝廷威靈山妖海孽以次芟夷
蘊崇之昔之贏糧而入保者
今得鼓篋而復脩其業矣則
何莫非
punctuated: 之事，賓興之舉乎？爰及唐、宋，文獻乃可徵，然亦堇堇指數。皇明受天景命，南嚮而聽，所漸摩覆露，無先于南者，粤自是蔚為文明之區。夷考科目得人，則莫若弘、正之際與嘉靖初元，雖立功立德，所究人人殊，總之弗遜于古。頃粤又稱兵，士惴焉未有寧宇。賴朝廷威靈，山妖海孽，以次芟夷蘊崇之。昔之贏糧而入保者，今得鼓篋而復脩其業矣，則何莫非
translation_en: … affairs, or the practice of recommending worthy men as honored guests to court? Down to the Tang and Song dynasties, literary documents and worthy men finally became verifiable, yet even then they could barely be counted on the fingers. When the August Ming received Heaven's great mandate and faced south to rule, in the regions it gradually transformed and sheltered under its dewy grace, none came before the South; from then on, Guangdong flourished as a realm of cultural brilliance. If one examines the talent obtained through the civil service examination categories, no period compares to the transition between the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras and the early years of the Jiajing era (1522–1566). Although in establishing merit and establishing virtue what each individual attained differed from person to person, taken all together they were in no way inferior to the ancients. Recently Guangdong once again saw the raising of troops, and scholars were fearful, without a peaceful dwelling. Relying on the awe-inspiring numinous power of the Imperial Court, the mountain demons and sea monsters [bandits and pirates] were successively mowed down, exterminated, heaped up, and destroyed. Those who in the past carried provisions on their backs to take refuge in fortifications can now beat the drum, open their book-boxes, and resume cultivating their studies. How could all of this be anything other than …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上恩哉故重俊竊伏讀多士之文
而知其盛之有自也夫攀翠
虯之逸鱗附朱鳳之靈羽出
潗離奧自燿于熙明者大人
之業也泳
玄澤戴
鴻施烝烝然思報效無巳者烈士
===
之槩也多士旦夕躡屩而上
公車試用伊始且安所成信
乎專言之與效實也則有異
矣志不幾于峻標峙坊而陽
浮以隨俗之好道不存于塞
違昭德而如韋以干主之澤
事不顓于詒法賴民而設色
punctuated: 上恩哉？故重俊竊伏讀多士之文，而知其盛之有自也。夫攀翠虯之逸鱗，附朱鳳之靈羽，出潗離奧，自燿于熙明者，大人之業也；泳玄澤，戴鴻施，烝烝然思報效無巳者，烈士之槩也。多士旦夕躡屩而上公車，試用伊始，且安所成信乎？專言之與效實也，則有異矣。志不幾于峻標峙坊，而陽浮以隨俗之好；道不存于塞違昭德，而如韋以干主之澤；事不顓于詒法賴民，而設色
translation_en: … His Majesty's grace? Thus as I, Chongjun, humbly read the writings of the many scholars, I know that their flourishing has its origin. Now, clinging to the soaring scales of the emerald horned dragon, attaching oneself to the numinous wings of the vermilion phoenix, emerging from bubbling springs and departing hidden recesses to shine forth in an era of radiant peace—this is the enterprise of a great man. Swimming in profound favor, bearing vast beneficence, and ardently thinking of rendering service in repayment without cease—this is the mettle of a heroic scholar. Sooner or later the many scholars will don straw sandals and board the official carriages for the capital; as their appointment to office begins, how shall they establish their trustworthiness? Focusing on words and delivering results are indeed two different things. When one's ambition does not aspire to set a lofty standard and stand as a moral bulwark, but instead puts on a superficial show to follow popular tastes; when one's Way does not lie in stemming transgressions and making virtue manifest, but instead bends like soft leather to seek the ruler's favor; when one's service is not devoted to bequeathing good laws and benefiting the people, but instead puts on false colors…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以要時之譽世所稱才賢大
率然已不者營私營利所如
滿志舉生平而弁髦之先資
謂何甚哉徒言之可畏也人
之材器固若升龠斗石然各
有所受不可強也乃如心無
不可自盡者是心之精潛深
===
入劤燭幽窮遐意有所注鬼
神輔之熊渠子援弓而射伏
石飲羽痀僂丈人承蜩猶掇
之也此精神之極也然心豈
有二用公私義利在決所擇
爾心乎為私而能奉公心乎
為利而能好義者無之故士
punctuated: 以要時之譽，世所稱才賢，大率然已。不者，營私營利，所如滿志，舉生平而弁髦之，先資謂何？甚哉，徒言之可畏也！人之材器，固若升龠斗石然，各有所受，不可強也。乃如心，無不可自盡者。是心之精，潛深入劤，燭幽窮遐，意有所注，鬼神輔之。熊渠子援弓而射，伏石飲羽；痀僂丈人承蜩，猶掇之也。此精神之極也。然心豈有二用？公私義利，在決所擇爾。心乎為私而能奉公，心乎為利而能好義者，無之。故士
translation_en: …to court the praise of the times—what the world calls talented and worthy men are mostly like this. Otherwise, they pursue private ends and seek personal profit; getting their wishes wherever they go, they cast aside the principles of their entire lives like a useless cap. What then becomes of the pledges they made before taking office? Terrible indeed is the danger of empty words! As for people's talents and capacities, they are naturally like measures of a pint, a flute-measure, a peck, or a stone—each has its own limit and cannot be forced. Yet when it comes to the mind, there is nothing in which one cannot fully exert oneself. The essence of this mind penetrates deeply into what is sinewy and tough, illuminates the dark, and reaches the distant; where the will is focused, ghosts and spirits lend their aid. When Xiong Quzi drew his bow and shot, the crouching stone swallowed the arrow up to its feathers; when the hunchbacked old man caught cicadas on his pole, it was as easy as picking them up with his hand. This is the utmost concentration of spirit. Yet how can the mind be used in two ways at once? Between public and private, righteousness and profit, everything depends on a decisive choice. There has never been anyone whose mind was set on private ends yet could serve the public good, or whose mind was set on profit yet could love righteousness. Therefore, if a scholar…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
誠服官思勤臨衆思辨在敵
思鬭銜命思不辱則盡心矣
心盡乃可以成信夫是之謂
眞才賢多士其無意不佞之
言乎繼自今以往永矢一心
以圖報塞勿以崇卑豐約多
岐岐之立功立德期有紹于
===
前聞使人謂科目得人無若
今玆爲最主司者亦竊知言
之名附于以人事
君之忠是士與主司耦俱得也昔
墨翟見素絲而歎曰此夫染
於蒼則蒼染於黃則黃者非
特物然士亦有之習俗之移
punctuated: 誠服官思勤，臨衆思辨，在敵思鬭，銜命思不辱，則盡心矣。心盡乃可以成信，夫是之謂眞才賢。多士其無意不佞之言乎？繼自今以往，永矢一心，以圖報塞，勿以崇卑、豐約多岐岐之，立功、立德，期有紹于前聞，使人謂科目得人，無若今玆爲最。主司者亦竊知言之名，附于以人事君之忠，是士與主司耦俱得也。昔墨翟見素絲而歎曰：「此夫染於蒼則蒼，染於黃則黃者。」非特物然，士亦有之，習俗之移
translation_en: …truly thinks of diligence when serving in office, thinks of clear discernment when facing the multitude, thinks of fighting when confronting the enemy, and thinks of not bringing disgrace when bearing a commission, then he has exhausted his mind. Only when the mind is fully devoted can trustworthiness be achieved; this is what is called true talent and worthiness. Will the many scholars have no regard for my unworthy words? From this day forward, forever pledge a single mind in seeking to repay the state and fulfill your duty, and do not let the many forkings of high or low station, abundance or austerity, lead it astray. In establishing merit and establishing virtue, aspire to carry on the renown of your predecessors, so that people will say that in obtaining men of talent through the examination system, no year has surpassed the present one as the very best. Those in charge of the examination would then also venture to claim a reputation for knowing men through their words, attaching themselves to the loyalty of serving the Sovereign by recommending worthy men; thus the scholars and the examiners will both have achieved their aims together. In antiquity, Mo Di 墨翟 saw undyed silk and sighed, saying: "This is that which becomes dark green when dyed in dark green, and becomes yellow when dyed in yellow." It is not only things that are thus; scholars are also subject to this, for the way custom transforms…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人也甚於染多士始進宜自
愛母使命儒者爲墨氏之徒
所竊歎哉
浙江台州府僊居縣儒學敎
諭楊重俊謹序
punctuated:
人也，甚於染。多士始進，宜自愛，母使命儒者爲墨氏之徒所竊歎哉！
浙江台州府僊居縣儒學敎諭楊重俊謹序。
translation_en:
… people is even more potent than dyeing! Now that you many scholars are first advancing into officialdom, you ought to cherish your integrity; do not let those who style themselves Confucians be secretly lamented over by the followers of Mozi!

Respectfully written as a postface by Yang Chongjun 楊重俊, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xianju County 僊居縣, Taizhou Prefecture 台州府, Zhejiang 浙江.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋八月天下復當
巡按廣東監察御史詹
===
阿一理李應
同考試官提調
臣右布政
使鄒善監試則按察使史朝
寀副使孫光祖旣入院百執
事受法約惟謹乃合提學副
使林如楚所選士二千有奇
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋八月，天下復當……巡按廣東監察御史詹……阿一理、李應……同考試官，提調……臣、右布政使鄒善，監試則按察使史朝寀、副使孫光祖。旣入院，百執事受法約惟謹。乃合提學副使林如楚所選士二千有奇，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), the empire once again was due to [hold the Provincial Examinations?] … Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor Zhan [Zhentai 詹貞泰] … [A Yili 阿一理?], Li Ying [李應] … as Associate Examiners; the Proctors were … [Your servant?] and Right Administration Commissioner Zou Shan 鄒善; and the Surveillance Officials of the Examination were Surveillance Commissioner Shi Chaocai 史朝寀 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Sun Guangzu 孫光祖. Once they had entered the examination compound, all the functionaries received the regulations and rules with utmost care. Then they gathered the more than two thousand scholars selected by Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lin Ruchu 林如楚, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
三試校其尤者七十有五人
竝其文籍
奏之〔貞泰〕不佞以職事宜宣言
首簡〔貞泰〕竊惟百匯莫弘於
以不知其幾
虚逼天津蓋天
□粵之雄注故
===
嶺海南冥之一都會也自任
囂開疆陸賈通使始入帝籍
而人文未宣彼其潗澯瀲灧
往往變雲物興寶藏珠璣犀
象瑇瑁丹砂之利甲於天下
唐宋以來儒術寢著則張九
齡余靖崔與之諸人相繼羽
punctuated:
三試，校其尤者七十有五人，竝其文籍奏之。〔貞泰〕不佞，以職事宜宣言首簡。

〔貞泰〕竊惟百匯莫弘於……以不知其幾……虚逼天津，蓋天……□粵之雄注，故嶺海、南冥之一都會也。自任囂開疆，陸賈通使，始入帝籍，而人文未宣。彼其潗澯瀲灧，往往變雲物，興寶藏，珠璣、犀象、瑇瑁、丹砂之利，甲於天下。唐、宋以來，儒術寢著，則張九齡、余靖、崔與之諸人，相繼羽
translation_en:
…through three sessions of examination, and evaluated the most outstanding among them, numbering seventy-five men, and submitted their names along with the texts of their essays to the throne. Unworthy as I, [Zhentai], am, by virtue of the duties of my office it is fitting that I make a declaration on the opening pages.

I, [Zhentai], venture to reflect that among the hundred convergences of waters, none is vaster than [the ocean?]… by one knows not how many [thousands of li?]… [its] emptiness presses close upon the Celestial Ford [?]; indeed, heaven… [?] the mighty outpouring of Yue, making it a great metropolis between the Mountains and the Sea, by the Southern Ocean. From the time Ren Xiao 任囂 opened up the frontier and Lu Jia 陸賈 came as envoy, the region was first entered into the imperial registers, yet its cultural refinement had not yet been made manifest. Its surging, brimming waters and rippling waves often transformed into auspicious clouds and vapors and gave rise to precious treasures, so that its wealth in pearls, rhinoceros horn, ivory, tortoiseshell, and cinnabar ranked first in the world. From the Tang and Song dynasties onward, Confucian learning gradually became prominent, and men such as Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, Yu Jing 余靖, and Cui Yuzhi 崔與之 successively arose as wings [of support]…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
翼後先起矣
明興
列聖紹熙代光揆以文教賓於制
科海隅蒼生靡然興文學冠
帶衣履與齊魯埒於是文章
如丘濬理學如陳獻章皆蔚
然為一時翹楚而其他名公
===
鉅卿炳烺相望未可一二數
向所云溟澥之精始鍾萃發
洩於交庾之間為俊藪而珠
璣犀象瑇瑁丹砂之利亦稍
間歇迺知天之至寶固有所
在不有以宣之不達今
皇上
punctuated: 翼，後先起矣。明興，列聖紹熙，代光揆以文教，賓於制科。海隅蒼生，靡然興文學，冠帶衣履，與齊魯埒。於是文章如丘濬、理學如陳獻章，皆蔚然為一時翹楚；而其他名公鉅卿，炳烺相望，未可一二數。向所云溟澥之精，始鍾萃發洩於交、庾之間，為俊藪；而珠璣、犀象、瑇瑁、丹砂之利，亦稍間歇。迺知天之至寶，固有所，在不有以宣之，不達。今皇上
translation_en: …serving as wings of support, arose one after another. When the Ming dynasty arose, the successive emperors continued and magnified the imperial enterprise, generation after generation illuminating and ordering the realm through literary education and welcoming worthies into the civil service examinations. The common people of this maritime corner were swept along in the rise of literary learning, until in caps, sashes, robes, and shoes—the markers of scholarly refinement—they rivaled Qi and Lu. Thereupon, in literary composition, figures such as Qiu Jun 丘濬, and in the Learning of Principle, figures such as Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章, all flourished as the preeminent talents of their age; while other renowned nobles and great ministers shone in succession within sight of one another, too numerous to be counted one by one. What was earlier called the essence of the vast seas thus began to gather and pour forth between Jiaozhi and Mount Dayu as amarshland of outstanding talents, while the riches of pearls, rhinoceros horn, ivory, tortoiseshell, and cinnabar somewhat abated. From this one knows that the supreme treasures of Heaven indeed have where they reside, yet without something to bring them forth, they do not manifest. Now His Majesty the Emperor…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
英睿神聖
握符凝
命覃聲敎之暨無間海內外靡不
矯翩思奮蓋千載一時也貞
泰始以聘往觀山河表裏臨
鴻濛測潏浤遠睨於扶桑之
標浩瀚兼天一瞬無際西矚
===
於蒼梧鬱林崛崎崒嵂應接
不暇廼喟然而歎文不在玆
乎諸賢之聯翩翔輝有然矣
比從事獲與諸生之業言人
人殊然類能採英拮華腴贍
道德卽不能者亦不失繩墨
庶幾哉有當足以備他日煌
punctuated: 英睿神聖，握符凝命，覃聲敎之暨，無間海內外，靡不矯翩思奮，蓋千載一時也。貞泰始以聘往，觀山河表裏，臨鴻濛，測潏浤，遠睨於扶桑之標，浩瀚兼天，一瞬無際；西矚於蒼梧、鬱林，崛崎崒嵂，應接不暇。廼喟然而歎：「文不在玆乎？諸賢之聯翩翔輝有然矣！」比從事，獲與諸生之業，言人人殊，然類能採英拮華，腴贍道德；卽不能者，亦不失繩墨，庶幾哉有當，足以備他日，煌
translation_en:
…is brilliant, sagacious, divine, and圣-like, holding the imperial tally and consolidating the Mandate of Heaven. The reach of his far-spreading prestige and moral instruction makes no distinction between within and beyond the seas; there is none who does not lift his wings and long to rouse himself to action—truly, this is a moment that comes once in a thousand years.

When I, Zhentai, first traveled here upon being invited to serve, I observed the inner and outer landscapes of mountains and rivers. Looking out over the primordial expanse and plumbing the surging depths, I gazed far off toward the landmark of Fusang in the east, where the vast waters merge with the sky, boundless in a single glance; to the west, I looked toward Cangwu and Yulin, where the peaks rise rugged and precipitous, more than the eye can take in. Thereupon I sighed in admiration and said: "Is not culture lodged right here? That the many worthies soar in succession with such radiance is surely because of this!"

When I took up my duties and was privileged to examine the essays of the candidates, their words differed from person to person, yet generally they were able to gather the finest blossoms and pluck the choicest flowers, enriching their writings with the Way and its Virtue. Even those who could not reach that level still did not depart from the proper standards. How close they come to hitting the mark, sufficient to prepare for future use—how resplendent…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
煌乎盛矣此寧獨氣數然其
諸有作於風者耶叔孫穆子
曰太上立德其次立言迺今
言則人能矣顧所取與所用
異也辭章功實其大指殊科
今必以立談之間槩平生之
業旣已難矣乃復求十一於
===
千百則難之難者也彼其貌
言不適聲實縣絕諸士謂何
國家需賢如責質程功棄僞增
實吾卽不敢設不然之事以
待異日脫有萬一將何所傅
其罪吾於是益竦然滋懼已
語曰文理未明不可與弁兼
punctuated: 煌乎盛矣！此寧獨氣數然，其諸有作於風者耶？叔孫穆子曰：「太上立德，其次立言。」迺今言則人能矣，顧所取與所用異也，辭章、功實，其大指殊科。今必以立談之間，槩平生之業，旣已難矣，乃復求十一於千百，則難之難者也。彼其貌言不適，聲實縣絕，諸士謂何？國家需賢，如責質程功，棄僞增實，吾卽不敢設不然之事以待異日，脫有萬一，將何所傅其罪？吾於是益竦然滋懼已。語曰：「文理未明，不可與弁兼；
translation_en: …splendidly flourishing indeed! Could this merely be the result of cosmic destiny, or is it not rather something roused by transforming customs? Shusun Muzi 叔孫穆子 said: "The highest achievement is to establish virtue; the next is to establish words." Yet nowadays people are capable enough when it comes to words; however, that by which men are selected differs from that for which they are employed, and literary composition and practical achievement diverge in their fundamental aims. Now, if one must judge the undertaking of a lifetime within the space of a brief discourse, that is already difficult enough; to go on and seek ten or a hundred out of thousands is the hardest of the hard! If someone's outward appearance and words do not correspond, and his reputation and reality are poles apart, what will you scholars say? The state stands in need of worthies; if it comes to demanding substance and measuring actual merit, discarding falsehood and increasing reality—even though I do not dare assume that anything untoward will happen in the future—should there by one chance in ten thousand be such a failure, upon whom will the blame be laid? Because of this, I am all the more awestruck and increasingly fearful. The proverb says: "Before a skin's pattern and grain are distinct, it cannot be used to line a cap;…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毛羽未成不可以高蜚今士
方負垂天之具躡風雲之會
將摵膠葛翼歊烝旁摰宇宙
而游乎太清此其表樹卽曲
江新會諸君子何多讓焉諸
士勉之毋自負
明時而令秀異獨稱山海已也是
===
舉也總督兩廣軍務兵部左
侍郎凌雲翼敷德宣威奠綏
南服提督南贛軍務都察院
右副都御史江一麟崇文振
武厎定粤疆若大理寺右寺
正田登年適至平刑樂觀盛
舉至于賛襄試事則左叅政
punctuated:
毛羽未成，不可以高蜚。」今士方負垂天之具，躡風雲之會，將摵膠葛、翼歊烝，旁摰宇宙而游乎太清。此其表樹，卽曲江、新會諸君子何多讓焉？諸士勉之，毋自負明時，而令秀異獨稱山海已也。
是舉也，總督兩廣軍務兵部左侍郎凌雲翼敷德宣威，奠綏南服；提督南贛軍務都察院右副都御史江一麟崇文振武，厎定粤疆。若大理寺右寺正田登年，適至平刑，樂觀盛舉。至于賛襄試事，則左叅政
translation_en:
… and when plumage and feathers are not yet fully formed, one cannot soar on high.” Now our scholars possess the capacity to spread wings like clouds hanging from the sky and tread upon a timely meeting of wind and clouds; they are about to shake the boundless expanses, wing through the rising vapors, range across the universe, and roam in the Great Purity. In their achievements and standing, why should they yield much even to the worthy gentlemen of Qujiang 曲江 and Xinhui 新會? Strive on, scholars! Do not fail this enlightened age and let outstanding distinction be praised only in the mountains and seas.

In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and Left Vice Minister of War Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼 spread virtue and proclaimed majesty, pacifying and securing the southern domain; Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs of Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Jiang Yilin 江一麟 exalted civil culture and invigorated military might, bringing stability to the frontiers of Guangdong. As for Right Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Dengnian 田登年, he happened to arrive to administer justice and gladly witnessed this grand event. As for assisting with the affairs of the examination, Left Administration Vice Commissioner …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周浩右參政劉志伊金淛左
參議何子明右參議石磐鄭
恭副使趙可懷劉經緯施觀
民許嶽僉事徐汝陽咸防範
維周都督同知總兵張元勳
副總兵晏繼芳參將侯繼高

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
賜也達於從政乎何有
義者宜也尊賢爲大
孟子曰君子所以異於人者以其存心也
君子以仁存心以禮存心
易
九五觀我生君子无咎象曰觀我生觀民
也
===
大壯利貞大者正也正大而天地之情可
見矣
縣象著明莫大乎日月
是以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義
書
敷納以言明庶以功
念終始典于學厥德脩罔覺
不役耳目百度惟貞
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
「賜也達，於從政乎何有？」
「義者，宜也，尊賢爲大。」
「孟子曰：『君子所以異於人者，以其存心也。君子以仁存心，以禮存心。』」

易
「九五，觀我生，君子无咎。象曰：『觀我生』，觀民也。」
「大壯，利貞，大者正也。正大而天地之情可見矣。」
「縣象著明，莫大乎日月。」
「是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。」

書
「敷納以言，明庶以功。」
「念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。」
「不役耳目，百度惟貞。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
"Si is a man of comprehension; what difficulty would he have in carrying on government?" (Analects 6.8)
"Righteousness means doing what is fitting, and honoring the worthy is its greatest exercise." (Doctrine of the Mean 20)
"Mencius said: 'That whereby the superior man is distinguished from other men is what he preserves in his heart: the superior man preserves benevolence in his heart, and preserves propriety in his heart.'" (Mencius 4B.28)

Book of Changes (Yijing)
"Nine in the fifth place: Contemplating my own life, the superior man is without blame. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating my own life' means contemplating the condition of the people." (Hexagram 20, Guan)
"Great Power (Dazhuang): It is advantageous to be firm and correct. That which is great is correct. Through correctness and greatness, the disposition of heaven and earth can be seen." (Commentary on the Decision, Hexagram 34, Dazhuang)
"Of the suspended images that shine brightly, none is greater than the sun and the moon." (Great Treatise, Part 1, Ch. 11)
"Therefore they established the way of heaven and called it the dark and the light (yin and yang), established the way of earth and called it the yielding and the firm, and established the way of man and called it benevolence and righteousness." (Discussion of the Trigrams, Ch. 2)

Book of Documents (Shujing)
"They set forth and received reports in words, and clearly tested the multitude by their achievements." (Canon of Shun)
"Be mindful from first to last to be constant in learning; then your virtue will be cultivated without your being conscious of it." (Charge to Yue, Part 3)
"Do not be a servant to your ears and eyes, and then all your measures will be贞 [correct]." (Hounds of Lü)

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
詩
彼茁者葭壹發五豝
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
成王之孚下土之式永言孝思孝思維則
龍旂陽陽和鈴央央鞗革有鶬
春秋
春王正月師次于郎以俟陳人蔡人甲
午治兵俱莊公八年
===
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳莊公十有五年
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀僖公三年
楚人伐鄭僖公三年春王正月公會齊侯
宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡
潰遂伐楚盟于召陵俱僖公四年衛
人伐晉文公元年夏六月公孫敖會宋
公陳侯鄭伯晉士縠盟于垂隴文公二
punctuated:
「六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。」

《詩》：
「彼茁者葭，壹發五豝。」
「有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。」
「成王之孚，下土之式。永言孝思，孝思維則。」
「龍旂陽陽，和鈴央央，鞗革有鶬。」

《春秋》：
「春，王正月，師次于郎，以俟陳人、蔡人。」「甲午，治兵。」俱莊公八年。
「秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。」莊公十有五年。
「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。」僖公元年。「秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。」僖公三年。
「楚人伐鄭。」僖公三年。「春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，盟于召陵。」俱僖公四年。「衛人伐晉。」文公元年。「夏，六月，公孫敖會宋公、陳侯、鄭伯、晉士縠盟于垂隴。」文公二
translation_en:
"The six Ministers divide their duties; each leads his subordinates to set an example for the pastors of the nine provinces, abundantly bringing the millions of people to perfection."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"Thickly grow the reeds; with one shot of arrows, five sows are pierced."
"The clouds gather densely, and the rain falls gently and plentifully. May it rain first on our public fields, and then reach our private ones."
"King Cheng inspired trust, becoming a model for the world below. Forever he cherished filial thoughts, and his filial thoughts were the standard."
"The dragon-banners wave brightly, the chariot bells and harness bells ring clearly, and the ornamented reins gleam."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In spring, in the King's first month, the army halted at Lang to wait for the men of Chen and the men of Cai." "On the jiawu day, the troops were drilled." Both from the eighth year of Duke Zhuang.
"In autumn, the men of Song, the men of Qi, and the men of Zhu attacked兒 [Ni]." From the fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
"In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and the men of Zhu at Cheng." From the first year of Duke Xi. "In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the men of Jiang, and the men of Huang met at Yanggu." From the third year of Duke Xi.
"The men of Chu attacked Zheng." From the third year of Duke Xi. "In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to raid Cai. Cai collapsed in rout; thereupon they attacked Chu and covenanted at Shaoling." Both from the fourth year of Duke Xi. "The men of Wei attacked Jin." From the first year of Duke Wen. "In summer, in the sixth month, Gongsun Ao met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, and Shi Hu of Jin to covenant at Chuilong." From the second [year of] Duke Wen…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
年
禮記
天子當宁而立諸公東面諸侯西面曰朝
史進象笏書思對命
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮
養其身以有爲也
第貳塲
論
===
人主以天下爲度
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉各一人詔〔元光元年〕
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡爲太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕
擬宋以范祖禹爲右諫議大夫兼侍講謝
表〔元祐四年〕
判語〔五條〕
磨勘卷宗
punctuated:
年。
《禮記》：
「天子當宁而立，諸公東面，諸侯西面，曰朝。」
「史進象笏，書思對命。」
「春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。」
「養其身，以有爲也。」

第貳塲
論：
「人主以天下爲度。」
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕：
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉各一人詔〔元光元年〕。
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡爲太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕。
擬宋以范祖禹爲右諫議大夫兼侍講謝表〔元祐四年〕。
判語〔五條〕：
磨勘卷宗。
translation_en:
… [second] year [of Duke Wen]).

Record of Rites (Liji):
"The Son of Heaven stands in the space between the gate and the screen; the dukes face east, and the marquises face west: this is called the morning audience."
"The scribe presents the ivory tablet, on which to write thoughts, replies, and commands."
"To initiate in spring and cause to grow in summer is benevolence; to harvest in autumn and store in winter is righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music, and righteousness is akin to rites."
"They nourish their bodies so as to be capable of action."

Second Session

Discourse:
"The ruler of men takes the entire world as his measure."

Edict, Patent, and Memorial [candidates are examined on one of these]:

Auditing case files.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
起解金銀足色
私借驛馬
門禁鎖鑰
脩理橋梁道路
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問郊祀以饗帝學校以崇儒二者皆帝王
爲政之首務也粤自禋祀燔柴辟雝思
服虞周之盛蔑以加矣而制作備于周
===
禮及大戴記傳諸篇其文質損益之儀
可得而詳與漢唐宋願治之主間亦慕
循其跡爲史美談然漢以黑帝而增北
畤唐于南郊祭太微宋竝五方上帝而
祀之果于饗帝之禮合與中元臨雍拜
老貞觀大召名儒慶曆增脩大學講殿
以備臨幸果于崇儒之心符與我
太祖至誠格天右文重道
寶位初定即謹
punctuated:
起解金銀足色；
私借驛馬；
門禁鎖鑰；
脩理橋梁道路。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：郊祀以饗帝，學校以崇儒，二者皆帝王爲政之首務也。粤自禋祀燔柴，辟雝思服，虞、周之盛，蔑以加矣。而制作備于《周禮》及《大戴記》傳諸篇，其文質損益之儀，可得而詳與？漢、唐、宋願治之主，間亦慕循其跡，爲史美談。然漢以黑帝而增北畤，唐于南郊祭太微，宋竝五方上帝而祀之，果于饗帝之禮合與？中元臨雍拜老，貞觀大召名儒，慶曆增脩大學講殿以備臨幸，果于崇儒之心符與？我太祖至誠格天，右文重道，寶位初定，即謹

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
圜丘之禮干戈未遑爰肅
臨雍之儀見于
諭起居注熊鼎及
遣使祭曲阜者可攷也
列聖相傳授守一道其詳可得而揚厲之與我
皇上
聖哲天縱
睿齡握紀誠敬之心純一無貳
經筵之講寒暑不輟天人巳協應矣邇又
===
親祀
南郊以嚴對越
臨幸太學以崇文教誠足近法
祖宗遠紹虞周而陋漢唐宋于不足言矣然或
者謂祀之與學猶有出于儀章之外者
諸士其敬陳之以籍聞于
上
問人受天地之中以生所謂性也識此者
謂之知性率此者謂之盡性其關於學
punctuated:
圜丘之禮，干戈未遑，爰肅臨雍之儀，見于諭起居注熊鼎及遣使祭曲阜者，可攷也。列聖相傳，授守一道，其詳可得而揚厲之與？我皇上聖哲天縱，睿齡握紀，誠敬之心，純一無貳，經筵之講，寒暑不輟，天人巳協應矣。邇又親祀南郊，以嚴對越；臨幸太學，以崇文教。誠足近法祖宗，遠紹虞、周，而陋漢、唐、宋于不足言矣。然或者謂祀之與學，猶有出于儀章之外者。諸士其敬陳之，以籍聞于上。
問：人受天地之中以生，所謂性也。識此者謂之知性，率此者謂之盡性，其關於學
translation_en:
… the rites of the Round Mound; and before military campaigns had even ceased, he thereupon solemnized the ceremony of visiting the Imperial University, as can be verified by examining his edict to the Imperial Diarist Xiong Ding 熊鼎 and his dispatching of an envoy to offer sacrifices at Qufu 曲阜. Successive Sacred Emperors have passed this down, transmitting and upholding a single Way; can the details of this be extolled and set forth? Our Majesty the Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sage wisdom and holding the reins of government at a youthful age, possesses a mind of sincerity and reverence that is pure and undivided, and continues the Classics Colloquium lectures without interruption through winter cold and summer heat, so that Heaven and humanity have already responded in harmony. Recently, he has also personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb to solemnize his communion with Heaven, and visited the Directorate of Education in person to exalt civil teachings. Truly, this suffices to model himself closely upon the Imperial Ancestors, continue from afar the traditions of Yu 虞 and Zhou 周, and look down upon Han 漢, Tang 唐, and Song 宋 as unworthy of mention. Yet some say that regarding sacrifices and learning, there is still something that goes beyond mere ceremonial forms and regulations. Let you scholars respectfully set this forth, so that it may be recorded and presented to the Emperor.

Question: Humans receive the centrality of Heaven and Earth at birth; this is what is called human nature (xing 性). To recognize this is called knowing one's nature; to follow this is called fully realizing one's nature. Its bearing upon the effort of learning …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖之功大矣然古之言性者不過曰上
帝降衷于下民若有恒性卽孔子垂訓
亦止曰性相近焉蓋至孟子而後性善
之說始著矣夫謂之性善其旨與性近
之語得無相格與然則謂其有功於聖
門者果安在也自是而下其說寖詳有
曰性惡者有曰善惡混者有曰善惡各
有定無善無不善者雖人持所見要皆
左右孟氏之說而同歸於從善背惡乃
===
不得與孟氏同功顧辭而闢之何與宋
儒善言性者宜莫如程子定性一書明
天地聖人之常揭大公順應之的說者
以爲功不在孟子下乃亦有惡亦不可
不謂性之說豈天命之體彼亦有未窺
與抑有得於相近之說而云然與後儒
或取譬於日或借喻於水毋亦各因所
見而言之與夫知性而後不謬於學知
性之初而後不昧於性彼謂聖賢教人
punctuated: 聖之功大矣。然古之言性者，不過曰「上帝降衷于下民，若有恒性」，卽孔子垂訓，亦止曰「性相近」焉。蓋至孟子，而後「性善」之說始著矣。夫謂之「性善」，其旨與「性近」之語得無相格與？然則謂其有功於聖門者，果安在也？自是而下，其說寖詳：有曰「性惡」者，有曰「善惡混」者，有曰「善惡各有定」、「無善無不善」者。雖人持所見，要皆左右孟氏之說，而同歸於從善背惡，乃不得與孟氏同功，顧辭而闢之，何與？宋儒善言性者，宜莫如程子。《定性》一書，明天地聖人之常，揭大公順應之的，說者以爲功不在孟子下。乃亦有「惡亦不可不謂性」之說，豈天命之體，彼亦有未窺與？抑有得於「相近」之說而云然與？後儒或取譬於日，或借喻於水，毋亦各因所見而言之與？夫知性而後不謬於學，知性之初而後不昧於性。彼謂「聖賢教人，
translation_en: …the work of learning to become a sage is great indeed! Yet when the ancients spoke of human nature, they said no more than: "The Lord on High has conferred the moral mean upon the people below; if they follow their constant nature..." Even when Confucius handed down his teachings, he went no further than to say, "By nature, people are close to one another." It was only when it came to Mencius that the doctrine that "human nature is good" first became prominent. Now, to call human nature "good"—does its purport not conflict with the saying that natures are "close to one another"? If so, where indeed does his supposed merit toward the school of the Sage lie? From that time onward, discussions of human nature grew increasingly detailed: there were those who said that "human nature is evil," those who said that "good and evil are mixed in it," and those who said that "good and evil are each predetermined" or that "human nature is neither good nor bad." Although each person held to his own view, in essence they all flanked Mencius's doctrine and converged on following the good and turning away from evil. Yet they are not granted the same merit as Mencius, and instead are refuted and rejected—why is this? Among the Song Confucians who spoke well on human nature, none should surpass Master Cheng. His single letter on "Settling the Nature" (Dingxing shu) clarified the constancy of Heaven, Earth, and the sages, and held up the standard of supreme impartiality and harmonious responsiveness; commentators consider his merit to be no less than that of Mencius. Yet he too had the saying that "evil also cannot but be called human nature." Could it be that even he had not fully glimpsed the substance of what Heaven ordains? Or did he say this because he had grasped something from the doctrine that natures are "close to one another"? Later Confucians sometimes drew analogies to the sun and sometimes borrowed metaphors from water—was each not speaking merely according to what he himself saw? Now, only after one knows human nature will one not err in learning, and only after one knows the original state of human nature will one not be blind to human nature itself. Those who say that "in teaching people, the sages and worthies…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
性非所先固未可以爲訓而觀性當觀
其初其與孔孟之論果相印證否與多
士固嘗潜心于此願折衷而極言之以
觀盡性之學
問士習民風相因而成故古今論風俗者
曰士人有廉恥則天下有風俗蓋以士
爲民之望也東粤自高固相楚人文漸
盛民俗日淳考之志曰衣冠禮樂無異
中州又曰今之交廣古之鄒魯其遺風
===
可稽矣果有雙倡之然乎嘗觀前代士
君子有厚彝倫篤行誼而民敬老親親
者有通經登膴仕而民博於學者有以
禮敦俗而民陋緇黄者有清風高節而
民守名義者有以經學文章自顯則俗
皆務學者夫廉頑起懦諸哲之流風遺
韻固在也可得聞其詳乎卽今
運際亨嘉嶺海人文稱盛矣而風俗視昔若
漸漓焉操翰墨者獵聲華逞豪俠者悖
punctuated:
「性非所先」，固未可以爲訓；而「觀性當觀其初」，其與孔、孟之論果相印證否與？多士固嘗潜心于此，願折衷而極言之，以觀盡性之學。

問：士習民風，相因而成。故古今論風俗者曰：「士人有廉恥，則天下有風俗。」蓋以士爲民之望也。東粤自高固相楚，人文漸盛，民俗日淳。考之志曰：「衣冠禮樂，無異中州。」又曰：「今之交廣，古之鄒魯。」其遺風可稽矣，果有雙倡之然乎？嘗觀前代士君子，有厚彝倫、篤行誼而民敬老親親者；有通經、登膴仕而民博於學者；有以禮敦俗而民陋緇黄者；有清風高節而民守名義者；有以經學文章自顯則俗皆務學者。夫廉頑起懦，諸哲之流風遺韻固在也，可得聞其詳乎？卽今運際亨嘉，嶺海人文稱盛矣，而風俗視昔若漸漓焉。操翰墨者獵聲華，逞豪俠者悖
translation_en:
… "human nature is not the first priority" certainly cannot be taken as a teaching; and as for the saying that "in observing human nature one ought to observe its initial state," does this indeed corroborate the discourses of Confucius and Mencius or not? You gentlemen have surely devoted your minds deeply to these matters; I hope you will weigh the arguments and speak of them to the fullest, so that we may observe your learning in fully realizing human nature.

Question: The habits of scholars and the customs of the common people take shape in mutual dependence. Thus those across antiquity and the present who discuss customs say: "When scholars possess a sense of integrity and shame, the realm possesses good customs." This is because scholars are the exemplars to whom the common people look up. In eastern Yue [Guangdong], ever since Gao Gu 高固 served as Minister of Chu, cultural refinement has gradually flourished and popular customs have grown daily more pure. Examining the regional gazetteers, one reads: "In ceremonial dress, ritual, and music, it is no different from the Central Plains." And again: "The Jiao and Guang regions of today are the Zou and Lu of antiquity." Those lingering customs can be verified; was it indeed because there were those who led the way [reading 雙 as 倡/先, ?] that it became so? Look at the scholar-gentlemen of former eras: there were those who esteemed the constant human relationships and practiced earnest conduct, whereupon the people respected the aged and loved their kin; there were those who mastered the Classics and rose to prominent offices, whereupon the people became broad in learning; there were those who enriched customs through ritual, whereupon the people disdained Buddhist monks and Daoist priests; there were those of pure character and lofty integrity, whereupon the people upheld moral duty; and there were those who distinguished themselves through classical scholarship and literary composition, whereupon popular custom universally devoted itself to study. Making the greedy pure and rousing the timid—the lingering influence and resonance of those various worthies certainly remain; may we hear their details in full? Even now, when our fortune meets an era of flourishing excellence, cultural refinement in the Lingnan coastal region is acclaimed as thriving; yet compared to the past, customs seem to have grown gradually thinner and more decadent. Those who wield brush and ink hunt after fame and splendor; those who indulge in swaggering bravado violate…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
倫理外禮教者事巫詛獷悍則弓刀兼
佩射利則淫巧競奇綠林聚嘯錦帆通
蹻而尚義勵節之風不多見矣此其故
何與說者謂民風倡於士習士習興於
教化我
國家膠庠之教遠暨海隅未甞無以風之也
而民風若此何與玆欲道德一而風俗
同將何以道之與此觀風者所欲聞其
詳諸士毋徒剿說焉也
===
問善生財者因天資地民不加賦官無轉
輸而公私俱利之若屯田若鹽法蓋其
大較也粤稽古制漢趙充國屯塞下稱
富饒矣彼唐宋關中之屯金陵兩淮岳
州之屯皆屯也法亦有合與管仲相齊
鬻海為利致富强矣近議者或謂毋縱
末作而歸之官或謂毋奪民利而捐之
民其見殊也議果孰當與
國家創典則以垂永久分屯設堡通商辦課
punctuated:
倫理，外禮教者事巫詛；獷悍則弓刀兼佩，射利則淫巧競奇；綠林聚嘯，錦帆通蹻，而尚義勵節之風不多見矣。此其故何與？說者謂民風倡於士習，士習興於教化。我國家膠庠之教遠暨海隅，未甞無以風之也，而民風若此，何與？玆欲道德一而風俗同，將何以道之與？此觀風者所欲聞其詳，諸士毋徒剿說焉也。
問：善生財者，因天資地，民不加賦，官無轉輸，而公私俱利之，若屯田、若鹽法，蓋其大較也。粤稽古制，漢趙充國屯塞下，稱富饒矣；彼唐宋關中之屯，金陵、兩淮、岳州之屯，皆屯也，法亦有合與？管仲相齊，鬻海為利，致富强矣；近議者或謂毋縱末作而歸之官，或謂毋奪民利而捐之民，其見殊也，議果孰當與？國家創典則以垂永久，分屯設堡，通商辦課，
translation_en:
…moral principles, and those who disregard ritual teaching engage in shamanism and curses. The fierce and unruly wear both bows and blades, while those who pursue profit compete in extravagant ingenuity and novelty. Bandits gather and whistle in the greenwoods, and brocade-sailed ships traffic in illicit goods [?], while the ethos of esteeming righteousness and encouraging moral integrity is rarely seen. What is the reason for this? Commentators say that popular customs are led by the habits of the literati, and the habits of the literati are aroused by moral transformation through education. Our Dynasty's teaching in the state schools extends far to the corners of the seas; it is not that we have lacked the means to influence them, yet popular customs are like this—why is that? Now, if we wish to unify morality and harmonize customs, how shall we guide them? This is what the observer of local customs wishes to hear in detail; let you gentlemen not merely repeat hackneyed words.

Question: Those who are skilled at generating wealth rely on the seasons of Heaven and the resources of the earth; the people are not burdened with additional taxes, the officials have no need for transport and shipment, and both public and private interests benefit from it. Military state farms (tuntian) and salt administration are the prime examples of this. Examining ancient institutions, in the Han dynasty Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 established military farms along the frontier, which was praised for producing abundance. As for those military farms in Guanzhong during the Tang and Song, and those in Jinling, Lianghuai, and Yuezhou—all were military farms; did their methods also accord with his? When Guan Zhong 管仲 served as Chief Minister of Qi, he derived profit from boiling sea water for salt and achieved wealth and power. Among subsequent commentators, some have said that we should not indulge secondary occupations and should turn the monopoly over to the state, while others have said that we should not seize profit from the people and should leave it to them. Their views differ; which argument is actually right? Our Dynasty established institutional norms to be handed down in perpetuity, dividing military farms and setting up forts, and facilitating merchants to fulfill tax quotas…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其爲屯鹽計豈不至周密哉奈之何法
久而弊滋也其在佗處姑勿論已如廣
東屯田自龍江分屯以來尺籍盡廢矣
比來綜核非不嚴也而武夫狡卒侵漁
逋負不可勝窮其尤敝者展轉典賣乾
沒於豪右而莫能究詰也玆欲釐正之
使梗者樂輸豪者革念安所決策與提
舉司鹽場課額舊頗稱溢今則額縮而
辦納日隳矣司事者議處非不詳也而
===
竈丁日困率多流移其尤蠹者貪夫逐
末亡命煽黨私販於海上至飄忽也玆
欲裁恤之使流移者甦興販者戢安所
取衷與夫調瑟者移柱捄弊者通變斯
二者當必有要領在也諸士挾策待用
必籌之熟矣其悉以對
問三代以降談兵者尚矣齊桓晉文威行
天下莫之能禁當時之稱兵何術而不
及食豈古者兵出於農餉皆自給與然
punctuated:
其爲屯鹽計，豈不至周密哉！奈之何法久而弊滋也。其在佗處姑勿論已，如廣東屯田，自龍江分屯以來，尺籍盡廢矣。比來綜核非不嚴也，而武夫狡卒侵漁逋負，不可勝窮；其尤敝者，展轉典賣，乾沒於豪右而莫能究詰也。玆欲釐正之，使梗者樂輸、豪者革念，安所決策與？提舉司鹽場，課額舊頗稱溢，今則額縮而辦納日隳矣。司事者議處非不詳也，而竈丁日困，率多流移；其尤蠹者，貪夫逐末，亡命煽黨，私販於海上，至飄忽也。玆欲裁恤之，使流移者甦、興販者戢，安所取衷與？夫調瑟者移柱，捄弊者通變，斯二者當必有要領在也。諸士挾策待用，必籌之熟矣，其悉以對。
問：三代以降，談兵者尚矣。齊桓、晉文威行天下，莫之能禁，當時之稱兵何術而不及食？豈古者兵出於農，餉皆自給與？然
translation_en:
…Could its planning for military colonies and the salt monopoly be anything less than thoroughly comprehensive? Yet how is it that as the regulations have endured for a long time, abuses have proliferated? Leaving aside those in other regions for now, take the military colonies of Guangdong: ever since the division of colonies at Longjiang 龍江, the military land registers have fallen completely into disuse. Recently, verification and auditing have not been lax, yet martial men and cunning soldiers encroach upon the land and default on their dues to an inexhaustible degree. Worst of all, the lands are repeatedly mortgaged and sold off, embezzled by powerful families so that no one can investigate or hold them to account. If we now wish to rectify this, making the recalcitrant gladly pay their dues and the powerful abandon their acquisitive designs, upon what strategy should we decide? As for the salt fields under the Salt Distribution Supervisorate (提舉司), their tax quotas were formerly said to be in considerable surplus, yet today the quotas have shrunk and collections and deliveries fall further into ruin by the day. Those in charge of affairs have not failed to deliberate on measures in detail, yet the salt-boiling households grow more destitute daily and for the most part flee and scatter. Most pernicious of all, greedy men pursue commercial profit, while fugitives stir up gangs to engage in illicit salt trafficking on the seas, moving as swiftly and elusively as the wind. If we now wish to regulate and relieve this situation, reviving the displaced and suppressing the smugglers, where should we find the right balance? Now, he who tunes a se zither shifts its bridges, and he who remedies abuses adapts to changing circumstances; between these two matters there must surely be an essential principle. You gentlemen, who hold strategies in readiness for official employment, must have planned for this thoroughly; set forth your replies in full.

Question: Since the Three Dynasties, discussions of military affairs have a long history. Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓 and Duke Wen of Jin 晉文 wielded authority across the realm, and none could withstand them; by what art did those who spoke of military matters at that time say nothing of food supplies? Was it that in antiquity soldiers were drawn from the peasantry and their provisions were all self-supplied? Yet…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
城濮之戰晉師在楚三日穀或者因敵
爲糧與吾觀向秦之兵初起高陽生勸
襲陳留以得積粟乃有從軍擊胡天子
至遣大官齎數十乘其重如此夫師行
糧食自古記之矣今粤之兵食可指掌
言也而日患不給其原安在與或謂在
兵或謂在民夫清海無波則寢兵之說
起剖膚實饑則兵民之說岐且治平不
忘戰養兵以衞民民出食甚艱則兵可
===
少與抑武惷精悍能枵腹格敵與粤兵
餉歲入四十餘萬惟正之逋負尚數十
萬司
國計者已不遺餘力然每至束手有司苦於
朘削介胄之士敫敫可無慮與有欲汰
冗兵蠲積逋與民更始者其毋牴牾否
諸士桑梓之邦搤掔而談計必有得於
衷願詳著之毋略毋隱
punctuated: 城濮之戰，晉師在楚三日穀，或者因敵爲糧與？吾觀向秦之兵初起，高陽生勸襲陳留以得積粟；乃有從軍擊胡，天子至遣大官齎數十乘，其重如此。夫師行糧食，自古記之矣。今粤之兵食，可指掌言也，而日患不給，其原安在與？或謂在兵，或謂在民。夫清海無波，則寢兵之說起；剖膚實饑，則兵民之說岐。且治平不忘戰，養兵以衞民。民出食甚艱，則兵可少與？抑武惷精悍，能枵腹格敵與？粤兵餉歲入四十餘萬，惟正之逋負尚數十萬。司國計者已不遺餘力，然每至束手；有司苦於朘削，介胄之士敫敫，可無慮與？有欲汰冗兵、蠲積逋，與民更始者，其毋牴牾否？諸士桑梓之邦，搤掔而談，計必有得於衷。願詳著之，毋略毋隱。
translation_en: …at the Battle of Chengpu, the armies of Jin fed on Chu’s grain for three days; was this perhaps relying on the enemy for provisions? When I observe how the forces opposing Qin first rose up, Master Gaoyang (Li Yiji 酈食其) urged a surprise attack on Chenliu in order to seize its stored grain; and later, when troops marched on campaign to strike the northern nomads (Hu), the Son of Heaven even sent the Director of Imperial Provisioning (da guan) to transport tens of cartloads—such was the importance attached to it. Indeed, that "an army marches on its provisions" has been recorded since antiquity. Today, the military and provisioning affairs of Guangdong (Yue) can be laid out as clearly as pointing to the palm of one's hand, yet day by day we suffer from insufficiency; where does the root cause lie? Some say it lies with the soldiers; others say it lies with the common people. When the seas are calm and waveless, arguments for laying down arms arise; when flesh is stripped away to satisfy hunger, the interests of soldiers and civilians diverge. Moreover, in times of peace and order one does not forget warfare, maintaining soldiers in order to protect the people. When it is exceedingly difficult for the people to produce grain, can the number of soldiers be reduced? Or can martial men, simple and fierce [? 武惷精悍], fight off the enemy on empty stomachs? The annual revenue for Guangdong’s military rations is over four hundred thousand, yet arrears in regular taxes still amount to several hundred thousand. Those in charge of state finances have spared no effort, yet they are constantly brought to a standstill, with their hands tied; local authorities suffer from the distress of fleecing the people, while armored soldiers cry out in clamor—how can this not be cause for concern? There are those who wish to weed out superfluous troops and remit accumulated tax arrears so as to make a fresh start with the people—would this not involve contradictions? For you gentlemen, this is your native land; when you grasp your wrists in earnest discussion, you must surely have reached sound conclusions in your hearts. Please set them forth in full detail, neither abbreviating nor concealing anything.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
賜也達於從政乎何有
鄭偉
同考試官教諭黃批此題人多於達字講欠
分曉惟是篇發揮明切而體格亦不凡錄之
考試官教諭楊批調高詞渾一洗塵格可
以式矣
考試官教諭朱批雄健可觀
===
聖人於賢者許其識之優於治焉甚矣治先識
也賢者有其識矣聖人之許之也宜哉想其告
季康子之意豈不以夫人之不同者才也而可
致于用則一而已矣子欲知賜乎自我觀之其
達可使也穎悟得於天成而智慮昭融已具乎
疏觀之哲推測深於多學而識見明敏足裕乎
康濟之猷理有出於常情所難度者賜獨先明
諸心焉明則足以類萬物之情而施于有政自
化裁之各當事有出於意見所不及者賜獨旁
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「賜也達，於從政乎何有？」
鄭偉
同考試官教諭黃批：此題人多於「達」字講欠分曉，惟是篇發揮明切，而體格亦不凡，錄之。
考試官教諭楊批：調高詞渾，一洗塵格，可以式矣。
考試官教諭朱批：雄健可觀。

聖人於賢者，許其識之優於治焉。甚矣，治先識也！賢者有其識矣，聖人之許之也宜哉。想其告季康子之意，豈不以夫人之不同者才也，而可致于用則一而已矣。子欲知賜乎？自我觀之，其達可使也。穎悟得於天成，而智慮昭融，已具乎疏觀之哲；推測深於多學，而識見明敏，足裕乎康濟之猷。理有出於常情所難度者，賜獨先明諸心焉；明則足以類萬物之情，而施于有政，自化裁之各當。事有出於意見所不及者，賜獨旁
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
"Si is discerning; what difficulty would he have in engaging in government?" [Analects 6.8]
Zheng Wei 鄭偉

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang: On this topic, most candidates failed to explain the word "discerning" (da 達) with sufficient clarity. Only this essay develops its meaning clearly and incisively, and its structure and style are also out of the ordinary; I therefore select it for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yang: Elevated in tone and integral in diction, it washes away vulgar conventions and can serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu: Vigorous and worthy of note.

With regard to a worthy, the Sage commended his insight as being more than equal to the task of governance. How crucial it is that governance puts insight first! Since the worthy possessed such insight, how fitting it was that the Sage commended him! Considering the intent of what he told Ji Kangzi 季康子, was it not that while men differ in their particular talents, when it comes to their capacity to be put to practical use, they are one and the same? "Do you wish to know about Si 賜 [Zigong 子貢]? As I see him, his discernment makes him fit for employment." His acute comprehension comes from natural endowment, and his wisdom and deliberation are bright and thorough, already possessing the perspicacity of broad observation; his powers of inference are deepened through extensive learning, and his insight is clear and keen, amply sufficing for plans of bringing peace and relief to the world. When there are principles that lie beyond what ordinary minds can fathom, Si alone first illuminates them within his mind; being thus illuminated, he is able to classify the conditions of the myriad things, so that when applied to governance, his adaptations and regulations are naturally appropriate in every case. When there are affairs that arise beyond the reach of ordinary foresight, Si alone comprehensively…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
通其故焉通則足以悉萬變之蹟而授之以政
自時措之咸宜入而議制則酌當否以效之君
而君之聰明不患於不逮雖萬化錯綜然即其
通達者運量之迎機而解綽綽乎有餘裕矣出
而施令則權輕重以致之民而民之情僞不苦
於難知雖庶務紛紜然即其練達者張弛之觸
類而通恢恢乎有餘地矣若賜者韞而藏之固
適用之器也知而使之則大夫之選也以之從
政亦何難之有吁此見聖門之多才而夫子之
===
知賜者亦審矣然他日宰信陽而告之曰勤之
愼之論治而又以進賢爲賢豈達未足以盡政
乎蓋達才也三者所以善其才者也夫子而得
邦家子貢從焉則綏和化成魯其東周矣奈世
之莫知也使子貢僅以辯名且曰夫子名聞列
國蓋子貢後先之噫淺之乎窺聖賢矣
義者宜也尊賢爲大
徐兆魁
同考試官教諭蔣 批 謂宜字爲大字有體認
punctuated:
通其故焉。通則足以悉萬變之蹟，而授之以政，自時措之咸宜。入而議制，則酌當否以效之君，而君之聰明不患於不逮；雖萬化錯綜，然即其通達者運量之，迎機而解，綽綽乎有餘裕矣。出而施令，則權輕重以致之民，而民之情僞不苦於難知；雖庶務紛紜，然即其練達者張弛之，觸類而通，恢恢乎有餘地矣。若賜者，韞而藏之，固適用之器也；知而使之，則大夫之選也。以之從政，亦何難之有？吁！此見聖門之多才，而夫子之知賜者亦審矣。然他日宰信陽，而告之曰：「勤之，愼之。」論治，而又以進賢爲賢，豈達未足以盡政乎？蓋達，才也；三者，所以善其才者也。夫子而得邦家，子貢從焉，則綏和化成，魯其東周矣。奈世之莫知也，使子貢僅以辯名，且曰：「夫子名聞列國，蓋子貢後先之。」噫！淺之乎窺聖賢矣！

義者宜也，尊賢爲大。
徐兆魁
同考試官教諭蔣批：謂「宜」字、「爲大」字有體認，
translation_en:
…comprehends their underlying causes across the board. Because he comprehends them, he is able to fathom the traces of ten thousand changes; when entrusted with governance, he naturally applies measures appropriately to the times. When he enters court to deliberate on institutions, he weighs what is fitting and what is not in order to offer his service to the ruler, so the ruler's perspicacity need never suffer from falling short. Even though the ten thousand transformations are intricately interwoven, if he manages them with his thorough comprehension, untangling problems at the first opportunity, he will act with ample ease to spare. When he goes out to issue commands, he weighs relative priorities in order to deliver them to the people, so the true and false sentiments of the people are not agonizingly difficult to know. Even though administrative affairs are numerous and tangled, if he tightens or relaxes them with his seasoned comprehension, extending his understanding by analogy, he will operate with plenty of room to spare. A man like Ci (Zigong 子貢), when kept hidden away like jade in a case, is assuredly a vessel suited for practical use; when recognized and employed, he is the choice for a Grand Master. What difficulty could there be in having him engage in governance?

Ah! From this we see the abundance of talent at the Sage's gate, and how discerning the Master was in knowing Ci. Yet on another day, when Zigong was made magistrate of Xinyang, the Master instructed him, saying, "Be diligent in it, be cautious in it"; and in discussing governance, he further regarded advancing the worthy as true worthiness. Could it be that comprehension alone is insufficient to exhaust the demands of governance? Indeed, comprehension is talent; those three things—diligence, caution, and advancing the worthy—are the means by which to perfect one's talent. Had the Master gained a state or a noble house, with Zigong following him in service, peace and harmony would have brought transformation to completion, and Lu would have become an Eastern Zhou! Alas that the world did not recognize them, leaving Zigong to be famed merely for his eloquence, with people even saying, "That the Master's name became known throughout the various states was because Zigong attended him before and after." Alas! How shallow is such a glimpse of sages and worthies!

"Righteousness means appropriateness; honoring the worthy is its greatest exercise." [Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), chap. 20]
Xu Zhaokui 徐兆魁
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang: In addressing the words "appropriateness" and "is its greatest exercise," there is genuine personal comprehension,…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有照應蓋詞理俱優者可錄
考試官敎諭楊批說理明切是有養之士
考試官敎諭朱批冲雅可式
中庸指義之爲義因揭其用之大者焉夫行而
宜之之謂義也然所宜莫大於尊賢圖治者其
知所重哉夫子迪哀公之意若曰吾性有仁必
有義本同出於一原而相須以爲用者也仁之
爲人莫大於親親矣至於義豈無可言者乎蓋
義之爲體雖原於吾心之制而義之爲用實妙
===
乎事物之宜達之於五常而秩然其不紊者此
義爲之權衡也顯之爲人紀而截然其各當者
此義爲之區别也是義卽宜之謂矣而孰爲宜
之大者哉亦曰尊賢爾已蓋賢者所賴以明親
親之道義之所宜尊者也故事得其理皆義也
而推誠下士乃揆事之大本物得其則皆義也
而尊德樂道乃宰物之先圖以秩天常孰不以
爲治理之所宜急者然惟於賢之明乎常道者
欽崇之則啓沃有資將德脩罔覺而天常之所
punctuated:
有照應，蓋詞理俱優者，可錄。
考試官敎諭楊批：說理明切，是有養之士。
考試官敎諭朱批：冲雅可式。
《中庸》指義之爲義，因揭其用之大者焉。夫行而宜之之謂義也，然所宜莫大於尊賢，圖治者其知所重哉！夫子迪哀公之意，若曰：吾性有仁，必有義，本同出於一原，而相須以爲用者也。仁之爲人，莫大於親親矣，至於義，豈無可言者乎？蓋義之爲體，雖原於吾心之制，而義之爲用，實妙乎事物之宜。達之於五常，而秩然其不紊者，此義爲之權衡也；顯之爲人紀，而截然其各當者，此義爲之區别也。是義卽宜之謂矣，而孰爲宜之大者哉？亦曰尊賢爾已。蓋賢者，所賴以明親親之道，義之所宜尊者也。故事得其理，皆義也，而推誠下士，乃揆事之大本；物得其則，皆義也，而尊德樂道，乃宰物之先圖。以秩天常，孰不以爲治理之所宜急者？然惟於賢之明乎常道者欽崇之，則啓沃有資，將德脩罔覺，而天常之所……
translation_en:
…and shows structural correspondence; it is superior in both diction and reasoning, and worthy of selection.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: The exposition of principle is clear and incisive; this is a scholar of cultivation.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Serene and elegant, worthy of serving as a model.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) points out the meaning of righteousness (yi), and thereby reveals its greatest application. Now, acting in accordance with what is fitting (yi) is called righteousness; yet among all that is fitting, nothing is greater than honoring the worthy. May those who plan for governance know where to place importance! The Master enlightened Duke Ai with the thought, as if to say: In our human nature, where there is benevolence (ren), there must also be righteousness. Originally they issue together from a single source and depend upon one another for their functioning. As for benevolence being humanity (ren), nothing in it is greater than loving one's kin; when we come to righteousness, how could there be nothing to say of it? Indeed, although the substance of righteousness originates in the determinations of our own mind, the function of righteousness truly lies wondrously in the appropriateness of affairs and things. Extending it to the Five Constant Virtues so that they are orderly and unconfused—it is this righteousness that serves as their balance and measure; manifesting it as the human relationships so that they are distinct and each properly matched—it is this righteousness that makes their distinctions. Thus righteousness is simply what is meant by "what is fitting." And what, then, is the greatest of what is fitting? It is simply called honoring the worthy, and nothing more. For the worthy are those upon whom one relies to clarify the Way of loving one's kin, and whom righteousness properly dictates should be honored. Therefore, when affairs attain their principle, all of that is righteousness, yet extending sincerity and humbling oneself before scholars is the great foundation for measuring affairs; when things attain their standard, all of that is righteousness, yet honoring virtue and delighting in the Way is the foremost plan for governing things. As for ordering the heavenly constants, who would not consider this an urgent priority in the principles of governance? Yet only when one reveres and exalts those among the worthy who understand the constant Way will there be a resource for enlightenment and enrichment; then virtue will be cultivated imperceptibly, and that whereby the heavenly constants…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君子之與人異者異以心之所存者焉夫仁禮
人之同心也惟君子存之此其所以異於人與
孟子欲人善事其心也故曰心之於人大矣一
存亡之間人品之所由判也善觀君子者辨諸
此而已彼君子雖與人並生於天下而能爲天
下立極焉共處於一世而能爲後世垂範焉若
是其異於人者豈其有所立異哉亦惟同此心
也而所以事其心者獨善是以同是人也而所
以立此身者獨異矣存心維何曰以仁也以禮
===
也天地好生之德人得之爲仁人而不仁無以
宅此心矣君子一心之所渾涵者惟在於元善
之懿焉任之也重道之也遠日孜孜焉體而全
之以至於中心安仁斯已矣天下後世所以覆
育於君子者非以此仁也哉天地秩敘之良人
得之爲禮人而無禮無以制此心矣君子一心
之所凝聚者惟在於亨嘉之會焉主之也敬持
之也莊日兢兢焉會而通之以至於中心至正
斯已矣天下後世所以範圍於君子者非以此
punctuated: 君子之與人異者，異以心之所存者焉。夫仁、禮，人之同心也，惟君子存之，此其所以異於人與！孟子欲人善事其心也，故曰：心之於人大矣，一存亡之間，人品之所由判也。善觀君子者，辨諸此而已。彼君子雖與人並生於天下，而能爲天下立極焉；共處於一世，而能爲後世垂範焉。若是其異於人者，豈其有所立異哉？亦惟同此心也，而所以事其心者獨善，是以同是人也，而所以立此身者獨異矣。存心維何？曰：以仁也，以禮也。天地好生之德，人得之爲仁，人而不仁，無以宅此心矣。君子一心之所渾涵者，惟在於元善之懿焉。任之也重，道之也遠，日孜孜焉體而全之，以至於中心安仁斯已矣。天下後世所以覆育於君子者，非以此仁也哉！天地秩敘之良，人得之爲禮，人而無禮，無以制此心矣。君子一心之所凝聚者，惟在於亨嘉之會焉。主之也敬，持之也莊，日兢兢焉會而通之，以至於中心至正斯已矣。天下後世所以範圍於君子者，非以此
translation_en: That wherein the superior man differs from other men lies in what he preserves in his mind. Now benevolence and propriety are the shared mind of all men; yet only the superior man preserves them—is this not whereby he differs from other men? Mencius wished for men to tend well to their minds, and thus he said: Great indeed is the mind to a man! Between its preservation and its loss is where a person's character is distinguished. Those who are skilled at observing the superior man simply discern it in this. Although that superior man is born together with other men in the world, he is able to establish the supreme standard for the world; although he lives together with them in the same age, he is able to hand down a model for later generations. That he differs from other men in such a way—how could it be that he deliberately sets out to be different? It is only that while sharing this same mind, the way he tends to his mind is uniquely good; therefore, while being the same as other men, the way he establishes his person is uniquely different. What is it that he preserves in his mind? It is said: It is with benevolence; it is with propriety. The virtue of Heaven and Earth in loving life is what man obtains to become benevolent; if a man is not benevolent, he has no means to give residence to this mind. What the superior man's single mind encompasses and nurtures lies solely in the excellence of primal goodness. His burden is heavy and his way is long; day by day he diligently embodies and completes it, stopping only when he rests peacefully in benevolence at the center of his mind. That whereby the world and later generations are sheltered and nurtured by the superior man—is it not through this benevolence? The innate goodness of Heaven and Earth's orderly arrangement is what man obtains to become propriety; if a man lacks propriety, he has no means to regulate this mind. What the superior man's single mind concentrates and consolidates lies solely in the convergence of flourishing excellence. He presides over it with reverence and maintains it with gravity; day by day he cautiously comprehends and carries it through, stopping only when he reaches utmost rectitude at the center of his mind. That whereby the world and later generations are bounded and molded by the superior man—is it not through this…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以允秩者在是矣此非義之最急而不容緩者
乎以脩人紀孰不以為君臨之所宜重者然惟
於賢之察乎人倫者優禮之則論思日廣將猷
為益懋而人紀之所以肇脩者胥此矣此非義
之至重而不容後者乎君誠知義之所宜又知
義之所以為大則由義以行仁由仁以脩身文
武之政其有興乎雖然尊賢急矣純心要焉故
緝熙敬止而四友多助敬勝義勝而十亂同心
此其自然之明驗□□誣也若哀公者有一孔
===
子而不能尊毋亦純心之學未之講歟君天下
者可以鑒矣
孟子曰君子所以異於人者以其存心也
君子以仁存心以禮存心
劉祖泗
同考試官教諭陳批發君子所以異人處意
融詞暢可以雄視諸作矣
考試官教諭楊批文不浮而意自足可取
考試官教諭朱批詞理精到
punctuated:
以允秩者在是矣。此非義之最急而不容緩者乎？以脩人紀，孰不以為君臨之所宜重者？然惟於賢之察乎人倫者優禮之，則論思日廣，將猷為益懋，而人紀之所以肇脩者胥此矣。此非義之至重而不容後者乎？君誠知義之所宜，又知義之所以為大，則由義以行仁，由仁以脩身，文武之政其有興乎！雖然，尊賢急矣，純心要焉。故緝熙敬止而四友多助，敬勝義勝而十亂同心，此其自然之明驗，□□誣也。若哀公者，有一孔子而不能尊，毋亦純心之學未之講歟？君天下者可以鑒矣。

孟子曰：「君子所以異於人者，以其存心也。君子以仁存心，以禮存心。」
劉祖泗
同考試官教諭陳批：發君子所以異人處，意融詞暢，可以雄視諸作矣。
考試官教諭楊批：文不浮而意自足，可取。
考試官教諭朱批：詞理精到。
translation_en:
… whereby they are properly ordered lies right here. Is this not what is most urgent in righteousness, brooking no delay? As for cultivating the moral bonds of human society, who does not consider it something that a ruler governing from above ought to value? Yet only when he treats with generous courtesy those worthies who clearly understand human relationships will discussion and reflection daily broaden; then plans and endeavors will grow ever more vigorous, and the means by which the moral bonds of society are initially cultivated will all rest on this. Is this not what is most weighty in righteousness, brooking no postponement? If a ruler truly knows what is fitting in righteousness, and further knows that whereby righteousness is great, then by proceeding from righteousness to practice benevolence, and from benevolence to cultivate his person, the governance of Kings Wen and Wu will surely flourish! Even so, while honoring the worthy is urgent, purifying the mind is fundamental. Thus, through bright and unceasing reverent resting in the highest good, the Four Friends gave abundant aid; through reverence prevailing and righteousness prevailing, the Ten Able Ministers were of one mind. This is its natural and clear verification, which [cannot be] [?] falsified. In the case of someone like Duke Ai, who had a Confucius yet was unable to honor him—was it not because the learning of purifying the mind had not been expounded to him? Those who rule the world may take this as a mirror.

Mencius said: "That whereby the gentleman differs from other men is that he preserves his mind. The gentleman preserves his mind with benevolence; he preserves his mind with propriety."
Liu Zusi 劉祖泗
Associate Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: It brings out that whereby the gentleman differs from other men; the thought is harmonious and the diction fluent, enough to tower over the other compositions.
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊 comments: The writing is not superficial and the meaning is self-sufficient; it is worthy of selection.
Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: The diction and reasoning are refined and thorough.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮也哉吁君子之所以異於人者以此然則欲
爲君子舍事心何以哉抑君子之存心非固以
求異於人也求無愧於心求不怍於人而已惟
求無愧於心故心學日純惟求不怍於人故人
道益全古好生溫恭之聖法天下傳後世者用
此道也雖然吾心有眞舜也存之如　舜而
已矣
易
九五觀我生君子无咎象曰觀我生觀民
===
也
徐兆魁
同考試官敎諭蔣批格調整雅辭理醇粹發
明中正爲觀之道可謂詳盡錄之
考試官敎諭楊批平實莊重且於自觀觀
民處交互得體
考試官敎諭朱批典雅
二聖交發五爻之義而爲觀之道備矣夫觀道
以中正示人者也考諸身而徵諸民觀道其備
punctuated:
禮也哉？吁！君子之所以異於人者以此。然則欲爲君子，舍事心何以哉？抑君子之存心，非固以求異於人也，求無愧於心，求不怍於人而已。惟求無愧於心，故心學日純；惟求不怍於人，故人道益全。古好生溫恭之聖，法天下、傳後世者，用此道也。雖然，吾心有眞舜也，存之如舜而已矣。

易

九五：觀我生，君子无咎。《象》曰：觀我生，觀民也。
徐兆魁
同考試官敎諭蔣批：格調整雅，辭理醇粹，發明中正爲觀之道，可謂詳盡。錄之。
考試官敎諭楊批：平實莊重，且於自觀、觀民處，交互得體。
考試官敎諭朱批：典雅。

二聖交發五爻之義，而爲觀之道備矣。夫觀道，以中正示人者也。考諸身而徵諸民，觀道其備
translation_en:
… propriety?! Ah, it is by this that the gentleman differs from other men. This being so, if one wishes to be a gentleman, how can one do so if one sets aside attending to the mind? Yet in preserving his mind, the gentleman does not do so expressly to seek to differ from other men; he merely seeks to have no shame in his own mind and to have nothing to be abashed about before other men. Because he seeks only to have no shame in his mind, the learning of his mind becomes daily more pure; because he seeks only to have nothing to be abashed about before other men, the way of humanity becomes ever more complete. The ancient sage who loved life and was温和 and reverent [Shun], in serving as a model for the world and transmitting it to posterity, used this very Way. Even so, within my own mind there is a true Shun; it is simply a matter of preserving it as Shun did.

Book of Changes (Yi)

"Nine in the fifth place: Contemplating my own life, the gentleman is without fault. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Contemplating my own life' means contemplating the people."
By Xu Zhaokui 徐兆魁.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: The structure and style are refined and elegant, and the diction and reasoning are pure and unadulterated. Its elucidation of the Way of setting an example through centrality and correctness can be called thorough and exhaustive. Record it.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: Plain, solid, and dignified; moreover, where it deals with contemplating oneself and contemplating the people, the interplay is handled with proper measure.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Classic and elegant.
