The two sages jointly brought forth the meaning of the fifth line, and thus the Way of setting an example to be contemplated was made complete. Now, the Way of setting an example is to display centrality and correctness to others. When one examines it in one's own person and verifies it among the people, the Way of setting an example is surely complete…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣乎且民之視效在君君之明徵在民不可不
合而觀之也九五以陽居尊四陰仰之誠爲觀
之主矣周公有見於自觀之道也故發其占曰
觀我生君子无咎意以君子之道本諸身身有
未善則加諸民者可知矣是必獨觀萬化之原
而考道期歸於無失內省百爲之主而視履務
協於其旋觀我之中即君子之建中與斯履帝
位而不疚也觀我之正即君子之表正與斯萃
有位而乃光也所謂有孚顒若立大觀之極者
===
此矣然則爲觀者可徒求之民哉夫子有見於
觀民之義也故申其象曰觀我生觀民也意以
君子之道徵諸民民有弗善則出乎身者可知
矣是必察民俗之淳漓以驗吾政之得失稽民
風之厚薄以徵吾治之隆汙民心罔中惟爾之
中而觀民以考其中者不容後也民心罔正惟
爾之正而觀民以考其正者不可忽也所謂省
方設教成下觀之化者此矣然則爲觀者可徒
信諸巳哉吁惟觀巳也則敷政於民者益善惟
punctuated: 矣乎！且民之視效在君，君之明徵在民，不可不合而觀之也。九五以陽居尊，四陰仰之，誠爲觀之主矣。周公有見於自觀之道也，故發其占曰：「觀我生，君子无咎。」意以君子之道本諸身，身有未善，則加諸民者可知矣。是必獨觀萬化之原，而考道期歸於無失；內省百爲之主，而視履務協於其旋。觀我之中，即君子之建中與？斯履帝位而不疚也；觀我之正，即君子之表正與？斯萃有位而乃光也。所謂「有孚顒若」，立大觀之極者，此矣。然則爲觀者，可徒求之民哉？夫子有見於觀民之義也，故申其象曰：「觀我生，觀民也。」意以君子之道徵諸民，民有弗善，則出乎身者可知矣。是必察民俗之淳漓，以驗吾政之得失；稽民風之厚薄，以徵吾治之隆汙。「民心罔中，惟爾之中」，而觀民以考其中者不容後也；「民心罔正，惟爾之正」，而觀民以考其正者不可忽也。所謂「省方設教」，成下觀之化者，此矣。然則爲觀者，可徒信諸巳哉？吁！惟觀巳也，則敷政於民者益善；惟
translation_en:
…complete! Moreover, what the people look to for emulation lies in the ruler, while the clear verification of the ruler lies in the people; one cannot fail to join them together and contemplate them.

Nine in the Fifth Place occupies the honored position with yang strength, and the four yin lines look up to it; truly, he is the lord of Contemplation (Guan). The Duke of Zhou perceived the Way of contemplating oneself, and therefore brought forth its divination, saying: "Contemplating my own life, the superior man is without blame." His meaning was that the Way of the superior man is rooted in his own person; if there is anything not yet good in his person, then what he extends to the people can be known from this. Therefore, he must independently contemplate the source of the myriad transformations, and in examining his Way, aim to return to faultlessness; he must inwardly reflect upon the master of the hundred actions, and in examining his conduct, strive to harmonize with its complete revolution. Contemplating the centrality within oneself—is this not the superior man's establishing of the central standard? Thus he treads the imperial position without regret. Contemplating the rectitude within oneself—is this not the superior man's displaying of rectitude? Thus he gathers those in office and shines forth. What is meant by "having sincerity and a dignified aspect," establishing the supreme standard of great contemplation, is precisely this. If so, how could one who acts as the model for contemplation merely seek it among the people?

The Master (Confucius) perceived the principle of contemplating the people, and therefore expounded its Image, saying: "'Contemplating my own life' means contemplating the people." His meaning was that the Way of the superior man is verified among the people; if there is anything not good among the people, then what issues from his own person can be known from this. Therefore, he must observe whether the people's customs are pure or degenerate in order to test the successes and failures of his governance; he must investigate whether the people's mores are generous or thin in order to verify the flourishing or decline of his rule. "The minds of the people have no centrality, save as you are central"—so contemplating the people in order to examine one's own centrality cannot be delayed. "The minds of the people have no rectitude, save as you are upright"—so contemplating the people in order to examine one's own rectitude cannot be neglected. What is meant by "inspecting the regions and establishing instruction," completing the transformation by which those below look up in contemplation, is precisely this. If so, how could one who acts as the model for contemplation merely trust in himself alone?

Ah! Only by contemplating oneself does the governance spread to the people become ever better; only…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
觀民也則考德於已者益詳二聖交發其義觀
道無餘蘊矣考之唐虞君臣相與飭戒惟是幾
安而清問下民咨詢岳牧其心曷甞一日忘耶
敬忽之際誠天命人心之所關也而禹猶曰寡
人之民各自以其心爲心噫何其詳且切耶吾
固曰堯舜之安民也大而禹之慮民也深
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
立人之道曰仁與義
楊文俊
===
同考試官教諭陳批此題作者昪拘於格則
歉於理惟是作兼得之可式
考試官教諭楊批說理精到處人不可及
考試官教諭朱批詞意俱足
觀三才之所以立而性命之理昭矣蓋性命一
理也具於三才者雖異其名孰非是理之貫哉
大傳言此以見易之大也意以易之爲書也功
用固無所不周精蘊亦無所不備是故聖人作
易固以順性命之理矣而性命之理果安在哉
punctuated:
觀民也，則考德於已者益詳。二聖交發其義，觀道無餘蘊矣。考之唐、虞君臣相與飭戒，惟是幾安，而清問下民，咨詢岳、牧，其心曷甞一日忘耶？敬忽之際，誠天命、人心之所關也。而禹猶曰：「寡人之民，各自以其心爲心。」噫！何其詳且切耶！吾固曰：「堯、舜之安民也大，而禹之慮民也深。」

以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔，立人之道曰仁與義。
楊文俊
同考試官教諭陳批：此題作者昪拘於格則歉於理，惟是作兼得之，可式。
考試官教諭楊批：說理精到處，人不可及。
考試官教諭朱批：詞意俱足。

觀三才之所以立，而性命之理昭矣。蓋性命一理也，具於三才者雖異其名，孰非是理之貫哉？《大傳》言此，以見《易》之大也。意以《易》之爲書也，功用固無所不周，精蘊亦無所不備。是故聖人作《易》，固以順性命之理矣，而性命之理果安在哉？
translation_en:
… only by observing the people does one's examination of virtue in oneself become ever more thorough. As the two sages mutually elucidated its meaning, no hidden depths of the Way of Observation remained unrevealed. When we examine how sovereign and ministers in the eras of Tang and Yu admonished and cautioned one another, it was solely over the subtle springs of peace; yet in inquiring clearly among the lower people and consulting the Four Peaks and Twelve Pastors, how could their minds ever forget this for a single day? The boundary between reverence and negligence is truly where the Mandate of Heaven and the hearts of the people are decided. And Yu still said, "The people of my humble self each take their own mind as their mind." Ah, how thorough and earnest that is! I therefore say: "Yao and Shun were great in giving peace to the people, and Yu was profound in his concern for the people."

"To establish the Way of Heaven, calling it yin and yang; to establish the Way of Earth, calling it the soft [and the hard]; to establish the Way of Man, calling it benevolence and righteousness."
Yang Wenjun 楊文俊
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: Writers on this topic mostly [? 昪, for 多] either are constrained by formal structure or fall short in principle; only this composition achieves both and can serve as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Yang's comment: Where it explicates principle with precision and depth, others cannot match it.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu's comment: Both diction and conception are fully realized.

When one observes that whereby the Three Powers are established, the principle of nature and destiny becomes manifest. For nature and destiny are a single principle; although what is endowed in the Three Powers differs in name, which of them is not penetrated by this principle? The Great Treatise (Dazhuan) speaks of this in order to show the greatness of the Changes (Yi). The meaning is that as a book, the Changes is indeed all-encompassing in its function and application, and likewise all-complete in its subtle essence. Therefore, when the sages made the Changes, it was indeed to accord with the principle of nature and destiny; yet where, after all, does the principle of nature and destiny reside? …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蓋天位乎上地位乎下人位乎中非徒有散殊
布列者以昭可見之迹亦必有幾微易簡者以
立無極之眞故以言乎立天之道則曰陰與陽
其靜也專其動也直一陰一陽以兩而運而確
然者由之不毁矣言乎立地之道則曰柔與剛
其靜也翕其動也闢一剛一柔以兩而化而隤
然者由之不變矣言乎立人之道則曰仁與義
蓋人得天地之氣以成形亦得天地之理以成
性藹然而爲和厚毅然而爲嚴凝一仁一義以
===
兩而施而混然中處者與天地合德矣觀其對
待之體則陰陽異氣也剛柔異質也仁義異德
也三才各以兩而相配分之一定而不移也察
其流行之機則陰陽互根也剛柔交錯也仁義
並用也兩者各相濟以成能理之循環而無端
也性命之理備于三才者如此易皆有以順之
其妙為何如哉抑性命一也特隨在而異名耳
蓋太極者本然之妙動靜者所乘之機其動也
則為陽為剛為仁其靜也則為陰為柔為義要
punctuated: 蓋天位乎上，地位乎下，人位乎中，非徒有散殊布列者以昭可見之迹，亦必有幾微易簡者以立無極之眞。故以言乎立天之道，則曰「陰與陽」，其靜也專，其動也直，一陰一陽以兩而運，而確然者由之不毁矣；言乎立地之道，則曰「柔與剛」，其靜也翕，其動也闢，一剛一柔以兩而化，而隤然者由之不變矣；言乎立人之道，則曰「仁與義」，蓋人得天地之氣以成形，亦得天地之理以成性，藹然而爲和厚，毅然而爲嚴凝，一仁一義以兩而施，而混然中處者與天地合德矣。觀其對待之體，則陰陽異氣也，剛柔異質也，仁義異德也，三才各以兩而相配，分之一定而不移也；察其流行之機，則陰陽互根也，剛柔交錯也，仁義並用也，兩者各相濟以成能，理之循環而無端也。性命之理備于三才者如此，易皆有以順之，其妙為何如哉！抑性命一也，特隨在而異名耳。蓋太極者，本然之妙；動靜者，所乘之機。其動也，則為陽、為剛、為仁；其靜也，則為陰、為柔、為義。要
translation_en:
For Heaven is positioned above, Earth is positioned below, and Man is positioned in the middle. There are not merely the dispersed and distinct manifestations laid out to reveal visible traces, but there must also be the subtle, easy, and simple principles to establish the reality of the Non-Ultimate (wuji). Therefore, speaking of the Way that establishes Heaven, it is called "yin and yang": in its stillness it is concentrated, and in its movement it is direct; alternating between yin and yang, it revolves as a pair, and through this, that which is firm and sure is never destroyed. Speaking of the Way that establishes Earth, it is called "the soft and the hard": in its stillness it closes, and in its movement it opens; alternating between the hard and the soft, it transforms as a pair, and through this, that which is docile and yielding never changes. Speaking of the Way that establishes Man, it is called "humaneness (ren) and righteousness (yi)": for Man receives the vital force (qi) of Heaven and Earth to form his physical body, and also receives the principle (li) of Heaven and Earth to form his nature; mild and genial, it becomes harmonious and generous, while resolute and firm, it becomes stern and composed; alternating between humaneness and righteousness, it is enacted as a pair, and thus he who dwells integrally in the middle matches his virtue with Heaven and Earth.

Observing their paired substance as opposites: yin and yang differ in vital force, the hard and the soft differ in material constitution, and humaneness and righteousness differ in virtue; each of the Three Powers (sancai) is matched in pairs, their allotments fixed and unshifting. Examining the mechanism of their active flow: yin and yang are rooted in each other, the hard and the soft interlock and alternate, and humaneness and righteousness are employed together; the two in each pair complement each other to accomplish their function, as principle circulates without beginning or end. Such is the way the principle of nature and destiny is fully present in the Three Powers, and the Changes (Yi) conforms to all of it—how marvelous indeed!

Yet nature and destiny are one; they merely take on different names according to where they reside. For the Supreme Ultimate (taiji) is the inherent mystery, while movement and stillness are the mechanisms upon which it rides. In its movement, it becomes yang, the hard, and humaneness; in its stillness, it becomes yin, the soft, and righteousness. In sum, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之根柢於太極者也故曰易有太極是生兩儀
學者能定之以仁義而主靜則太極在吾心而
三才之道一以貫之矣
書
念終始典于學厥德脩罔覺
馮名望
同考試官教諭黃批辭𡊮意懇深得傅說論
舉之旨宜式多士
考試官教諭易批說典學義盡而詞密足
懷忠藎者
考試官教諭朱批典雅精融
大臣告君之務學由純心而進于化焉夫德脩
罔覺化不可知矣然必由一念之純致之明君
可不以務學爲急乎宜傅說以是迪高宗也其
意以爲帝王之治本于道帝王之學純于心是
故自學斆人學之始終備矣王可一念之或怠
耶殆必會體用以兼脩而遜志純于罔間合內
外以並進而時敏勵于有常恭默思道始固此
punctuated:
之，根柢於太極者也。故曰：「《易》有太極，是生兩儀。」學者能定之以仁義而主靜，則太極在吾心，而三才之道一以貫之矣。

書
念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。
馮名望
同考試官教諭黃批：辭𡊮意懇，深得傅說論舉之旨，宜式多士。
考試官教諭易批：說典學義盡而詞密，足懷忠藎者。
考試官教諭朱批：典雅精融。

大臣告君之務學，由純心而進于化焉。夫德脩罔覺，化不可知矣；然必由一念之純致之，明君可不以務學爲急乎？宜傅說以是迪高宗也。其意以爲：帝王之治本于道，帝王之學純于心。是故自學斆人，學之始終備矣，王可一念之或怠耶？殆必會體用以兼脩，而遜志純于罔間；合內外以並進，而時敏勵于有常。恭默思道，始固此
translation_en:
…in summary, they are rooted in the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji). Therefore it is said: "In the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate, which generates the Two Modes." If the student can settle himself with humanity and righteousness and take tranquility as fundamental, then the Supreme Ultimate will reside within our own mind, and the Way of the Three Powers will be threaded together as one.

Book of Documents (Shu)
"Hold fast to learning inside your thoughts from beginning to end, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being aware of it."
Feng Mingwang 馮名望
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang: The diction is rich [?] and the intent earnest; it deeply grasps the purport of Fu Yue's discussion of learning [reading 學 for 舉?], and ought to serve as a model for the multitude of scholars.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yi: In explaining constant devotion to learning, the meaning is exhaustive and the phrasing tight, sufficient to inspire those who cherish loyal devotion.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: Classically elegant, refined, and harmonious.

When a great minister counsels his ruler on devoting himself to learning, it proceeds from a pure mind and advances to transformation. Now, for virtue to be cultivated without one's being aware of it is a transformation beyond conscious knowing; yet because it must be brought about through the purity of a single thought, how could an enlightened ruler not regard devotion to learning as an urgent priority? Rightly did Fu Yue 傅說 guide Gaozong 高宗 with these words. His meaning was as follows: The governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and the learning of emperors and kings is made pure in the mind. Therefore, from studying for oneself to teaching others, the beginning and end of learning are complete—how could the King allow even a single thought to grow lax? He must surely unite substance and function so as to cultivate both together, keeping a humble will pure and without interruption; he must join the internal and external so as to advance in both side by side, exerting himself in timely diligence with constancy. When in reverent silence he pondered the Way, at the beginning it was indeed this very…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
念也推之以至于承式百官其惺惺而不昧者
猶夫初也寤寐思治始固此心也推之以至于
作則萬邦其孳孳而不忘者未甞替也由是操
存愈專則進脩愈妙而幾非在我念慮益精則
充養益融而化不可爲始之脩而來也猶可知
也茲則體用爲之無方而來者愈來不知其所
以來焉承式之具其冥會於此矣尚何罔顯之
慮于已哉始之來而積也猶有意也茲則内外
爲之合德而積者日積不知其所以積焉作則
===
之原其默運于是矣又何多聞之求諸人哉至
是則學古之功爲益密有獲之效爲已盡矣使
不自純其念而徒望諸人亦安能以有得耶抑
是道也即堯舜之允執成湯之日新而帝王授
受心法也高宗可謂知學矣而傅說猶惓惓及
此蓋以聖帝明王心學之純望之者不可以覿
明良相遇之盛乎然以中興之主而厥後猶有
祖巳之訓焉則人主之心安可以終始易慮哉
吁可以戒矣
punctuated: 念也，推之以至于承式百官，其惺惺而不昧者，猶夫初也；寤寐思治，始固此心也，推之以至于作則萬邦，其孳孳而不忘者，未甞替也。由是操存愈專，則進脩愈妙，而幾非在我；念慮益精，則充養益融，而化不可爲。始之脩而來也，猶可知也；茲則體用爲之無方，而來者愈來，不知其所以來焉，承式之具，其冥會於此矣，尚何罔顯之慮于已哉！始之來而積也，猶有意也；茲則内外爲之合德，而積者日積，不知其所以積焉，作則之原，其默運于是矣，又何多聞之求諸人哉！至是則學古之功爲益密，有獲之效爲已盡矣。使不自純其念，而徒望諸人，亦安能以有得耶？抑是道也，即堯、舜之允執，成湯之日新，而帝王授受心法也。高宗可謂知學矣，而傅說猶惓惓及此，蓋以聖帝明王心學之純望之者，不可以覿明良相遇之盛乎！然以中興之主，而厥後猶有祖巳之訓焉，則人主之心，安可以終始易慮哉？吁！可以戒矣。
translation_en: …thought; extended all the way to when the hundred officials receive his model, that alert and unclouded awareness remains just as it was at the beginning. Waking and sleeping he thinks of good governance—at the start it is indeed this mind; extended all the way to when he sets the standard for the myriad states, that tireless and unforgetful diligence has never slackened. Through this, the more focused his preservation and grasp of the mind, the more wondrous his moral advancement and cultivation become, until the subtle springs of action are beyond mere conscious effort; the more refined his thoughts and deliberations, the more harmonious his nourishment and fulfillment become, reaching a transformation that cannot be artificially contrived. At first, when cultivation brings attainment, it can still be consciously perceived; now, however, substance and function operate without fixed bounds, and what comes continues to come without his knowing how it comes. The wherewithal for the officials to receive his model is tacitly united herein—what anxiety could remain within himself that his virtue might not be manifest? At first, when attainment leads to accumulation, there is still deliberate intent; now, however, the internal and the external merge in virtue, and what is accumulated grows daily without his knowing how it is accumulated. The source for setting the standard for all states operates silently herein—what need is there anymore to seek extensive learning from others? At this point, the effort of studying antiquity becomes ever more thorough, and the efficacy of genuine attainment is fully realized. If he did not purify his own thoughts from within, and merely looked to others for it, how could he ever achieve anything? Moreover, this Way is none other than the "sincere hold of the Mean" of Yao and Shun, and the "daily renewal" of Cheng Tang—the method of the mind transmitted from one sovereign to another. Gaozong may well be said to have understood learning, yet Fu Yue still earnestly spoke to him of this, because he hoped for him to achieve the pure learning of the mind of the sage emperors and enlightened kings. In this, can we not behold the splendid encounter between an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister? Yet even for a sovereign of dynastic restoration, there still followed later the admonition of Zu Ji; how then can a ruler's mind afford to alter its concern between the beginning and the end? Alas, one must take warning from this!

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
李樹聲
同考試官敎諭羅批精醇古雅宛然董正治
官氣象經義之佳者
考試官敎諭楊批聯□□貫最爲得體
考試官敎諭朱批詞整理到
賢王總命大臣惟欲其率下以治民焉蓋設官
分職以爲民也率內以倡外而治可致矣寧非
大臣之當務哉成王訓官至此以爲朝廷立四
===
方之極綱紀爲萬化之原冢宰而下六卿各有
攸司矣然豈徒自盡其職已哉蓋天生兆民使
司牧之內而卿士又外牧之表也顧其率而倡
之者非爾六卿責乎是必正色以率下於以懋
敦乎倡導之原端己以作先於以共起夫精明
之治佐理于一人之下而垂範于百寮之間將
使外而牧伯皆知朝廷意向所在而承流以宣
厥化者旁敷於不窮也輔理于朝著之內而儀
刑于寮屬之上將使外而州長皆知廟廊德意
punctuated:
「六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。」
李樹聲
同考試官、敎諭羅批：精醇古雅，宛然「董正治官」氣象，經義之佳者。
考試官、敎諭楊批：聯□□貫，最爲得體。
考試官、敎諭朱批：詞整理到。
賢王總命大臣，惟欲其率下以治民焉。蓋設官分職，以爲民也；率內以倡外，而治可致矣，寧非大臣之當務哉？成王訓官至此，以爲朝廷立四方之極，綱紀爲萬化之原，冢宰而下，六卿各有攸司矣；然豈徒自盡其職已哉？蓋天生兆民，使司牧之，內而卿士，又外牧之表也。顧其率而倡之者，非爾六卿責乎？是必正色以率下，於以懋敦乎倡導之原；端己以作先，於以共起夫精明之治。佐理于一人之下，而垂範于百寮之間，將使外而牧伯，皆知朝廷意向所在，而承流以宣厥化者，旁敷於不窮也。輔理于朝著之內，而儀刑于寮屬之上，將使外而州長，皆知廟廊德意…
translation_en:
"The Six Ministers divide their duties, each leading his subordinates to set an example for the Pastors of the Nine Provinces, thereby enriching and perfecting the millions of people."

Li Shusheng 李樹聲

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Luo 羅: Refined, pure, antique, and elegant; it vividly captures the spirit of "supervising and rectifying the governing officials," making it an excellent exposition of the Classic.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yang 楊: Connected and [?] coherent, most fitting in style.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱: The diction is well-ordered and the reasoning thorough.

When the worthy king issued his general charge to the great ministers, he desired only that they lead their subordinates in governing the people. For establishing offices and dividing duties is done for the sake of the people; by leading those at the inner court to set an example for those in the outer provinces, good governance can be achieved—is this not the foremost duty of great ministers? When King Cheng 成王 reached this point in instructing his officials, he considered that the court establishes the standard for the four quarters and that state regulations form the source of myriad transformations. From the Premier (zhongzai 冢宰) downward, each of the Six Ministers had his respective charge; yet how could they merely fulfill their own individual duties and nothing more? Heaven gave birth to the millions of people and appointed pastors to govern them, while the ministers and officers at the inner court serve in turn as models for those pastors outside. Now then, does not the responsibility for leading and setting an example for them rest upon you, the Six Ministers? Therefore, you must maintain a solemn demeanor in leading your subordinates, thereby earnestly strengthening the source of leadership and guidance; and you must rectify yourselves to take the lead, thereby jointly rousing an administration of keen discernment. Assisting in governance beneath the One Man and setting a standard among the hundred officials, you will cause the regional pastors and earls on the outside all to know where the intentions of the court lie, so that those who receive its currents and proclaim its transforming influence will spread them widely without end. Aiding the administration within the court ranks and serving as a model above your subordinate colleagues, you will cause the provincial chiefs on the outside all to know where the virtuous intentions of the temple and court…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所存而行令以致之民者四達而不悖也內與
外以勤恤而膏澤神于下究樂其樂焉利其利
焉煕煕乎阜厚之俗自畿甸以及侯服者廓如
矣所謂制治于未亂者非以是耶中與外以合
德而紀法因之丕著道德一焉風俗同焉皥皥
乎化成之休由都會以及四海者沛如矣所謂
保邦于未危者其在兹耶是雖阜成之職在諸
臣有同心而統率之權則六卿有專責矣果能
此道而國家建官之意其無負矣哉雖然此周
===
官之法度也推原其本又係于人君之一心蓋
君心一正則卿相皆正人而內之寮屬外之牧
伯各以彙進而兆民竝受其福唐虞之朝師師
濟濟卒致惟和咸寧之風者豈徒以其建官哉
故謂君心爲萬化之原信矣
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
鄭偉
同考試官教諭陳批周民愛君之情發揮明
punctuated:
所存，而行令以致之民者，四達而不悖也。內與外以勤恤，而膏澤神于下究，樂其樂焉，利其利焉，煕煕乎阜厚之俗，自畿甸以及侯服者廓如矣。所謂「制治于未亂」者，非以是耶？中與外以合德，而紀法因之丕著，道德一焉，風俗同焉，皥皥乎化成之休，由都會以及四海者沛如矣。所謂「保邦于未危」者，其在兹耶？是雖阜成之職，在諸臣有同心，而統率之權，則六卿有專責矣。果能此道，而國家建官之意，其無負矣哉！雖然，此周官之法度也；推原其本，又係于人君之一心。蓋君心一正，則卿相皆正人，而內之寮屬、外之牧伯，各以彙進，而兆民竝受其福。唐虞之朝，師師濟濟，卒致惟和咸寧之風者，豈徒以其建官哉？故謂君心爲萬化之原，信矣。

詩
有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。
鄭偉
同考試官教諭陳批：周民愛君之情，發揮明
translation_en:
…lies, and the execution of orders to bring them to the people reaches in all four directions without contradiction. Those within and without join in diligent compassion, so that enriching grace wondrously penetrates down to the lowest levels; the people rejoice in their joys and profit from their benefits, and how harmonious and prosperous are the generous customs that expand broadly from the royal domain to the feudal dependencies! Is not what is called "securing order before disorder arises" achieved by this? The court and the provinces unite in virtue, and the laws and regulations thereby become greatly manifest; morality is unified and customs are made uniform, and how vast and bright are the blessings of transformative completion that flow abundantly from the capital to the四海 (Four Seas)! Does not what is called "preserving the state before danger arises" lie right here? Thus, although the duty of bringing about abundance and completion is shared in one heart by all the officials, the authority to lead and direct is the exclusive responsibility of the Six Ministers. If this Way can truly be practiced, the dynasty's intent in establishing offices will surely not be betrayed! Even so, this is the institutional system of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan); if we trace it back to its root, it further depends upon the single mind of the ruler. For once the ruler's mind is rectified, the ministers and councillors will all be upright men, and the subordinate officials within and the regional pastors and earls without will each advance according to their kind, while the millions of common people will together receive their blessings. In the courts of Tang and Yu, officials emulated one another in dignified array and ultimately brought about an ethos of harmony and universal peace—was this merely because of their establishment of offices? Therefore, to say that the ruler's mind is the source of myriad transformations is truly credible.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"The clouds form in dense masses, and the rain falls gently and steadily. May it rain first on our public fields, and then reach our private ones."
Zheng Wei 鄭偉
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Chen comments: The affection of the people of Zhou for their ruler is expounded clearly…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
透且詞復委婉是善說詩者
考試官教諭楊批冲雅不羣
考試官教諭朱批悠陽
周人致望於天澤而冀蒙君之餘休焉夫天澤
無分於公私也周人以是而致望於天其歸德
於君者至矣大田答君之詞若曰養民者君之
德生物者天之功苗生盛矣苗害除矣能無望
於天澤耶彼雲所以興雨非盛不足以致之安
得雲之作也淒淒其盛有以兆多雨之徵矣乎
===
雨所以潤物非徐不足以入土安得雨之興也
祁祁其徐有以極深入之漸矣乎雨也而雲以
先之雲也而雨以繼之是誠生物之一機而天
地之大德也然豈吾人之所敢必哉亦曰天之
所眷在德而君之格天有素有公田焉乃公家
之所需者天必鑒君德而雨之矣則凡我私田
皆其所同井者有不因君澤而及之乎由中達
外均被乎霑足之休是天雖無意於民不能無
意於君而降康於君亦以斂福於民矣足此通
punctuated:
透，且詞復委婉，是善說詩者。
考試官教諭楊批：冲雅不羣。
考試官教諭朱批：悠陽。

周人致望於天澤，而冀蒙君之餘休焉。夫天澤無分於公私也，周人以是而致望於天，其歸德於君者至矣。《大田》答君之詞若曰：養民者，君之德；生物者，天之功。苗生盛矣，苗害除矣，能無望於天澤耶？彼雲所以興雨，非盛不足以致之，安得雲之作也，淒淒其盛，有以兆多雨之徵矣乎？雨所以潤物，非徐不足以入土，安得雨之興也，祁祁其徐，有以極深入之漸矣乎？雨也，而雲以先之；雲也，而雨以繼之。是誠生物之一機，而天地之大德也。然豈吾人之所敢必哉？亦曰：天之所眷在德，而君之格天有素。有公田焉，乃公家之所需者，天必鑒君德而雨之矣；則凡我私田，皆其所同井者，有不因君澤而及之乎？由中達外，均被乎霑足之休，是天雖無意於民，不能無意於君，而降康於君，亦以斂福於民矣；足此通
translation_en:
…and thorough, and the phrasing is moreover nuanced and tactful; this is someone who excels at explicating the Odes.
Examiner and Instructor Yang's comment: Serene, refined, and extraordinary.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu's comment: Leisurely and expansive [悠揚].

The people of Zhou placed their hopes in the moisture of Heaven, wishing to receive the overflow of their sovereign's blessings. Now, the moisture of Heaven makes no distinction between public and private. That the people of Zhou expressed their hopes to Heaven in these terms shows to the utmost how they attributed virtue to their sovereign. The words in "Da tian" (Large Fields) responding to the sovereign are as if to say: Nourishing the people is the virtue of the sovereign; generating living things is the achievement of Heaven. Now that the sprouts are growing luxuriantly and the pests have been eliminated, how could we not hope for the moisture of Heaven? Clouds are what give rise to rain, yet unless they are dense they are insufficient to bring it about; how might we have the rising of the clouds be so densely massed as to portend abundant rain? Rain is what moistens things, yet unless it falls gently it is insufficient to soak into the soil; how might we have the falling of the rain be so gentle and steady as to reach the utmost gradualness of deep penetration? There is rain, and clouds precede it; there are clouds, and rain follows them. This is truly a vital mechanism for generating things and the great virtue of Heaven and Earth. Yet how could we dare take it for granted? We say only that what Heaven favors is virtue, and our sovereign has long moved Heaven by his sincerity. There are the public fields, which supply the needs of the ruling house; Heaven will surely behold our sovereign's virtue and rain upon them. Then as for all our private fields, which share the same well-field system—how could the rain not reach them through the grace of our sovereign? From the center reaching to the outer plots, all alike receive the blessing of soaking abundance. Thus even if Heaven had no particular regard for the people, it could not be without regard for the sovereign; and in sending down prosperity upon the sovereign, it thereby also gathers blessings for the people. By sufficing here and extending…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
彼同獲乎優渥之慶是民雖無賴於天不能無
賴於君而公田旣足百姓與之俱足矣吁以其
所望於天者望君周人之所賴於君者何切以
其所德於天者德君周人之所感於君者亦何
至耶雖然農夫何以有是言哉蓋有周盛時務
農重穀聖天子倡之賢公卿和之爲之民者鼓
舞而歌詠之一時氣象宛然康衢擊壤遺意也
而猶惓惓於先後間如此吾固知盛世之民處
畝畝而不忘君也巳
===
成王之孚下土之式永言孝思孝思維則
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭羅 批 作此題者於孚式二字
講多未融獨此篇能悉其旨而精暢古雅是邃養
之士
考試官敎諭楊 批 意周詞俊
考試官敎諭朱 批 清健
聖孝之法天下惟其純而巳矣蓋孝道通於人
心者也武王以純孝感天下而民之則之也有
punctuated:
彼，同獲乎優渥之慶。是民雖無賴於天，不能無賴於君；而公田旣足，百姓與之俱足矣。吁！以其所望於天者望君，周人之所賴於君者何切；以其所德於天者德君，周人之所感於君者亦何至耶！雖然，農夫何以有是言哉？蓋有周盛時，務農重穀，聖天子倡之，賢公卿和之，爲之民者鼓舞而歌詠之，一時氣象，宛然康衢、擊壤遺意也。而猶惓惓於先後間如此，吾固知盛世之民，處畝畝而不忘君也巳。

「成王之孚，下土之式。永言孝思，孝思維則。」
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭羅批：作此題者，於「孚」、「式」二字講多未融，獨此篇能悉其旨，而精暢古雅，是邃養之士。
考試官敎諭楊批：意周詞俊。
考試官敎諭朱批：清健。

聖孝之法天下，惟其純而巳矣。蓋孝道，通於人心者也。武王以純孝感天下，而民之則之也，有
translation_en:
… the other, jointly obtaining the blessing of abundant moisture. Thus, even if the people cannot rely directly upon Heaven, they cannot but rely upon the ruler; and once the public fields are sufficiently watered, the common people have sufficiency along with them. Ah! Looking to the ruler for what they hope for from Heaven, how earnest was the people of Zhou's reliance upon their ruler; attributing to the ruler's virtue what they owed to the virtue of Heaven, how utmost was the people of Zhou's gratitude toward their ruler! Even so, why did the farmers utter such words? In the flourishing era of the Zhou, agriculture was promoted and grain was valued. The sage Son of Heaven led the way, the worthy dukes and ministers harmonized with him, and those who were the people were inspired to dance and sing of it. The spirit of that age truly preserved the lingering ethos of the ballads of the "Highroad" and "Beating the Clods." Yet they were still so earnestly attentive to the sequence of what came first and what came after; from this I truly know that the people of a flourishing age, though dwelling among the furrowed fields, never forget their ruler.

"He achieved the confidence of a true king, a model for the lands below. Forever thinking filial thoughts, his filial thoughts were the pattern."
Che Pingchen 車聘臣
Associate Examiner and Instructor Luo comments: Those who wrote on this topic mostly failed to blend and thoroughly explain the two words "confidence" (*fu*) and "model" (*shi*). This essay alone grasps their full purport, and in its refined fluency and classical elegance it shows a scholar of deep cultivation.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: The ideas are comprehensive and the phrasing is striking.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Clear and vigorous.

That the sage's filial piety serves as a model for All under Heaven lies solely in its purity. For the way of filial piety is something that communicates with every human heart. When King Wu moved All under Heaven through his pure filial piety, that the people took him as their pattern had…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以哉此美武王之詩也若曰傳之異世而相通
者道推之天下而皆準者心人惟孝心之未純
斯無以孚天下而使之則耳惟我武王人紀肇
脩天下不言而信丕式見德道化不肅而成世
德之求匪直彰信之廣而已是則是倣以近天
子之光而黎民之敏德翕如焉配命之永匪特
默成之孚而已是訓是彝以會惟皇之極而四
海之德教沛如焉此武王之為天下則也而何
以得此哉蓋由其持執競之思而三后之丕緒
===
篤厚之而不忘崇大化之本而哲王之心法祗
承之而罔間以永世德也以此始亦以此終亹
亹乎神明之通也而一孝之感觸天下之為父
子者定矣以永配命也暫如是乆亦如是翼翼
乎孝心之純也而一德之孚格天下之為愛敬
者同矣下土之孚而則也豈偶然哉吁武王之
感人心如此觀其所感而配京之實可徵矣武
王其達孝矣乎雖然文王以服事殷夫子稱為
至德而謂武未盡善豈其求德永命尚有間然
punctuated: 以哉。此美武王之詩也。若曰：傳之異世而相通者，道；推之天下而皆準者，心。人惟孝心之未純，斯無以孚天下而使之則耳。惟我武王，人紀肇脩，天下不言而信；丕式見德，道化不肅而成。世德之求，匪直彰信之廣而已，是則是倣，以近天子之光，而黎民之敏德翕如焉；配命之永，匪特默成之孚而已，是訓是彝，以會惟皇之極，而四海之德教沛如焉。此武王之為天下則也。而何以得此哉？蓋由其持執競之思，而三后之丕緒篤厚之而不忘；崇大化之本，而哲王之心法祗承之而罔間。以永世德也，以此始，亦以此終，亹亹乎神明之通也，而一孝之感觸，天下之為父子者定矣；以永配命也，暫如是，乆亦如是，翼翼乎孝心之純也，而一德之孚格，天下之為愛敬者同矣。下土之孚而則也，豈偶然哉！吁！武王之感人心如此，觀其所感，而配京之實可徵矣。武王其達孝矣乎！雖然，文王以服事殷，夫子稱為至德，而謂武未盡善，豈其求德永命，尚有間然
translation_en: … a reason indeed! This is an ode in praise of King Wu. It is as if to say: What is transmitted across different eras and yet remains mutually connected is the Way; what is extended throughout the world and holds universally true is the mind. Only when a person's filial mind is not yet pure does he lack the means to inspire trust in the world and cause it to take him as a model. Only our King Wu initiated the cultivation of human relationships, and the world trusted him without his speaking; vastly modeling and manifesting his virtue, his moral transformation was achieved without severity. His seeking of the hereditary virtue of his predecessors did not merely spread wide a manifest trust; people took him as a model and imitated him in order to draw near the radiance of the Son of Heaven, and the black-haired people were harmonious in their diligence in virtue. His perpetually matching the Mandate of Heaven was not merely a trust achieved in silence; people took him as their instruction and constant norm in order to converge upon the august standard of perfection, and moral teaching flowed abundantly throughout the Four Seas. This was how King Wu served as a model for the world. And how did he attain this? It was because he maintained a resolute and vigorous mindfulness, enriching and never forgetting the great enterprise of the Three Rulers; he exalted the root of great transformation, reverently succeeding to the method of the mind of the wise kings without interruption. In perpetuated hereditary virtue, he began with this and also ended with this—how tireless was his communion with the spiritual intelligence! And moved by this single filial piety, all who were fathers and sons in the world were settled in their places. In perpetually matching the Mandate, it was thus for a moment and thus for a long time—how reverent was the purity of his filial mind! And reached by the trust of this single virtue, all who practiced love and respect in the world were united. Was it by chance that the lower earth trusted him and took him as a model? Ah! Such was the way King Wu moved human minds; observing what he moved, the reality of his being a worthy counterpart in the capital can be verified. Was not King Wu a man of far-reaching filial piety! Even so, because King Wen served the Yin, the Master praised him as having supreme virtue, whereas he said of Wu that he was not yet utterly good—could it be that in his seeking of virtue and perpetuating the Mandate there was still some flaw…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
耶不知時未至則遵養時晦時用介則應天順
人武王亦何心哉心乎奉天而已然而非武王
意也尚論武王之世者當原其心
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳荘公十有五年
李王
同考試官教諭黃批春秋望覇之意此作獨
能發揮明悉而詞更謹嚴可錄爲式
考試官教諭楊批詞氣剴切非徒作者
===
考試官教諭朱批明確
春秋紀兵而主大國所以望伯業之成也夫伯
業成則行乎諸侯矣此伐郳之役齊猶後宋聖
人屬望之意深哉且郳曷爲而伐也爲宋討也
夫伯者專征而先諸侯例也齊何爲序宋下耶
曰伯業未成而望之也蓋以成大業者在乎得
天下之權而孚大衆者在乎得天下之心桓也
北杏創會非不足以昭賜履也而安攘未臻何
以號召乎列辟伐宋節兵非不足以紹寔征也
punctuated:
耶？不知時未至則遵養時晦，時用介則應天順人，武王亦何心哉？心乎奉天而已。然而非武王意也，尚論武王之世者，當原其心。

《春秋》
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔荘公十有五年〕
李王
同考試官教諭黃批：《春秋》望覇之意，此作獨能發揮明悉，而詞更謹嚴，可錄爲式。
考試官教諭楊批：詞氣剴切，非徒作者。
考試官教諭朱批：明確。

《春秋》紀兵而主大國，所以望伯業之成也。夫伯業成，則行乎諸侯矣。此伐郳之役，齊猶後宋，聖人屬望之意深哉！且郳曷爲而伐也？爲宋討也。夫伯者專征而先諸侯，例也；齊何爲序宋下耶？曰：伯業未成而望之也。蓋以成大業者在乎得天下之權，而孚大衆者在乎得天下之心。桓也，北杏創會，非不足以昭賜履也，而安攘未臻，何以號召乎列辟？伐宋節兵，非不足以紹寔征也，
translation_en:
… [Could it be that in seeking to perpetuate virtue and the Mandate there was still some flaw] in him? They do not realize that when the time had not yet arrived, one observed the times in obscurity and nourished one's strength; when the great moment came, one responded to Heaven and accorded with men. What selfish intent did King Wu have? His heart was solely set on obeying Heaven. Yet even this was not King Wu's original wish; those who evaluate the age of King Wu ought to trace his true heart.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In autumn, men of Song, men of Qi, and men of Zhu invaded兒 (Ni)." [Fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang]
By Li Wang
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang comments: The intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in hoping for a hegemon is uniquely expounded with clarity and thoroughness in this piece, and its diction is even more rigorous and disciplined; it may be recorded as a model.
Examiner, Instructor Yang comments: The tone and phrasing are incisive and pertinent; this is no mere ordinary writer.
Examiner, Instructor Zhu comments: Clear and precise.

The Spring and Autumn Annals records military expedition and places a great state in the lead as a way of hoping for the accomplishment of the hegemonic enterprise. Now once the hegemonic enterprise is accomplished, one's authority prevails among the feudal lords. In this campaign to invade Ni, Qi is still listed after Song—how profound is the Sage's intent in placing his hopes upon Qi! Moreover, why was Ni invaded? It was a punitive expedition on behalf of Song. For a hegemon to exercise sole authority over punitive expeditions and take precedence over the feudal lords is the standard rule; why then is Qi ranked below Song? The answer is: because its hegemonic enterprise was not yet accomplished, and the Sage was expressing his hope for it. For accomplishing a great enterprise lies in gaining authority over the realm, and winning the trust of the multitude lies in gaining the hearts of the realm. As for Duke Huan of Qi, his initiating the assembly at Beixing was not insufficient to display the territory granted to his ancestors to govern, yet while bringing peace to the central states and repelling the barbarians had not yet been achieved, wherewith could he summon and command the various rulers? His restraining the troops during the invasion of Song was not insufficient to continue the legacy of rightful punitive authority (shizheng), …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而富強未盛何以震懾于中華鄭人未同之先
列國之人心何如也齊能必中國之我安乎天
下果能信齊之必伯乎未可知也于幽未盟之
日東州之伯勢何如也齊能必外夷之我攘乎
天下果能信伯之必成乎未可知也今兹役也
征伐之權猶主乎上公而屈巳從人正其經營
圖回之始率賦之從僅同乎小邦而聽命討貳
實為收拾人心之機吾知桓公君臣方將舒徐
以俟之而敢偃然以自居耶聖人於此以為使
===
桓伯而有成也中夏之藩屛可恃也或阻於業
之未成也世道之綱維奚賴焉故於是役而首
宋非尊宋也所以寓望齊之意也嗚呼安得謀
協志孚遂臻一匡之績也哉此聖人不得已之
心也抑齊自平宋以來其圖伯者無遺力矣而
何難成若此當時人心猶知有周桓能率諸侯
而朝之卽崛起東海無難者又奚俟于幽之盟
故今日為宋討其附庸不過欲以為宋德耳然
不知鄭且間而侵宋矣噫前日于鄄之盟幷失
punctuated: 而富強未盛，何以震懾于中華？鄭人未同之先，列國之人心何如也？齊能必中國之我安乎？天下果能信齊之必伯乎？未可知也。于幽未盟之日，東州之伯勢何如也？齊能必外夷之我攘乎？天下果能信伯之必成乎？未可知也。今兹役也，征伐之權猶主乎上公，而屈巳從人，正其經營圖回之始；率賦之從僅同乎小邦，而聽命討貳，實為收拾人心之機。吾知桓公君臣方將舒徐以俟之，而敢偃然以自居耶？聖人於此，以為使桓伯而有成也，中夏之藩屛可恃也；或阻於業之未成也，世道之綱維奚賴焉？故於是役而首宋，非尊宋也，所以寓望齊之意也。嗚呼！安得謀協志孚，遂臻一匡之績也哉？此聖人不得已之心也。抑齊自平宋以來，其圖伯者無遺力矣，而何難成若此？當時人心猶知有周，桓能率諸侯而朝之，卽崛起東海，無難者，又奚俟于幽之盟？故今日為宋討其附庸，不過欲以為宋德耳，然不知鄭且間而侵宋矣。噫！前日于鄄之盟幷失
translation_en:
…yet its wealth and military strength were not yet at their peak, so how could it overawe the Central States? Before the people of Zheng joined in concord, what were the sentiments of the various states? Could Qi be certain that the Central States would rely on it for peace? Could the realm truly trust that Qi would inevitably become hegemon? That could not yet be known. On the day before the covenant at You was sworn, what was the state of hegemonic power in the eastern region? Could Qi be certain that the foreign tribes would be repelled by it? Could the realm truly trust that the hegemony would inevitably succeed? That could not yet be known.

Now, in this campaign, the authority to launch punitive expeditions still rested with the premier Duke [of Song], while humbling oneself to follow others was precisely the beginning of [Qi's] planning and maneuvering; leading its levied troops in the train of others made it no different from a minor state, yet obeying commands to punish the disloyal was in fact the關鍵 opportunity to win over people's hearts. I know that Duke Huan and his ministers were just then proceeding unhurriedly to await the right moment—how would they dare arrogantly claim the leading place for themselves?

Here the Sage considered that if Huan's hegemony were to succeed, the defensive screen of the Central Xia could be relied upon; if, however, it were thwarted before the enterprise was accomplished, upon what would the mainstay of world order depend? Therefore, placing Song first in this campaign was not to honor Song, but to lodge his hope in Qi. Alas! How could their counsels be harmonized and their intentions win trust so as to achieve at last the merit of uniting and rectifying all under Heaven? This was the Sage's reluctant frame of mind.

Yet ever since Qi pacified Song, it had spared no effort in seeking the hegemony—why then was it so difficult to achieve? At that time, the minds of men still knew that the house of Zhou existed. Had Huan been able to lead the feudal lords to pay court to Zhou, then rising up from the Eastern Sea would have posed no difficulty at all; what need would there have been to wait for the covenant at You? Thus, today in punishing Song's dependency on Song's behalf, he merely wished to do Song a favor, not realizing that Zheng would meanwhile take advantage of the opening to invade Song! Alas, that even the previous covenant at Juan was lost as well…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之伊誰繇哉
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕
杜華秋
同考試官教諭黃批〔構思精密命詞蒼古發〕
〔明桓仲念深處宛然〕
考試官教諭楊批〔辭嚴意足深于經者〕
考試官教諭朱批〔整雅〕
===
觀伯主之威信而制外之念深矣夫于以見威信
迭著齊伯之所以謀楚者何至也始事之勤不
有足尚者哉且楚肆暴橫以陵鄭而復挾江黃
以為已援其目中已無齊矣惟時桓與仲之經
營已非一日其能以忘情乎於是為檉與陽穀
之會焉夫檉之會兵革不試曷言乎威之振蓋
威天下者在握天下之勢方楚氛之孔熾也使
無威以振之則北方之國未必協從齊也念攘
楚之要樞在鄭也乃就犖地以結盟而彌縫匡
punctuated:
之，伊誰繇哉？
「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。」〔僖公元年〕「秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。」〔僖公三年〕
杜華秋
同考試官教諭黃批：〔構思精密，命詞蒼古，發明桓、仲念深處宛然。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔辭嚴意足，深于經者。〕
考試官教諭朱批：〔整雅。〕
觀伯主之威信，而制外之念深矣。夫于以見威信迭著，齊伯之所以謀楚者，何至也！始事之勤，不有足尚者哉？且楚肆暴橫以陵鄭，而復挾江、黃以為已援，其目中已無齊矣。惟時桓與仲之經營已非一日，其能以忘情乎？於是為檉與陽穀之會焉。夫檉之會，兵革不試，曷言乎威之振？蓋威天下者，在握天下之勢。方楚氛之孔熾也，使無威以振之，則北方之國未必協從。齊也念攘楚之要樞在鄭也，乃就犖地以結盟，而彌縫匡…
translation_en:
… [forfeit even the previous covenant at Juan]—whose fault was this?

"In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a man of Zhu at Cheng." [First year of Duke Xi] "In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a man of Jiang, and a man of Huang met at Yanggu." [Third year of Duke Xi]

Du Huaqiu 杜華秋
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Huang: [The conception is precise and thorough, the phrasing antique and vigorous; it vividly brings to light the deep intentions of Duke Huan and Guan Zhong.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Yang: [Rigorous in diction and ample in meaning; one who is deeply versed in the Classic.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zhu: [Orderly and elegant.]

Observing the Hegemon's awe-inspiring authority and trustworthiness, one sees how deep was his concern for controlling external threats! For by seeing his authority and trustworthiness displayed in turn, how thorough were the means by which the Hegemon of Qi plotted against Chu! Is not his diligence at the inception of the enterprise worthy of esteem? Moreover, Chu was wantonly exercising tyranny and arrogance to bully Zheng, and furthermore coerced Jiang and Huang into serving as its own support; in its eyes, Qi already ceased to exist. At that time, the planning and management of Duke Huan and Guan Zhong had been underway for more than a single day—how could they remain indifferent? Thereupon they held the meetings at Cheng and Yanggu. Now, at the meeting of Cheng, weapons and armor were not put to use; why then speak of the rousing of authority? Because overawing the world lies in grasping the strategic posture of the world. Just when the miasma of Chu was blazing fiercely, had there been no authority with which to rouse them, the states of the north would not necessarily have joined in following harmoniously. Qi reflected that the crucial pivot for repelling Chu lay in Zheng; therefore, it went to the territory of Luo [Cheng] to conclude a covenant, and to mend and rectify…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
救與列國共圖之夫以素所未集之兵一旦致
之麾下蓋不越乎樽俎之間而先聲所及中國
之威著矣異日次陘庭以納款楚竟不敢遺鄭
人一矢謂非振威之所致耶陽穀之會神明不
要曷言乎信之敦蓋信天下者在一天下之心
方夷屬之新附也使無信以申之則東方之國
未必堅從齊也念斷楚之右臂在江黃也乃繼
貫澤以講好而奇正分合俾二國共守之夫以
素所未同之國一旦聽吾約束蓋不藉于壇坫
===
之歃而意氣所感中國之信孚矣異日偕二國
以伐陳楚竟不敢越中原一步謂非敦信之所
致耶吁此一桓仲也能愼於楚未帖之先而不
能不肆於陳旣執之後君子有以識齊君臣之
量與器矣雖然獨濤塗之役已哉楚師三至鄭
郊而救不力惡乎勤且齊藉力於江黃者不少
而使楚竟滅之遠齊近楚之諫徒廑仲父之思
矣然是時楚用子文以紓國難抑亦仲父耦也
謂無競維人信哉
punctuated: 救，與列國共圖之。夫以素所未集之兵，一旦致之麾下，蓋不越乎樽俎之間，而先聲所及，中國之威著矣。異日次陘庭以納款，楚竟不敢遺鄭人一矢，謂非振威之所致耶？陽穀之會，神明不要，曷言乎信之敦？蓋信天下者，在一天下之心。方夷屬之新附也，使無信以申之，則東方之國未必堅從齊也。念斷楚之右臂在江、黃也，乃繼貫澤以講好，而奇正分合，俾二國共守之。夫以素所未同之國，一旦聽吾約束，蓋不藉于壇坫之歃，而意氣所感，中國之信孚矣。異日偕二國以伐陳，楚竟不敢越中原一步，謂非敦信之所致耶？吁！此一桓、仲也，能愼於楚未帖之先，而不能不肆於陳旣執之後，君子有以識齊君臣之量與器矣。雖然，獨濤塗之役已哉？楚師三至鄭郊而救不力，惡乎勤？且齊藉力於江、黃者不少，而使楚竟滅之，遠齊近楚之諫，徒廑仲父之思矣。然是時楚用子文以紓國難，抑亦仲父耦也。謂「無競維人」，信哉！
translation_en:
…and rescue [Zheng], planning it together with the various states. By bringing troops that had never before been assembled under his command in a single morning, without going beyond the realm of banquet vessels, the advance reputation of his might spread, and the prestige of the Central States was made manifest. On a later day, when he encamped at Xingting to receive terms of submission, Chu ultimately did not dare to shoot a single arrow at the people of Zheng—how could one say this was not the result of his rousing of prestige?

At the meeting of Yanggu, no oaths were exacted before the spirits; why then speak of the strengthening of good faith? For winning the trust of the world lies in unifying the hearts of the world. Just when the subordinate夷 (Yi) states had newly attached themselves, if there had been no good faith to reassure them, the eastern states would not necessarily have firmly followed Qi. Reflecting that cutting off the right arm of Chu depended on Jiang and Huang, Qi followed up the meeting at Guanze by cultivating friendly relations; coordinating unorthodox and orthodox tactics, dividing and combining forces, it enabled the two states to defend themselves together. When states that had never before joined us submitted in a single morning to our stipulations, without relying on blood-oaths upon the covenant altar, moved by spirit and intent, the good faith of the Central States inspired confidence. On a later day, when Qi joined the two states in attacking Chen, Chu ultimately did not dare to cross a single step into the Central Plains—how could one say this was not the result of strengthening good faith?

Alas! It was this very same Duke Huan and Guan Zhong who were able to be cautious before Chu was subdued, yet could not help becoming arrogant after [Yuan] Taotu of Chen had been seized; from this the gentleman can discern the measure and capacity of the ruler and minister of Qi. Even so, was it only the campaign involving [Yuan] Taotu? The army of Chu thrice reached the outskirts of Zheng and Qi's relief was not vigorous—where then was its diligence? Moreover, Qi relied not a little on the strength of Jiang and Huang, yet allowed Chu in the end to annihilate them; the remonstrance about Qi being distant and Chu near merely left "Uncle Zhong" [Guan Zhong] with anxious regrets. Yet at that time Chu employed Ziwen to relieve the state's difficulties, and he too was a match for Uncle Zhong. Truly it is said, "What is most powerful is the man!"

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
天子當宁而立諸公東面諸侯西面曰朝
劉祖泗
同考試官教諭蔣批發揮君臣相得氣象若
躬逢其盛者可以占忠愛矣録之以式
考試官教諭楊批立格正大造詞峻整
考試官教諭朱批氣勁意足非苟作者
王者之親其臣因禮行於春而名之也蓋君臣
非以時接其情弗親也此春朝之禮行而名有
===
所取歟且天下有不容不辨之分而亦有不容
不孚之情者君臣是也故非惟覲禮爲然時乎
春也天地訢合自然之和肇矣天子於諸侯能
忘情乎於是當門屏以宁立一人隆晉接之儀
位內廟而序進列辟謹對揚之度東面公也而
諸爲公者從之矣西面侯也而諸爲侯者從之
矣斯時也贄則朝受享則廟受故斯禮也不謂
之覲而謂之朝君爲明主而忘勢以親其臣非
瀆也受朝之禮宜然也臣爲嘉賓而上比以親
punctuated:
《禮記》
天子當宁而立，諸公東面，諸侯西面，曰朝。
劉祖泗
同考試官教諭蔣批：發揮君臣相得氣象，若躬逢其盛者，可以占忠愛矣。録之以式。
考試官教諭楊批：立格正大，造詞峻整。
考試官教諭朱批：氣勁意足，非苟作者。
王者之親其臣，因禮行於春而名之也。蓋君臣非以時接，其情弗親也。此春朝之禮行，而名有所取歟？且天下有不容不辨之分，而亦有不容不孚之情者，君臣是也。故非惟覲禮爲然。時乎春也，天地訢合，自然之和肇矣，天子於諸侯，能忘情乎？於是當門屏以宁立，一人隆晉接之儀；位內廟而序進，列辟謹對揚之度。東面，公也，而諸爲公者從之矣；西面，侯也，而諸爲侯者從之矣。斯時也，贄則朝受，享則廟受，故斯禮也，不謂之覲而謂之朝。君爲明主，而忘勢以親其臣，非瀆也，受朝之禮宜然也；臣爲嘉賓，而上比以親…
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)

"The Son of Heaven stands in the space between the gate and screen; the dukes face east, and the marquises face west; this is called the morning audience (chao)."

Liu Zusi 劉祖泗

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: He brings out the spirit of mutual rapport between ruler and minister, as though he had personally witnessed that flourishing age; from this one may gauge his loyalty and devotion. Recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Yang 楊: The structure he establishes is upright and grand; his phrasing is lofty and well-ordered.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu 朱: Vigorous in vital breath and full in meaning—not something casually composed.

That the true king draws close to his ministers is named after the rite performed in spring. For if ruler and minister do not meet at the proper seasons, their feelings will not be close. Is it not from the performance of this rite of the spring audience that its name is derived? Moreover, in the world there is a distinction of rank that cannot but be differentiated, yet there is also a bond of affection that cannot but be held in mutual trust: such is the relation between ruler and minister. Therefore, this is true not only of the autumn audience rite (jin). When the season is spring, Heaven and Earth join in joyful harmony, and natural concord begins; how could the Son of Heaven remain unmoved in his feelings toward the feudal lords? Thereupon, standing in the space between the gate and screen, the One Man exalts the ceremony of receiving them; taking their places in the inner ancestral temple and advancing in order, the assembled rulers carefully observe the proper measure of responding to and extolling his grace. Facing east are the dukes, and all who hold the rank of duke follow them; facing west are the marquises, and all who hold the rank of marquis follow them. At this time, the ceremonial gifts of introduction are received at court, while the tributary offerings are received in the ancestral temple; therefore, this rite is not called the autumn audience (jin), but is called the morning/spring audience (chao). The ruler acts as an enlightened sovereign and forgets his power in order to draw close to his ministers—this is not familiarity, for the rite of receiving the spring audience ought to be so. The ministers act as honored guests and associate upwardly in order to draw close…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎君非亢也入朝之禮宜爾也體統不廢而歡
心常聯于一德之交諸父諸舅式相好矣都俞
吁咈之風其可想乎禮度雖明而順氣常孚于
一堂之感兄弟婚姻無相遠矣明良喜起之盛
其可挹乎名之曰朝是之取爾而非徒以其來
朝之早也已嗟夫是天道也天以秋肅萬物而
煦以春君以義正天下而和以仁仁義並行此
天子所以養諸侯而兵不用諸侯之所以尊尊
而親親也三代之長也豈獨其積厚而制備哉
===
以其共和夾輔者有人也厥後下堂見河陽狩
矣朝禮其廢乎仲尼刪詩而存菀柳之章有以
也
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮
吳遜之
同考試官教諭蔣 批 禮樂發端之理渾融貫
能發明於義可錄
考試官教諭楊 批 約而該清而整善言禮
punctuated:
乎君，非亢也，入朝之禮宜爾也。體統不廢，而歡心常聯于一德之交，「諸父諸舅，式相好矣」，都俞吁咈之風，其可想乎！禮度雖明，而順氣常孚于一堂之感，「兄弟婚姻，無相遠矣」，明良喜起之盛，其可挹乎！名之曰「朝」，是之取爾，而非徒以其來朝之早也已。嗟夫！是天道也。天以秋肅萬物而煦以春，君以義正天下而和以仁。仁義並行，此天子所以養諸侯而兵不用，諸侯之所以尊尊而親親也。三代之長也，豈獨其積厚而制備哉？以其共和夾輔者有人也。厥後下堂見、河陽狩矣，朝禮其廢乎！仲尼刪《詩》而存《菀柳》之章，有以也。

「春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。」
吳遜之
同考試官教諭蔣批：禮樂發端之理，渾融貫□，能發明於義，可錄。
考試官教諭楊批：約而該，清而整，善言禮…
translation_en:
…toward his ruler, this is not arrogance; it is simply what the ritual of attending court requires. The hierarchical order is not set aside, yet joyful hearts are ever united in the fellowship of shared virtue—"Paternal and maternal uncles, let us be on good terms with one another!" Can we not imagine the spirit of harmonious agreement and candid remonstrance of antiquity? Although ritual regulations are clearly defined, an atmosphere of concord ever inspires trust within the shared hall—"Brothers and relatives by marriage, let none keep at a distance from one another!" Can we not draw upon the flourishing age when enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoiced together? That this ceremony is named the "spring court audience" (chao) takes its meaning from this, and not merely from their coming to court early in the morning or the year.

Alas, this is the Way of Heaven! Heaven disciplines the myriad things with autumn and warms them with spring; the ruler rectifies the realm with righteousness and harmonizes it with benevolence. When benevolence and righteousness operate together, this is how the Son of Heaven nurtures the feudal lords without resorting to arms, and how the feudal lords honor the honorable and cherish their kin. That the Three Dynasties endured so long—was it solely because their accumulated merit was deep and their institutions complete? It was because they had men who joined in harmonious cooperation and gave them flanking support. In later times, when the king descended from the hall to receive the feudal lords and went hunting at Heyang, was not the ritual of the court audience abandoned? When Confucius edited the Odes (Shi) and preserved the stanza of "Luxuriant Willow" (Wanliu), there was good reason for it!

"Spring'ssprouting and summer's growth are benevolence; autumn's harvesting and winter's storing are righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music, and righteousness is akin to ritual."
Wu Xunzhi 吳遜之
Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang comments: The principle of the origin of ritual and music is seamlessly integrated and thoroughly […], capable of elucidating the meaning; worthy of selection.
Examiner Instructor Yang comments: Concise yet comprehensive, clear yet well-ordered; one who excels at discussing ritual…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
樂者
考試官敎諭朱批明淨得旨
論造化生成之德幾於禮樂也蓋仁義者造化
生成之德也而與禮樂相近焉效法其有本乎
樂記之意謂夫人知禮樂肇端於天地矣而未
知其理之一也何言乎物不自生也作之以春
鼓出機於東震長之以夏壯化工於南離此天
地絪縕之德普萬物而無私者吾於合同而知
資生之仁也物不自成也秋而斂焉肅之以兌
===
金冬而藏焉止之以坎水此性命各正之理別
羣物而不過者吾於散殊而知曲成之義也然
是仁也氣行同和者也樂之有聲非氣之爲而
以和爲主乎取聲氣之順成者與元氣之順布
者而比之相去特幾希爾雖謂無聲爲有聲之
象可也樂之興于合同之初也以此是義也質
具異序者也禮之有體非質之爲而以序爲主
乎取制度之森嚴者與法象之森列者而比之
相去亦無幾爾雖謂無體爲有體之寓可也禮
punctuated:
樂者。
考試官敎諭朱批：明淨得旨。
論造化生成之德，幾於禮樂也。蓋仁義者，造化生成之德也，而與禮樂相近焉，效法其有本乎！《樂記》之意，謂夫人知禮樂肇端於天地矣，而未知其理之一也。何言乎？物不自生也，作之以春，鼓出機於東震；長之以夏，壯化工於南離。此天地絪縕之德，普萬物而無私者，吾於合同而知資生之仁也。物不自成也，秋而斂焉，肅之以兌金；冬而藏焉，止之以坎水。此性命各正之理，別羣物而不過者，吾於散殊而知曲成之義也。然是仁也，氣行同和者也。樂之有聲，非氣之爲而以和爲主乎？取聲氣之順成者與元氣之順布者而比之，相去特幾希爾，雖謂無聲爲有聲之象可也，樂之興于合同之初也以此。是義也，質具異序者也。禮之有體，非質之爲而以序爲主乎？取制度之森嚴者與法象之森列者而比之，相去亦無幾爾，雖謂無體爲有體之寓可也，禮
translation_en:
…and music.

Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: Lucid, clean, and grasps the main import.

It discusses how the virtues of creation and completion in nature approximate ritual and music. For benevolence and righteousness are the virtues of creation and completion in nature, and they are close to ritual and music—surely taking them as models has a fundamental basis! The meaning of the Record of Music (Yueji) is that people know ritual and music originate in Heaven and Earth, yet they do not know that their principle is one. Why is this said? Things do not generate themselves: they are stirred into activity by spring, drumming forth the mechanism of emergence in the eastern trigram Zhen; they are nourished to growth by summer, strengthening the work of transformation in the southern trigram Li. This is the generative virtue of Heaven and Earth, extending universally to the myriad things without partiality; in their union and harmony, we recognize the benevolence that provides for life. Things do not bring themselves to completion: in autumn they are gathered in, made solemn through the metal of the trigram Dui; in winter they are stored away, brought to rest through the water of the trigram Kan. This is the principle whereby each nature and destiny is rectified, distinguishing the multitude of things without excess; in their differentiation and particularity, we recognize the righteousness that brings things to intricate completion. Now, this benevolence is that in which vital energy moves in shared harmony. When music has sound, is it not the working of vital energy taking harmony as its keynote? If we take the smooth accomplishment of musical sound and breath and compare it with the smooth diffusion of primal vital energy, the difference between them is slight indeed. Even to say that the soundless is the image of the sounded is permissible; it is for this reason that music arises at the beginning of union and harmony. And this righteousness is that in which substantial form possesses distinct order. When ritual has its structure, is it not the working of substantial form taking order as its keynote? If we take the strict array of ritual institutions and compare it with the orderly arrangement of natural models and phenomena, the difference between them is likewise slight. Even to say that the formless is the abode of the formed is permissible; that ritual…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之行於散殊之際也以此噫是探本之論也雖
然禮樂豈判然二物哉春夏秋冬一氣也生長
斂藏一機也知仁樂義禮所以爲近又知其所
以爲一則功用之妙不在聖人在吾心矣三代
而下古禮雖廢其數可陳若大樂則寥寥絕響
矣豈一元生物之仁流行於天地者有時而息
歟無亦求中聲者過也非知道者孰能識之
第貳場
論
===
人主以天下爲度
徐兆魁
同考試官敎諭陳 批 以天爲喻切中題旨而
束結處尤見卓識取之
考試官敎諭楊 批 體裁嚴整議論正大
考試官敎諭朱 批 宏博中有奇特
人主之制治也以法而其行法也以天夫然後
可以通天下之志而善天下之治法者人主之
所制也法制于人主固宜可以自行其意而不
punctuated:
之行於散殊之際也，以此。噫！是探本之論也。雖然，禮樂豈判然二物哉？春夏秋冬，一氣也；生長斂藏，一機也。知仁樂、義禮所以爲近，又知其所以爲一，則功用之妙，不在聖人，在吾心矣。三代而下，古禮雖廢，其數可陳；若大樂，則寥寥絕響矣。豈一元生物之仁流行於天地者，有時而息歟？無亦求中聲者過也。非知道者，孰能識之！

第貳場
論
人主以天下爲度
徐兆魁
同考試官敎諭陳 批：以天爲喻，切中題旨，而束結處尤見卓識，取之。
考試官敎諭楊 批：體裁嚴整，議論正大。
考試官敎諭朱 批：宏博中有奇特。

人主之制治也以法，而其行法也以天，夫然後可以通天下之志，而善天下之治。法者，人主之所制也。法制于人主，固宜可以自行其意，而不
translation_en:
… operates amidst dispersal and differentiation is because of this. Ah! This is a discourse that probes to the fundamental root. Even so, how could ritual and music be two completely separate things? Spring, summer, autumn, and winter are a single vital force (qi); sprouting, growing, harvesting, and storing are a single mechanism. If one understands why benevolence and music, and righteousness and ritual, are close to one another, and also understands why they are one, then the subtlety of their efficacy lies not in the sages, but in our own minds. From the Three Dynasties downward, although ancient rituals have fallen into disuse, their forms and numbers can still be set forth; as for great music, however, its echoes have died out into silence. Could it be that the benevolence of the primordial unity that gives life to all things, flowing between Heaven and Earth, at times ceases? Or is it rather the fault of those who seek the harmonious mean in sound alone? Who other than one who understands the Way could recognize this!

Second Session
Discourse
"The ruler takes the empire as his measure"
Xu Zhaokui 徐兆魁
Associate Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: Using Heaven as a metaphor hits the exact point of the theme, and the concluding section especially shows outstanding insight; selected.
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊 comments: The structure is rigorous and orderly, and the argument is upright and grand.
Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: Within its breadth and erudition there is something extraordinary.

The ruler establishes governance through law, and he carries out the law by modeling himself on Heaven; only then can he connect the wills of all under Heaven and bring perfection to the governance of the empire. Law is what the ruler establishes. Since laws are established by the ruler, it would seem fitting that he could simply carry out his own intentions, without…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
必於斤斤然操尺幅以求合於天下之人爲也
人主而操尺幅以求合於天下之人不幾於一
人而徇天下乎法之所存道之所存也道之所
從出者天也天之愛民也甚矣豈其使一人恣
於民上而行其意以失天下之平必不然矣明
主知其然是故廓吾心以通于天下而不敢咈
天下以從吾心舉天下善善惡惡功功罪罪一
準之蕩平正直之理而一毫之私意無所與於
其間非徇之也公之也公則心平心平則氣龢
===
氣龢而天地之龢應之此治古之極也人主以
天下爲度言賞罰也請繹胡氏之旨且人主何
爲而有賞罰哉天下至大也天下之人善者惡
者功者罪者紛然待命於我千緒萬縷如絲之
繰于盆而不可紀也人主何恃而能自理耶賞
與罰也是故山川土田玄衮赤舄介圭樂懸牛
羊寶龜路車乗馬淑旂綏章彤弓之錫秬鬯之
賚賞也所以彰善而勸功也五刑三就五流三
宅象典流宥官鞭教扑移郊移遂遠方之屏貶
punctuated:
必於斤斤然操尺幅以求合於天下之人爲也。人主而操尺幅以求合於天下之人，不幾於一人而徇天下乎？法之所存，道之所存也；道之所從出者，天也。天之愛民也甚矣，豈其使一人恣於民上，而行其意以失天下之平？必不然矣。明主知其然，是故廓吾心以通于天下，而不敢咈天下以從吾心。舉天下善善惡惡、功功罪罪，一準之蕩平正直之理，而一毫之私意無所與於其間。非徇之也，公之也。公則心平，心平則氣龢，氣龢而天地之龢應之，此治古之極也。「人主以天下爲度」，言賞罰也，請繹胡氏之旨。
且人主何爲而有賞罰哉？天下至大也，天下之人，善者、惡者、功者、罪者，紛然待命於我，千緒萬縷，如絲之繰于盆而不可紀也。人主何恃而能自理耶？賞與罰也。是故山川土田、玄衮赤舄、介圭樂懸、牛羊寶龜、路車乗馬、淑旂綏章、彤弓之錫、秬鬯之賚，賞也，所以彰善而勸功也。五刑三就、五流三宅、象典流宥、官鞭教扑、移郊移遂、遠方之屏、貶…
translation_en:
…need to fastidiously wield a measuring stick to seek conformity with the people of the world. If the ruler were to wield a measuring stick to seek conformity with the people of the world, would that not come close to one man pandering to the world? Where the law resides is where the Way resides; and that from which the Way issues forth is Heaven. Heaven loves the people deeply indeed! How could it allow one man to act unrestrainedly above the people, carrying out his own willful desires so as to lose the fairness of the world? Surely it is not so. The enlightened ruler knows this to be so; therefore, he broadens his own mind to connect with all under Heaven, and dares not defy all under Heaven to make it follow his own mind. Taking all the world's praising of the good and hating of the evil, rewarding of merit and punishing of crime, he measures everything entirely by the principles of broad fairness and uprightness, without allowing a single hair's breadth of selfish intent to intrude therein. This is not pandering to them; it is treating them with public impartiality. When there is impartiality, the mind is balanced; when the mind is balanced, the vitalvital energy (qi) is harmonious; and when the vital energy is harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds to it. This was the pinnacle of governance in antiquity. The statement "The ruler takes all under Heaven as his measure" speaks of rewards and punishments; allow me to unfold the purport of Mr. Hu's words.

Moreover, why does the ruler possess rewards and punishments? The world is vast indeed. The people of the world—the good, the evil, the meritorious, and the guilty—all clamorously await orders from him, in thousands of threads and tens of thousands of strands, like silk being reeled from a basin, impossible to untangle and count. On what does the ruler rely to bring order to it himself? Rewards and punishments. Therefore, hills, streams, lands, and fields; dark dragon-robes and red slippers; great jade tablets and suspended musical instruments; cattle, sheep, and precious tortoises; grand carriages and teams of four horses; fine banners and feathered pennants; the bestowal of red bows and the granting of black-millet sacrificial wine—these are rewards, the means by which to manifest the good and encourage merit. The five punishments and their three places of execution; the five banishments and their three places of settlement; the statutory punishments depicted in images and mitigation by exile; the whip in government offices and the rod in schools; removal to the outer suburbs and removal to the rural districts; banishment to distant regions; demotion in…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爵削地六師之移衣冠之畫嘉石之坐刑也所
以癉惡而懲罪也書曰天命有德五服五章哉
天討有罪五刑五用哉易曰火在天上大有君
子以遏惡揚善順天休命曰德曰服曰善曰揚
言賞也曰罪曰刑曰惡曰遏言刑也然而必曰
天命曰天討曰天之休命者明其皆出於天也
天之道福善而禍淫其於人也制以意不制以
形人或疑而翫焉於是舉禍福之柄而授之君
使司平之是賞罰者人主之所以代天以行其
===
理而非其所得恣已以便其私者也人主之尊
猶之天也有言遜於乃心則泰然喜逆於乃心
則艴然怒其情得肆也喜之發也甘雨煕陽怒
之發也疾霆隕霜其勢得行也憸夫壬人之欲
作威而作福也必有所窺而後動上徵好則諛
人者進上徵惡則譖人者進其機易投也以得
肆之情濟之以得行之勢而乘之以易投之機
然則人主之法何自而當天下之治亦何自而
善乎此其所以必天下爲度也物之有分寸尺
punctuated: 爵削地、六師之移、衣冠之畫、嘉石之坐，刑也，所以癉惡而懲罪也。《書》曰：「天命有德，五服五章哉！天討有罪，五刑五用哉！」《易》曰：「火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。」曰德、曰服、曰善、曰揚，言賞也；曰罪、曰刑、曰惡、曰遏，言刑也。然而必曰天命、曰天討、曰天之休命者，明其皆出於天也。天之道，福善而禍淫，其於人也，制以意，不制以形，人或疑而翫焉。於是舉禍福之柄而授之君，使司平之。是賞罰者，人主之所以代天以行其理，而非其所得恣已以便其私者也。人主之尊，猶之天也。有言遜於乃心，則泰然喜；逆於乃心，則艴然怒，其情得肆也。喜之發也，甘雨煕陽；怒之發也，疾霆隕霜，其勢得行也。憸夫壬人之欲作威而作福也，必有所窺而後動：上徵好，則諛人者進；上徵惡，則譖人者進，其機易投也。以得肆之情，濟之以得行之勢，而乘之以易投之機，然則人主之法何自而當？天下之治亦何自而善乎？此其所以必天下爲度也。物之有分、寸、尺、
translation_en:
… demotion in rank and reduction of fiefs, the mobilization of the Six Armies, the symbolic garments painted to mark offenders, and making wrongdoers sit upon the admonitory stone—these are punishments, the means by which evil is chastised and crimes are penalized. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Heaven graciously distinguishes the virtuous; are there not the five habiliments, fivefold variegated? Heaven punishes the guilty; are there not the five punishments, to be severally used for that purpose?" The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Fire above heaven forms the hexagram Great Possession (Dayou); the superior man, in accordance with this, represses evil and揚 [promotes] the good, and thereby obeys the beneficent mandate of Heaven." To speak of "virtue," "habiliments," "the good," and "promoting" is to speak of rewards; to speak of "guilt," "punishments," "evil," and "repressing" is to speak of punishments. Yet the texts invariably call them "Heaven's charge," "Heaven's punishment," and "the beneficent mandate of Heaven" in order to make clear that they all issue from Heaven.

The Way of Heaven is to bless the good and bring calamity upon the wicked. In dealing with mankind, however, Heaven governs through intent rather than through visible form, and so people sometimes doubt it and treat it lightly. Therefore, Heaven takes the handle of calamity and blessing and entrusts it to the ruler, commissioning him to administer it with fairness. Thus, rewards and punishments are the means by which the ruler acts on behalf of Heaven to carry out its principles, and not something in which he may indulge himself to serve his private ends.

The exalted position of the ruler is like that of Heaven. When words are agreeable to his mind, he is serenely pleased; when they go against his mind, he flushes with anger—his emotions are free to run their course. When his pleasure goes forth, it is like sweet rain and warm sunshine; when his anger goes forth, it is like a sudden thunderbolt and falling frost—his power is free to take effect. When crafty and artful men wish to usurp the power to terrorize and to bless, they inevitably spy out his inclinations before making a move. If the sovereign shows a sign of favor, flatterers step forward; if the sovereign shows a sign of dislike, slanderers step forward—such opportunities are easy to exploit. When emotions that are free to run their course are backed by power that is free to take effect, and are further seized upon by opportunities that are easy to exploit, how then can the ruler's laws be fitting, and how can the governance of the empire be good? This is why he must take the empire as his standard of measure. That things have tenths of an inch, inches, feet, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
丈引者度也而天下之度物者準於是矣織帛
於宮既成而鬻之市廣者不可狹而狹者不可
廣長者不可短而短者不可長其度定也是故
家有家度國有國度天下有天下之度卿大夫
以一家爲度故親愛賤惡不可忽於家諸侯以
國爲度故一嚬一笑不可輕於國至若人主所
以爲之度者非特一國一家也天下之人孰非
人主之人哉御得其道戎夷蠻貊有莫敢不來
享不來王者吾安得而勿獎之也而何以私勞
===
爲也御失其道匹夫匹婦有敢怒而不敢言者
吾安得而盡讎之也而何以私怨爲也私意行
則公道蔽而人主之度失矣況其始之者濫觴
而繼之者滔天而不可止也於是有虐煢獨而
畏高明者焉有賞僭而及惡人刑濫而及善人
者焉有賞數而人不見德罰敝而人不知懼者
焉有輿臺緤組廝養續貂而帑藏爲竭者焉有
赭衣半道斷獄數萬而民無所措手足者焉其
甚也干陰陽之龢殄羣生之命此無他由其不
punctuated: 丈、引者，度也，而天下之度物者準於是矣。織帛於宮，既成而鬻之市，廣者不可狹而狹者不可廣，長者不可短而短者不可長，其度定也。是故家有家度，國有國度，天下有天下之度。卿大夫以一家爲度，故親愛、賤惡不可忽於家；諸侯以國爲度，故一嚬一笑不可輕於國。至若人主所以爲之度者，非特一國一家也。天下之人，孰非人主之人哉？御得其道，戎、夷、蠻、貊有莫敢不來享、不來王者，吾安得而勿獎之也？而何以私勞爲也？御失其道，匹夫匹婦有敢怒而不敢言者，吾安得而盡讎之也？而何以私怨爲也？私意行則公道蔽，而人主之度失矣。況其始之者濫觴，而繼之者滔天而不可止也。於是有虐煢獨而畏高明者焉；有賞僭而及惡人，刑濫而及善人者焉；有賞數而人不見德，罰敝而人不知懼者焉；有輿臺緤組、廝養續貂，而帑藏爲竭者焉；有赭衣半道、斷獄數萬，而民無所措手足者焉。其甚也，干陰陽之龢，殄羣生之命。此無他，由其不
translation_en: …ten-foot lengths (zhang), and hundred-foot lengths (yin) is the standard of measure (du), and those across the realm who measure things take their standard from this. When silk is woven in the household and, once finished, sold in the marketplace, what is wide cannot be made narrow and what is narrow cannot be made wide; what is long cannot be made short and what is short cannot be made long, because its measure is fixed. Therefore, a household has the measure of a household, a state has the measure of a state, and the realm has the measure of the realm. Grandees and high officials take a single household as their measure, and so affection and loathing cannot be treated carelessly within the household; feudal lords take a state as their measure, and so a single frown or smile cannot be taken lightly within the state. As for what a ruler takes as his measure, it is not merely a single state or a single household. Among all the people of the realm, who is not the ruler's own person? If he governs according to the proper Way, even among the Rong, Yi, Man, and Mo tribes there will be none who dare not come to present offerings and pay homage—how could I fail to reward them, and what room would there be for rewarding only private service? If he loses the proper Way in governing, even ordinary men and women will dare to feel anger though they dare not speak—how could I treat them all as enemies, and what room would there be for acting on private resentment? When private bias prevails, public justice is obscured, and the ruler's measure is lost. How much worse when what begins as an overflowing goblet continues until it floods the heavens and cannot be stopped! Thereupon there are cases of oppressing the solitary and helpless while fearing the high and mighty; cases where rewards overstep bounds and reach the wicked, while punishments overflow and reach the good; cases where rewards are so frequent that people see no grace in them, and penalties so worn out that people feel no fear; cases where menial servants wear silk cords of office and stable boys add sable tails to their caps, exhausting the state treasuries; and cases where convicts in reddish-brown garb fill half the roads and tens of thousands of criminal cases are decided, leaving the people nowhere to place their hands and feet. At its worst, it violates the harmony of yin and yang and cuts short the lives of the multitude of living beings. This is due to nothing other than his failure to…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知以天下爲度故也以天下爲度者以天下之
心爲心也以天下之心爲心者以天之心爲心
也以天之心爲心者公而不私也喜怒一人之
喜怒也非天下人之喜怒也私也好惡天下人
之好惡也非一人之好惡也公也吾弗欲窮吾
得肆之情而天下之同情可弗順乎吾弗欲挾
吾得行之勢而天下之大勢可弗合乎吾弗欲
啓吾易投之機而天下之大機可弗執乎善吾
彰焉功吾勸焉所以彰之勸之者無心也以天
===
下之好好之也非謂其私勞我故喜也卽有舊
怨吾賞之矣惡吾癉焉罪吾懲焉所以癉之懲
之者無心也以天下之惡惡之也非謂其私怨
我故怒也卽有微勞吾罰之矣溫原陽樊之田
可賜而地不可隧也邑可多予而纓不可請也
執羈勒而從者不可私班邑也驚屬車之塵剚
寢廟之環者可誅而廷尉之法不可加也人主
之賞罰非固如此之徇乎天下之人也道本至
公惡得而參之以私治本至順惡得而與之以
punctuated: 知以天下爲度故也。以天下爲度者，以天下之心爲心也；以天下之心爲心者，以天之心爲心也；以天之心爲心者，公而不私也。喜怒，一人之喜怒也，非天下人之喜怒也，私也；好惡，天下人之好惡也，非一人之好惡也，公也。吾弗欲窮吾得肆之情，而天下之同情可弗順乎？吾弗欲挾吾得行之勢，而天下之大勢可弗合乎？吾弗欲啓吾易投之機，而天下之大機可弗執乎？善吾彰焉，功吾勸焉，所以彰之勸之者無心也，以天下之好好之也，非謂其私勞我故喜也，卽有舊怨，吾賞之矣；惡吾癉焉，罪吾懲焉，所以癉之懲之者無心也，以天下之惡惡之也，非謂其私怨我故怒也，卽有微勞，吾罰之矣。溫、原、陽樊之田可賜，而地不可隧也；邑可多予，而纓不可請也；執羈勒而從者，不可私班邑也；驚屬車之塵、剚寢廟之環者可誅，而廷尉之法不可加也。人主之賞罰，非固如此之徇乎天下之人也。道本至公，惡得而參之以私？治本至順，惡得而與之以
translation_en: …know how to take the Empire as one's measure. To take the Empire as one's measure is to take the mind of the Empire as one's mind; to take the mind of the Empire as one's mind is to take the mind of Heaven as one's mind; to take the mind of Heaven as one's mind is to be impartial and not self-serving. Delight and anger are the delight and anger of a single person, not the delight and anger of the people of the Empire; they are private. Likes and dislikes are the likes and dislikes of the people of the Empire, not the likes and dislikes of a single person; they are public. While I do not wish to indulge to the utmost the passions that I am in a position to unleash, how could I fail to follow the shared sentiments of the Empire? While I do not wish to presume upon the power that I am in a position to wield, how could I fail to accord with the great tendencies of the Empire? While I do not wish to open up avenues by which my inclinations are easily pandered to, how could I fail to grasp the great pivot of the Empire? The good I make manifest, and the meritorious I encourage; yet that by which I manifest and encourage them is devoid of personal preconception—it is liking them with the likes of the Empire. It is not that I rejoice because they have rendered private service to me; even if there were an old grievance against them, I would reward them. The evil I abominate, and the guilty I chastise; yet that by which I abominate and chastise them is devoid of personal preconception—it is disliking them with the dislikes of the Empire. It is not that I am angry because they harbor private resentment against me; even if they had some minor merit, I would punish them. The fields of Wen, Yuan, and Yangfan might be bestowed, yet a tunneled passage to the grave could not be granted; towns might be given in abundance, yet the ceremonial cap-tassels could not be requested; those who held the bridle and followed in attendance could not be privately awarded towns; those who startled the horses in the dust of the imperial retinue or stole the jade ring from the ancestral temple might deserve execution, yet the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement could not go beyond the statutory penalty. The rewards and punishments of a ruler of men are not stubbornly bent to please the people of the Empire like this; rather, the Way is fundamentally utmost impartiality—how could one adulterate it with selfishness? Governance is fundamentally utmost compliance with what is natural—how could one intrude upon it with…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
已吾不能使天下不賞而勸不怒而畏而恃吾
所以使之勸使之畏者皆得其平有以大當天
下之心焉爾此其方寸之內豁然混闢洞然昭
曠天地不足爲囊括日月不足爲照臨豈與夫
用智自私較恩怨於一介之微者同日語哉故
當其時殺之者不怨利之者不庸舉四海之內
含生之倫受氣之屬無不遵路遵道畏威懷德
共惟皇極之歸治與協風翔德與顥氣游九苞
儀庭庶草蕃廡人主凝旒端冕垂拱而舉萬年
===
之觴而天下晏然無事矣吾故曰人主之行法
以天有以通天下之志而善天下之治者此也
反是私意隔閡以之爲一家一國且不可況天
下乎蓋嘗稽古而知堯舜至公之心矣窮奇饕
餮之徒之不肖也禹益夷垂諸人之賢也堯豈
有不知哉而必以付之舜舜亦豈不能亟命而
遄罰之哉而必俟之欽哉惟恤之後詢岳咨牧
之餘其罰之也如畏其命之也如疑凜凜然唯
恐吾之好惡參之以先入之見而失其平也是
punctuated:
已？吾不能使天下不賞而勸、不怒而畏，而恃吾所以使之勸、使之畏者，皆得其平，有以大當天下之心焉爾。此其方寸之內，豁然混闢，洞然昭曠，天地不足爲囊括，日月不足爲照臨，豈與夫用智自私、較恩怨於一介之微者同日語哉！故當其時，殺之者不怨，利之者不庸。舉四海之內，含生之倫、受氣之屬，無不遵路遵道，畏威懷德，共惟皇極之歸。治與協風翔，德與顥氣游，九苞儀庭，庶草蕃廡，人主凝旒端冕，垂拱而舉萬年之觴，而天下晏然無事矣。吾故曰：人主之行法以天，有以通天下之志而善天下之治者，此也。反是，私意隔閡，以之爲一家、一國且不可，況天下乎？

蓋嘗稽古而知堯、舜至公之心矣。窮奇、饕餮之徒之不肖也，禹、益、夷、垂諸人之賢也，堯豈有不知哉？而必以付之舜。舜亦豈不能亟命而遄罰之哉？而必俟之欽哉惟恤之後、詢岳咨牧之餘。其罰之也如畏，其命之也如疑，凜凜然唯恐吾之好惡參之以先入之見而失其平也。是
translation_en:
… oneself? I cannot cause the world to be encouraged without rewards or to stand in awe without anger; rather, I rely on the fact that the means by which I encourage them and make them stand in awe all attain fairness, and thus greatly satisfy the minds of the world. Within such a ruler's heart, all is vast and open, clear and luminous—Heaven and Earth are not enough to encompass his capacity, nor the sun and moon enough to match his illumination. How could he be spoken of in the same breath as those who use cleverness for selfish ends and calculate favors and grudges over the slightest trifles! Therefore, in such times, those who are put to death do not feel resentment, and those who are benefited do not take it as personal favor. Throughout the Four Seas, all living beings and creatures endowed with vital breath follow the proper road and the true Way, standing in awe of majesty and cherishing virtue, together turning in allegiance to the Supreme Standard. Order soars with the harmonious winds, virtue roams with the luminous ether, the nine-hued phoenix displays its grace in the courtyard, and the myriad plants flourish in abundance. The ruler, with steady pendant-beads and upright ceremonial cap, lets his robes hang down with folded hands and raises the goblet of ten thousand years, while the empire is tranquil and free of trouble. Thus I say: When the ruler enforces the law in accordance with Heaven, having the means to unite the wills of the world and perfect the governance of the world, this is what it means. Conversely, if selfish intentions create barriers, one could not even govern a single family or a single state by such means, let alone the empire!

Indeed, I have examined antiquity and come to know the supremely impartial minds of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜. That the likes of Qiongqi 窮奇 and Taotie 饕餮 were unworthy, and that men such as Yu 禹, Yi 益, Yi 夷 (Boyi 伯夷), and Chui 垂 were worthy—how could Yao not have known this? Yet he insisted on entrusting the matter to Shun. And how could Shun have been unable to promptly appoint the worthy and swiftly punish the wicked? Yet he insisted on waiting until after he had enjoined reverence and compassion in punishments, and after he had consulted the Four Peaks and taken counsel with the Twelve Pastors. When he punished, it was as though he were fearful; when he appointed, it was as though he were hesitant—trembling with caution, lest his own likes and dislikes be mixed with preconceived notions and thereby lose their fairness. This…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
堯舜之心也能以天下爲度者堯舜也而宋之
儒者猶有言曰堯不從皐陶之殺人而聽四岳
之用鯀也以爲是聖人之好賞而惡刑也亦不
獨宋人言之也陽居大夏以生育長養爲事陰
居大冬而積於空虛不用之處是天之貴德而
不貴刑也漢董生亦嘗言之矣豈治天下者固
不可使私蔽公而尤不可使刑勝德耶之二言
者是或一道也人主所以奉天而弘其度於天
下者此也不然信賞必罰申韓之刻核無以異
===
於聖人矣敢以是而足胡氏未發之意謹論
表
擬宋以范祖禹爲右諫議大夫兼侍講謝
表〔元祐四年〕
鄭偉
同考試官教諭黃批場中作者不靡則俗獨
是作體嚴詞整頌而能規可以觀忠藎之素豫矣
錄之
考試官教諭楊批事核語麗忠悃藹然
punctuated:
堯、舜之心也，能以天下爲度者，堯、舜也。而宋之儒者猶有言曰：「堯不從皐陶之殺人，而聽四岳之用鯀也，以爲是聖人之好賞而惡刑也。」亦不獨宋人言之也。「陽居大夏，以生育長養爲事；陰居大冬，而積於空虛不用之處。是天之貴德而不貴刑也。」漢董生亦嘗言之矣。豈治天下者，固不可使私蔽公，而尤不可使刑勝德耶？之二言者，是或一道也，人主所以奉天而弘其度於天下者此也。不然，信賞必罰，申、韓之刻核，無以異於聖人矣。敢以是而足胡氏未發之意。謹論。

表
擬宋以范祖禹爲右諫議大夫兼侍講謝表〔元祐四年〕
鄭偉
同考試官教諭黃批：場中作者，不靡則俗。獨是作體嚴詞整，頌而能規，可以觀忠藎之素豫矣，錄之。
考試官教諭楊批：事核語麗，忠悃藹然。
translation_en:
…the mind of Yao and Shun; those who could take the whole world as their measure were Yao and Shun. Yet a Confucian scholar of the Song dynasty still remarked: "That Yao did not follow Gao Yao in putting men to death, yet heeded the Four Peaks in employing Gun, shows that the sage delights in rewarding and abhors punishing." Nor was it only a man of the Song who said this. "Yang resides in high summer and makes giving birth, nurturing, and fostering growth its business; yin resides in deep winter and accumulates in empty, unused places. This shows that Heaven values virtue and does not value punishment." Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] of the Han also once said this. Could it be that in governing the world, while one certainly must not let private partiality obscure impartiality, one must even more not let punishment prevail over virtue? These two sayings perhaps express a valid principle; it is by this that a ruler obeys Heaven and enlarges his measure over the whole world. Otherwise, in making rewards certain and punishments inevitable, the harsh severity of Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非 would not differ from the sages! I venture with this to fill out the meaning that Mr. Hu [Hu Anguo 胡安國 / Hu Yin 胡寅] left unexpressed. I respectfully submit this discourse.

Memorial
Imitating a Memorial of Thanks from the Song Dynasty on Appointing Fan Zuyu 范祖禹 as Right Policy Critic and Concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting [4th year of Yuanyou (1089)]
Zheng Wei 鄭偉
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang: Among writers in the examination compound, if they are not florid, they are vulgar. This piece alone is strict in form and orderly in diction; it praises while being able to admonish. From it one can observe a long-standing preparedness in loyal devotion. Record it.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yang: The facts are precise and the language is graceful; sincere loyalty shines forth.

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭朱批〔駢贍典雅〕
元祐四年某月某日具官臣范祖禹伏蒙
聖恩以臣爲右諫議大夫兼侍講謹奉
表稱
謝者伏以
螭頭風動光依
黼扆之居
鳳翥雲開榮並
瀛洲之選
===
禮特隆於晉接
道欣遇於泰交
寵命倂臨微衷實惴臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊
以人君日有萬幾從諫則聖帝王道存六
籍兼聽乃明遐想風牧之時載稽明良之
盛合宮衢室光千載之洪謨詢岳闢門垂
百王之懿範惟廣延乎弼直爰疇咨乎臣
鄰禹拜昌言鐘鼓鐸鞀並設說求古訓鹽
梅麴糵交脩勿以憸人其惟吉士漢用大
punctuated:
考試官敎諭朱批〔駢贍典雅。〕

元祐四年某月某日，具官臣范祖禹伏蒙聖恩，以臣爲右諫議大夫兼侍講，謹奉表稱謝者。伏以螭頭風動，光依黼扆之居；鳳翥雲開，榮並瀛洲之選。禮特隆於晉接，道欣遇於泰交。寵命倂臨，微衷實惴。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以人君日有萬幾，從諫則聖；帝王道存六籍，兼聽乃明。遐想風牧之時，載稽明良之盛。合宮衢室，光千載之洪謨；詢岳闢門，垂百王之懿範。惟廣延乎弼直，爰疇咨乎臣鄰。禹拜昌言，鐘鼓鐸鞀並設；說求古訓，鹽梅麴糵交脩。勿以憸人，其惟吉士。漢用大
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zhu's comment: 〔Richly parallel and classically elegant.〕

On a certain day of a certain month in the fourth year of the Yuanyou era (1089), I, your subject Fan Zuyu 范祖禹, holding my official titles, having humbly received Imperial Grace appointing me Policy Critic-Adviser of the Right and concurrently侍講 Expositor-in-Waiting, respectfully present this memorial to express my gratitude.

Humbly I reflect: as the breeze stirs by the dragon-carved balustrade, I bask in the radiance near the dwelling of the axe-embroidered screen; as the phoenixes soar and the clouds part, my honor equals the selection for Mount Yingzhou. Courtesy is specially lavished through repeated audiences [as in the Jin hexagram], and the Way joyfully meets a time of harmonious communion [as in the Tai hexagram]. As these favored commands descend together, my humble heart is truly filled with trepidation. Truly in awe and truly in fear, I bow my head to the ground again and again.

I humbly consider that a ruler of men attends to ten thousand affairs every day, and becomes sage by following remonstrance; the Way of emperors and kings is preserved in the Six Classics, and only by listening to all sides does one attain clarity. Looking far back to the age of Feng Hou 風后 and Li Mu 力牧, and examining again the flourishing era of enlightened rulers and worthy ministers: the 合宮 Hegong and 衢室 Qushi halls shed luster upon the grand counsels of a thousand years; consulting the Four Peaks and throwing open the four gates handed down a fine model for a hundred kings. Only by widely inviting upright assistants did they inquire of their ministerial associates. Yu 禹 bowed before splendid words, setting out bells, drums, clappers, and hand-drums side by side; Fu Yue 傅說 sought ancient teachings, cultivating himself and his lord like salt and plum, or leaven and malt. Do not employ flatterers, but only good men! The Han dynasty employed Grand…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫兼諫諍唐以學士職論思止輦受言誼
辟每勤於聽納橫經問道叔世尤切于箴
摩蓋學必講然後明而過以聞廼能改如
陽城有道猶或貽諍臣之譏必陸贄愛君
始不負平生之學洪惟
昭代尤愼任人謂諫院
經筵均屬根本之地故講官言責並稱侍從
之臣班列
北扉直隨
===
東閣事關
廊廟玉簡起而嚴霜飛語傍
絲綸
金鑾開而
春陽藹程功積事雖無尺寸可書端本澄源則
與尋常有間是宜人傑乃稱
國華玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
睿德日新
punctuated: 夫兼諫諍，唐以學士職論思。止輦受言，誼辟每勤於聽納；橫經問道，叔世尤切于箴摩。蓋學必講然後明，而過以聞廼能改。如陽城有道，猶或貽諍臣之譏；必陸贄愛君，始不負平生之學。洪惟昭代，尤愼任人。謂諫院、經筵，均屬根本之地；故講官、言責，並稱侍從之臣。班列北扉，直隨東閣。事關廊廟，玉簡起而嚴霜飛；語傍絲綸，金鑾開而春陽藹。程功積事，雖無尺寸可書；端本澄源，則與尋常有間。是宜人傑，乃稱國華。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇睿德日新，
translation_en:
… Grand Masters to concurrently serve as remonstrators, while the Tang assigned Scholars the duty of deliberation and counsel. Halting the imperial carriage to receive advice, righteous sovereigns were ever diligent in listening and accepting; spreading out the classics to inquire into the Way, even in eras of decline it was especially urgent to offer admonition and moral polishing. For learning becomes clear only after it is expounded, and faults can be corrected only after they are heard. Even someone as principled as Yang Cheng 陽城 still incurred criticism through Han Yu's "On Censors"; only with a love for one's sovereign like that of Lu Zhi 陸贄 can one truly live up to a lifetime of learning.

Reflecting broadly upon our Illustrious Dynasty, it is especially cautious in appointing men. Holding that the Bureau of Policy Criticism and the Classics Colloquium are both fundamental institutions, Lecturers and Censors with Speaking Responsibility are alike designated as Court Attendants. Their ranks are arrayed at the Northern Gate, and their shifts follow into the Eastern Hall. When matters concern the imperial court, jade tablets are raised and stern frost flies; when words accompany the silken imperial decrees, the Golden Bell Hall opens and spring sunshine beams warmly. In measuring achievements and accumulating deeds, though they have not an inch or foot of tangible service to record, in rectifying the root and purifying the source, their role is far set apart from the ordinary. Thus it is fitting that only outstanding heroes can match being the glory of the state.

This is indeed because I humbly encounter Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇], whose sagely virtue is daily renewed, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
英資天啓屬
旋乾轉坤之運正
親賢論道之時
動準成規舉經明行脩之士
志稽彞典
詔直言極諫之官法始罷新人惟求舊巋然大
老首歸圖任之初蕞爾小才亦濫
甄收之及俾從柱後獨立
禁中玉筍仍綴乎初銜寶珥載承乎
===
新渥臣草茅微賤章句荒疎弓必為箕蚤服家
庭之訓田不納履久謝姻黨之容固陋之
身以榮為懼要華之選欲報彌難念當
訪落之元亦有勸學之疏雖拳拳而□己知
錄錄以何庸豈謂兼官猥加一介
渙汗莫收于
成命傴僂徒切於下情敢不益竭駑資仰承
鴻造立身惟名節自許進講非王道不陳苟有
裨于吾
