punctuated: 英資天啓，屬旋乾轉坤之運，正親賢論道之時；動準成規，舉經明行脩之士；志稽彞典，詔直言極諫之官。法始罷新，人惟求舊。巋然大老，首歸圖任之初；蕞爾小才，亦濫甄收之及。俾從柱後，獨立禁中；玉筍仍綴乎初銜，寶珥載承乎新渥。臣草茅微賤，章句荒疎。弓必為箕，蚤服家庭之訓；田不納履，久謝姻黨之容。固陋之身，以榮為懼；要華之選，欲報彌難。念當訪落之元，亦有勸學之疏；雖拳拳而□己，知錄錄以何庸！豈謂兼官，猥加一介。渙汗莫收于成命，傴僂徒切於下情。敢不益竭駑資，仰承鴻造！立身惟名節自許，進講非王道不陳。苟有裨于吾…
translation_en:
…and possesses heroic gifts opened by Heaven. At this juncture of revolving Heaven and turning Earth, it is precisely the time to draw close to the worthy and discuss the Way. In every action conforming to established rules, You promote scholars who understand the Classics and cultivate their conduct; with a mind examining the constant canons, You summon by edict officials who speak frankly and remonstrate to the utmost. Having begun by abolishing the new laws, in seeking men You look only to the old. Towering elder statesmen are the first to return at the outset of Your planning and appointments; even a tiny talent such as myself is unworthily reached by Your selective gathering. You allow me to follow behind the pillars and stand alone within the Forbidden Palace; in the jade-shoot ranks I still retain my initial title, and with jeweled ear-ornaments I once again receive Your new favor.

Your servant is lowly and humble from the thatched cottages, rustic and unpolished in textual learning. Teaching that the bow-maker's son must learn to weave willow baskets, I early submitted to my family's instruction; not adjusting my shoes in a melon patch, I long ago declined the indulgence of relatives and partisans. With my stubborn and vulgar person, I take honor as a cause for fear; chosen for so vital and illustrious a post, I find it ever harder to repay. Recalling the beginning of Your consultations upon ascending the throne, I too submitted a memorial encouraging imperial study; though earnest and [?] myself, I knew how mediocre and of what little use I was! How could I expect that concurrent offices would be undeservedly bestowed upon a mere individual? Since the sweeping perspiration of an established command cannot be recalled, in my stooped humility I feel all the more keenly in my lowly sentiments. How dare I not further exhaust my dull capacities to look up and receive Your vast creation! In establishing myself, I pledge myself solely to reputation and integrity; in advancing to lecture, I shall set forth nothing that is not the Kingly Way. If only it may be of some benefit to my…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君自甘焚草誓欲酬於國士竊慕獻芹伏願
惟木從繩
若金作礪
遜志典學由六經而會帝王之精
純心任賢達四聰以廣忠直之益
驗天命民情去留之際常如日之方中
察君子小人消長之機惟在心之不息
善繼善述調
玉燭於五辰
===
不愆不忘撫
瑤圖於千禩臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
punctuated:
君，自甘焚草；誓欲酬於國士，竊慕獻芹。伏願惟木從繩，若金作礪。遜志典學，由六經而會帝王之精；純心任賢，達四聰以廣忠直之益。驗天命民情去留之際，常如日之方中；察君子小人消長之機，惟在心之不息。善繼善述，調玉燭於五辰；不愆不忘，撫瑤圖於千禩。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場

策
translation_en:
… Lord, I would gladly burn the draft of my memorial; vowing to repay Your Majesty's treatment of me as a scholar of the state, I privately aspire to offer my humble gift, like the peasant who presented wild celery. I humbly pray that Your Majesty will be like wood that follows the marking-line, and like metal put to the whetstone: with a humble mind devoting yourself to constant study, grasping the essence of the ancient emperors and kings through the Six Classics; with a pure heart employing the worthy, opening your ears to the four quarters so as to broaden the benefit of loyal and upright counsel; examining the juncture at which the Mandate of Heaven and the sentiments of the people stay or depart, keeping ever like the sun at high noon; discerning the subtle tendencies by which gentlemen and petty men wax or wane, which rests solely on the unceasing vigilance of the mind. Excelling in carrying forward the work of your predecessors and in continuing their intentions, may You harmonize the Jade Candle of the seasons through the five phases of time; neither erring nor forgetting, may You govern the precious realm for a thousand generations. Your servant is overcome with the utmost emotion and trepidation as he gazes up toward Heaven and looks up to Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session

Policy Essays

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第一問
馮名望
同考試官教諭蔣批饗
帝崇儒典禮最重此作考古覈今敷對詳盡末歸之身心尤有關鍵真
足以楊厲
昭代制作之隆宜錄以式
考試官教諭楊批揄揚
盛典無出此篇矣取之
考試官教諭朱批規
===
頌得體
人君其天命之主乎必心合乎天而後可
以事天人君其道統之宗乎必身體乎道
而後可以崇道蓋道原於天故事天者人
君之職天不可見求諸心以若之則天心
可監而滋至之休迓矣治本乎道故崇道
者人君之務道具於聖求諸身以體之則
聖學可明而日新之德成矣二者帝王所
以立人極而致盛治之大端也由今而遡
punctuated:
第一問
馮名望
同考試官教諭蔣批：饗帝崇儒，典禮最重。此作考古覈今，敷對詳盡，末歸之身心，尤有關鍵。真足以楊厲昭代制作之隆，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭楊批：揄揚盛典，無出此篇矣，取之。
考試官教諭朱批：規頌得體。

人君其天命之主乎！必心合乎天，而後可以事天。人君其道統之宗乎！必身體乎道，而後可以崇道。蓋道原於天，故事天者人君之職；天不可見，求諸心以若之，則天心可監，而滋至之休迓矣。治本乎道，故崇道者人君之務；道具於聖，求諸身以體之，則聖學可明，而日新之德成矣。二者，帝王所以立人極而致盛治之大端也。由今而遡
translation_en:
First Question
Feng Mingwang 馮名望

Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: "Sacrificing to the Supreme Lord and honoring the Confucians are the most weighty of state rituals. This composition examines antiquity and verifies the present, presenting a detailed and thorough response; at the end, it brings the matter back to the mind and body, which is especially crucial. It is truly sufficient to extol and celebrate the splendor of the institutions established by our illustrious dynasty, and ought to be recorded as a model."
Examiner and Instructor Yang 楊 comments: "In extolling the grand canon of rituals, nothing surpasses this essay. Accepted."
Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: "Both its admonition and its praise hit the proper mark."

Is the ruler of men not the master of the Mandate of Heaven? Only when his mind is in harmony with Heaven can he serve Heaven. Is the ruler of men not the patriarch of the transmission of the Way? Only when he embodies the Way in his own person can he honor the Way. For the Way originates in Heaven, and therefore serving Heaven is the duty of the ruler of men; Heaven cannot be seen, yet if one seeks it in one's own mind so as to conform to it, the mind of Heaven can be perceived and ever-increasing blessings will be welcomed. Good governance is rooted in the Way, and therefore honoring the Way is the task of the ruler of men; the Way is complete in the sages, yet if one seeks it in one's own person so as to embody it, the learning of the sages can be illuminated and daily-renewed virtue will be achieved. These two are the grand principles whereby emperors and kings establish the ultimate standard for humankind and bring about flourishing governance. Tracing back from the present…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之唐虞其理可知也自漢而下昭事之禮
旣瀆亂而不經表章之功又彌文之徒飾
曠儀令典若有所待此有志之士所以願
舉
明主於三代之隆者也請遂言之郊祀何昉乎
記曰因名山升中于天因吉土饗帝于郊
蓋人主受命于天猶人受命于祖人子不
可一日不見父母故君不可一歲不祭天
郊之祭也大報本反始也故以其祖配焉
===
四代之郊見於祭法禋祀燔柴舜實先之
其重可知矣其制則掃地而祭器用陶匏
牲用犢之尚其質王被衮戴冕龍章而設
日月之象其文八變而黃鍾大呂以終之
盡其變然所以如此者豈徒飾於外哉必
有爲之本矣秦漢以來代有其制而其鑿
者漢以黑帝而增北畤唐罷感生而復祭
太微宋又兼五方帝而祀之皆謬妄不經
之甚攷而論之漢文天資謙讓祠官致敬
punctuated:
之唐、虞，其理可知也。自漢而下，昭事之禮旣瀆亂而不經，表章之功又彌文之徒飾，曠儀令典，若有所待。此有志之士所以願舉明主於三代之隆者也。

請遂言之。郊祀何昉乎？《記》曰：「因名山升中于天，因吉土饗帝于郊。」蓋人主受命于天，猶人受命于祖。人子不可一日不見父母，故君不可一歲不祭天。郊之祭也，大報本反始也，故以其祖配焉。四代之郊見於《祭法》，禋祀燔柴，舜實先之，其重可知矣。其制則掃地而祭，器用陶匏，牲用犢之尚其質；王被衮戴冕，龍章而設日月之象，其文；八變而黃鍾、大呂以終之，盡其變。然所以如此者，豈徒飾於外哉？必有爲之本矣。秦、漢以來，代有其制。而其鑿者：漢以黑帝而增北畤，唐罷感生而復祭太微，宋又兼五方帝而祀之，皆謬妄不經之甚。攷而論之，漢文天資謙讓，祠官致敬，
translation_en:
… back to the eras of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], this principle can be known. From the Han dynasty downward, the rites of reverently serving [Heaven] became profane, disordered, and uncanonical, while the work of honoring and promoting [the Way] became mere outward ornament of elaborate文 [formality]; it was as if the neglected ceremonies and fine canons were awaiting someone to restore them. This is why men of high aspiration wish to raise our enlightened Sovereign to the flourishing height of the Three Dynasties.

Allow me to speak of this in detail. Where did the suburban sacrifice originate? The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "By means of famous mountains, they reported the attainment of the grand mean to Heaven; by means of auspicious ground, they feasted the Supreme Lord in the suburbs." Indeed, a ruler receives his mandate from Heaven just as a person receives life from his ancestors. A filial son cannot go a single day without seeing his parents, and so a ruler cannot go a single year without sacrificing to Heaven. The suburban sacrifice is the great requital of the root and return to the beginning; therefore, one's ancestor is associated in the sacrifice. The suburban sacrifices of the Four Dynasties appear in the "Law of Sacrifices" (Jifa), and the pure sacrifice with burnt offerings of wood was in fact initiated by Shun—from which its importance can be known. As for its institution: sweeping the ground to sacrifice, using vessels of earthenware and bottle-gourds, and using a calf for the victim, esteemed simplicity; the king wearing the ceremonial robe and cap with dragon emblems and displaying the images of sun and moon, embodied cultural pattern; and the eight changes of music concluding with the Huangzhong and Dalü pitch-pipes, exhausted musical transformation. Yet why were things done in this manner? Was it merely external ornament? There was surely something that served as its root. Since the Qin and Han, every dynasty has had its own institutions. Yet among their forced fabrications: the Han added the Northern Altar on account of the Black Emperor; the Tang abolished the sacrifice to the Generative Emperor only to resume sacrificing to the Taiwei enclosure; and the Song additionally combined the Emperors of the Five Directions and sacrificed to them—all of which were the height of absurdity and uncanonical error. If we examine and discuss them, Emperor Wen of Han was by nature modest and yielding, and when his sacrificial officials offered reverence …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毋有所祈猶有敬天之遺意嗣後而角獸
赤雞竝侈歌頌祇增矯誣一年四祭疑於
瀆三歲一郊疑於慢而溢恩濫賞有司困
不能供則其失可勝道哉蓋上無奉先思
孝之君下無據經守禮之臣欲其格天而
克享也胡可得哉視學何昉乎記曰三王
四代惟其師人君受天命而爲之主以師
表萬民也民之向背從違君實司之祀三
老五更於太學冕而總干所以敎諸侯之
弟也四代之學至周人備鎬京辟雍無思
不服而化民成俗矣其始也大昕鼓徵以
警眾也皮弁祭菜示敬道也簡不率敎者
屏之寄棘以示懲也所以如此者亦豈徒
具其儀哉必有爲之要矣秦漢而下代舉
其儀而其尤著者漢明帝臨雍拜老唐太
宗大召名儒宋仁宗增脩學舍數御臨幸
皆於鋪張顯設之具詳焉要而言之辟陋
之邦擾攘之際其視學校若敝屣斷梗而
punctuated:
毋有所祈，猶有敬天之遺意。嗣後而角獸、赤雞，竝侈歌頌，祇增矯誣。一年四祭，疑於瀆；三歲一郊，疑於慢。而溢恩濫賞，有司困不能供，則其失可勝道哉？蓋上無奉先思孝之君，下無據經守禮之臣，欲其格天而克享也，胡可得哉？

視學何昉乎？《記》曰：「三王四代惟其師。」人君受天命而爲之主，以師表萬民也，民之向背從違，君實司之。祀三老五更於太學，冕而總干，所以敎諸侯之弟也。四代之學，至周人備。鎬京辟雍，「無思不服」，而化民成俗矣。其始也，大昕鼓徵，以警眾也；皮弁祭菜，示敬道也；簡不率敎者，屏之寄棘，以示懲也。所以如此者，亦豈徒具其儀哉？必有爲之要矣。秦漢而下，代舉其儀，而其尤著者：漢明帝臨雍拜老，唐太宗大召名儒，宋仁宗增脩學舍，數御臨幸，皆於鋪張顯設之具詳焉。要而言之，辟陋之邦，擾攘之際，其視學校若敝屣斷梗，而
translation_en:
…without praying for personal blessings, which still preserved a remnant of the ancient reverence for Heaven. Thereafter, unicorns and red wildfowl were celebrated together in extravagant songs and eulogies, which only increased fabrication and deceit. Sacrificing four times in a single year borders on profanation; performing the suburban sacrifice once in three years borders on negligence. Moreover, with excessive favors and lavish rewards that the authorities are too exhausted to supply, how could all the failings possibly be recounted? Indeed, when above there is no ruler who honors his ancestors and meditates on filial piety, and below there are no ministers who stand upon the Classics and uphold the rites, how could one possibly hope to reach Heaven and have the sacrifices accepted?

When did the imperial inspection of the schools begin? The Record of Rites says: "The Three Kings and the Four Dynasties took only the worthy as their teachers." The ruler receives the Mandate of Heaven and becomes its lord in order to serve as a teacher and model for the myriad people; the allegiance or estrangement, compliance or defiance of the people are truly in the ruler's charge. Sacrificing to the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men (Sanlao Wugeng) in the Directorate of Education (Taixue), wearing the ceremonial cap and holding the shield, was the means to teach fraternal respect to the feudal lords. The schools of the Four Dynasties reached their complete form under the Zhou. With the Circular Moat Hall (Piyong) in the capital of Hao, "there was none who thought and did not submit," and thus the people were transformed and customs perfected. At the outset of the ceremony, drums were beaten at early dawn to summon and rouse the multitude; wearing the deerskin cap, offerings of water plants were made to show reverence for the Way; and those who did not follow instruction were singled out and banished to the frontier regions of Jiyi and Jiji to demonstrate punishment. Why was all this done? Was it merely to furnish the outward ceremonies? There must certainly have been an essential principle behind it. From the Qin and Han dynasties downward, each age performed these ceremonies, and among the most notable instances were Emperor Ming of Han visiting the Circular Moat Hall and bowing to the elders, Emperor Taizong of Tang summoning renowned Confucian scholars on a grand scale, and Emperor Renzong of Song expanding and repairing the school buildings and repeatedly gracing them with his imperial presence—all of whom were meticulous in the trappings of ostentation and grand display. To sum it up: in remote and rustic states or during times of turmoil, schools were regarded like worn-out sandals or broken twigs; yet…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於天理民彝自反有不能已者及治定功
成乃欲藉此以為粉飾太平之具則其意
已失矣况圜橋觀聽內德已慚沙門作俑
名敎首禍其如學何蓋上所先者多欲而
施仁義之君下所司者權□□財車馬之
臣欲其興道致治也又安可得哉世降風
漓愈趨愈下不有
卓然英睿者出孰能舉而正之我
聖祖卽位卽舉
===
郊壇之祭觀其
語起居注熊鼎曰此事雖不盡合古制然一
念事天之誠不敢忘一哉
皇心所以為
敬天之本者豫矣又于
紀元之始卽脩辟雍太學之規
遣使詣曲阜致祭而曰仲尼之道與天地並
今為天下主期明敎化以行先王之道至哉
皇言所以繼往聖之統者全矣請得而揚之蓋
punctuated: 於天理民彝，自反有不能已者；及治定功成，乃欲藉此以為粉飾太平之具，則其意已失矣。况圜橋觀聽，內德已慚；沙門作俑，名敎首禍，其如學何？蓋上所先者，多欲而施仁義之君；下所司者，權□□財車馬之臣。欲其興道致治也，又安可得哉？世降風漓，愈趨愈下，不有卓然英睿者出，孰能舉而正之？我聖祖卽位，卽舉郊壇之祭，觀其語起居注熊鼎曰：「此事雖不盡合古制，然一念事天之誠，不敢忘。」一哉皇心！所以為敬天之本者豫矣。又于紀元之始，卽脩辟雍太學之規，遣使詣曲阜致祭，而曰：「仲尼之道，與天地並。今為天下主，期明敎化以行先王之道。」至哉皇言！所以繼往聖之統者全矣。請得而揚之。蓋
translation_en:
… yet regarding heavenly principle and the moral norms of the people, upon self-reflection they represent something that cannot be ceased; when order is established and merit achieved, if one then wishes to use these [schools] merely as tools to gloss over an era of peace, the true meaning has already been lost. How much more so when, despite crowds gathering around the circular moat of the Imperial Academy to watch and listen, the ruler's inner virtue was already cause for shame; and by initiating the patronage of Buddhist monks, he brought the first calamity upon Confucian moral teaching—what could the schools do about that? For at the top, what came first were rulers full of desires who merely put on a display of benevolence and righteousness; below, those in charge were ministers concerned with power, scheming [?], wealth, and carriages and horses. Even if one wished for them to promote the Way and bring about good governance, how could that possibly be attained? As the ages declined and customs grew thin, things sank ever lower; were there not an outstandingly brilliant and wise ruler to emerge, who could take them up and rectify them?

When our Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu] ascended the throne, he immediately performed the sacrifices at the Suburban Altar. Observe what he said to Imperial Diarist Xiong Ding 熊鼎: "Although this matter does not entirely conform to ancient institutions, in my single-minded sincerity in serving Heaven, I dare not be forgetful." How unified was the Imperial mind! That by which he established the foundation for revering Heaven was prepared well in advance. Moreover, at the very beginning of his reign era, he immediately restored the regulations for the Imperial Academy (Biyong Taixue), and dispatched an envoy to Qufu 曲阜 to offer sacrifices, saying: "The Way of Zhongni [Confucius] is coeval with Heaven and Earth. Now that I am the ruler of All Under Heaven, I aim to clarify moral teaching and transformation so as to practice the Way of the Former Kings." How consummate were the Imperial words! That by which he continued the succession of the past sages was complete. Allow me to extol this. For…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖卽位之初正
順天應人之會
省躬之旨深達于天人之際而革前代山川
之號正
宗廟祭祀之規却祥瑞而重農桑因脩省而
諭羣臣無一事不當於天心則不必求之齋
明盛服之時而心已無往非敬矣
聖祖紀元之始適用夏變夷之機
觀心之旨首得乎道統之傳而斥方術焚其
===
===
書
書大學衍義于壁大易有
講契絕學之微言洪範有
訓示皇極之要道無一事而不合於聖人則
不必於視學之時而念已無適非誠矣
精誠謨烈啓佑後人
列聖一心守而勿失二百年來海宇晏清禎瑞
畢至謂非
天心之所昭假乎六經昭垂道德同文謂非
punctuated: 聖祖卽位之初，正順天應人之會，省躬之旨，深達于天人之際。而革前代山川之號，正宗廟祭祀之規，却祥瑞而重農桑，因脩省而諭羣臣，無一事不當於天心，則不必求之齋明盛服之時，而心已無往非敬矣。聖祖紀元之始，適用夏變夷之機，觀心之旨，首得乎道統之傳。而斥方術，焚其書，書《大學衍義》于壁，《大易》有講，契絕學之微言，《洪範》有訓，示皇極之要道，無一事而不合於聖人，則不必於視學之時，而念已無適非誠矣。精誠謨烈，啓佑後人，列聖一心，守而勿失。二百年來，海宇晏清，禎瑞畢至，謂非天心之所昭假乎？《六經》昭垂，道德同文，謂非
translation_en: …At the very beginning of the Sacred Ancestor’s accession to the throne, it was precisely the juncture of complying with Heaven and responding to men; the purport of his self-examination deeply penetrated the nexus between Heaven and humanity. Thus, he abolished the titles conferred on mountains and rivers by previous dynasties, rectified the regulations for ancestral temple sacrifices, rejected auspicious omens while emphasizing agriculture and sericulture, and instructed the assembled officials in light of his self-cultivation and introspection. Not a single matter failed to accord with the mind of Heaven; thus one need not seek it only at times of fasting, purification, and donning ceremonial attire, for his mind was already reverent in every respect. At the very beginning of the Sacred Ancestor’s era, it was just the opportune moment to transform the barbarians through Chinese ways; the purport of his contemplation of the mind first grasped the transmission of the Orthodox Way (daotong). Thus, he rejected occult arts and burned their books, inscribed the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) upon the palace walls, held lectures on the Great Changes (Dayi) that tallied with the subtle words of lost learning, and issued instructions on the Great Plan (Hongfan) that revealed the essential principles of the August Ultimate. Not a single matter failed to conform to the sages; thus one need not wait for the occasion of his ceremonial visit to the Imperial University, for his thoughts were already sincere in every pursuit. His pure sincerity and illustrious plans and achievements enlightened and aided his descendants; the successive emperors, with one mind, guarded them without fail. For two hundred years, the realm has been tranquil and clear, and auspicious signs have all arrived—how could one say this is not the manifestation of Heaven’s favor? The Six Classics shine forth to posterity, moral virtue is unified, and writing is standardized—how could one say this is not…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖學之所講明乎夫五緯曜芒而萬古不晦以
其有樞也百川分派而萬古不息以其有
宗也
皇上
聖哲篤生
英年握紀
至誠之心純一不雜殆與周之成王異世同
符
諒闇旣釋卽
===
命宗伯秩禮司空治途肇祀
南郊嚴對越之禮
駕臨大學
躬釋奠之儀大小臣工薄海内外罔不顒顒
然快覩
聖人之興矣執事又欲外儀章而别有所陳毋
亦忠愛無已之心乎愚也涓滴而增渤澥
之波壘土而加泰山之岏竊甞求之我將
之詩成王之所以祭天也惟天其右之外
punctuated: 聖學之所講明乎？夫五緯曜芒而萬古不晦，以其有樞也；百川分派而萬古不息，以其有宗也。皇上聖哲篤生，英年握紀，至誠之心，純一不雜，殆與周之成王異世同符。諒闇旣釋，卽命宗伯秩禮、司空治途，肇祀南郊，嚴對越之禮；駕臨大學，躬釋奠之儀。大小臣工、薄海内外，罔不顒顒然快覩聖人之興矣。執事又欲外儀章而别有所陳，毋亦忠愛無已之心乎？愚也涓滴而增渤澥之波，壘土而加泰山之岏，竊甞求之：《我將》之詩，成王之所以祭天也，「惟天其右之」外，
translation_en: … elucidated by the sage’s learning? Indeed, the five planets shine with brilliance and never grow dim through ten thousand ages because they have a pivot; the hundred rivers branch into streams and never cease through ten thousand ages because they have a source. His Majesty, born with sage wisdom, took hold of the reins of government in his youthful prime. His mind of utmost sincerity, pure and unmixed, matches like a tally that of King Cheng of Zhou across different eras. Once the period of imperial mourning concluded, he immediately commanded the Minister of Rites to order the ceremonies and the Minister of Works to prepare the roads. He initiated the sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, solemnly performing the rites ofresponding to Heaven above; his imperial carriage visited the Grand Academy, where he personally performed the ceremonies of the libation offering to Confucius. Officials great and small, within and beyond the seas, all looked up with reverent expectation, delighted to witness the rise of a sage. Yet you, Sir, wish to set aside ceremonial regulations and have something else presented—is this not out of a heart of boundless loyalty and devotion? Stupid though I am, like adding a tiny drop to swell the waves of the Bohai Sea or heaping a clod of earth to heighten the peak of Mount Tai, I have ventured to seek it out. The ode "I Bring My Offerings" (Wo jiang) is that whereby King Cheng sacrificed to Heaven. Beyond the words "May Heaven alone accept and favor it," …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不敢加一詞焉其敬天何至也而必曰我
其夙夜畏天之威于時保之夫人君一身
視聽言動無非天者不特
郊壇承祭之時而不聞不覩天命已降監焉必
寅恭朝夕而不敢懈也必顧畏民碞而不
敢康也于匹夫匹婦而常若勝予焉于祁
寒暑雨而常若怨咨焉不求諸在天之天
而求在己之天則天可對而後其敬始純
訪落之詩成王之所以求學也將予就之
===
繼猶判渙其自省何至也而必曰日就月
將學有緝熙于光明夫人君一身內外動
靜無非學者不特
臨幸講說之際而
深宮內庭君德實成就焉必謹於人心道心
之幾而不敢忽也必察于君子小人之際
而不敢輕也一話一言必惟成德之彥若
好若惡考諸惟皇之極不求聖于聖而求
聖于心則聖可學而後其德始進敬旣盡
punctuated: 不敢加一詞焉，其敬天何至也！而必曰：「我其夙夜畏天之威，于時保之。」夫人君一身，視聽言動無非天者。不特郊壇承祭之時，而不聞不覩，天命已降監焉。必寅恭朝夕而不敢懈也，必顧畏民碞而不敢康也，于匹夫匹婦而常若勝予焉，于祁寒暑雨而常若怨咨焉。不求諸在天之天，而求在己之天，則天可對，而後其敬始純。《訪落》之詩，成王之所以求學也。「將予就之，繼猶判渙」，其自省何至也！而必曰：「日就月將，學有緝熙于光明。」夫人君一身，內外動靜無非學者。不特臨幸講說之際，而深宮內庭，君德實成就焉。必謹於人心、道心之幾而不敢忽也，必察于君子、小人之際而不敢輕也，一話一言，必惟成德之彥；若好若惡，考諸惟皇之極。不求聖于聖，而求聖于心，則聖可學，而後其德始進。敬旣盡
translation_en:
…he did not dare add a single word. How utmost was his reverence for Heaven! Yet he still insisted on saying: "May I day and night revere the majesty of Heaven, and thereby preserve what it has bestowed." Now, in the sovereign's own person, his seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting are none other than Heaven itself. It is not only at the moment of performing sacrifices at the suburban altar; even in what is unheard and unseen, the Mandate of Heaven has already descended to inspect him. He must be reverent and respectful morning and evening without daring to be lax; he must look with awe upon the perilousness of the common people without daring to take his ease. Toward ordinary men and women, he always feels as though they might prevail over him; in bitter cold and sultry rain, he always feels as though they are murmuring in resentment. If he does not seek Heaven in the Heaven above, but seeks the Heaven within himself, then he can stand before Heaven, and only then does his reverence become pure.

The ode "Taking Counsel at the Beginning of Rule" (Fangluo) is how King Cheng sought learning. "As I strive to reach it, in continuing I am still scattered and dispersed"—how utmost was his self-examination! Yet it also insisted on saying: "With daily progress and monthly advance, my learning shall have continuous brightness unto illumination." Now, in the sovereign's own person, his inner and outer life, his movement and stillness, are none other than learning itself. It is not only during the occasions when he graces the lecture hall with his presence; within the deep palace and inner court, the ruler's virtue is truly brought to completion. He must be cautious at the subtle inception of the human mind and the mind of the Way without daring to be neglectful; he must discern the boundary between the noble man and the petty man without daring to take it lightly. In every word and utterance, he must rely solely on men of accomplished virtue; in whatever he likes or dislikes, he must test it against the August Supreme Standard. If he does not seek sagehood in the sages, but seeks sagehood within his own mind, then sagehood can be learned, and only then does his virtue advance. Once reverence has been exhausted…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣則以之
尊祖以之
敬宗以之
祈穀以之
報賽皆於此乎行之德旣進矣則以此用人
以此納諫以此行政以此養民皆於此乎
推之我
皇上聰明
天啓
===
仁孝聿至此正周旦所謂自貽哲命之初所其
無逸之日也自茲以往苟禁防稍弛則知
慮或分涵養未純則心志或逸所以乘時
而造就之者不有資於輔養乎啓沃有講
章而微辭奧義或未盡於心得史書有疏
解而嘉言格論或未罄於面陳所以隨事
而充廣之者不有賴於弼直乎今
經筵日
御無輟于寒暑章疏徹
punctuated: 矣，則以之尊祖、以之敬宗、以之祈穀、以之報賽，皆於此乎行之；德旣進矣，則以此用人、以此納諫、以此行政、以此養民，皆於此乎推之。我皇上聰明天啓，仁孝聿至，此正周旦所謂「自貽哲命」之初，「所其無逸」之日也。自茲以往，苟禁防稍弛，則知慮或分；涵養未純，則心志或逸。所以乘時而造就之者，不有資於輔養乎？啓沃有講章，而微辭奧義或未盡於心得；史書有疏解，而嘉言格論或未罄於面陳。所以隨事而充廣之者，不有賴於弼直乎？今經筵日御，無輟于寒暑；章疏徹
translation_en:
… has been exhausted, then by means of it honoring the ancestors, by means of it revering the imperial lineage, by means of it praying for grain, and by means of it offering thanksgivings—all are carried out from this. Once virtue has advanced, then by means of this employing men, by means of this accepting remonstrance, by means of this conducting administration, and by means of this nourishing the people—all are extended from this.

Our Sovereign's intelligence is inspired by Heaven, and His benevolence and filial piety have reached the utmost. This is precisely the beginning of what Zhou Dan [the Duke of Zhou] called "bestowing upon oneself a wise decree," and the day of "making abstention from idleness one's abode." From this time onward, if restraints and precautions are slightly relaxed, then wisdom and deliberation might be divided; if self-cultivation is not yet pure, then the mind and will might stray into idleness. As for that whereby one seizes the timely moment to bring this to completion, does it not depend upon assisting nourishment? For enlightenment and guidance there are lecture texts, yet their subtle words and profound meanings might not be fully exhausted in personal comprehension; for the historical records there are commentaries and explanations, yet their admirable words and standard discourses might not be completely set forth in face-to-face presentation. As for that whereby one expands and broadens this in accordance with affairs, does it not rely upon corrective assistance? Now the Classics Mat is attended daily, without interruption in winter's cold or summer's heat; memorials and reports are thoroughly …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
覽不倦于昕夕眞德秀所謂惟學惟敬惟親
君子旣交盡而無歉卽此可以近法
列祖遠紹虞周而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣書曰
念終始典于學愚也敢以此規詩曰於乎
皇王繼序思不忘愚又敢以此
頌
第二問
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭蔣批聖賢言性隨時立訓其
旨本不異是作發揮明悉非勦說比錄之
===
考試官敎諭楊批醞藉宏深議論明正窺
性學之奧者敬服敬服
考試官敎諭朱批知性盡性學聖功夫也
此作得之
達乎理之原者可與論性矣明乎性之初
者可與語學矣所謂理之原者何無極之
眞天載之神純粹至善者也固性之從出
也所謂性之初者何不雜于質不囿于氣
punctuated:
覽，不倦于昕夕。眞德秀所謂「惟學、惟敬、惟親君子」，旣交盡而無歉。卽此可以近法列祖，遠紹虞、周，而陋漢、唐、宋於不足言矣。《書》曰：「念終始典于學。」愚也敢以此規。《詩》曰：「於乎皇王，繼序思不忘。」愚又敢以此頌。

第二問
車聘臣
同考試官敎諭蔣批：聖賢言性，隨時立訓，其旨本不異。是作發揮明悉，非勦說比，錄之。
考試官敎諭楊批：醞藉宏深，議論明正，窺性學之奧者。敬服，敬服！
考試官敎諭朱批：知性盡性，學聖功夫也，此作得之。

達乎理之原者，可與論性矣；明乎性之初者，可與語學矣。所謂理之原者何？無極之眞、天載之神，純粹至善者也，固性之從出也。所謂性之初者何？不雜于質，不囿于氣，
translation_en:
… inspects them, untiring from morning to evening. What Zhen Dexiu 眞德秀 called "devotion to learning, devotion to reverence, and devotion to closeness with noble men" have all been mutually fulfilled without deficiency. Through this alone, His Majesty can take the Imperial Ancestors as a near model and continue the line of Yu and Zhou from afar, looking down upon Han, Tang, and Song as unworthy of mention. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Be mindful from beginning to end to be constant in learning." In my simplicity, I venture to offer this as admonition. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Oh, august sovereign! Succeeding to the line, we think of you unceasingly." In my simplicity, I also venture to offer this as praise.

Second Policy Question
Che Pingchen 車聘臣
Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Sages and worthies spoke of human nature by establishing teachings suited to their times, yet their underlying purport was originally no different. This essay elucidates the matter clearly and thoroughly; it is not to be compared with plagiarized clichés. Selected for inclusion.
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: Cultivated and profound, its arguments clear and upright—the work of one who has peered into the depths of the learning of human nature. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: Knowing human nature and fully realizing human nature are the effort of learning to become a sage. This essay has grasped it.

With one who has penetrated the source of principle, one may discuss human nature; with one who understands the original state of human nature, one may speak of learning. What is meant by the source of principle? It is the reality of the Ultimateless and the numinous power of Heaven's operation, pure and supremely good; indeed, it is that from which human nature issues. What is meant by the original state of human nature? Unmixed with physical substance and unconstrained by vital force (qi), …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有善而無惡者也乃理之本然也是故性
可以恒言可以善言而不可以清濁厚薄
論也清濁可以言氣厚薄可以言質而不
可以論性之初也嗚呼人性皆善也人性
之初皆相近也而岐而二之是豈知性者
哉君子明乎帝降之原察乎民秉之始則
諸說之紛紛可以折衷之而無惑矣且性
之說奚始乎自伏羲氏之一畫而陰陽之
理著自堯授舜以允執厥中之一言而精
===
一之旨闡雖未甞明言性而性之說已肇
矣及成湯之誥曰上帝降衷于下民若有
恒性衷者中也言乎其弗偏也恒者常也
言乎其弗易也弗偏弗易雖未甞明言善
而善之旨已昭矣嗣後一變爲春秋而詐
力興再變爲戰國而功利熾于是近者習
而遠矣乃不曰吾自背馳之而諉曰我性
則然善者流而惡矣乃不曰吾自戕賊之
而諉曰我性則然孔子憂性學之失眞也
punctuated: 有善而無惡者也，乃理之本然也。是故性可以恒言，可以善言，而不可以清濁厚薄論也。清濁可以言氣，厚薄可以言質，而不可以論性之初也。嗚呼！人性皆善也，人性之初皆相近也，而岐而二之，是豈知性者哉？君子明乎帝降之原，察乎民秉之始，則諸說之紛紛可以折衷之而無惑矣。且性之說奚始乎？自伏羲氏之一畫，而陰陽之理著；自堯授舜以「允執厥中」之一言，而精一之旨闡。雖未甞明言性，而性之說已肇矣。及成湯之誥曰：「上帝降衷于下民，若有恒性。」衷者，中也，言乎其弗偏也；恒者，常也，言乎其弗易也。弗偏弗易，雖未甞明言善，而善之旨已昭矣。嗣後一變爲春秋而詐力興，再變爲戰國而功利熾。于是近者習而遠矣，乃不曰吾自背馳之，而諉曰：「我性則然。」善者流而惡矣，乃不曰吾自戕賊之，而諉曰：「我性則然。」孔子憂性學之失眞也，
translation_en:
… possesses goodness and has no evil; this is the original state of principle. Therefore, human nature may be spoken of as constant, and may be spoken of as good, but it cannot be discussed in terms of clarity and turbidity or thickness and thinness. Clarity and turbidity can be used to speak of vital force (qi), and thickness and thinness can be used to speak of physical constitution (zhi), but they cannot be used to discuss the original state of human nature. Alas! Human nature is in all cases good, and in its original state human nature is in all cases mutually close; to split them into two—how could this be someone who understands human nature? When the gentleman understands the source conferred by the Lord on High and examines the beginning of what the people hold fast to, then the welter of competing doctrines can be weighed and settled without confusion.

Moreover, where did the doctrine of human nature begin? From the single stroke drawn by Fuxi 伏羲, the principle of yin and yang was made manifest; from the single phrase "sincerely hold fast the Mean" with which Yao 堯 handed down the rule to Shun 舜, the import of refinement and unity was elucidated. Although they never explicitly spoke of human nature, the doctrine of human nature had already begun. When it came to the announcement of Cheng Tang 成湯, he said: "The Lord on High conferred the moral center upon the people below; if they follow their constant nature..." "Moral center" (zhong) means equilibrium (zhong), referring to its being unskewed; "constant" (heng) means invariable, referring to its being unchanging. Being unskewed and unchanging—although this never explicitly spoke of goodness, the import of goodness was already clear.

Thereafter, with a first transformation into the Spring and Autumn period, deceit and force arose; with a second transformation into the Warring States period, utilitarianism and profit-seeking blazed forth. Thereupon, those who were close in nature grew distant through habit, yet instead of saying, "I myself have run counter to it," they shifted the blame, saying, "My nature is simply so." Those who were good flowed into evil, yet instead of saying, "I myself have violated and ruined it," they shifted the blame, saying, "My nature is simply so." Confucius 孔子, worried that the learning of human nature was losing its truth, …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而有性相近之說焉近者對遠言之譬之
五方童子習於齊則爲齊語習於楚則爲
楚語甚至重九譯而不能相通然其初呱
呱之聲舉相似也朱子所謂以其初而言
之則皆不甚相遠者是也是性之爲體固
不離乎氣質而亦不囿於氣質之中矣孟
子憂聖道之失而欲閑之也而有性善之
說焉善者對惡言之譬諸眾水之流在江
淮則爲江淮在河漢則爲河漢甚至千支
===
萬派之不一然其就下之勢罔不一也朱
子所謂人之情本但可以爲善而不可以
爲惡者是也是聖賢之爲教言雖若有異
同而意則實無牴牾矣謂孟子之見不出
于孔氏不可也謂孟子非有功于聖門不
可也夫性一理也理一性也上古忘象而
得意故存之而不論聖人識精以達微故
論之而不辯君子貞教以軌物故辯之而
極詳孟子而下羣說競起告子立赤幟以
punctuated: 而有「性相近」之說焉。近者，對遠言之。譬之五方童子，習於齊則爲齊語，習於楚則爲楚語，甚至重九譯而不能相通，然其初呱呱之聲，舉相似也。朱子所謂「以其初而言之，則皆不甚相遠」者是也。是性之爲體，固不離乎氣質，而亦不囿於氣質之中矣。孟子憂聖道之失而欲閑之也，而有「性善」之說焉。善者，對惡言之。譬諸眾水之流，在江淮則爲江淮，在河漢則爲河漢，甚至千支萬派之不一，然其就下之勢，罔不一也。朱子所謂「人之情本但可以爲善，而不可以爲惡」者是也。是聖賢之爲教，言雖若有異同，而意則實無牴牾矣。謂孟子之見不出于孔氏，不可也；謂孟子非有功于聖門，不可也。夫性一理也，理一性也。上古忘象而得意，故存之而不論；聖人識精以達微，故論之而不辯；君子貞教以軌物，故辯之而極詳。孟子而下，羣說競起。告子立赤幟以
translation_en: …and thus set forth the doctrine that "human natures are close to one another." "Close" is spoken of in contrast to "far apart." Compare it to children from the five directions: if accustomed to Qi, they speak the language of Qi; if accustomed to Chu, they speak the language of Chu; and at the extreme, even through ninefold translation they cannot understand one another—yet at the very beginning, the sound of their infant cries is entirely alike. This is what Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] meant when he said, "Speaking of them in their initial state, none are very far apart from one another." Thus the substance of human nature, while certainly not separate from psychophysical endowment, is also not confined within psychophysical endowment. Mencius, worried over the loss of the Way of the Sages and wishing to defend it, set forth the doctrine that "human nature is good." "Good" is spoken of in contrast to "evil." Compare it to the flowing of the multitude of waters: in the Jiang and the Huai they become the Jiang and the Huai; in the Yellow River and the Han they become the Yellow River and the Han; and at the extreme, though divided into a thousand branches and ten thousand tributaries, in their tendency to flow downward they are without exception the same. This is what Master Zhu meant when he said, "Man's feelings are originally such that they can only do good and cannot do evil." Thus in the teachings of the sages and worthies, although their words seem to have differences and similarities, in their meaning there is truly no contradiction. To say that Mencius's view did not derive from Confucius is untenable; to say that Mencius did not perform a meritorious service for the gate of the Sage is untenable. Now, human nature is one with principle, and principle is one with human nature. In high antiquity, people forgot the outward emblems and grasped the inner meaning, so they preserved it without discussing it; the Sage [Confucius] had refined insight that penetrated the subtle, so he discussed it without debating it; the worthy gentleman [Mencius] rectified the teachings to regulate things, so he debated it in the utmost detail. From Mencius onward, a multitude of doctrines arose in competition. Gaozi raised his red banner to…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
角勝天下杞柳湍水之喻起性惡與善惡
混之端矣荀子謂枸木必檃栝而後直鈍
金必礱厲而後利非杞柳之說乎揚子謂
有刀者礱諸有王者錯諸不礱不錯焉攸
用非湍水之說乎此其意非不欲天下同
歸於善與孟氏之書相左右豈知直利卽
性檃厲非矯也刀玉本器礱錯非强也故
東西上下之折情才四端之說辭而闢之
不遺餘力豈好辯哉不得已也自今觀之
===
孟子之言善也窮其本始而究理之原循
其性之自然也諸子之言性也迷其本始
而徇氣之迹舍其性之本然也吁性豈易
言哉宋儒之善言性者莫如程伯子定性
一書其言普物無心者天地之常順事無
情者聖人之常廓然大公物來順應者君
子法天地希聖人之要斯言也真有以窺
孔孟之奧探性命之原矣說者疑其有惡
亦不可不謂性之說似與性善相近之旨
punctuated: 角勝天下，杞柳、湍水之喻，起性惡與善惡混之端矣。荀子謂「枸木必檃栝而後直，鈍金必礱厲而後利」，非杞柳之說乎？揚子謂「有刀者礱諸，有王者錯諸，不礱不錯，焉攸用」，非湍水之說乎？此其意非不欲天下同歸於善，與孟氏之書相左右，豈知直、利卽性，檃、厲非矯也；刀、玉本器，礱、錯非强也。故東西上下之折，情才四端之說，辭而闢之，不遺餘力，豈好辯哉？不得已也。自今觀之，孟子之言善也，窮其本始而究理之原，循其性之自然也；諸子之言性也，迷其本始而徇氣之迹，舍其性之本然也。吁，性豈易言哉！宋儒之善言性者，莫如程伯子《定性》一書。其言「普物無心」者，天地之常；「順事無情」者，聖人之常；「廓然大公，物來順應」者，君子法天地、希聖人之要。斯言也，真有以窺孔、孟之奧，探性命之原矣。說者疑其有「惡亦不可不謂性」之說，似與「性善」、「相近」之旨…
translation_en: …vie for supremacy in the world. His analogies of the杞 willow (qiliu) and the whirling water (tuanshui) gave rise to the beginnings of the doctrines that human nature is evil and that good and evil are intermingled in it. Xunzi 荀子 said, "Crooked wood must be steamed and pressed before it becomes straight; blunt metal must be ground and whetted before it becomes sharp." Is this not the argument of the willow? Yangzi 揚子 [Yang Xiong 揚雄] said, "He who has a blade grinds it; he who has jade [printed 王 for 玉] polishes it. If not ground and not polished, of what use are they?" Is this not the argument of the whirling water? In their intentions, it was not that they did not wish all under Heaven to return alike to goodness, lending support to the book of Master Meng [Mencius]; yet how could they failed to understand that straightness and sharpness are themselves the nature, and pressing and whetting are not a distortion of it; that the blade and the jade are inherently vessels, and grinding and polishing are not a forcing of them? Therefore, with his refutations regarding flowing east or west, up or down, and his explanations of the feelings, capacities, and the four beginnings (siduan), Mencius spoke out to repudiate them, sparing no effort. Was it that he was fond of disputing? He had no choice! Viewed from the present, when Mencius spoke of goodness, he traced it to its ultimate beginning and investigated the source of principle (li), following what is spontaneous in human nature; when the various other masters spoke of human nature, they lost sight of its ultimate beginning and pursued the traces of material force (qi), abandoning the original state of human nature. Alas, how could human nature be easy to speak of! Among the Song-dynasty Confucians who spoke well of human nature, none surpassed Master Cheng the Elder [Cheng Hao 程顥] in his single letter on "Steadying the Nature" (Dingxing shu 定性書). What it calls "extending universally to all things without deliberate mind" is the constancy of Heaven and Earth; "accordance with affairs without personal emotion" is the constancy of the sage; "being vast and utterly impartial, responding harmoniously to things as they come" is the essential way for the noble man to model himself on Heaven and Earth and aspire to the sage. These words truly succeeded in peering into the profound depths of Confucius and Mencius and exploring the source of human nature and Heaven's decree. Yet commentators doubt his statement that "evil also cannot but be called nature," which seems to… [conflict] with the purport of "human nature is good" and "by nature men are nearly alike"…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或戾豈知孔孟之言直探乎天命之體程
子之言示人以澄治之功夫性之體本善
也猶水之體本清也善失而流於惡甚至
於倍蓰無算者謂之非性固不可謂爲性
之本然可乎清失而流於濁甚至於塵滓
莫辨者謂之非水固不可謂爲水之本然
可乎謂越椒爲滅宗者以豺聲也使能如
周處之速改焉何至於滅耶謂叔魚爲賄
亡者以豕喙也使能如戴淵之急反焉何
===
至於亡耶知下愚之不出於天則惡之非
性也明矣知暴棄之皆由於巳則性之貴
乎善反而非有定也又明矣孟子發性善
之旨于仁義充塞之時所以距詖行正人
心者功固不在禹下程子闡性卽理之旨
干理學幾晦之日所以繼往聖開來學者
功亦不在孟子下矣後儒取譬於日借喻
於水豈謾言哉觀日者有自蔀屋之下觀
者皆雲翳也有自山之中而觀者雲與日
punctuated: 或戾。豈知孔、孟之言，直探乎天命之體；程子之言，示人以澄治之功。夫性之體本善也，猶水之體本清也。善失而流於惡，甚至於倍蓰無算者，謂之非性固不可，謂爲性之本然可乎？清失而流於濁，甚至於塵滓莫辨者，謂之非水固不可，謂爲水之本然可乎？謂越椒爲滅宗者，以豺聲也，使能如周處之速改焉，何至於滅耶？謂叔魚爲賄亡者，以豕喙也，使能如戴淵之急反焉，何至於亡耶？知下愚之不出於天，則惡之非性也明矣；知暴棄之皆由於巳，則性之貴乎善反而非有定也又明矣。孟子發「性善」之旨于仁義充塞之時，所以距詖行、正人心者，功固不在禹下；程子闡「性卽理」之旨干理學幾晦之日，所以繼往聖、開來學者，功亦不在孟子下矣。後儒取譬於日、借喻於水，豈謾言哉？觀日者，有自蔀屋之下觀者，皆雲翳也；有自山之中而觀者，雲與日
translation_en: …might be at odds with them. How could they fail to realize that the words of Confucius and Mencius probe directly into the substance of the Mandate of Heaven, whereas the words of Master Cheng show people the effort of clarifying and ordering it? Now, the substance of human nature is originally good, just as the substance of water is originally clear. When goodness is lost and flows into evil, even to the point of diverging two-fold, five-fold, or beyond reckoning—to say that this is not human nature is certainly inadmissible, yet can one say it is the original state of human nature? When clarity is lost and flows into turbidity, even to the point where dust and dregs cannot be distinguished from it—to say that this is not water is certainly inadmissible, yet can one say it is the original state of water? It was said of Yuejiao 越椒 that he would destroy his lineage because he had the voice of a jackal; yet had he been able to reform swiftly like Zhou Chu 周處, how would he have come to destruction? It was said of Shuyu 叔魚 that he would perish through bribery because he had the snout of a pig; yet had he been able to turn back urgently like Dai Yuan 戴淵, how would he have come to ruin? Once we know that the lowest stupidity does not issue from Heaven, it is clear that evil is not original human nature; once we know that self-violence and self-abandonment all stem from oneself, it is even clearer that what matters for human nature is skillfully returning to it rather than it being fixed in deficiency. Mencius set forth the doctrine that "human nature is good" at a time when benevolence and righteousness were blocked up; in repelling one-sided deeds and rectifying human minds, his merit was truly not inferior to that of Yu 禹. Master Cheng expounded the doctrine that "human nature is principle" in an age when the Learning of Principle was nearly obscured; in continuing the work of past sages and opening the way for future scholars, his merit too was not inferior to that of Mencius. When later Confucians drew analogies from the sun and borrowed metaphors from water, were they speaking idly? Among those who observe the sun, there are some who observe it from beneath a screened-off hut, and all they see is cloudy haze; there are some who observe it from halfway up a mountain, and clouds and sun…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
半也惟登泰山之巔而觀之則雲霧在下
杲日當空矣觀水者有自下流觀者皆濁
流也有自江漢合流而觀者清與濁半也
惟窮岷山之原而觀之則山下出泉靜清
無殽矣荀子其蔀屋下流之見乎楊子其
山半與合流之見乎孟子則直登泰嶽之
巔窮岷山之原而有眞見乎言雖不同各
因所見而已矣見雖不同各隨所造而已
矣執事又謂觀性當觀其初請即朱子之
===
言以溯孟氏而究言之可乎乍見孺子將
入於井一事之初也其眞心之發曷甞參
以要譽惡聲之私哉平旦之好惡一日之
初也其良心之露曷甞參以旦晝之所爲
哉人少則慕父母一生之初也其一念之
眞曷甞參以好色慕君之情哉此則如水
之未波而澄也如日之未翳而瑩也粹然
善而已學者能即此而充之一事之始終
皆乍見時也衆念不得而間之則事即理
punctuated: 半也。惟登泰山之巔而觀之，則雲霧在下，杲日當空矣。觀水者有自下流觀者，皆濁流也；有自江、漢合流而觀者，清與濁半也。惟窮岷山之原而觀之，則山下出泉，靜清無殽矣。荀子其蔀屋、下流之見乎！楊子其山半與合流之見乎！孟子則直登泰嶽之巔、窮岷山之原，而有眞見乎！言雖不同，各因所見而已矣；見雖不同，各隨所造而已矣。執事又謂觀性當觀其初，請即朱子之言以溯孟氏而究言之，可乎？乍見孺子將入於井，一事之初也，其眞心之發，曷甞參以要譽、惡聲之私哉？平旦之好惡，一日之初也，其良心之露，曷甞參以旦晝之所爲哉？人少則慕父母，一生之初也，其一念之眞，曷甞參以好色、慕君之情哉？此則如水之未波而澄也，如日之未翳而瑩也，粹然善而已。學者能即此而充之，一事之始終皆乍見時也，衆念不得而間之，則事即理
translation_en:
…half and half. Only when one ascends to the summit of Mount Tai and observes it does one see the clouds and mist below and the bright sun high in the sky. Among those who observe water, there are those who observe it from the lower reaches, where it is all turbid currents; and there are those who observe it from the confluence of the Yangzi and Han rivers, where clarity and turbidity are half and half. Only when one traces it back to its source in the Min Mountains and observes it does one see the spring issuing from beneath the mountain, still, clear, and unadulterated. Is Xunzi's view not that of the shaded hut and the lower reaches? Is Yang Xiong's view not that of halfway up the mountain and the confluence of the rivers? Mencius, however, directly ascended the summit of Mount Tai and traced the source in the Min Mountains, thus possessing true insight! Although their words differ, each simply follows from what he observed; although their observations differ, each simply accords with the level he attained.

Your Excellency also states that in observing human nature, one ought to observe its beginning. May I be permitted to draw upon the words of Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] to trace back to Mencius and discuss this exhaustively? Suddenly seeing a child about to fall into a well is the beginning of a single affair; in that stirring of the true heart, how could it ever be mixed with the selfish motives of seeking praise [from the child's parents or neighbors] or disliking the reputation [of being unmoved]? The likes and dislikes at dawn are the beginning of a single day; in that manifestation of the innate good mind, how could it ever be mixed with the deeds of the daytime? When a person is young, he yearns for his parents—this is the beginning of an entire life; in the genuineness of that single thought, how could it ever be mixed with the desires for sensual beauty or the yearning for a ruler? This is like water that is clear before it ripples, and like the sun that is lustrous before it is obscured—purely good and nothing more. If the student can take this as his starting point and extend it, then from beginning to end a single affair will be entirely as it was at the moment of sudden perception; when sundry thoughts cannot intrude upon it, the affair itself is principle…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣一日之好惡皆平旦時也旦晝不得而
牿之則可語日至矣一生之耄倪皆孩提
時也婚宦不得而移之則可語終身慕矣
學而至此是之謂知性知性則知止矣知
止則定矣定則無將迎無内外無自私用
智而大公之體立順應之用行矣體用一
顯微合而天地聖人之常不在君子而在
我矣斯固盡性之極功而學性者之標準
也彼謂教人性非所先者烏足以達此哉
===
雖然天下之言性亦多矣然性不貴言貴
盡也必如曾子之慎獨而後謂之盡必如
周子之研幾而後謂之盡必如程子之定
性而後謂之盡性盡則天地之性自存氣
質之性自弗性矣悟孔子所謂性近雖有
舊習而吾可奪也識孟子所謂性善雖有
頹俗而吾可挽也斯非所謂揭日於重光
廻狂瀾而東之者乎繼程子而興者世豈
無其人耶愚也有志而未得其要惟執事
punctuated: 矣。一日之好惡，皆平旦時也，旦晝不得而牿之，則可語日至矣。一生之耄倪，皆孩提時也，婚宦不得而移之，則可語終身慕矣。學而至此，是之謂知性。知性則知止矣，知止則定矣。定則無將迎、無内外、無自私用智，而大公之體立、順應之用行矣。體用一、顯微合，而天地聖人之常不在君子而在我矣。斯固盡性之極功，而學性者之標準也。彼謂教人性非所先者，烏足以達此哉？雖然，天下之言性亦多矣，然性不貴言，貴盡也。必如曾子之慎獨，而後謂之盡；必如周子之研幾，而後謂之盡；必如程子之定性，而後謂之盡。性盡，則天地之性自存，氣質之性自弗性矣。悟孔子所謂性近，雖有舊習而吾可奪也；識孟子所謂性善，雖有頹俗而吾可挽也。斯非所謂揭日於重光、廻狂瀾而東之者乎？繼程子而興者，世豈無其人耶？愚也有志而未得其要，惟執事
translation_en:
… principle. If one's likes and dislikes throughout a single day are all as they are at dawn, and the actions of the morning and daytime cannot fetter them, then one may speak of attaining it daily. If throughout one's entire life, from infancy to old age, one remains as a young child, and marriage and official career cannot alter it, then one may speak of lifelong yearning for one's parents. When learning reaches this point, this is what is called knowing human nature. Knowing human nature, one knows where to rest; knowing where to rest, one is settled. Being settled, there is neither anticipation nor lingering, neither inner nor outer, neither selfishness nor reliance on cleverness; thus the substance of great impartiality is established, and the function of harmonious response operates. Substance and function become one, the manifest and the subtle merge, and the constant way of Heaven, Earth, and the sages resides not merely in the noble man, but within oneself. This is indeed the ultimate achievement of fully realizing human nature, and the standard for those who study it. As for him who claimed that in teaching others, human nature is not the first priority—how could he be capable of comprehending this?

Even so, discussions of human nature in the world are already numerous; yet with human nature, what is valued is not discussing it, but fully realizing it. Only when one is like Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) in being watchful over oneself when alone can it be called fully realizing it; only when one is like Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) in investigating the subtle incipient tendencies can it be called fully realizing it; only when one is like Master Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥) in settling human nature can it be called fully realizing it. When human nature is fully realized, the nature of Heaven and Earth is naturally preserved, and the physical nature is naturally not treated as one's true nature. Awakening to what Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) called human natures being near to one another, even though there are old habits, we can overcome them; recognizing what Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) called human nature being good, even though there are decadent customs, we can reverse them. Is this not what is meant by holding up the sun to shine anew and turning back the raging waves to flow eastward? Could the world really lack someone who will rise up to succeed the Masters Cheng? Ignorant though I am, I have the aspiration but have not yet grasped its essentials; I only pray that Your Excellency…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
揭性真而進教之幸甚
第三問
陳其美
同考試官教諭羅批粤風俗談之比比而莫
爲正救子獨以士習歸之教化寓轉移之機其根
極理要者錄之以式
考試官教諭楊批民風士習統之在上不
在下是作得旨而文復爾雅取之
考試官教諭朱批以政本立論有味乎其
===
言之也可以式矣
善天下之俗者不可不慎其機挽天下之
敝者不可不求其本機也者倡於一人而
傚於衆人興於一時而流於百世相率而
趨莫知所自不慎其機而欲俗之善也難
矣本也者運之於上而導之於下行之於
近而通之於遠不令而行不疾而速不求
其本而欲敝之挽也難矣士習者其民風
之機乎政教者其士習之本乎知此始可
punctuated:
揭性真而進教之，幸甚。

第三問
陳其美〔同考試官教諭羅批：粤風俗談之比比，而莫爲正救；子獨以士習歸之教化，寓轉移之機，其根極理要者。錄之以式。考試官教諭楊批：民風士習，統之在上不在下。是作得旨，而文復爾雅，取之。考試官教諭朱批：以政本立論，有味乎其言之也，可以式矣。〕

善天下之俗者，不可不慎其機；挽天下之敝者，不可不求其本。機也者，倡於一人而傚於衆人，興於一時而流於百世，相率而趨，莫知所自。不慎其機而欲俗之善也，難矣。本也者，運之於上而導之於下，行之於近而通之於遠，不令而行，不疾而速。不求其本而欲敝之挽也，難矣。士習者，其民風之機乎！政教者，其士習之本乎！知此，始可
translation_en:
…hold up the true nature of humanity and advance my instruction, I would be most fortunate.

Third Policy Question
Chen Qimei 陈其美 [Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Luo 罗: Everyone talks about the customs of Guangdong, yet no one offers a proper remedy; you alone trace the habits of scholars back to moral instruction and transformation, wherein lies the pivotal mechanism of change—this gets to the very root and essence of principle. I record it to serve as a model. Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yang 杨: Popular customs and scholarly habits are governed from above, not from below. This composition grasps the main point, and its prose is moreover refined and classic; I select it. Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱: Establishing its argument upon the fundamental principles of governance, there is deep savor in what it says; it may well serve as a model.]

Those who would improve the customs of the world cannot but be cautious about their pivotal mechanism; those who would reverse the abuses of the world cannot but seek their root. As for the pivotal mechanism, it is initiated by a single person and imitated by the multitude, arises in a single moment and flows down through a hundred generations, with people leading one another forward to follow it without knowing whence it came. To wish for customs to become good without being cautious about this mechanism is difficult indeed. As for the root, it is set in motion from above and guides those below, is practiced near at hand and extends far abroad, is carried out without commands being issued, and achieves swiftness without haste. To wish to reverse abuses without seeking this root is difficult indeed. Are not the habits of scholars the pivotal mechanism of popular customs? Are not governance and moral instruction the root of the habits of scholars? Only when one understands this can one…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
語於東粤之風俗矣夫風俗何自而起乎
上行下效謂之風衆心安定謂之俗風之
所在如影之於形響之於聲嚴刑不為禁
重賞不為勸俗所喜好非有徴發期會而
遠近若一其所係於民者非小於此而無
所以化導之可乎故一其道德同其風俗
命太師陳詩以觀民風令輶軒循行天下
問俗凡所以維持誨導之者無所不至記
曰脩其敎不易其俗齊其政不易其宜管
===
子曰禮義廉恥是謂四維皆言化導之具
也夫風俗又何自而敝乎上無以敎則下
無以學情欲不節則流好尚不謹則辟風
俗不厚則媮民情愈趨愈下將至於大壞
極敗而不可反而其本初則不然於此而
無所以救正之可乎故齊其法制詳其命
令禮禁未然之前法施已然之後所以挽
回整頓之者無所不至易曰窮則變變則
通通則久董子曰已雕已琢還反其樸皆
punctuated: 語於東粤之風俗矣。夫風俗何自而起乎？上行下效謂之風，衆心安定謂之俗。風之所在，如影之於形，響之於聲，嚴刑不為禁，重賞不為勸；俗所喜好，非有徴發期會，而遠近若一。其所係於民者非小，於此而無所以化導之，可乎？故一其道德，同其風俗，命太師陳詩以觀民風，令輶軒循行天下問俗，凡所以維持誨導之者，無所不至。《記》曰：「脩其敎，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。」《管子》曰：「禮義廉恥，是謂四維。」皆言化導之具也。夫風俗又何自而敝乎？上無以敎則下無以學，情欲不節則流，好尚不謹則辟，風俗不厚則媮。民情愈趨愈下，將至於大壞極敗而不可反，而其本初則不然。於此而無所以救正之，可乎？故齊其法制，詳其命令，禮禁未然之前，法施已然之後，所以挽回整頓之者，無所不至。《易》曰：「窮則變，變則通，通則久。」董子曰：「已雕已琢，還反其樸。」皆…
translation_en:
…speak of the customs and mores of eastern Yue [Guangdong]. Now, how do customs and mores arise? What those above practice and those below imitate is called "wind" [prevailing influence]; what settles and stabilizes in the hearts of the multitude is called "custom." Where the prevailing wind blows, it is like the shadow following the form or the echo following the sound—severe punishments cannot prohibit it, and heavy rewards cannot encourage it. In what customs delight in and favor, even without requisitions or appointed gatherings, near and far act as one. Their bearing upon the people is no small matter; at this juncture, would it do to lack the means to transform and guide them? Therefore, the ancients unified their morality and harmonized their customs, commanding the Grand Music Master (Taishi) to present poems in order to observe the popular mores, and ordering light-carriage envoys (youxuan) to tour the realm and inquire into local customs; in all the ways of maintaining, instructing, and guiding them, nothing was left undone. The Record [Book of Rites (Liji)] says: "Cultivate their instruction without changing their customs; regularize their governance without changing what is suitable to them." Master Guan [Guanzi] says: "Propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame—these are called the Four Bonds." Both speak of the instruments of transformation and guidance.

Now, how again do customs and mores fall into decay? When those above have nothing with which to instruct, those below have nothing from which to learn; when passions and desires are not moderated, they become dissolute; when preferences and fashions are not guarded, they become depraved; when customs and mores are not generous, they become frivolous and苟 [remiss]. As popular sentiment sinks ever lower, it will reach a state of utter ruin and extreme corruption from which there is no return—yet in its original beginning, it was not so. At such a point, would it do to lack the means to rescue and rectify it? Therefore, one regularizes the laws and institutions and makes detailed the ordinances and commands: propriety prohibits before things happen, and law is applied after they have occurred; in all the ways of restoring and setting them in order, nothing is left undone. The Changes (Yi) says: "When a state of affairs reaches exhaustion, it changes; through change, it achieves continuity; through continuity, it endures." Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu] says: "Once carved and polished, return again to uncarved simplicity." All of these…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
言反正之機也故曰廉耻者士人之美節
敎化者朝廷之急務不知敎化而欲望士
習民風之善也難矣夫粤天下之澤國也
負山阻海火耕水耨其民樸重諺慤若難
遽以道德一之者然其貞元未散良心易
感而嘉言易入一有賢者倡之其從善更
輕而守志益堅也是故高固以才能相楚
威王始進鐸椒春秋引君當道因致五羊
銜榖之瑞南海之民風動而圖像以表厥
===
賢自是人文漸盛民俗漸淳志曰衣冠禮
樂無異中州又曰今之交廣古之鄒魯其
化民成俗之休可想見矣自玆以後代不
乏賢士勤于德民易其俗若羅威唐頌之
厚彛倫篤行誼則民化而敬老親親矣馮
元之通經術登膴仕則民化而博學好古
矣俗崇正道而陋緇黃非因梁觀國之以
禮敦俗乎俗守名義而樂恬退非由崔與
之之清風高節乎俗皆務學非因二陳以
punctuated: 言反正之機也。故曰：廉耻者，士人之美節；敎化者，朝廷之急務。不知敎化而欲望士習民風之善也，難矣。夫粤，天下之澤國也。負山阻海，火耕水耨，其民樸重諺慤，若難遽以道德一之者。然其貞元未散，良心易感而嘉言易入，一有賢者倡之，其從善更輕而守志益堅也。是故高固以才能相楚威王，始進《鐸椒春秋》，引君當道，因致五羊銜榖之瑞，南海之民風動，而圖像以表厥賢。自是人文漸盛，民俗漸淳。《志》曰：「衣冠禮樂，無異中州。」又曰：「今之交廣，古之鄒魯。」其化民成俗之休，可想見矣。自玆以後，代不乏賢，士勤于德，民易其俗。若羅威、唐頌之厚彛倫、篤行誼，則民化而敬老親親矣；馮元之通經術、登膴仕，則民化而博學好古矣。俗崇正道而陋緇黃，非因梁觀國之以禮敦俗乎？俗守名義而樂恬退，非由崔與之之清風高節乎？俗皆務學，非因二陳以
translation_en:
… speak of the turning point for returning to what is right. Therefore it is said: a sense of honor and shame is the fine integrity of scholars; moral transformation and instruction are the urgent business of the court. If one does not understand moral instruction and yet hopes for the customs of scholars and the mores of the common people to be good, it will be difficult indeed.

Now Yue [Guangdong] is a land of marshes and waters in the realm. Backing against mountains and bounded by the sea, its people practice slash-and-burn and flooded-field agriculture; they are simple, stolid, blunt, and sincere [? 諺慤, for 喭慤], as if it were difficult to unite them all at once through moral virtue. Yet their pure primordial vitality has not dissipated; their innate good conscience is easily moved and fine words easily enter their hearts. Once there is a worthy person to take the lead, they follow the good all the more readily and hold fast to their resolve all the more firmly.

For this reason, when Gao Gu 高固 served King Wei of Chu 楚威王 as minister by virtue of his talent and ability, he first presented Duo Jiao's Spring and Autumn Annals (Duo Jiao Chunqiu 鐸椒春秋) and guided his ruler along the proper Way. This brought about the auspicious omen of the Five Rams holding ears of grain in their mouths; the people of Nanhai 南海 were stirred as by the wind, and painted his portrait to honor his worthiness. From this time onward, cultural refinement gradually flourished and popular customs gradually grew pure. The Gazetteer (Zhi 志) says: "In caps and robes, rites and music, it is no different from the Central Plain." It also says: "Jiao 交 and Guang 廣 of today are the Zou 鄒 and Lu 魯 of antiquity." The beauty of its transforming the people and perfecting customs can well be imagined!

Ever since then, no generation has lacked worthies; scholars have been diligent in virtue, and the people have changed their customs. With figures like Luo Wei 羅威 and Tang Song 唐頌 enriching the cardinal human relationships and practicing earnest righteousness, the people were transformed and came to respect the aged and love their kin. With Feng Yuan 馮元 mastering classical learning and ascending to high and lucrative office, the people were transformed and came to study broadly and cherish antiquity. That popular customs esteem the orthodox Way and disdain Buddhist monks and Daoist priests—is this not because Liang Guanguo 梁觀國 enriched customs through ritual propriety? That popular customs uphold moral duty and delight in quiet retirement—does this not stem from the pure ethos and lofty integrity of Cui Yuzhi 崔與之? That popular customs all devote themselves to learning—is this not because the Two Chens 二陳…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
經學鳴二莫以文章顯乎上下相觀後先
相望流風餘韻郁郁彬彬固皆諸賢有以
倡之也謂民風不本於士習可乎夫粵以
質直慓悍之地賴諸賢興起斯文旣已化
爲禮義之俗又加以我
國家仁漸義摩之敎名世之賢相繼迭出弘
正以前士多羔羊素絲之風而民亦知重
義輕利以共享夫盜息民安之治古今稱
全盛焉乃今則若有異往昔者風敎漸澆
===
則士賤行檢矣俗化漸侈則人棄本業矣
嶺之東西海之南北所云沃野千里者有
未墾之土矣惠潮山海之交向所云新民
復業者有集榖啄粟之思矣流移逋播之
民昔之嗷嗷待哺者有仳離無家之歎矣
男不耕耘女不蠶織而靡衣媮食者有競
淫尚侈之習矣貴游賈竪侈靡儇譎而信
義衰廢矣豪右大俠田連阡陌賦不盈銖
兩而齊民編戶相朘削以趨於盡矣禮讓
punctuated: 經學鳴，二莫以文章顯乎？上下相觀，後先相望，流風餘韻，郁郁彬彬，固皆諸賢有以倡之也。謂民風不本於士習，可乎？夫粵以質直慓悍之地，賴諸賢興起斯文，旣已化爲禮義之俗；又加以我國家仁漸義摩之敎，名世之賢，相繼迭出。弘、正以前，士多羔羊素絲之風，而民亦知重義輕利，以共享夫盜息民安之治，古今稱全盛焉。乃今則若有異往昔者：風敎漸澆，則士賤行檢矣；俗化漸侈，則人棄本業矣。嶺之東西、海之南北，所云沃野千里者，有未墾之土矣。惠、潮山海之交，向所云新民復業者，有集榖啄粟之思矣。流移逋播之民，昔之嗷嗷待哺者，有仳離無家之歎矣。男不耕耘，女不蠶織，而靡衣媮食者，有競淫尚侈之習矣。貴游賈竪，侈靡儇譎，而信義衰廢矣。豪右大俠，田連阡陌，賦不盈銖兩，而齊民編戶相朘削以趨於盡矣。禮讓
translation_en: … renowned for their classical learning, and the two Mo 莫 distinguished for their literary compositions? Superiors and inferiors observed one another, predecessors and successors looked to each other across time, and the enduring customs and lingering refinement were rich and cultivated—surely all of this was because these worthies took the lead in initiating it. How, then, could one say that popular customs are not rooted in the habits of the literati? Now, Guangdong, originally a land of blunt simplicity and fierce boldness, relied on these worthies to rouse this culture of ours, and was already transformed into a society of ritual and righteousness; added to this was the teaching of our Dynasty, which gradually steeped the people in benevolence and polished them with righteousness, so that world-renowned worthies emerged one after another in succession. Prior to the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras, the literati mostly possessed the pure and upright character celebrated in the ode "Lambskin and White Silk" (Gaoyang susi), while the common people also knew to value righteousness and slight profit, thereby sharing together in a governance where banditry ceased and the people were at peace—acclaimed past and present as an age of complete flourishing. Yet today things seem different from the past: as moral teaching gradually grows thin, the literati despise personal conduct and self-restraint; as popular customs gradually grow extravagant, people abandon their fundamental agricultural occupations. East and west of the mountains, north and south of the sea, in what were called a thousand li of fertile plains, there is now uncultivated land. At the junction of mountains and sea in Huizhou 惠州 and Chaozhou 潮州, those formerly called "new people" who had returned to their livelihoods now harbor thoughts of flocking to the paper-mulberry trees to peck at grain [like the displaced people in the *Book of Odes*]. Displaced and fleeing vagrants, who in the past cried out waiting to be fed, now heave sighs over separation and homelessness. Men do not plow and weed, women do not tend silkworms and weave, while those who wear extravagant clothes and live idly for the moment indulge in habits of competing in licentiousness and prizing luxury. Noble idlers and petty merchants are extravagant, frivolous, and deceitful, so that trustworthiness and righteousness have declined and fallen into disuse. Powerful magnates and great local bullies own fields stretching across the footpaths between paddies yet pay taxes not even amounting to a few grains or taels of silver, while the registered commoners are fleeced and exploited until they are driven to utter exhaustion. In a place of ritual and deference…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之地師徒相遠三家九市衣冠雜遝而夕
敎鮮敦綱維不立矣民風士習日趨於敝
蓋不止於執事所云獵聲華悖倫理事巫
詛者其綠林嘯聚錦帆通蹻何惑也此固
風之所靡可爲太息者其視向之衣冠禮
樂文章節義羔羊素絲盜息民安之俗不
啻逕庭矣能無待於敎化乎所以握其機
要而反其本初者誠不可不汲汲矣夫今
日之事豈庠序學校之未設乎設矣而實
===
德未脩也豈六德三物之未講乎講矣而
實意未孚也豈衣冠文物之未盛乎盛矣
而實行未覩也豈法制禁令之未備乎備
矣而實政未舉也豈督促稽查之未嚴乎
嚴矣而實效未臻也孔子曰敎化之流非
家至而人益之也以身先之而已賈生曰
移風易俗使天下回心而向道類非俗吏
之所能爲則夫示之以好惡陳之以禮義
謹之以好尚所以端士習而淑民風信有
punctuated: 之地，師徒相遠，三家九市，衣冠雜遝，而夕敎鮮敦，綱維不立矣。民風士習，日趨於敝，蓋不止於執事所云獵聲華、悖倫理、事巫詛者；其綠林嘯聚、錦帆通蹻，何惑也？此固風之所靡，可爲太息者，其視向之衣冠禮樂、文章節義、羔羊素絲、盜息民安之俗，不啻逕庭矣！能無待於敎化乎？所以握其機要而反其本初者，誠不可不汲汲矣。夫今日之事，豈庠序學校之未設乎？設矣，而實德未脩也。豈六德三物之未講乎？講矣，而實意未孚也。豈衣冠文物之未盛乎？盛矣，而實行未覩也。豈法制禁令之未備乎？備矣，而實政未舉也。豈督促稽查之未嚴乎？嚴矣，而實效未臻也。孔子曰：「敎化之流，非家至而人益之也，以身先之而已。」賈生曰：「移風易俗，使天下回心而向道，類非俗吏之所能爲。」則夫示之以好惡，陳之以禮義，謹之以好尚，所以端士習而淑民風，信有
translation_en: … of ritual deference, teachers and disciples are estranged from one another; in hamlets of three families and markets of nine, caps and robes mingle in noisy crowds, yet evening instruction [?] is rarely earnest and the moral mainstays are not established. Popular customs and the habits of scholars grow more degraded by the day, going well beyond what Your Excellency referred to as hunting after showy reputation, violating moral relationships, and practicing shamanism and cursing; what wonder is it, then, that bandits whistle to gather in the greenwood and brocade-sailed pirates traffic like Robber Zhi [?]? This is truly a trend of moral decline over which one may heave a deep sigh. Compared to the former customs—of caps and robes, rites and music, literary refinement and moral integrity, the lambskin and white silk of pure officialdom, when banditry ceased and the people were at peace—it is nothing less than a world apart! Can this do without moral transformation through education? That whereby we grasp the pivotal mechanism and return things to their original foundation is truly something we cannot fail to pursue with urgency. Now, as for the state of affairs today: is it that community and state schools have not been established? They have been established, yet substantive virtue is not cultivated. Is it that the Six Virtues and Three Matters have not been expounded? They have been expounded, yet the genuine intent has not inspired trust. Is it that caps, robes, and cultural institutions are not flourishing? They are flourishing, yet substantive conduct is not seen. Is it that laws, regulations, and prohibitions are not complete? They are complete, yet substantive governance is not carried out. Is it that supervision, urging, and inspection are not strict? They are strict, yet substantive results have not been achieved. Confucius said: "The spread of moral transformation does not come from visiting every household and adding to every person; one simply leads them in person." Master Jia [Jia Yi 賈誼] said: "Transforming customs and changing habits, causing the whole world to turn its heart toward the Way—this is the sort of thing that vulgar officials are incapable of doing." Thus, showing them what to love and hate, setting forth rites and righteousness for them, and being circumspect about what is valued and esteemed—the means to rectify the habits of scholars and purify the customs of the people truly lies …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不在人而在我者是故風敎澆則挽之以
樸俗化侈則程之以儉土蕪穢則勸之以
耒耜民反側則中之以法令逋播者業之
蝓惰者作之詛盟者詰之幷兼則均之以
賦役而權其豪奢庠序則課之以章程而
黜其浮靡如此則民有所趨避而回行易
嚮孰敢不式士習有不端民風有不淑者
否也雖然主之不可以不斷而行之又不
可以不力其政令貴一其誅賞貴必無牽
===
於游詞無脂韋於權豪無姑息於諧媚之
夫如是而猶不從不得不深治之如所謂
屏之遠方終身不齒者則其勢自不能不
變而奚患其靡也語曰更化則善治今適
更化之時猶日以簿書期會爲大故而不
知所以易民視匡失俗豈理也哉嗟夫齊
其法制詳其命令期於必行固矣然衣食
足而後禮義興粵兵興數十年繼以水旱
重以征輸民無食矣奚暇治禮義哉則所
punctuated: 不在人而在我者。是故風敎澆，則挽之以樸；俗化侈，則程之以儉；土蕪穢，則勸之以耒耜；民反側，則中之以法令。逋播者業之，蝓惰者作之，詛盟者詰之。幷兼則均之以賦役，而權其豪奢；庠序則課之以章程，而黜其浮靡。如此則民有所趨避，而回行易嚮，孰敢不式？士習有不端、民風有不淑者，否也。雖然，主之不可以不斷，而行之又不可以不力。其政令貴一，其誅賞貴必，無牽於游詞，無脂韋於權豪，無姑息於諧媚之夫。如是而猶不從，不得不深治之，如所謂「屏之遠方，終身不齒」者，則其勢自不能不變，而奚患其靡也？語曰：「更化則善治。」今適更化之時，猶日以簿書期會爲大故，而不知所以易民視、匡失俗，豈理也哉！嗟夫！齊其法制，詳其命令，期於必行，固矣。然衣食足而後禮義興。粵兵興數十年，繼以水旱，重以征輸，民無食矣，奚暇治禮義哉？則所
translation_en:
… does not depend on others, but on ourselves. Therefore, when moral teachings become thin and decadent, restore them with simplicity; when popular customs grow extravagant, regulate them with frugality; when lands lie overgrown and uncultivated, encourage the people with plow and share; when the people are restless and rebellious, hold them to account with laws and ordinances. Settle in occupations those who have fled and scattered; rouse to action those who are indolent; investigate and punish those who form illicit oaths and covenants. Where there is land engrossment, equalize it through taxes and labor services and curb the powerful and extravagant; in the local schools, examine students according to established regulations and dismiss the superficial and华丽 [showy]. If this is done, the people will know what to pursue and what to avoid; turning their conduct around and changing their direction, who would dare not follow the model? Could it then happen that literati habits remain unrectified or popular customs remain impure? No, indeed.

Even so, in presiding over these measures one cannot lack decisiveness, and in carrying them out one cannot lack vigor. Administrative orders must be unified, and punishments and rewards must be certain. Do not be swayed by floating talk, do not be pliant and obsequious toward the powerful and mighty, and do not be overly indulgent toward flattering and sycophantic men. If after doing all this there are still those who do not obey, one cannot avoid punishing them severely—as in the saying, "banish them to distant regions, and for the rest of their lives do not rank them among the community"—and then by necessity the trend cannot but change; what worry would there be of its decay? The proverb says: "When moral transformation is renewed, governance becomes good." Now, right at a time for renewing moral transformation, if we still daily treat routine registers and scheduled meetings as the great affairs of state, without knowing how to change the people's outlook and rectify errant customs, how could that be reasonable!

Alas! Uniformly ordering the laws and institutions and making commands detailed, with the expectation that they will surely be carried out—this is certainly necessary. Yet only when clothing and food are sufficient do rites and righteousness flourish. In Guangdong, military campaigns have been waged for several decades, followed by floods and droughts and compounded by tax levies and transport duties; the people have nothing to eat, so what leisure do they have to cultivate rites and righteousness? Thus, that by which…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以節其財力遂其生養使得優游於仁義
禮樂之中以待其善念自生而民志自定
者不可不首加之意也一其道德同其風
俗其機在上固矣然親民之職莫若守令
敎化之務如所謂興社學舉義倉行保甲
之法布激勸之典皆其所最急者非得賢
守令身任而力行之實德不能以流通善
政不可以遍及矣則慎選守令又爲脩敎
化之首務也此其機本所在尤不可忽敢
===
敬申言之
第四問
李王
同考試官敎諭陳批 如鹽利蠹作者迄無定
焦此所畫釐正裁恤公私兼利具見經濟之略非
徒文之工也宜錄
考試官敎諭楊批 指陳利弊切中機宜
考試官敎諭朱批 條對明悉
天下有自然之利善興利者循其法以導
punctuated:
以節其財力，遂其生養，使得優游於仁義禮樂之中，以待其善念自生而民志自定者，不可不首加之意也。一其道德，同其風俗，其機在上，固矣；然親民之職莫若守令，敎化之務，如所謂興社學、舉義倉、行保甲之法、布激勸之典，皆其所最急者。非得賢守令身任而力行之，實德不能以流通，善政不可以遍及矣。則慎選守令，又爲脩敎化之首務也。此其機本所在，尤不可忽，敢敬申言之。

第四問
李王
同考試官敎諭陳批：如鹽利蠹作者，迄無定焦。此所畫釐正裁恤，公私兼利，具見經濟之略，非徒文之工也。宜錄。
考試官敎諭楊批：指陳利弊，切中機宜。
考試官敎諭朱批：條對明悉。

天下有自然之利，善興利者循其法以導
translation_en:
…to conserve their financial and physical resources and fulfill their livelihood and nourishment, enabling them to live at ease amidst benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, while waiting for their good intentions to arise naturally and the people's minds to settle of their own accord—this is something to which attention must first be paid. To unify their morality and harmonize their customs—that the pivot for this lies with those above is certainly true. Yet among the offices close to the people, none compares to Prefects and Magistrates. In the task of moral transformation through education, matters such as establishing community schools, setting up charitable granaries, implementing the mutual-responsibility (baojia) system, and promulgating statutes for encouragement and exhortation are all the most urgent priorities. Unless worthy Prefects and Magistrates are obtained to take personal responsibility and carry them out vigorously, genuine virtue cannot circulate and good governance cannot reach everywhere. Therefore, carefully selecting Prefects and Magistrates is in turn the foremost task in cultivating moral transformation. This is where the fundamental pivot lies, and it especially must not be neglected; I venture respectfully to state this in full.

Fourth Question
Li Wang 李王
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: Those who discuss the abuses in the salt monopoly have hitherto reached no settled conclusion [? 迄無定焦, likely a transcription error for 論議執一 / 定論]. The plans laid out here for rectification, retrenchment, and relief benefit both public and private interests, fully demonstrating strategic statecraft and not merely literary skill. It should be recorded.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yang 楊: Points out advantages and abuses, hitting squarely upon what is opportune and appropriate.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu 朱: The point-by-point response is clear and thorough.

All under Heaven possesses natural benefits; those skilled at promoting benefits follow the proper methods to guide…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之而後其利爲不窮天下無不敝之法善
行法者因其敝而通之而後其法爲可久
何則法以正經若持衡然一成而不易者
也變以趨時若轉圜然推行於不滯者也
用法者知其利之所由興又知其法之所
由廢酌古以準今補偏以救敝
國家之大計可從而理矣是故屯政也鹽法
也先王所以因天地自然之利而裕軍國
之需於不匱者也第法玩於因循之久而
===
害成於姑息之過乗其弊而亟反之在今
日誠不容緩者愚嘗考鏡古今綜覈利弊
而得其捄之之要矣屯田非古也自趙充
國祖鼂錯屯戍之議以制諸羌計羌虜故
田及公田民未墾者爲屯塞下内有亡費
之利外有守禦之備古今防邊之法莫是
過矣唐因之而屯關中魏因之而屯金陵
兩淮宋因之而屯荆襄岳州取而較之漢
止數郡之屯宋有括牛之擾唐法爲最善
punctuated: 之，而後其利爲不窮；天下無不敝之法，善行法者循其敝而通之，而後其法爲可久。何則？法以正經，若持衡然，一成而不易者也；變以趨時，若轉圜然，推行於不滯者也。用法者知其利之所由興，又知其法之所由廢，酌古以準今，補偏以救敝，國家之大計可從而理矣。是故屯政也、鹽法也，先王所以因天地自然之利，而裕軍國之需於不匱者也。第法玩於因循之久，而害成於姑息之過，乗其弊而亟反之，在今日誠不容緩者。愚嘗考鏡古今，綜覈利弊，而得其捄之之要矣。屯田非古也，自趙充國祖鼂錯屯戍之議以制諸羌，計羌虜故田及公田民未墾者爲屯塞下，内有亡費之利，外有守禦之備，古今防邊之法莫是過矣。唐因之而屯關中，魏因之而屯金陵、兩淮，宋因之而屯荆、襄、岳州。取而較之，漢止數郡之屯，宋有括牛之擾，唐法爲最善…
translation_en: … it, and only then will that benefit become inexhaustible; under heaven there is no institution that does not fall into decay, and those skilled at implementing institutions adapt to their decay and make them flexible, and only then can those institutions endure. Why is this? Institutions serve to rectify fundamental principles; like holding a balance scale, once established they are unchanging. Adaptation serves to keep pace with the times; like turning a wheel, it is carried out without stagnation. When those who apply the institutions understand how their benefits arise and also understand how the institutions fall into disuse, deliberating on antiquity to set standards for the present and remedying imbalances to rescue them from decay, the great plans of the state can thereby be put in order. Therefore, the administration of state farms and the salt laws are the means by which the former kings drew upon the natural benefits of heaven and earth to supply the needs of the military and the state without exhaustion. Yet when laws are treated lightly through prolonged routinism, and harms take shape through excessive indulgence, seizing upon their abuses and urgently reversing them is truly something that brooks no delay today. I have examined the past and present, comprehensively verified the benefits and abuses, and grasped the essentials of how to remedy them. State farms do not date from high antiquity. Ever since Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 followed Chao Cuo's 鼂錯 proposals for garrison farming in order to control the various Qiang peoples—calculating the former lands of the Qiang captives as well as public lands not yet cultivated by the people to establish farms along the frontier fortifications—internally there was the benefit of avoiding expenditure, and externally there was preparedness for defense. Among frontier defense methods past and present, none has surpassed this. The Tang followed it and established state farms in Guanzhong; the Wei followed it and established state farms in Jinling and the Lianghuai region; the Song followed it and established state farms in Jingzhou, Xiangyang, and Yuezhou. Taking them together and comparing them: the Han had state farms in only a few commanderies, and the Song suffered the disruption of requisitioning cattle, whereas the Tang method was the finest…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
焉鹽筴非古也自齊管敬仲遡周禮鹽人
之意以開利源計其丁口給之種釜令百
姓毋得聚庸鬻鹽取諸商賈之贏以實帑
藏之儲古今生財之法莫是過矣廼魏甄
琛議捐之民而毋奪民利彭城王勰議歸
之官而毋縱末作要而言之與其取之於
農孰若取之於商勰論為近優焉我
國家度衛所閒曠之區分軍置屯特設憲臣
綜理之履畝定稅建營隸籍雖力耕供租
===
而操閱不廢蓋損益漢唐之法而規制為
至備矣奈之何日久而弊生也或隱其尺
籍或任其荒蕪屯政幾于廢矣而廣東尤
有甚焉者廣州等六十衛所屯田之營五
十六歲徵稅十五萬四千有奇乃籍丁則
虛耗而無實覈田則迷亂而鮮稽其他黠
猾豪右巧為侵漁乾沒以逞其私者無筭
也是可不亟為之處乎
國家於各處產鹽之所通商辦鹽各設轉運
punctuated: 焉。鹽筴非古也，自齊管敬仲遡《周禮》鹽人之意以開利源，計其丁口，給之種釜，令百姓毋得聚庸鬻鹽，取諸商賈之贏以實帑藏之儲，古今生財之法莫是過矣。廼魏甄琛議捐之民而毋奪民利，彭城王勰議歸之官而毋縱末作。要而言之，與其取之於農，孰若取之於商？勰論為近優焉。我國家度衛所閒曠之區，分軍置屯，特設憲臣綜理之。履畝定稅，建營隸籍，雖力耕供租，而操閱不廢，蓋損益漢、唐之法而規制為至備矣。奈之何日久而弊生也？或隱其尺籍，或任其荒蕪，屯政幾于廢矣。而廣東尤有甚焉者，廣州等六十衛所，屯田之營五十六，歲徵稅十五萬四千有奇。乃籍丁則虛耗而無實，覈田則迷亂而鮮稽，其他黠猾豪右巧為侵漁乾沒以逞其私者無筭也。是可不亟為之處乎？國家於各處產鹽之所，通商辦鹽，各設轉運、
translation_en:
… was the best. The salt monopoly is not from antiquity. Ever since Guan Jingzhong (Guan Zhong 管仲) of Qi traced back the intent of the Salt Men (yanren) in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) to open up a source of profit—counting the population, supplying them with tools and cauldrons, forbidding the common people from gathering hired laborers to boil and sell salt, and taking from the surplus of merchants to fill the reserves of the state treasury—no method of generating wealth from antiquity to the present has surpassed this. Later, in the Northern Wei, Zhen Chen 甄琛 proposed relinquishing it to the people so as not to deprive them of profit, whereas Yuan Xie 元勰, Prince of Pengcheng, proposed returning it to the government so as not to indulge secondary occupations (commerce). In essence, rather than taking from the farmers, how much better is it to take from the merchants? Xie's argument comes closer to being superior.

Our dynasty measured the idle and open lands of the Guards and Battalions (weisuo), divided the soldiers to establish military farms (tuntian), and specially appointed Surveillance Commission officials to oversee them. They surveyed the acreage to fix the tax, established camps and attached them to registers; although the soldiers worked hard at plowing to supply rent, their military drills and inspections were not neglected. Indeed, this adapted and refined the methods of the Han and Tang dynasties, making the regulations utterly complete. Yet how is it that as days pass, abuses arise? Some conceal their military registers, while others allow the land to fall into ruin, so that the administration of military farms is nearly defunct. And in Guangdong this is especially severe. In the sixty Guards and Battalions of Guangzhou and other places, there are fifty-six military farm camps, annually levying a tax of over 154,000 [piculs]. Yet when registering able-bodied males, the numbers are depleted and devoid of reality; when verifying the fields, the records are confused and rarely audited; and beyond this, the crafty villains and powerful magnates who cleverly encroach, expropriate, and embezzle to gratify their private interests are beyond count. Can we fail to deal with this urgently?

At the various salt-producing places, the state engages merchants to handle the salt, establishing Salt Distribution Commissions and …

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
提舉司專理之課額有定徵行鹽有分地
令輸粟實塞而照引支給蓋斟酌唐宋之
法而計慮爲益精矣奈之何日久而弊滋
也餘鹽行而常股滯正引阻而邊儲匱鹽
法幾大壞矣而廣東又其甚焉者東北二
提舉司鬻鹽之場二十八歲徵課一萬五
千九百有奇乃核丁則逋而亡者十三督
課則負而縮者十五兼之豪家悍卒揚帆
聯艦興販飄忽於鯨波者寔繁也是可不
===
===
亟爲之治乎夫樂因循而憚變更者曲士
之所守也任骯髒而重怨嫌者委儒之所
希也粵之屯鹽弊非一日執事謂瑟不調
當移其柱誠然也玆欲祛積習之弊以復
祖宗之盛是不必別求所謂法也惟申明
舊制去其所以害法者而已何者屯田之弊端
雖多而逋負於頑梗兼併於豪右此其大
較也釐正之要在憲臣執其綱於上而嚴
有司清理之寄夫列田爲屯尺寸皆官土
punctuated:
提舉司專理之，課額有定徵，行鹽有分地，令輸粟實塞而照引支給，蓋斟酌唐、宋之法，而計慮爲益精矣。奈之何日久而弊滋也？餘鹽行而常股滯，正引阻而邊儲匱，鹽法幾大壞矣。而廣東又其甚焉者，東、北二提舉司鬻鹽之場二十八，歲徵課一萬五千九百有奇。乃核丁則逋而亡者十三，督課則負而縮者十五，兼之豪家悍卒，揚帆聯艦，興販飄忽於鯨波者，寔繁也。是可不亟爲之治乎？

夫樂因循而憚變更者，曲士之所守也；任骯髒而重怨嫌者，委儒之所希也。粵之屯、鹽弊非一日，執事謂瑟不調當移其柱，誠然也。玆欲祛積習之弊，以復祖宗之盛，是不必別求所謂法也，惟申明舊制，去其所以害法者而已。何者？屯田之弊端雖多，而逋負於頑梗、兼併於豪右，此其大較也。釐正之要，在憲臣執其綱於上，而嚴有司清理之寄。夫列田爲屯，尺寸皆官土…
translation_en:
…and Salt Tax Supervisorates to manage them exclusively. The tax quotas have fixed levies, and the distribution of salt has designated territories. Merchants are ordered to transport grain to provision the frontier garrisons and are issued salt in accordance with their salt vouchers. Indeed, this was adapted after deliberation from the methods of the Tang and Song dynasties, and the planning behind it was even more refined. How is it that as days pass, abuses proliferate? As surplus salt circulates, the regular reserve stock stagnates; as regular salt vouchers are obstructed, frontier supplies run short—the salt laws are nearly ruined altogether. And in Guangdong this is even more acute: the two Salt Tax Supervisorates of Guangdong and Haibei have twenty-eight salterns for selling salt, collecting an annual tax quota of more than fifteen thousand nine hundred. Yet when the registered salt-workers are verified, three out of ten have defaulted and fled; when the tax quota is pressed for collection, five out of ten are in arrears and fall short. Moreover, powerful families and unruly soldiers hoist sails and link vessels, engaging in illicit trafficking and darting unpredictably across the whale-tossed waves in truly great numbers. Can one fail to urgently bring order to this?

Now, delighting in routine and dreading change is what parochial scholars cling to; tolerating corruption and shrinking from resentment and suspicion is what accommodating literati aspire to. The abuses in Guangdong's military farms and salt administration did not arise in a single day; Your Excellency's remark that when the se zither is out of tune one must shift its bridges is truly so. If we now wish to dispel the abuses of long-standing habit in order to restore the flourishing state of our imperial ancestors, there is no need to seek elsewhere for some so-called new law; we need only reaffirm the old regulations and eliminate that which harms the law. Why is this? Although the abuses of the military farms are many, tax evasion and default by the obstinate and annexation by powerful magnates are the main outlines of the problem. The key to rectifying this lies in the Censorate officials upholding the overarching principles from above while strictly charging the local authorities with the responsibility of clearing up the records. For when land is laid out as military farms, every inch and foot is government land…

title: 萬曆四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也按畝起徵升斗皆公儲也而併兼逋負
邦有常刑必也稽戸籍之存亡舉丈量之
明法盜賣者必懲私佃者必禁即界紊籍
去而閭閻故老豈無一二存者自首者宥
占據自其祖父者宥其亂籍私匿而弗悛
者繩之無少貸也而有田無税者行沒官
之令計丁分給者嚴限田之條畫之經界
載諸版籍東作則秉耒以耕西成則荷戈
以練食不虧而兵亦足雖充國金城之屯
===
孔明渭濱之耕率是道也何憂乎屯政之
不復耶鹽法之弊孔雜出而課額折於流
移商賈阨於私販此其大都也整飭之要
在憲臣握其樞於上而重有司稽察之柄
夫分漏辦鹽凡以恤竈也戢販防姦凡以
通商也而公課私鹺國有成憲必也先覈
額辦之丁申布招商之令戸絕者速為查
豁拖負者以漸追徵即流離轉徙而遺埕
故漏必有私自封殖者願自陪納者聽願
punctuated:
也，按畝起徵，升斗皆公儲也，而併兼逋負，邦有常刑。必也稽戸籍之存亡，舉丈量之明法。盜賣者必懲，私佃者必禁。即界紊籍去，而閭閻故老豈無一二存者？自首者宥，占據自其祖父者宥，其亂籍私匿而弗悛者，繩之無少貸也。而有田無税者，行沒官之令；計丁分給者，嚴限田之條。畫之經界，載諸版籍，東作則秉耒以耕，西成則荷戈以練。食不虧而兵亦足，雖充國金城之屯、孔明渭濱之耕，率是道也，何憂乎屯政之不復耶？

鹽法之弊孔雜出，而課額折於流移，商賈阨於私販，此其大都也。整飭之要，在憲臣握其樞於上，而重有司稽察之柄。夫分漏辦鹽，凡以恤竈也；戢販防姦，凡以通商也。而公課私鹺，國有成憲。必也先覈額辦之丁，申布招商之令。戸絕者速為查豁，拖負者以漸追徵。即流離轉徙，而遺埕故漏，必有私自封殖者。願自陪納者聽，願
translation_en:
…and when taxes are levied by the mu, every pint and peck belongs to the public granaries. For annexing land and defaulting on payments, the state has regular penalties. What is essential is to verify whether registered households still exist or have died out, and to enforce the clear laws of land surveying. Those who illicitly sell colony land must be punished, and those who privately lease it must be prohibited. Even if the boundaries are confused and the registers lost, among the village elders are there not one or two survivors who know the truth? Pardon those who confess voluntarily, and pardon those whose occupation of the land dates back to their grandfathers or fathers; as for those who tamper with the registers, privately conceal land, and refuse to repent, prosecute them without the slightest leniency. Where there is land paying no tax, enforce the order of confiscation by the state; where land is allotted according to adult males, strictly enforce the regulations limiting landholdings. Demarcate the boundaries, record them in the registers, so that in the spring season of work they hold the plow to till, and in the autumn harvest they shoulder weapons to drill. Thus food will not be lacking and soldiers will also be sufficient. Even Zhao Chongguo's 趙充國 military colonies at Jincheng and Zhuge Kongming's 諸葛孔明 farming on the banks of the Wei River followed this very principle. Why then worry that the administration of military colonies cannot be restored?
